description.zh: 一个下午，爱丽丝追着一只揣着怀表的白兔掉进兔子洞，走进一个讲规矩、也讲荒唐的世界。
description.en: One afternoon Alice follows a waistcoat-wearing White Rabbit down a hole into a world that is as rule-bound as it is absurd.

source.note: Text from the Wikisource transcription of the 1866 Macmillan printing (PD worldwide; Carroll died 1898). Illustrations are not bundled.

paragraphs.text: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having nothing to do: once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it had no pictures or conversations in it, "and what is the use of a book," thought Alice, "without pictures or conversations?"

sentences.text: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having nothing to do: once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it had no pictures or conversations in it, "and what is the use of a book," thought Alice, "without pictures or conversations?"
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝挨着姐姐坐在河岸上，无事可做，开始觉得非常厌烦：她朝姐姐正在读的那本书瞄了一两次，可书里既没有图画，也没有对话。“一本书，”爱丽丝心想，“没有图画、没有对话，又有什么用呢？”

hints.zh: 爱丽丝，本书的小主角，一个爱幻想的小女孩。
hints.en: Alice, the young heroine of the book.

paragraphs.text: So she was considering in her own mind, (as well as she could, for the hot day made her feel very sleepy and stupid,) whether the pleasure of making a daisy-chain would be worth the trouble of getting up and picking the daisies, when suddenly a white rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her.

sentences.text: So she was considering in her own mind, (as well as she could, for the hot day made her feel very sleepy and stupid,) whether the pleasure of making a daisy-chain would be worth the trouble of getting up and picking the daisies, when suddenly a white rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her.
sentences.zh: 于是她在心里盘算（也只能勉强想想，因为炎热的天气让她昏昏欲睡、脑袋发木）：编一个雏菊花环的乐趣，值不值得费劲爬起来去摘雏菊？就在这时，一只粉红眼睛的白兔忽然从她身边跑过。

hints.zh: 雏菊花环：把雏菊的花茎互相穿起来做成的链子。
hints.en: A chain made by joining daisy stems together.

hints.zh: 白兔，一只揣着怀表的兔子，故事就从它跑过这里开始。
hints.en: The White Rabbit, whose watch sets the story going.

paragraphs.text: There was nothing so very remarkable in that; nor did Alice think it so very much out of the way to hear the Rabbit say to itself, "Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be too late!" (when she thought it over afterwards, it occurred to her that she ought to have wondered at this, but at the time it all seemed quite natural;) but when the Rabbit actually took a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket, and looked at it, and then hurried on, Alice started to her feet, for it flashed across her mind that she had never before seen a rabbit with either a waistcoat-pocket, or a watch to take out of it, and, burning with curiosity, she ran across the field after it, and was just in time to see it pop down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge.

sentences.text: There was nothing so very remarkable in that; nor did Alice think it so very much out of the way to hear the Rabbit say to itself, "Oh dear!
sentences.zh: 这本来没什么可大惊小怪的；爱丽丝也不觉得听兔子自言自语“哦，天哪！

sentences.text: Oh dear!
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪！

sentences.text: I shall be too late!" (when she thought it over afterwards, it occurred to her that she ought to have wondered at this, but at the time it all seemed quite natural;) but when the Rabbit actually took a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket, and looked at it, and then hurried on, Alice started to her feet, for it flashed across her mind that she had never before seen a rabbit with either a waistcoat-pocket, or a watch to take out of it, and, burning with curiosity, she ran across the field after it, and was just in time to see it pop down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge.
sentences.zh: 我要迟到了！”有什么反常（事后回想起来，她才觉得自己当时本该觉得奇怪，可那会儿一切都显得很自然。）可是，当兔子真的从背心口袋里掏出一块怀表，看了看，又匆匆往前赶时，爱丽丝一下子站了起来，因为她猛然想到：自己从没见过哪只兔子有背心口袋，也从没见过哪只兔子能从里面掏出怀表。她好奇心起，追着兔子跑过田野，正好赶上看见它钻进树篱下的一个大兔子洞。

hints.zh: 反常的、异乎寻常的；not … out of the way 就是“不算稀奇”。
hints.en: Unusual; not out of the way means not strange.

hints.zh: 背心口袋；waistcoat 是英式英语里的马甲。
hints.en: A pocket in a waistcoat, the British word for a vest.

paragraphs.text: In another moment down went Alice after it, never once considering how in the world she was to get out again.

sentences.text: In another moment down went Alice after it, never once considering how in the world she was to get out again.
sentences.zh: 转眼间，爱丽丝也跟着跳了下去，压根没想过自己究竟要怎么再出来。

hints.zh: 究竟、到底，用在疑问句里加强语气，相当于 on earth。
hints.en: Used in questions for emphasis, like 'on earth'.

introduction.zh: 河岸上的下午又热又闷，爱丽丝无事可做，姐姐的书里连图画也没有。忽然，一只白兔从她身边跑过，嘴里念着“要迟到了”，还从背心口袋里掏出一块怀表。你会跟上去吗？
introduction.en: A hot, sleepy afternoon by the river, and Alice has nothing to do. Her sister's book has no pictures in it. Then a white rabbit runs past, muttering that it will be late — and it takes a watch out of its waistcoat pocket. Would you follow it?

quiz.question: Why does Alice find the afternoon boring?
options: The book has no pictures or conversations
Her sister will not speak to her
She is lost in a field
She has finished all her lessons

feedback.zh: 姐姐在看书，书里既没有图画也没有对话，爱丽丝无事可做，只觉得厌烦。
feedback.en: Her sister's book has no pictures or conversations in it, so Alice has nothing to do.

quiz.question: What makes Alice jump up and run after the Rabbit?
options: The Rabbit drops a golden key
The Rabbit asks her the way
The Rabbit speaks to her
The Rabbit takes a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket

feedback.zh: 兔子开口说话她并不觉得奇怪，真正让她吃惊的是兔子掏出怀表看时间。
feedback.en: A talking rabbit does not surprise her; the watch from its waistcoat pocket does.

grammar.excerpt: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister

focus.zh: was beginning 是过去进行时，把“开始觉得”写成一个正在展开的过程，而不是一下子就觉得。
focus.en: Was beginning is past continuous: it makes the feeling a process unfolding rather than a single moment.

paragraphs.text: The rabbit-hole went straight on like a tunnel for some way, and then dipped suddenly down, so suddenly that Alice had not a moment to think about stopping herself before she found herself falling down what seemed to be a very deep well.

sentences.text: The rabbit-hole went straight on like a tunnel for some way, and then dipped suddenly down, so suddenly that Alice had not a moment to think about stopping herself before she found herself falling down what seemed to be a very deep well.
sentences.zh: 兔子洞像隧道一样笔直向前延伸了一段，随后突然向下陡降——陡得爱丽丝连想一想该怎么让自己停下来的工夫都没有，就已经发现自己正朝下落，落进一口似乎很深的井里。

hints.zh: 让自己停下来、刹住自己；stop oneself 指靠自己的力量停住。
hints.en: Bringing herself to a stop.

paragraphs.text: Either the well was very deep, or she fell very slowly, for she had plenty of time as she went down to look about her, and to wonder what was going to happen next. First, she tried to look down and make out what she was coming to, but it was too dark to see anything: then she looked at the sides of the well, and noticed that they were filled with cupboards and book-shelves: here and there she saw maps and pictures hung upon pegs. She took down a jar from one of the shelves as she passed; it was labelled "ORANGE MARMALADE," but to her great disappointment it was empty: she did not like to drop the jar for fear of killing somebody underneath, so managed to put it into one of the cupboards as she fell past it.

sentences.text: Either the well was very deep, or she fell very slowly, for she had plenty of time as she went down to look about her, and to wonder what was going to happen next.
sentences.zh: 要么是这口井非常深，要么是她落得非常慢，因为往下落的时候，她有充足的时间环顾四周，琢磨接下来会发生什么事。

sentences.text: First, she tried to look down and make out what she was coming to, but it was too dark to see anything: then she looked at the sides of the well, and noticed that they were filled with cupboards and book-shelves: here and there she saw maps and pictures hung upon pegs.
sentences.zh: 起初，她试着往下看，想弄清自己会落到什么地方，可下面太黑，什么也看不见；于是她去看井壁，发现壁上满是碗柜和书架；她还时不时看见挂在木钉上的地图和图画。

sentences.text: She took down a jar from one of the shelves as she passed; it was labelled "ORANGE MARMALADE," but to her great disappointment it was empty: she did not like to drop the jar for fear of killing somebody underneath, so managed to put it into one of the cupboards as she fell past it.
sentences.zh: 她经过一个架子时，从上面取下一只罐子；罐子上贴着“橘子果酱”的标签，可让她大失所望的是，罐子是空的。她不愿把罐子扔下去，怕砸死下面的人，于是趁着下落经过一个碗柜时，设法把它放了进去。

hints.zh: 辨认出、看清，常与 can/could 连用。
hints.en: To see or understand something with difficulty.

hints.zh: 橘子果酱；英国下午茶抹在面包上的常见果酱，所以爱丽丝一看标签就认得。
hints.en: Orange marmalade, a common British jam for bread at tea; Alice knows the label at once.

hints.zh: 因为怕……、唯恐……；后面接名词或 -ing。
hints.en: Because of being afraid that something bad may happen.

paragraphs.text: "Well!" thought Alice to herself, "after such a fall as this, I shall think nothing of tumbling down stairs! How brave they'll all think me at home! Why, I wouldn't say anything about it, even if I fell off the top of the house!" (Which was very likely true.)

sentences.text: "Well!" thought Alice to herself, "after such a fall as this, I shall think nothing of tumbling down stairs!
sentences.zh: “好啊！”爱丽丝心里想，“摔过这么一跤之后，从楼梯上滚下去我都不当回事了！

sentences.text: How brave they'll all think me at home!
sentences.zh: 家里人该会觉得我多勇敢啊！

sentences.text: Why, I wouldn't say anything about it, even if I fell off the top of the house!" (Which was very likely true.)
sentences.zh: 哎，就算我从屋顶上摔下去，我也不会提这件事的！”（这倒很可能是真的。）

hints.zh: 不把……当回事、觉得……不算什么。
hints.en: To consider something easy or unimportant.

introduction.zh: 兔子洞先像隧道一样笔直向前，接着猛地向下陡降，爱丽丝连收住脚的工夫都没有，就落进了一口深井。井壁上竟然排着碗柜和书架，她还能伸手取下一只罐子。这一路到底有多深？
introduction.en: The hole runs straight like a tunnel, then drops without warning, and Alice is falling down a well. The sides are lined with cupboards and book-shelves, and she can even take down a jar as she passes. How deep can it be?

quiz.question: What happens to the rabbit-hole after it runs straight for a while?
options: It ends at a locked door
It turns back towards the field
It suddenly drops down
It opens into a wide cave

feedback.zh: 兔子洞先像隧道一样笔直延伸，随后突然向下陡降，爱丽丝来不及反应就落了下去。
feedback.en: The hole runs straight like a tunnel, then drops without warning, and Alice is falling.

quiz.question: Why does Alice put the empty jar into a cupboard?
options: She is afraid it would hit somebody below
The cupboard is full of marmalade
The jar is too heavy to hold
She wants to keep it for the journey

feedback.zh: 她怕把罐子扔下去会砸到下面的人，只好在下落经过碗柜时把它放进去。
feedback.en: She is afraid the jar would hit somebody underneath, so she puts it into a cupboard as she falls.

grammar.excerpt: so suddenly that Alice had not a moment to think about stopping herself

focus.zh: so + 副词 suddenly 说陡降的程度，that 从句给出结果：她连想停下来的时间都没有。
focus.en: So with the adverb suddenly measures the drop, and the that-clause gives the result: she had no time to think about stopping.

paragraphs.text: Down, down, down. Would the fall never come to an end! "I wonder how many miles I've fallen by this time'?" she said aloud. "I must be getting somewhere near the centre of the earth. Let me see: that would be four thousand miles down, I think—" (for, you see, Alice had learnt several things of this sort in her lessons in the schoolroom, and though this was not a very good opportunity for showing off her knowledge, as there was no one to listen to her, still it was good practice to say it over) "—yes, that's about the right distance—but then I wonder what Latitude or Longitude I've got to?" (Alice had not the slightest idea what Latitude was, or Longitude either, but she thought they were nice grand words to say.)

sentences.text: Down, down, down.
sentences.zh: 向下，向下，向下。

sentences.text: Would the fall never come to an end!
sentences.zh: 这坠落难道永远没有尽头吗！

sentences.text: "I wonder how many miles I've fallen by this time'?" she said aloud.
sentences.zh: “不知道这会儿我已经落了多少英里了？”她大声说。

sentences.text: "I must be getting somewhere near the centre of the earth.
sentences.zh: “我准是快落到地心附近的什么地方了。

sentences.text: Let me see: that would be four thousand miles down, I think—" (for, you see, Alice had learnt several things of this sort in her lessons in the schoolroom, and though this was not a very good opportunity for showing off her knowledge, as there was no one to listen to her, still it was good practice to say it over) "—yes, that's about the right distance—but then I wonder what Latitude or Longitude I've got to?" (Alice had not the slightest idea what Latitude was, or Longitude either, but she thought they were nice grand words to say.)
sentences.zh: 让我想想：那该是往下四千英里吧，我想——”（因为，你要知道，爱丽丝在学堂的课上听讲过不少这一类的东西；虽说这不是炫耀学问的好机会，因为根本没人听她说话，可把它念叨一遍仍然是很好的练习）“——对，差不多就是这个距离——可这么一来，我不知道自己落到了什么纬度或经度？”（爱丽丝对纬度是什么、经度又是什么，一点概念也没有，只觉得这些词念起来又气派又好听。）

hints.zh: 结束、到头；这里说她盼着这一路坠落别再没完没了。
hints.en: To finish or stop.

hints.zh: 炫耀、卖弄；show off 的 -ing 形式。
hints.en: Trying to make others admire what one knows, as show off does.

hints.zh: 纬度；紧挨着的 Longitude 是“经度”。
hints.en: Distance north or south of the equator; Longitude, just after, is distance east or west.

paragraphs.text: Presently she began again. "I wonder if I shall fall right through the earth! How funny it'll seem to come out among the people that walk with their heads downwards! The Antipathies, I think—" (she was rather glad there was no one listening, this time, as it didn't sound at all the right word) "—but I shall have to ask them what the name of the country is, you know. Please, Ma'am, is this New Zealand or Australia?" (and she tried to curtsey as she spoke—fancy curtseying as you're falling through the air! Do you think you could manage it?) "And what an ignorant little girl she'll think me for asking! No, it'll never do to ask: perhaps I shall see it written up somewhere."

sentences.text: Presently she began again.
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，她又开口了。

sentences.text: "I wonder if I shall fall right through the earth!
sentences.zh: “不知道我会不会一直穿过地球掉下去！

sentences.text: How funny it'll seem to come out among the people that walk with their heads downwards!
sentences.zh: 从那些头朝下走路的人中间钻出来，那该多滑稽啊！

sentences.text: The Antipathies, I think—" (she was rather glad there was no one listening, this time, as it didn't sound at all the right word) "—but I shall have to ask them what the name of the country is, you know.
sentences.zh: 我想那地方叫‘对跖地’吧——”（这回她倒挺庆幸没人在听，因为这听起来根本不是那个正确的词）——“不过我得问问他们这个国家叫什么名字，你知道的。

sentences.text: Please, Ma'am, is this New Zealand or Australia?" (and she tried to curtsey as she spoke—fancy curtseying as you're falling through the air!
sentences.zh: “请问，夫人，这里是新西兰还是澳大利亚？”（她说着还想行个屈膝礼——想想看，人在半空里往下掉的时候还行屈膝礼！

sentences.text: Do you think you could manage it?) "And what an ignorant little girl she'll think me for asking!
sentences.zh: 你觉得你办得到吗？）“而且她准会觉得我是个多么无知的小姑娘，居然问这种问题！

sentences.text: No, it'll never do to ask: perhaps I shall see it written up somewhere."
sentences.zh: 不行，绝不能问：说不定我会在什么地方看到它写着呢。”

hints.zh: 不久、过了一会儿；不是“目前”。
hints.en: Soon, after a short time — not 'at present'.

hints.zh: 爱丽丝把 antipodes（对跖地，地球上正相对的地方）说成了 Antipathies（“反感”），她自己也知道这词不对。
hints.en: Alice's mistake for antipodes, the places on the opposite side of the earth; antipathies means feelings of dislike.

hints.zh: 行屈膝礼：女子微微屈膝打招呼的礼节，也拼作 curtsy。
hints.en: To bend the knees slightly as a polite greeting; also spelled curtsy.

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝还在往下落。为了不让自己害怕，她搬出课堂上学过的“纬度”“经度”，估算自己已经掉了多少英里，又想到自己会不会一直穿过地球，从另一头钻出来。她该怎么跟那边的人打招呼？
introduction.en: Alice is still falling, so she keeps herself busy with the Latitude and Longitude she learnt in the schoolroom. She works out how many miles she has dropped, then wonders whether she might fall right through the earth. How should she greet the people on the other side?

quiz.question: What is Alice trying to work out as she falls?
options: How she can climb back up
What time it is
How far down she has fallen
Where the White Rabbit has gone

feedback.zh: 她大声猜自己已经落了多少英里，还据此推算到地心的距离。
feedback.en: She guesses aloud how many miles she has fallen and works from that towards the centre of the earth.

quiz.question: What does Alice decide about asking the people the name of the country?
options: She will ask them politely
She will ask the Rabbit instead
She decides not to ask at all
She will write the name down herself

feedback.zh: 她怕人家觉得她无知，最后决定不问，只盼着能在什么地方看到地名写着。
feedback.en: She fears the people will think her ignorant, so she decides not to ask and hopes to see the name written somewhere.

grammar.excerpt: I wonder how many miles I've fallen by this time

focus.zh: wonder 后接 how many miles 引导的从句，从句用陈述语序 I've fallen，不能倒装成 have I fallen。
focus.en: Wonder is followed by a how many clause in statement order, I've fallen, not the question order have I fallen.

paragraphs.text: Down, down, down. There was nothing else to do, so Alice soon began talking again. "Dinah'll miss me very much to-night, I should think!" (Dinah was the cat.) "I hope they'll remember her saucer of milk at tea-time. Dinah, my dear! I wish you were down here with me! There are no mice in the air, I'm afraid, but you might catch a bat, and that's very like a mouse, you know. But do cats eat bats, I wonder?" And here Alice began to get rather sleepy, and went on saying to herself, in a dreamy sort of way, "Do cats eat bats? Do cats eat bats?" and sometimes, "Do bats eat cats?" for, you see, as she couldn't answer either question, it didn't much matter which way she put it. She felt that she was dozing off, and had just begun to dream that she was walking hand in hand with Dinah, and was saying to her very earnestly, "Now, Dinah, tell me the truth: did you ever eat a bat?" when suddenly, thump! thump! down she came upon a heap of sticks and dry leaves, and the fall was over.

sentences.text: Down, down, down.
sentences.zh: 向下，向下，向下。

sentences.text: There was nothing else to do, so Alice soon began talking again.
sentences.zh: 没有别的事可做，于是爱丽丝很快又开始说起话来。

sentences.text: "Dinah'll miss me very much to-night, I should think!" (Dinah was the cat.) "I hope they'll remember her saucer of milk at tea-time.
sentences.zh: “我想，黛娜今晚一定会很想我！”（黛娜就是那只猫。）“但愿他们别忘了在下午茶时给她留一碟牛奶。

sentences.text: Dinah, my dear!
sentences.zh: 黛娜，我亲爱的！

sentences.text: I wish you were down here with me!
sentences.zh: 我真希望你也在这下面，跟我在一起！

sentences.text: There are no mice in the air, I'm afraid, but you might catch a bat, and that's very like a mouse, you know.
sentences.zh: 恐怕这空中没有老鼠，不过你也许能抓只蝙蝠——你知道，蝙蝠长得很像老鼠。

sentences.text: But do cats eat bats, I wonder?"
sentences.zh: 可猫吃蝙蝠吗，我倒想知道？”

sentences.text: And here Alice began to get rather sleepy, and went on saying to herself, in a dreamy sort of way, "Do cats eat bats?
sentences.zh: 这时爱丽丝开始觉得相当困了，便用一种恍恍惚惚的口气继续自言自语：“猫吃蝙蝠吗？

sentences.text: Do cats eat bats?" and sometimes, "Do bats eat cats?" for, you see, as she couldn't answer either question, it didn't much matter which way she put it.
sentences.zh: 猫吃蝙蝠吗？”有时又说，“蝙蝠吃猫吗？”——你知道，既然这两个问题她一个也答不上来，那她怎么个问法也就没多大关系了。

sentences.text: She felt that she was dozing off, and had just begun to dream that she was walking hand in hand with Dinah, and was saying to her very earnestly, "Now, Dinah, tell me the truth: did you ever eat a bat?" when suddenly, thump! thump! down she came upon a heap of sticks and dry leaves, and the fall was over.
sentences.zh: 她觉得自己正在打瞌睡，刚做起梦来：梦见自己正和黛娜手拉着手走，还非常认真地对她说：“黛娜，现在你跟我说实话：你到底吃过蝙蝠没有？”就在这时，突然砰！砰！她落到了一堆枯枝和干叶上，这一摔总算结束了。

hints.zh: 黛娜，爱丽丝养的猫；她在下坠时一直惦记着它。
hints.en: Dinah, Alice's cat, who is on her mind all the way down.

hints.zh: 一碟牛奶；saucer 是托茶杯的浅碟，常用来给猫盛奶。
hints.en: A saucer of milk: a saucer is the shallow dish under a teacup, often used to feed a cat.

hints.zh: 恐怕、很遗憾，用来客气地说出不好的消息，不是“我害怕”。
hints.en: Used politely to announce bad news; it does not mean 'I am frightened'.

hints.zh: 老鼠；空中没有老鼠，爱丽丝只好退一步说蝙蝠长得很像老鼠。
hints.en: A mouse. There are no mice in the air, so Alice offers a bat as the next best thing.

hints.zh: 打瞌睡、迷迷糊糊地睡着；doze off 指不知不觉睡过去。
hints.en: Falling asleep gradually without noticing; doze off.

paragraphs.text: Alice was not a bit hurt, and she jumped up on to her feet in a moment: she looked up, but it was all dark overhead; before her was another long passage, and the White Rabbit was still in sight, hurrying down it. There was not a moment to be lost: away went Alice like the wind, and was just in time to hear it say, as it turned a corner, "Oh my ears and whiskers, how late it's getting!" She was close behind it when she turned the corner, but the Rabbit was no longer to be seen: she found herself in a long, low hall, which was lit up by a row of lamps hanging from the roof.

sentences.text: Alice was not a bit hurt, and she jumped up on to her feet in a moment: she looked up, but it was all dark overhead; before her was another long passage, and the White Rabbit was still in sight, hurrying down it.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝一点儿也没摔伤，她立刻跳了起来：抬头一看，头顶上漆黑一片；她面前又是一条长长的通道，白兔还在视线之内，正匆匆沿着通道跑去。

sentences.text: There was not a moment to be lost: away went Alice like the wind, and was just in time to hear it say, as it turned a corner, "Oh my ears and whiskers, how late it's getting!"
sentences.zh: 一刻也不能耽搁了：爱丽丝像一阵风似的飞奔出去，正好赶上听见它拐过弯时说道：“哦，我的耳朵和胡子啊，时候已经这么晚了！”

sentences.text: She was close behind it when she turned the corner, but the Rabbit was no longer to be seen: she found herself in a long, low hall, which was lit up by a row of lamps hanging from the roof.
sentences.zh: 她拐过弯时就在兔子后面不远，可兔子已经不见了：她发现自己来到一个又长又低的大厅，屋顶上挂着一排灯，把大厅照得通亮。

hints.zh: “哎呀，我的耳朵和胡子！”兔子的口头惊叹，相当于“天哪”。
hints.en: The Rabbit's exclamation of alarm, rather like 'Oh dear me!'

introduction.zh: 下落还没停止，爱丽丝开始跟家里的猫黛娜说话，一遍遍念着“猫吃蝙蝠吗”，念得自己越来越困。就在她快要睡着的时候，身下忽然响起两声闷响。她落到什么地方了？
introduction.en: Still falling, Alice talks to Dinah, her cat, and asks over and over whether cats eat bats. The question makes her drowsier and drowsier, until something thumps beneath her. Where has she landed?

quiz.question: Why does Alice begin talking to herself again?
options: There is nothing else for her to do
She wants her sister to hear her
She is angry with the Rabbit
She is trying to wake herself up

feedback.zh: 她在往下掉，没有别的事可做，只好又自言自语起来。
feedback.en: Falling with nothing else to do, she starts talking to herself again.

quiz.question: What is Alice doing just before she lands?
options: Looking for mice in the air
Counting the lamps above her
Crying for her sister
Dreaming that she is walking with Dinah

feedback.zh: 她打着瞌睡做起梦来，梦见和黛娜手拉手散步，还认真地问黛娜吃没吃过蝙蝠。
feedback.en: She is dozing and dreaming that she walks with Dinah, asking her earnestly whether she has ever eaten a bat.

grammar.excerpt: I wish you were down here with me

focus.zh: wish 后接与现在事实相反的愿望时用过去式，be 动词用 were：她希望黛娜此刻在身边，可它并不在。
focus.en: After wish, a wish contrary to the present takes the past tense, with were for be: she wants Dinah beside her now, but the cat is not there.

paragraphs.text: There were doors all round the hall, but they were all locked; and when Alice had been all the way down one side and up the other, trying every door, she walked sadly down the middle, wondering how she was ever to get out again.

sentences.text: There were doors all round the hall, but they were all locked; and when Alice had been all the way down one side and up the other, trying every door, she walked sadly down the middle, wondering how she was ever to get out again.
sentences.zh: 大厅四周全是门，可门全都锁着；爱丽丝顺着一边一路走到头，又顺着另一边走回来，把每扇门都试了一遍，然后伤心地走到大厅中央，心里琢磨着自己究竟还能怎么出去。

paragraphs.text: Suddenly she came upon a little three-legged table, all made of solid glass; there was nothing on it but a tiny golden key, and Alice's first idea was that this might belong to one of the doors of the hall; but, alas! either the locks were too large, or the key was too small, but at any rate it would not open any of them. However, on the second time round, she came upon a low curtain she had not noticed before, and behind it was a little door about fifteen inches high: she tried the little golden key in the lock, and to her great delight it fitted!

sentences.text: Suddenly she came upon a little three-legged table, all made of solid glass; there was nothing on it but a tiny golden key, and Alice's first idea was that this might belong to one of the doors of the hall; but, alas! either the locks were too large, or the key was too small, but at any rate it would not open any of them.
sentences.zh: 忽然，她来到一张小小的三条腿的桌子前，桌子整个是用实心玻璃做的；桌上什么也没有，只有一把小小的金钥匙。爱丽丝的第一个念头是：这把钥匙也许属于大厅里的某扇门；可是，唉！要么是锁太大，要么是钥匙太小，总之哪一扇门都打不开。

sentences.text: However, on the second time round, she came upon a low curtain she had not noticed before, and behind it was a little door about fifteen inches high: she tried the little golden key in the lock, and to her great delight it fitted!
sentences.zh: 不过，她第二圈转回来时，来到一道先前没注意到的矮帘子前，帘子后面是一扇大约十五英寸高的小门：她把那把小金钥匙插进锁里试了试，让她大喜过望的是，它正好合适！

hints.zh: 偶然发现、碰上；come upon 的过去式。
hints.en: Came across or found by chance; the past of come upon.

hints.zh: 三条腿的；-legged 表示“……条腿的”。
hints.en: Having three legs; -legged means 'having legs of that kind'.

hints.zh: 无论如何、反正；用来说不管哪种情况，结果都一样。
hints.en: In any case; whatever the reason, the result is the same.

hints.zh: （钥匙）正好合适、对得上；fit 的过去式。
hints.en: Was the right size for the lock; the past of fit.

paragraphs.text: Alice opened the door and found that it led into a small passage, not much larger than a rat-hole: she knelt down and looked along the passage into the loveliest garden you ever saw. How she longed to get out of that dark hall, and wander about among those beds of bright flowers and those cool fountains, but she could not even get her head through the doorway; "and even if my head would go through," thought poor Alice, "it would be of very little use without my shoulders. Oh, how I wish I could shut up like a telescope! I think I could, if I only knew how to begin." For, you see, so many out-of-the-way things had happened lately, that Alice had begun to think that very few things indeed were really impossible.

sentences.text: Alice opened the door and found that it led into a small passage, not much larger than a rat-hole: she knelt down and looked along the passage into the loveliest garden you ever saw.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝打开门，发现门通向一条小通道，比老鼠洞大不了多少：她跪下来，顺着通道望过去，望见一座你从没见过的最可爱的花园。

sentences.text: How she longed to get out of that dark hall, and wander about among those beds of bright flowers and those cool fountains, but she could not even get her head through the doorway; "and even if my head would go through," thought poor Alice, "it would be of very little use without my shoulders.
sentences.zh: 她多么渴望走出那个昏暗的大厅，到那些鲜艳的花圃和清凉的喷泉之间去游荡啊，可她连头都伸不过那个门洞；“就算我的头能伸过去，”可怜的爱丽丝想，“没有肩膀也是白搭。

sentences.text: Oh, how I wish I could shut up like a telescope!
sentences.zh: 哦，我多希望能像望远镜那样收起来呀！

sentences.text: I think I could, if I only knew how to begin."
sentences.zh: 我想我能做到，只要我知道该从哪儿开头。”

sentences.text: For, you see, so many out-of-the-way things had happened lately, that Alice had begun to think that very few things indeed were really impossible.
sentences.zh: 因为，你要知道，近来发生过那么多稀奇古怪的事，爱丽丝已经开始觉得，真正不可能的事实在没有几件了。

hints.zh: 渴望、极想；long to do 或 long for something。
hints.en: Wanted something very much; long to do or long for something.

hints.zh: 像望远镜那样收起来、折叠缩短；这里不是“闭嘴”。
hints.en: To fold up small like a telescope; it does not mean 'be quiet' here.

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝落进一间又长又低的大厅，四周的门全都锁着。她在玻璃桌上找到一把小金钥匙，第二圈转回来时，发现帘子后面藏着一扇十五英寸高的小门。门后是什么，她进得去吗？
introduction.en: Alice lands in a long, low hall where every door is locked. On a glass table she finds a tiny golden key, and on her second time round she spots a little door behind a curtain. What lies behind it, and is she small enough to go through?

quiz.question: Why does Alice walk sadly down the middle of the hall?
options: Every door round the hall is locked
The hall is too dark to see
She has lost the golden key
She cannot find her sister

feedback.zh: 她沿两边把每扇门都试过，门全锁着，只好伤心地走到大厅中央。
feedback.en: She has tried every door on both sides of the hall and found them all locked.

quiz.question: What does Alice find on her second time round the hall?
options: The White Rabbit's glove
A window looking onto the garden
A table with a cake on it
A low curtain with a little door behind it

feedback.zh: 第二圈时她发现一道先前没注意到的矮帘子，帘子后面是一扇十五英寸高的小门。
feedback.en: On her second time round she finds a low curtain she had not noticed, with a little door behind it.

grammar.excerpt: but they were all locked

focus.zh: were locked 是过去时的被动语态：门不是自己去锁，而是被人锁上的状态；all 放在 were 后面。
focus.en: Were locked is the past passive: the doors did not lock themselves; all follows were.

paragraphs.text: There seemed to be no use in waiting by the little door, so she went back to the table, half hoping she might find another key on it, or at any rate a book of rules for shutting people up like telescopes: this time she found a little bottle on it, ("which certainly was not here before," said Alice,) and tied round the neck of the bottle was a paper label, with the words "DRINK ME," beautifully printed on it in large letters.

sentences.text: There seemed to be no use in waiting by the little door, so she went back to the table, half hoping she might find another key on it, or at any rate a book of rules for shutting people up like telescopes: this time she found a little bottle on it, ("which certainly was not here before," said Alice,) and tied round the neck of the bottle was a paper label, with the words "DRINK ME," beautifully printed on it in large letters.
sentences.zh: 守在小门旁边干等似乎也没什么用，于是她回到桌子旁，心里还抱着一半希望：也许能在桌上找到另一把钥匙，或者至少找到一本教人怎样像望远镜那样把人收起来的规矩书。这一回，她在桌上发现了一个小瓶子（“这东西刚才肯定不在这儿，”爱丽丝说），而瓶颈上系着一张纸标签，上面用漂亮的字体、大大的字母印着“喝我”。

hints.zh: 像望远镜那样把人收起来：老式望远镜能一节节缩回去，这里指把人折叠、缩小收好，是爱丽丝觉得荒唐又盼望的办法。
hints.en: Folding people up like old telescopes, which slide shut in sections; Alice imagines shrinking someone down to fit.

paragraphs.text: It was all very well to say "Drink me," but the wise little Alice was not going to do that in a hurry. "No, I'll look first," she said, "and see whether it's marked 'poison' or not;" for she had read several nice little stories about children who had got burnt, and eaten up by wild beasts and other unpleasant things, all because they would not remember the simple rules their friends had taught them: such as, that a red-hot poker will burn you if you hold it too long; and that if you cut your finger very deeply with a knife, it usually bleeds; and she had never forgotten that, if you drink much from a bottle marked "poison," it is almost certain to disagree with you, sooner or later.

sentences.text: It was all very well to say "Drink me," but the wise little Alice was not going to do that in a hurry.
sentences.zh: 说一声“喝我”倒容易，可聪明的小爱丽丝并不打算急急忙忙就照办。

sentences.text: "No, I'll look first," she said, "and see whether it's marked 'poison' or not;" for she had read several nice little stories about children who had got burnt, and eaten up by wild beasts and other unpleasant things, all because they would not remember the simple rules their friends had taught them: such as, that a red-hot poker will burn you if you hold it too long; and that if you cut your finger very deeply with a knife, it usually bleeds; and she had never forgotten that, if you drink much from a bottle marked "poison," it is almost certain to disagree with you, sooner or later.
sentences.zh: “不行，我得先看看，”她说，“看上面有没有标着‘毒药’。”因为她念过好几篇有趣的小故事，讲的都是小孩子被烧伤、被野兽吃掉，还有遇上别的倒霉事，全是因为他们不肯记住朋友们教给他们的那些简单道理：比如，烧得通红的火钳，你要是握得太久，就会把你烫伤；又比如，你要是用刀把手指割得很深，通常就会流血；而且她从来没忘记，要是你从一个标着“毒药”的瓶子里喝下很多，那几乎可以肯定，它迟早会让你不舒服。

hints.zh: 匆忙地、急急忙忙；not … in a hurry 就是“不急着……”，不慌不忙。
hints.en: Quickly or too fast; not … in a hurry means 'in no rush at all'.

hints.zh: 烧得通红的火钳；poker 是拨火、捅炉子用的铁棍。
hints.en: A red-hot poker, the iron rod used to stir a fire.

hints.zh: （食物、饮料）让……肠胃不舒服、闹肚子；这里不是“不同意你”。
hints.en: Of food or drink: to make someone ill; not 'to argue with you'.

hints.zh: 迟早、早晚，表示不管怎样最后都会发生。
hints.en: At some time in the future, whatever happens.

paragraphs.text: However, this bottle was not marked "poison," so Alice ventured to taste it, and finding it very nice, (it had, in fact, a sort of mixed flavour of cherry-tart, custard, pine-apple, roast turkey, toffee, and hot buttered toast,) she very soon finished it off.

sentences.text: However, this bottle was not marked "poison," so Alice ventured to taste it, and finding it very nice, (it had, in fact, a sort of mixed flavour of cherry-tart, custard, pine-apple, roast turkey, toffee, and hot buttered toast,) she very soon finished it off.
sentences.zh: 不过，这个瓶子并没有标着“毒药”，于是爱丽丝壮着胆子尝了一口，觉得味道很好（其实，它有一股混合的味道，像樱桃馅饼、蛋奶糊、菠萝、烤火鸡、太妃糖和热黄油吐司混在一起），她很快就把它喝光了。

hints.zh: 把它喝光、吃光；finish something off 指把剩下的全部解决掉。
hints.en: Drank or ate all of it; finish something off means to use up what is left.

introduction.zh: 桌上多了一个小瓶子，标签上用大字印着“喝我”。爱丽丝没有马上照办：她先要看清楚瓶子上有没有写“毒药”，还想起了故事里那些忘了规矩的孩子。这瓶东西能喝吗？
introduction.en: A little bottle has appeared on the table, with DRINK ME printed on the label. Alice will not drink it in a hurry: first she checks for the word poison, and remembers the children in stories who forgot simple rules. Is it safe to drink?

quiz.question: Why does Alice go back to the table at the start of this unit?
options: She wants to write a letter to her sister
She hopes to find another key or a book of rules
She wants to fetch her gloves and her fan
She is hungry and hopes to find some food

feedback.zh: 在门边干等没用，她回桌子是想找另一把钥匙，或者至少找一本讲规矩的书。
feedback.en: Waiting by the door is no use, so she goes back hoping for another key or a book of rules.

quiz.question: Why does Alice refuse to drink from the bottle at once?
options: She wants to check that it is not marked "poison"
She thinks the bottle belongs to the Rabbit
She cannot get the cork out of the bottle
She is not at all thirsty

feedback.zh: 她要先看看标签上有没有写“毒药”，因为故事里的孩子就是忘了这些规矩才出事的。
feedback.en: She wants to check for the word poison first, because children in stories came to harm by forgetting such rules.

grammar.excerpt: if you drink much from a bottle marked "poison," it is almost certain to disagree with you

focus.zh: if 从句讲条件，用一般现在时 drink，主句用 is 说结果；英语条件句里从句不用 will。
focus.en: The if-clause states the condition in the present simple, drink, and the main clause gives the result with is; English does not use will in the if-clause.

paragraphs.text: "What a curious feeling!" said Alice; "I must be shutting up like a telescope."

sentences.text: "What a curious feeling!" said Alice; "I must be shutting up like a telescope."
sentences.zh: “多么奇怪的感觉啊！”爱丽丝说，“我一定是在像望远镜一样收拢起来了。”

hints.zh: 奇怪的、离奇的；这里不是“好奇的”，说的是身体变小这件事很古怪。
hints.en: Strange or odd here, not 'eager to know'.

paragraphs.text: And so it was indeed: she was now only ten inches high, and her face brightened up at the thought that she was now the right size for going through the little door into that lovely garden. First, however, she waited for a few minutes to see if she was going to shrink any further: she felt a little nervous about this; "for it might end, you know," said Alice to herself, "in my going out altogether, like a candle. I wonder what I should be like then?" And she tried to fancy what the flame of a candle looks like after the candle is blown out, for she could not remember ever having seen such a thing.

sentences.text: And so it was indeed: she was now only ten inches high, and her face brightened up at the thought that she was now the right size for going through the little door into that lovely garden.
sentences.zh: 确实如此：她现在只有十英寸高了，想到自己现在的个头正好能穿过那扇小门，走进那座可爱的花园，她脸上顿时露出了喜色。

sentences.text: First, however, she waited for a few minutes to see if she was going to shrink any further: she felt a little nervous about this; "for it might end, you know," said Alice to herself, "in my going out altogether, like a candle.
sentences.zh: 不过，她先等了几分钟，看看自己是不是还会再缩小：她为此有点紧张；“因为，你知道，这也许会，”爱丽丝对自己说，“弄到最后我整个人都没了，就像一支蜡烛。

sentences.text: I wonder what I should be like then?"
sentences.zh: 那我到时候会是什么样子呢？”

sentences.text: And she tried to fancy what the flame of a candle looks like after the candle is blown out, for she could not remember ever having seen such a thing.
sentences.zh: 她试着去想象蜡烛被吹灭之后火苗是什么样子，因为她记不起自己曾见过这样的景象。

hints.zh: （脸上）露出喜色、高兴起来。
hints.en: Of a face: to light up with pleasure.

hints.zh: 缩小、缩回去；这里指身体越变越小。
hints.en: To become smaller; here Alice's body is getting tinier.

hints.zh: （蜡烛、灯火）熄灭；爱丽丝用它比喻自己整个人消失掉。
hints.en: Of a flame: to go out; Alice uses it for vanishing completely.

hints.zh: 想象、设想；fancy 在这里是动词，tried to fancy 就是“努力去想象”。
hints.en: To imagine; here fancy is a verb, so tried to fancy means 'tried to picture'.

paragraphs.text: After a while, finding that nothing more happened, she decided on going into the garden at once; but, alas for poor Alice! when she got to the door, she found she had forgotten the little golden key, and when she went back to the table for it, she found she could not possibly reach it: she could see it quite plainly through the glass, and she tried her best to climb up one of the legs of the table, but it was too slippery; and when she had tired herself out with trying, the poor little thing sat down and cried.

sentences.text: After a while, finding that nothing more happened, she decided on going into the garden at once; but, alas for poor Alice! when she got to the door, she found she had forgotten the little golden key, and when she went back to the table for it, she found she could not possibly reach it: she could see it quite plainly through the glass, and she tried her best to climb up one of the legs of the table, but it was too slippery; and when she had tired herself out with trying, the poor little thing sat down and cried.
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，她发现再没有别的事情发生，就决定马上到花园里去；可是，可怜的爱丽丝真倒霉！她走到门口时，发现自己把小金钥匙忘了，等她回到桌边去取，又发现自己根本够不着它：隔着玻璃她看得清清楚楚，还想尽办法顺着一条桌腿往上爬，可桌腿太滑了；等她试得筋疲力尽，这可怜的小家伙就坐下来哭了。

hints.zh: 把自己累得筋疲力尽；tire oneself out。
hints.en: Made herself completely exhausted; tire oneself out.

introduction.zh: 喝下瓶里的东西后，爱丽丝真的缩了下去，只剩十英寸高，正好能钻过那扇小门。可她先站着等了几分钟，怕自己会一直缩下去，像蜡烛一样烧完。等她决定进花园，又出了什么岔子？
introduction.en: The drink works: Alice shrinks to ten inches, just the right size for the little door. But she waits a few minutes first, afraid that she may keep shrinking and go out like a candle. When she finally decides to go into the garden, what goes wrong?

quiz.question: Why does Alice wait a few minutes instead of going to the garden at once?
options: She cannot find the little door
She is too tired to walk
She wants the White Rabbit to come back
She is afraid she may go on shrinking and vanish like a burnt-out candle

paragraphs.text: "Come, there's no use in crying like that!" said Alice to herself, rather sharply; "I advise you to leave off this minute!" She generally gave herself very good advice, (though she very seldom followed it,) and sometimes she scolded herself so severely as to bring tears into her eyes; and once she remembered trying to box her own ears for having cheated herself in a game of croquet she was playing against herself, for this curious child was very fond of pretending to be two people. "But it's no use now," thought poor Alice, "to pretend to be two people! Why, there's hardly enough of me left to make one respectable person!"

paragraphs.text: She ate a little bit, and said anxiously to herself, "Which way? which way?" holding her hand on the top of her head to feel which way it was growing, and she was quite surprised to find that she remained the same size: to be sure, this is what generally happens when one eats cake, but Alice had got so much into the way of expecting nothing but out-of-the-way things to happen, that it seemed quite dull and stupid for life to go on in the common way.

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝一边哭，一边严厉地训斥自己，还想起自己平常给自己出的那些好主意。不久，她的目光落到桌下一只玻璃盒上，里面是一块用醋栗干写着“吃我”的小蛋糕。这一次她敢吃吗？
introduction.en: Crying and scolding herself at the same time, Alice remembers all the good advice she usually gives herself. Then she notices a glass box under the table, with a tiny cake inside marked EAT ME in currants. Will she dare to eat it?

quiz.question: What does Alice tell herself to do at the start of this unit?

Either way, larger or smaller, she will get into the garden

paragraphs.text: "Curiouser and curiouser!" cried Alice (she was so much surprised, that for the moment she quite forgot how to speak good English); "now I'm opening out like the largest telescope that ever was! Good-bye, feet!" (for when she looked down at her feet, they seemed to be almost out of sight, they were getting so far off). "Oh, my poor little feet, I wonder who will put on your shoes and stockings for you now, dears? I'm sure I shan't be able! I shall be a great deal too far off to trouble myself about you: you must manage the best way you can;—but I must be kind to them," thought Alice, "or perhaps they won't walk the way I want to go! Let me see: I'll give them a new pair of boots every Christmas."

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝在门厅里越长越高，双脚远得几乎看不见了。她索性盘算起圣诞节的事，要给自己的一双脚寄一双新靴子。可她的头顶忽然撞上了天花板，花园的小门还是过不去——她还能变回去吗？
introduction.en: Alice keeps growing taller in the hall until her own feet are almost out of sight. She starts planning a Christmas present for them: a new pair of boots. Then her head hits the roof, and the little door to the garden still will not let her through.

quiz.question: Why does Alice begin talking to her feet?
options: They are so far away that she can hardly see them.
They hurt after she hit the roof.
They are cold and need shoes.

quiz.question: What keeps Alice out of the garden?
options: She has grown far too big for the little door.
The key no longer fits the door.
The garden door is locked from the other side.

title.en: Who in the World Am I?

But she went on all the same, shedding gallons of tears, until there was a large pool all round her, about four inches deep and reaching half down the hall.

paragraphs.text: After a time she heard a little pattering of feet in the distance, and she hastily dried her eyes to see what was coming. It was the White Rabbit returning, splendidly dressed, with a pair of white kid gloves in one hand and a large fan in the other: he came trotting along in a great hurry, muttering to himself as he came, "Oh! the Duchess, the Duchess! Oh! won't she be savage if I've kept her waiting!" Alice felt so desperate that she was ready to ask help of any one; so, when the Rabbit came near her, she began, in a low, timid voice, "If you please, sir——" The Rabbit started violently, dropped the white kid gloves and the fan, and skurried away into the darkness as hard as he could go.

paragraphs.text: Alice took up the fan and gloves, and, as the hall was very hot, she kept fanning herself all the time she went on talking: "Dear, dear! How queer everything is to-day! And yesterday things went on just as usual. I wonder if I've been changed in the night? Let me think: was I the same when I got up this morning? I almost think I can remember feeling a little different. But if I'm not the same, the next question is. Who in the world am I? Ah, that's the great puzzle!" And she began thinking over all the children she knew, that were of the same age as herself, to see if she could have been changed for any of them.

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝一个人待在门厅里，边哭边责怪自己，眼泪竟在地上积成了一片水池。白兔从旁边经过，她捡起了地上那把扇子。扇着风，她忽然冒出一个念头：一夜之间，自己会不会已经变成了另一个人？
introduction.en: Alone in the hall, Alice scolds herself for crying, but her tears soon make a pool on the floor. When the White Rabbit passes, she picks up the fan he has dropped. Fanning herself, she begins to wonder whether the night has turned her into somebody else.

quiz.question: Why does the Rabbit run off when Alice speaks to him?
options: He is already late and cannot stop.
He does not like the way she speaks.

feedback.en: She wonders whether she has been changed in the night.

grammar.excerpt: You ought to be ashamed of yourself

focus.zh: ought to 后接动词原形，说的是“按理应该”；这里是爱丽丝在责备自己。

paragraphs.text: "I'm sure I'm not Ada," she said, "for her hair goes in such long ringlets, and mine doesn't go in ringlets at all; and I'm sure I can't be Mabel, for I know all sorts of things, and she, oh! she knows such a very little! Besides, she's she, and I'm I, and—oh dear, how puzzling it all is! I'll try if I know all the things I used to know. Let me see: four times five is twelve, and four times six is thirteen, and four times seven is—oh dear! I shall never get to twenty at that rate! However, the Multiplication Table doesn't signify: let's try Geography. London is the capital of Paris, and Paris is the capital of Rome, and Rome—no, that's all wrong, I'm certain! I must have been changed for Mabel! I'll try and say 'How doth the little—'" and she crossed her hands on her lap as if she were saying lessons, and began to repeat it, but her voice sounded hoarse and strange, and the words did not come the same as they used to do:—

sentences.text: "I'm sure I'm not Ada," she said, "for her hair goes in such long ringlets, and mine doesn't go in ringlets at all; and I'm sure I can't be Mabel, for I know all sorts of things, and she, oh! she knows such a very little!
sentences.zh: “我肯定不是艾达，”她说，“因为她的头发是一长串卷儿，我的头发根本卷不起来；我也肯定不是梅布尔，因为我懂各种各样的事，而她，哦！她懂的可太少啦！

sentences.text: Besides, she's she, and I'm I, and—oh dear, how puzzling it all is!
sentences.zh: 再说，她是她，我是我，而且——哦天哪，这一切多让人糊涂啊！

sentences.text: I'll try if I know all the things I used to know.
sentences.zh: 我来试试还记不记得从前会背的那些东西。

sentences.text: Let me see: four times five is twelve, and four times six is thirteen, and four times seven is—oh dear!
sentences.zh: 让我想想：四乘五等于十二，四乘六等于十三，四乘七等于——哦天哪！

sentences.text: I shall never get to twenty at that rate!
sentences.zh: 照这个速度，我一辈子也数不到二十！

sentences.text: However, the Multiplication Table doesn't signify: let's try Geography.
sentences.zh: 不过，乘法表不要紧：咱们来试试地理。

sentences.text: London is the capital of Paris, and Paris is the capital of Rome, and Rome—no, that's all wrong, I'm certain!
sentences.zh: 伦敦是巴黎的首都，巴黎是罗马的首都，罗马——不对，全错了，我敢肯定！

sentences.text: I must have been changed for Mabel!
sentences.zh: 我一定是被换成梅布尔了！

sentences.text: I'll try and say 'How doth the little—'" and she crossed her hands on her lap as if she were saying lessons, and began to repeat it, but her voice sounded hoarse and strange, and the words did not come the same as they used to do:—
sentences.zh: “我来背背‘小小——’”她把手交叉放在膝上，好像在做功课，然后开始背起来，可她的声音又哑又怪，词儿也不像从前那样出来了：——

hints.zh: 艾达，爱丽丝认识的小姑娘。
hints.en: Ada, a girl Alice knows.

hints.zh: 梅布尔，爱丽丝认识的另一个小姑娘。
hints.en: Mabel, another girl Alice knows.

hints.zh: 不要紧、无关紧要。
hints.en: Does not matter.

hints.zh: 当时课本里一首训诫诗的开头，原诗讲勤劳的小蜜蜂。
hints.en: The opening of a moral poem children learned, about the busy bee.

paragraphs.text: "How doth the little crocodile Improve his shining tail, And pour the waters of the Nile On every golden scale!

sentences.text: "How doth the little crocodile Improve his shining tail, And pour the waters of the Nile On every golden scale!
sentences.zh: “小小的鳄鱼怎样／把闪亮的尾巴打理，／把尼罗河的水／浇在每一片金色的鳞甲上！

hints.zh: 爱丽丝背出来的这一版把原诗的蜜蜂换成了鳄鱼。
hints.en: In Alice's version of the poem the busy bee has become a crocodile.

paragraphs.text: "How cheerfully he seems to grin, How neatly spreads his claws, And welcomes little fishes in With gently smiling jaws!"

sentences.text: "How cheerfully he seems to grin, How neatly spreads his claws, And welcomes little fishes in With gently smiling jaws!"
sentences.zh: “他笑得多开心，／爪子张得多齐整，／把小鱼儿一条条请进来，／用温柔微笑的下巴！”

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝想用功课证明自己还是原来的自己：她背乘法表，四乘五竟成了十二；她又考自己地理，伦敦成了巴黎的首都。她只好换一首早已背熟的训诫诗，看看嘴里的词儿还对不对。
introduction.en: Alice tries to prove she is still herself by reciting what she has learned. The multiplication table comes out wrong, and so does her geography. So she turns to a moral poem she once knew by heart, to see whether the words still come out right.

quiz.question: How does Alice test whether she is still herself?
options: She repeats lessons she used to know.
She asks the Mouse to tell her name.
She compares her hair with Ada's.

feedback.zh: 她决定试试自己还记不记得从前会背的功课，用这个来判断自己有没有变。
feedback.en: She tries the lessons she used to know, to see whether she is still the same girl.

quiz.question: What goes wrong when Alice tries her geography?
options: She cannot remember any capital city.
She mixes up which city is the capital of which country.
She forgets what the word 'capital' means.

feedback.zh: 她说伦敦是巴黎的首都、巴黎是罗马的首都，自己也马上知道全错了。
feedback.en: She gives London as the capital of Paris and Paris as the capital of Rome, then admits it is all wrong.

grammar.excerpt: I'll try if I know all the things I used to know.

focus.zh: used to + 动词原形，表示“从前会、过去常常”，与前面的 I'll try 形成对照。
focus.en: 'Used to' + base verb means 'knew or did in the past', in contrast with 'I'll try' now.

paragraphs.text: "I'm sure those are not the right words," said poor Alice, and her eyes filled with tears again as she went on, "I must be Mabel after all, and I shall have to go and live in that poky little house, and have next to no toys to play with, and oh! ever so many lessons to learn! No, I've made up my mind about it; if I'm Mabel, I'll stay down here! It'll be no use their putting their heads down and saying, 'Come up again, dear!' I shall only look up and say, 'Who am I then? Tell me that first, and then, if I like being that person, I'll come up: if not, I'll stay down here till I'm somebody else'—but, oh dear!" cried Alice, with a sudden burst of tears, "I do wish they would put their heads down! I am so very tired of being all alone here!"

sentences.text: "I'm sure those are not the right words," said poor Alice, and her eyes filled with tears again as she went on, "I must be Mabel after all, and I shall have to go and live in that poky little house, and have next to no toys to play with, and oh! ever so many lessons to learn!
sentences.zh: “我肯定这些词都不对，”可怜的爱丽丝说，眼里又涌出了泪水，她接着说，“我终究还是梅布尔，我得去住那间又小又破的房子，几乎没有玩具可玩，而且，哦！要学那么多功课！

sentences.text: No, I've made up my mind about it; if I'm Mabel, I'll stay down here!
sentences.zh: 不，我已经拿定主意了；如果我是梅布尔，我就待在这下面！

sentences.text: It'll be no use their putting their heads down and saying, 'Come up again, dear!' I shall only look up and say, 'Who am I then?
sentences.zh: 他们就是把头探下来喊‘上来吧，亲爱的！’也没用。我只会抬起头说：‘那我是谁？

sentences.text: Tell me that first, and then, if I like being that person, I'll come up: if not, I'll stay down here till I'm somebody else'—but, oh dear!" cried Alice, with a sudden burst of tears, "I do wish they would put their heads down!
sentences.zh: 先告诉我这个，然后，如果我愿意做那个人，我就上去；要是不愿意，我就待在这下面，直到我变成别人’——可是，哦天哪！”爱丽丝突然大哭起来，“我真希望他们能把头探下来！

sentences.text: I am so very tired of being all alone here!"
sentences.zh: 我一个人待在这儿，实在太累太累了！”

hints.zh: 又小又破的房子。
hints.en: A small, cramped house.

hints.zh: 几乎没有玩具；next to 在这里是“几乎”。
hints.en: 'Next to' here means 'almost': almost no toys at all.

hints.zh: 拿定主意、下了决心。
hints.en: Decided.

paragraphs.text: As she said this she looked down at her hands, and was surprised to see that she had put on one of the Rabbit's little white kid gloves while she was talking. "How can I have done that?" she thought. "I must be growing small again." She got up and went to the table to measure herself by it, and found that, as nearly as she could guess, she was now about two feet high, and was going on shrinking rapidly: she soon found out that the cause of this was the fan she was holding, and she dropped it hastily, just in time to save herself from shrinking away altogether.

sentences.text: As she said this she looked down at her hands, and was surprised to see that she had put on one of the Rabbit's little white kid gloves while she was talking.
sentences.zh: 说着，她低头看自己的手，惊讶地发现自己说话的时候竟戴上了白兔的一只白色小山羊皮手套。

sentences.text: "How can I have done that?" she thought.
sentences.zh: “我怎么会戴上的呢？”她想。

sentences.text: "I must be growing small again."
sentences.zh: “我一定是又变小了。”

sentences.text: She got up and went to the table to measure herself by it, and found that, as nearly as she could guess, she was now about two feet high, and was going on shrinking rapidly: she soon found out that the cause of this was the fan she was holding, and she dropped it hastily, just in time to save herself from shrinking away altogether.
sentences.zh: 她站起来，走到桌边拿桌子量自己，发现——照她估计——她现在大约两英尺高，而且还在飞快地缩小：她很快弄明白，原因就是她手里那把扇子；她赶紧把扇子扔掉，正好及时，没让自己缩得一点不剩。

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝认定自己已经变成了梅布尔，赌气说宁可待在下面，也不上去做别人。说着说着，她低头看自己的手，却发现手上戴着一只白兔的小手套——她是什么时候戴上的？她站起来，走到桌边想量量自己到底有多高。
introduction.en: Alice is now sure that she has turned into Mabel, and she refuses to go back up. Then she looks down and finds one of the Rabbit's gloves on her hand. She gets up and goes to the table to measure how tall she has become.

quiz.question: Why does Alice say she will stay down there?
options: She believes she is Mabel and does not want to be someone else.
She cannot reach the little door any more.
She likes the hall and wants to stay.

feedback.zh: 她认定自己成了梅布尔，宁可留在下面，等弄清自己到底是谁再说。
feedback.en: She is sure she is Mabel, so she would rather stay down there than be someone else.

quiz.question: What is making Alice shrink this time?
options: The fan she is holding.
The white kid gloves on her hands.
The table she is standing beside.

feedback.zh: 她发现缩小的原因是手里的扇子，赶紧把它扔掉，才没缩得一点不剩。
feedback.en: She works out that the fan is the cause and drops it just in time.

grammar.excerpt: she was now about two feet high, and was going on shrinking rapidly

focus.zh: was going on shrinking 是过去进行时：把缩小写成一个持续不停的过程。
focus.en: 'Was going on shrinking' is past continuous: it makes the shrinking a process that goes on and on.

paragraphs.text: "That was a narrow escape!" said Alice, a good deal frightened at the sudden change, but very glad to find herself still in existence; "and now for the garden!" and she ran with all speed back to the little door: but, alas! the little door was shut again, and the little golden key was lying on the glass table as before, "and things are worse than ever," thought the poor child, "for I never was so small as this before, never! And I declare it's too bad, that it is!"

sentences.text: "That was a narrow escape!" said Alice, a good deal frightened at the sudden change, but very glad to find herself still in existence; "and now for the garden!" and she ran with all speed back to the little door: but, alas! the little door was shut again, and the little golden key was lying on the glass table as before, "and things are worse than ever," thought the poor child, "for I never was so small as this before, never!
sentences.zh: “好险哪！”爱丽丝说，她被这突然的变化吓得不轻，但发现自己还活着，又很高兴；“现在去花园！”她用最快的速度跑回那扇小门：可是，唉！小门又关上了，那把小小的金钥匙还像先前一样躺在玻璃桌上，“事情比什么时候都糟，”这可怜的孩子想，“因为我从来没有这么小过，从来没有！

sentences.text: And I declare it's too bad, that it is!"
sentences.zh: 我敢说这太不像话了，真是太不像话了！”

hints.zh: 死里逃生、好险。
hints.en: A very close call.

paragraphs.text: As she said these words her foot slipped, and in another moment, splash! she was up to her chin in salt water. Her first idea was that she had somehow fallen into the sea, "and in that case I can go back by railway," she said to herself. (Alice had been to the seaside once in her life, and had come to the general conclusion, that wherever you go to on the English coast you find a number of bathing machines in the sea, some children digging in the sand with wooden spades, then a row of lodging houses, and behind them a railway station.) However, she soon made out that she was in the pool of tears which she had wept when she was nine feet high.

sentences.text: As she said these words her foot slipped, and in another moment, splash! she was up to her chin in salt water.
sentences.zh: 她话音未落，脚下一滑，转眼间，哗啦一声，水已经没到她的下巴。

sentences.text: Her first idea was that she had somehow fallen into the sea, "and in that case I can go back by railway," she said to herself. (Alice had been to the seaside once in her life, and had come to the general conclusion, that wherever you go to on the English coast you find a number of bathing machines in the sea, some children digging in the sand with wooden spades, then a row of lodging houses, and behind them a railway station.) However, she soon made out that she was in the pool of tears which she had wept when she was nine feet high.
sentences.zh: 她起初以为自己不知怎么掉进了大海，“那样的话，我还能坐火车回去，”她自言自语。（爱丽丝这辈子只去过一次海边，得出的结论是：不管你去英国海岸的哪个地方，总能看到海里停着一排更衣车，几个孩子拿着木铲在沙滩上挖沙，接着是一排出租公寓，公寓后面就是火车站。）不过她很快就弄明白，自己是在眼泪池里——就是她长到九英尺高时哭出来的那个池子。

hints.zh: 海滨更衣车，19 世纪的人下海前在里面换上泳衣的木车。
hints.en: Wheeled wooden cabins on the beach where people changed into bathing clothes.

hints.zh: 按周出租房间的家庭旅店，度假的人住在这里。
hints.en: Houses that let rooms to holiday visitors.

hints.zh: 弄清楚、辨认出来。
hints.en: Worked out, realised.

paragraphs.text: "I wish I hadn't cried so much!" said Alice, as she swam about, trying to find her way out. "I shall be punished for it now, I suppose, by being drowned in my own tears! That will be a queer thing, to be sure! However, everything is queer to-day."

sentences.text: "I wish I hadn't cried so much!" said Alice, as she swam about, trying to find her way out.
sentences.zh: “我真希望自己没哭那么多！”爱丽丝一边游着，一边想找条出路。

sentences.text: "I shall be punished for it now, I suppose, by being drowned in my own tears!
sentences.zh: “我想，现在我要遭报应了，会被自己的眼泪淹死！

sentences.text: That will be a queer thing, to be sure!
sentences.zh: 那可真是一件怪事，肯定的！

sentences.text: However, everything is queer to-day."
sentences.zh: 不过，今天什么事都怪。”

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝变得比任何时候都小，小门却又关上了，金钥匙还躺在玻璃桌上。她泄气地埋怨自己运气太坏。就在这时，她发觉脚下的水有些不对劲——她好像正在一片水里游动。
introduction.en: Alice is smaller than ever, but the little door is shut again and the golden key is back on the glass table. She complains about her bad luck. Then she notices that the ground under her is not ground at all: she is swimming.

quiz.question: Why can't Alice get into the garden now?
options: The garden has vanished.
The door is shut and the key is back on the table.
The door has grown too large for her.

feedback.zh: 她跑回小门，门又关上了，金钥匙仍旧躺在玻璃桌上。
feedback.en: She runs back, but the door is shut again and the golden key is lying on the glass table.

quiz.question: What does Alice realise about the water she is in?
options: It is rain that came through the roof.
It is the pool of tears she cried when she was huge.
It is the sea near a railway station.

feedback.zh: 她终于明白，自己正泡在九英尺高时哭出来的那片眼泪池里。
feedback.en: She makes out that she is in the pool of tears she wept when she was nine feet high.

grammar.excerpt: the pool of tears which she had wept when she was nine feet high

focus.zh: had wept 是过去完成时：哭发生在她“明白过来”之前，是更早的事。
focus.en: 'Had wept' is past perfect: the crying happened before she understood where she was.

paragraphs.text: Just then she heard something splashing about in the pool a little way off, and she swam nearer to make out what it was: at first she thought it must be a walrus or hippopotamus, but then she remembered how small she was now, and she soon made out that it was only a mouse that had slipped in like herself.

sentences.text: Just then she heard something splashing about in the pool a little way off, and she swam nearer to make out what it was: at first she thought it must be a walrus or hippopotamus, but then she remembered how small she was now, and she soon made out that it was only a mouse that had slipped in like herself.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，她听见不远处的水里有东西在扑腾，就游近去弄清那是什么：起初她以为准是海象或河马，但随后想起自己现在有多小，很快就看清那不过是一只老鼠，像她一样滑进了水里。

hints.zh: 老鼠，掉进眼泪池的小动物。
hints.en: The Mouse, an animal that has slipped into the pool.

hints.zh: 海象，一种长着长牙的大海兽。
hints.en: A walrus, a large sea animal with tusks.

paragraphs.text: "Would it be of any use, now," thought Alice, "to speak to this mouse? Everything is so out-of-the-way down here, that I should think very likely it can talk: at any rate, there's no harm in trying." So she began: "O Mouse, do you know the way out of this pool? I am very tired of swimming about here, O Mouse!" (Alice thought this must be the right way of speaking to a mouse: she had never done such a thing before, but she remembered having seen in her brother's Latin Grammar, "A mouse—of a mouse—to a mouse—A mouse—O mouse!") The Mouse looked at her rather inquisitively, and seemed to her to wink with one of its little eyes, but it said nothing.

sentences.text: "Would it be of any use, now," thought Alice, "to speak to this mouse?
sentences.zh: “现在，”爱丽丝想，“跟这只老鼠说说话，会有用吗？

sentences.text: Everything is so out-of-the-way down here, that I should think very likely it can talk: at any rate, there's no harm in trying."
sentences.zh: 这下面什么都古怪得出格，我想它很可能会说话：无论如何，试一试也没坏处。”

sentences.text: So she began: "O Mouse, do you know the way out of this pool?
sentences.zh: 于是她开口了：“哦，老鼠，你知道怎么出这个水池吗？

sentences.text: I am very tired of swimming about here, O Mouse!" (Alice thought this must be the right way of speaking to a mouse: she had never done such a thing before, but she remembered having seen in her brother's Latin Grammar, "A mouse—of a mouse—to a mouse—A mouse—O mouse!") The Mouse looked at her rather inquisitively, and seemed to her to wink with one of its little eyes, but it said nothing.
sentences.zh: 我在这儿游来游去，实在累坏了，哦，老鼠！”（爱丽丝觉得，跟老鼠说话一定得用这种方式：她以前从没干过这种事，但她记得在哥哥的拉丁语法书里见过，“一只老鼠——一只老鼠的——给一只老鼠——一只老鼠——哦，老鼠！”）老鼠相当好奇地看了看她，她觉得它的一只小眼睛好像朝她眨了眨，可它什么也没说。

hints.zh: 古怪、不合常理。
hints.en: Strange and unconventional.

hints.zh: 带着探究、好奇地打量。
hints.en: In a questioning, curious way.

hints.zh: 拉丁语语法课本，当时的学生要学拉丁语，书里会列出名词的各种格。
hints.en: The Latin grammar book used at school, which lists the cases of nouns.

introduction.zh: 不远处有什么东西在水里扑腾。爱丽丝游近去看，起初以为那是海象或河马，随即想起自己现在有多小——那不过是一只老鼠。她决定跟它说说话，还用上了从哥哥的拉丁语法书里学来的最客气的称呼。
introduction.en: Something is splashing in the pool a little way off. Alice swims closer, certain at first that it is a walrus or a hippopotamus, then remembering how small she is. It is only a mouse. She decides to speak to it in the politest way she knows.

quiz.question: What does Alice first take the splashing creature to be?
options: A bird from the garden.
A mouse like herself.
A walrus or a hippopotamus.

feedback.zh: 她一开始以为水里的东西是海象或河马，后来才看清那是一只老鼠。
feedback.en: At first she thinks it must be a walrus or a hippopotamus; only then does she see it is a mouse.

quiz.question: How does the Mouse answer Alice's question?
options: It answers in Latin.
It says nothing at all.
It tells her the way out.

feedback.zh: 老鼠只是好奇地看看她，好像朝她眨了眨眼，却一句话也没说。
feedback.en: It looks at her inquisitively and seems to wink, but says nothing.

grammar.excerpt: Alice thought this must be the right way of speaking to a mouse

focus.zh: must be 这里不表示“必须”，而是推断：想必这就是对的说话方式。
focus.en: 'Must be' here is not obligation but a strong guess: surely this is the right way to speak.

paragraphs.text: "Perhaps it doesn't understand English," thought Alice; "I daresay it's a French mouse, come over with William the Conqueror." (For, with all her knowledge of history, Alice had no very clear notion how long ago anything had happened.) So she began again: "Où est ma chatte?" which was the first sentence in her French lesson-book. The Mouse gave a sudden leap out of the water, and seemed to quiver all over with fright. "Oh, I beg your pardon!" cried Alice hastily, afraid that she had hurt the poor animal's feelings. "I quite forgot you didn't like cats."

sentences.text: "Perhaps it doesn't understand English," thought Alice; "I daresay it's a French mouse, come over with William the Conqueror." (For, with all her knowledge of history, Alice had no very clear notion how long ago anything had happened.) So she began again: "Où est ma chatte?" which was the first sentence in her French lesson-book.
sentences.zh: “也许它不懂英语，”爱丽丝想，“我敢说它是一只法国老鼠，是跟着征服者威廉过来的。”（因为，尽管爱丽丝历史知识不少，她对任何事情发生在多久以前却没有很清楚的概念。）于是她又开口：“Où est ma chatte?”这是她法语课本上的第一句。

sentences.text: The Mouse gave a sudden leap out of the water, and seemed to quiver all over with fright.
sentences.zh: 老鼠猛地从水里跳起来，好像吓得全身都在发抖。

sentences.text: "Oh, I beg your pardon!" cried Alice hastily, afraid that she had hurt the poor animal's feelings.
sentences.zh: “哦，我请你原谅！”爱丽丝急忙喊道，怕自己伤了这可怜动物的感情。

sentences.text: "I quite forgot you didn't like cats."
sentences.zh: “我完全忘了你不喜欢猫。”

hints.zh: 征服者威廉，1066 年从法国诺曼底征服英格兰的国王。
hints.en: William of Normandy, who conquered England in 1066.

hints.zh: 法语：“我的猫在哪儿？”
hints.en: French for 'Where is my cat?'

hints.zh: 我想、大概是（旧时的说法）。
hints.en: I suppose, most likely (an old-fashioned phrase).

paragraphs.text: "Not like cats!" cried the Mouse, in a shrill, passionate voice. "Would you like cats if you were me?"

sentences.text: "Not like cats!" cried the Mouse, in a shrill, passionate voice.
sentences.zh: “不喜欢猫！”老鼠用尖利、激动的声音喊道。

sentences.text: "Would you like cats if you were me?"
sentences.zh: “你要是我的话，你会喜欢猫吗？”

hints.zh: 本句指“激动的、气冲冲的”，不是“热情的”。
hints.en: Here it means 'flushed with strong feeling', not 'loving'.

paragraphs.text: "Well, perhaps not," said Alice in a soothing tone: "don't be angry about it. And yet I wish I could show you our cat Dinah: I think you'd take a fancy to cats if you could only see her. She is such a dear quiet thing," Alice went on, half to herself, as she swam lazily about in the pool, "and she sits purring so nicely by the fire, licking her paws and washing her face—and she is such a nice soft thing to nurse—and she's such a capital one for catching mice——oh, I beg your pardon!" cried Alice again, for this time the Mouse was bristling all over, and she felt certain it must be really offended. "We won't talk about her any more if you'd rather not." "We, indeed!" cried the Mouse, who was trembling down to the end of his tail. "As if I would talk on such a subject! Our family always hated cats: nasty, low, vulgar things! Don't let me hear the name again!"

sentences.text: "Well, perhaps not," said Alice in a soothing tone: "don't be angry about it.
sentences.zh: “也许不会吧，”爱丽丝用安抚的口气说，“别为这个生气。

sentences.text: And yet I wish I could show you our cat Dinah: I think you'd take a fancy to cats if you could only see her.
sentences.zh: 不过我真希望你能见见我们的猫黛娜：你要是能看见她，我想你也会喜欢猫的。

sentences.text: She is such a dear quiet thing," Alice went on, half to herself, as she swam lazily about in the pool, "and she sits purring so nicely by the fire, licking her paws and washing her face—and she is such a nice soft thing to nurse—and she's such a capital one for catching mice——oh, I beg your pardon!" cried Alice again, for this time the Mouse was bristling all over, and she felt certain it must be really offended.
sentences.zh: 她是个多么可爱、安静的小东西，”爱丽丝半是自言自语地继续说，一边懒洋洋地在池子里游着，“她坐在炉火边，呼噜呼噜叫得那么好听，舔舔爪子，洗洗脸——抱起来又软又舒服——她抓老鼠可真是一把好手——哦，对不起！”爱丽丝又叫了起来，因为这回老鼠浑身的毛都竖了起来，她确信它一定真的生气了。

sentences.text: "We won't talk about her any more if you'd rather not."
sentences.zh: “你要是嫌烦，我们就别再提她了。”

sentences.text: "We, indeed!" cried the Mouse, who was trembling down to the end of his tail.
sentences.zh: “我们，真是的！”老鼠喊道，它连尾巴尖都在发抖。

sentences.text: "As if I would talk on such a subject!
sentences.zh: “好像我会谈这种话题似的！

sentences.text: Our family always hated cats: nasty, low, vulgar things!
sentences.zh: 我们家一向恨猫：那些下流、卑劣、粗俗的东西！

sentences.text: Don't let me hear the name again!"
sentences.zh: 别让我再听见那个名字！”

hints.zh: 粗俗的、没教养的。
hints.en: Rude and low-class.

hints.zh: 黛娜，爱丽丝养的猫。
hints.en: Dinah, Alice’s cat.

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝断定这只老鼠听不懂英语，说不定是跟着征服者威廉从法国来的，于是用课堂上学的第一句法语向它搭话。她万万没想到，这一句话会让对方一下子跳起来。那句法语到底说了什么？
introduction.en: Alice decides the Mouse cannot understand English, and may have come over from France with William the Conqueror. She tries the first sentence of her French lesson-book on it, and the mouse leaps straight out of the water. What did she say?

quiz.question: Why does Alice try French on the Mouse?
options: She is practising for her French lesson.
She has forgotten the English word for 'mouse'.
She thinks it may be a French mouse.

feedback.zh: 她觉得老鼠也许听不懂英语，说不定是跟着征服者威廉从法国来的。
feedback.en: She guesses it may not understand English, and that it could be a French mouse.

quiz.question: What makes the Mouse furious?
options: Alice mentions cats, which its family hates.
Alice splashed water in its face.
Alice laughed at its long tail.

feedback.zh: 老鼠说它全家一向恨猫，骂它们是下流、卑劣、粗俗的东西。
feedback.en: The Mouse says its family has always hated cats: nasty, low, vulgar things.

grammar.excerpt: Would you like cats if you were me?

focus.zh: if you were me 用 were，是与现在事实相反的假设；主句的 would like 与之呼应。
focus.en: 'If you were me' is an unreal condition about the present, and the main clause takes 'would'.

paragraphs.text: "I won't indeed!" said Alice, in a great hurry to change the subject of conversation. "Are you—are you fond—of—of dogs?" The Mouse did not answer, so Alice went on eagerly: "There is such a nice little dog near our house I should like to show you! A little bright-eyed terrier, you know, with oh! such long curly brown hair! And it'll fetch things when you throw them, and it'll sit up and beg for its dinner, and all sorts of things—I can't remember half of them—and it belongs to a farmer, you know, and he says it's so useful, it's worth a hundred pounds! He says it kills all the rats and—oh dear!" cried Alice in a sorrowful tone. "I'm afraid I've offended it again!" For the Mouse was swimming away from her as hard as it could go, and making quite a commotion in the pool as it went.

sentences.text: "I won't indeed!" said Alice, in a great hurry to change the subject of conversation.
sentences.zh: “我保证不提了！”爱丽丝说，急着换个话题。

sentences.text: "Are you—are you fond—of—of dogs?"
sentences.zh: “你——你喜欢——喜——喜欢狗吗？”

sentences.text: The Mouse did not answer, so Alice went on eagerly: "There is such a nice little dog near our house I should like to show you!
sentences.zh: 老鼠没有回答，于是爱丽丝热切地继续说：“我们家附近有一只很好的小狗，我真想让你看看！

sentences.text: A little bright-eyed terrier, you know, with oh! such long curly brown hair!
sentences.zh: 一只眼睛亮亮的小梗犬，你知道，毛是棕色卷的，哦！那么长！

sentences.text: And it'll fetch things when you throw them, and it'll sit up and beg for its dinner, and all sorts of things—I can't remember half of them—and it belongs to a farmer, you know, and he says it's so useful, it's worth a hundred pounds!
sentences.zh: 你把东西扔出去，它就会叼回来；它还会坐起来讨晚饭吃，还会好些别的——我连一半都记不住——它属于一个农夫，你知道，他说它很有用，值一百英镑！

sentences.text: He says it kills all the rats and—oh dear!" cried Alice in a sorrowful tone.
sentences.zh: 他说它把所有的老鼠都咬死，还有——哦天哪！”爱丽丝伤心地说。

sentences.text: "I'm afraid I've offended it again!"
sentences.zh: “我怕我又得罪它了！”

sentences.text: For the Mouse was swimming away from her as hard as it could go, and making quite a commotion in the pool as it went.
sentences.zh: 因为老鼠正拼命从她身边游开，游的时候在水池里搅起好大一片动静。

hints.zh: 梗犬，一种体型不大、爱追爱刨的小狗。
hints.en: A terrier, a small lively dog.

hints.zh: 值一百英镑；在当时这是一大笔钱。
hints.en: Worth a hundred pounds, a large sum in those days.

hints.target: as hard as it could go
hints.zh: 拼命地、尽力地。
hints.en: As fast as it possibly could.

paragraphs.text: So she called softly after it: "Mouse dear! Do come back again, and we won't talk about cats or dogs either, if you don't like them! " When the Mouse heard this, it turned round and swam slowly back to her: its face was quite pale (with passion, Alice thought), and it said in a low, trembling voice, "Let us get to the shore, and then I'll tell you my history, and you'll understand why it is I hate cats and dogs."

sentences.text: So she called softly after it: "Mouse dear!
sentences.zh: 于是她跟在后面轻声唤道：“亲爱的老鼠！

sentences.text: Do come back again, and we won't talk about cats or dogs either, if you don't like them! " When the Mouse heard this, it turned round and swam slowly back to her: its face was quite pale (with passion, Alice thought), and it said in a low, trembling voice, "Let us get to the shore, and then I'll tell you my history, and you'll understand why it is I hate cats and dogs."
sentences.zh: 回来吧，你要是不喜欢，我们就不谈猫，也不谈狗了！”老鼠听见这话，转过身来，慢慢游回她身边：它的脸很苍白（爱丽丝想，是气成这样的），它用低沉、发抖的声音说：“我们上岸吧，然后我把我的经历讲给你听，你就会明白我为什么恨猫和狗。”

hints.zh: “亲爱的老鼠”的倒装说法，把称呼放在后面。
hints.en: An inverted 'dear Mouse', with the endearment at the end.

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝赶紧换了个话题，讲起家附近一只可爱的小狗：它会叼东西，会坐着讨晚饭，还特别会抓老鼠。她越讲越起劲。老鼠会怎么想这只狗呢？
introduction.en: Alice hurries on to a safer subject: a charming little terrier near her house that fetches things, begs for its dinner and is very useful about rats. She talks with growing enthusiasm. How will the Mouse take this?

quiz.question: Why does Alice start talking about dogs?
options: The Mouse asks her about her pets.
She wants to change the subject after upsetting the Mouse.
She wants to show that dogs are useful animals.

feedback.zh: 她刚惹恼了老鼠，急忙换个话题，就问起狗来。
feedback.en: She is in a great hurry to change the subject after offending the Mouse.

quiz.question: What makes the Mouse swim away from her?
options: The mention of a dog that kills rats.
Alice's soft, gentle voice.
A loud noise from the shore.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝说到那狗“把所有的老鼠都咬死”，老鼠听了立刻拼命游开。
feedback.en: She describes a dog that kills all the rats, and the Mouse swims away as hard as it can.

grammar.excerpt: There is such a nice little dog near our house

focus.zh: such 放在 a 前面：such a + 形容词 + 单数名词，强调“这么……的一只”。
focus.en: 'Such' comes before 'a': such a + adjective + singular noun, stressing what kind of dog it is.

paragraphs.text: It was high time to go, for the pool was getting quite crowded with the birds and animals that had fallen into it: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet, and several other curious creatures. Alice led the way, and the whole party swam to the shore.

sentences.text: It was high time to go, for the pool was getting quite crowded with the birds and animals that had fallen into it: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet, and several other curious creatures.
sentences.zh: 该走了，因为池子里渐渐挤满了掉进来的鸟和动物：有一只鸭子、一只渡渡鸟、一只鹦鹉、一只小鹰，还有好几个古怪的家伙。

sentences.text: Alice led the way, and the whole party swam to the shore.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝带头，大伙儿一起游向岸边。

hints.zh: 早该……的时候，再不行动就太迟了。
hints.en: More than time; almost too late.

hints.zh: 渡渡鸟，一种不会飞的大鸟。
hints.en: The Dodo, a large flightless bird.

hints.zh: 鹦鹉，一种羽色鲜艳的鸟。
hints.en: The Lory, a brightly coloured parrot.

hints.zh: 小鹰、雏鹰。
hints.en: The Eaglet, a young eagle.

introduction.zh: 眼泪池里渐渐挤满了掉进来的鸟和动物：一只鸭子、一只渡渡鸟、一只鹦鹉、一只小鹰，还有好几个古怪的家伙。它们个个浑身湿透，挤在爱丽丝身边。这么多湿淋淋的鸟兽，该怎么把自己弄干呢？
introduction.en: The pool of tears is filling with the birds and animals that have fallen in: a Duck, a Dodo, a Lory, an Eaglet and several other curious creatures. Soaked and crowded together, they have no idea what to do next. How does a wet bird get dry?

quiz.question: Why is the pool getting crowded?
options: The water is rising quickly.
Birds and animals have fallen into it.
Alice has called her friends to join her.

feedback.zh: 池子里挤满了掉进来的鸟和动物，鸭子、渡渡鸟、鹦鹉、小鹰都在其中。
feedback.en: The pool fills with birds and animals that have fallen in, among them a Duck, a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet.

quiz.question: What does Alice do when it is time to go?
options: She swims off on her own.
She leads the whole party to the shore.
She waits for the Dodo to go first.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝带头游，大伙儿跟着她一起往岸边去。
feedback.en: Alice leads the way, and the whole party swims to the shore.

grammar.excerpt: It was high time to go

focus.zh: it 是形式主语，真正的内容是 to go；high time 意思是“早该走了”。
focus.en: 'It' is a placeholder subject, the real content is 'to go', and 'high time' means 'already time'.

title.zh: 一场会议式赛跑和一段长故事
title.en: A Caucus-Race and a Long Tale

paragraphs.text: They were indeed a queer-looking party that assembled on the bank—the birds with draggled feathers, the animals with their fur clinging close to them, and all dripping wet, cross, and uncomfortable.

sentences.text: They were indeed a queer-looking party that assembled on the bank—the birds with draggled feathers, the animals with their fur clinging close to them, and all dripping wet, cross, and uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 聚在岸上的这一群，样子确实古怪——鸟的羽毛湿透了，黏成一绺一绺；兽的毛紧紧贴在身上；大家浑身滴水，又恼火又难受。

hints.zh: 生气的、恼火的（不是“穿过”）。
hints.en: Angry and annoyed here, not the verb 'to go across'.

paragraphs.text: The first question of course was, how to get dry again: they had a consultation about this, and after a few minutes it seemed quite natural to Alice to find herself talking familiarly with them, as if she had known them all her life. Indeed, she had quite a long argument with the Lory, who at last turned sulky, and would only say, "I am older than you, and must know better;" and this Alice would not allow, without knowing how old it was, and as the Lory positively refused to tell its age, there was no more to be said.

sentences.text: The first question of course was, how to get dry again: they had a consultation about this, and after a few minutes it seemed quite natural to Alice to find herself talking familiarly with them, as if she had known them all her life.
sentences.zh: 首先要解决的当然是怎么把身上弄干：大家商量了一阵，几分钟之后，爱丽丝发现自己已经跟他们熟络地聊起来，好像跟他们认识了一辈子似的，她也不觉得奇怪了。

sentences.text: Indeed, she had quite a long argument with the Lory, who at last turned sulky, and would only say, "I am older than you, and must know better;" and this Alice would not allow, without knowing how old it was, and as the Lory positively refused to tell its age, there was no more to be said.
sentences.zh: 她还真跟鹦鹉争了好一阵。鹦鹉最后赌起气来，只说：“我比你大，肯定比你懂。”爱丽丝不认这话——她连它多大都不知道；而鹦鹉死活不肯说自己的年纪，也就没什么好争的了。

hints.zh: 爱丽丝，本书主人公，追着白兔掉进兔子洞的女孩。
hints.en: Alice, the girl who followed the White Rabbit down its hole.

hints.zh: 鹦鹉，池中的一只鸟。
hints.en: The Lory, a small parrot and one of the birds from the pool.

paragraphs.text: At last the Mouse, who seemed to be a person of some authority among them, called out, "Sit down, all of you, and listen to me! I'll soon make you dry enough!" They all sat down at once, in a large ring, with the Mouse in the middle. Alice kept her eyes anxiously fixed on it, for she felt sure she would catch a bad cold if she did not get dry very soon.

sentences.text: At last the Mouse, who seemed to be a person of some authority among them, called out, "Sit down, all of you, and listen to me!
sentences.zh: 最后，那只老鼠——它在这群动物里似乎颇有威信——喊道：“都坐下，听我说！

sentences.text: I'll soon make you dry enough!"
sentences.zh: 我很快就能让你们干得透透的！”

sentences.text: They all sat down at once, in a large ring, with the Mouse in the middle.
sentences.zh: 大家立刻坐了下来，围成一个大圆圈，老鼠坐在中间。

sentences.text: Alice kept her eyes anxiously fixed on it, for she felt sure she would catch a bad cold if she did not get dry very soon.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝焦急地盯着它看，因为她确信，要是不能赶快弄干，自己一定会得重感冒。

hints.zh: 老鼠，眼泪池里的老鼠，眼下出来主持局面。
hints.en: The Mouse from the pool, who now takes charge of the party.

paragraphs.text: "Ahem!" said the Mouse with an important air, "are you all ready? This is the driest thing I know. Silence all round, if you please! 'William the Conqueror, whose cause was favoured by the pope, was soon submitted to by the English, who wanted leaders, and had been of late much accustomed to usurpation and conquest. Edwin and Morcar, the earls of Mercia and Northumbria—'"

sentences.text: "Ahem!" said the Mouse with an important air, "are you all ready?
sentences.zh: “咳！”老鼠摆出一副郑重其事的架势，“都准备好了吗？

sentences.text: This is the driest thing I know.
sentences.zh: 这是我所知道的最“干”的东西。”

sentences.text: Silence all round, if you please! 'William the Conqueror, whose cause was favoured by the pope, was soon submitted to by the English, who wanted leaders, and had been of late much accustomed to usurpation and conquest.
sentences.zh: 请大家安静！‘征服者威廉的事业得到教皇的支持，英国人很快就向他屈服了；他们需要首领，而且近来早已习惯了篡位与征服。

sentences.text: Edwin and Morcar, the earls of Mercia and Northumbria—'"
sentences.zh: 埃德温与莫卡，也就是麦西亚和诺森布里亚的两位伯爵——’”

hints.zh: 最“干”的；dry 在这里一语双关，既指“干燥”，也指“枯燥”。
hints.en: Driest is a pun: it means both 'most free of water' and 'most boring'.

hints.zh: 征服者威廉，1066 年率诺曼人征服英格兰的国王。
hints.en: William the Conqueror, the Norman king who conquered England in 1066.

paragraphs.text: "Ugh!" said the Lory, with a shiver.

sentences.text: "Ugh!" said the Lory, with a shiver.
sentences.zh: “呃！”鹦鹉打了个哆嗦说道。

introduction.zh: 从眼泪池里爬上岸的是一群古怪的旅客：鸟的羽毛湿透，兽的毛贴在身上。大家最想解决的事只有一件——怎么把身上弄干。这时，老鼠站出来，说自己知道最“干”的办法。
introduction.en: A strange, soaked company has climbed out of the pool: birds with draggled feathers, animals with wet fur clinging to them. Everyone wants one thing — to be dry. Then the Mouse stands up and offers the driest thing it knows.

quiz.question: What was the first problem the party had to solve?
options: How to get dry again.
Where to find something to eat.
Who should lead them home.

feedback.zh: 第 2 句说，最先要解决的自然是怎么再弄干身子，于是大家先商量这件事。
