feedback.en: Sentence 2 says their first question was how to get dry again, so they held a consultation about it.

quiz.question: How did the Lory behave when Alice argued with it?
options: It turned sulky and refused to give its age.
It asked the other birds to argue for it.
It told Alice exactly how old it was.

feedback.zh: 第 3 句写鹦鹉绷起了脸，只肯说“我比你大”，而且死活不肯说自己的年纪。
feedback.en: In sentence 3 the Lory turns sulky and positively refuses to tell its age.

grammar.excerpt: the Lory, who at last turned sulky, and would only say

focus.zh: who 前的逗号说明这是非限制性从句，只补充鹦鹉的情况，不限定是哪一只。
focus.en: The comma before who marks a non-defining relative clause: it adds information about the Lory instead of identifying it.

paragraphs.text: "I beg your pardon!" said the Mouse, frowning, but very politely: "Did you speak?"

sentences.text: "I beg your pardon!" said the Mouse, frowning, but very politely: "Did you speak?"
sentences.zh: “请再说一遍！”老鼠皱着眉，却非常有礼貌地说，“是你说话了吗？”

paragraphs.text: "Not I!" said the Lory hastily.

sentences.text: "Not I!" said the Lory hastily.
sentences.zh: “不是我！”鹦鹉急忙说。

paragraphs.text: "I thought you did," said the Mouse.—"I proceed. 'Edwin and Morcar, the earls of Mercia and Northumbria, declared for him; and even Stigand, the patriotic archbishop of Canterbury, found it advisable—'"

sentences.text: "I thought you did," said the Mouse.—"I proceed. 'Edwin and Morcar, the earls of Mercia and Northumbria, declared for him; and even Stigand, the patriotic archbishop of Canterbury, found it advisable—'"
sentences.zh: “我还以为是你呢，”老鼠说。“我接着讲。‘埃德温与莫卡，麦西亚和诺森布里亚的两位伯爵，宣布拥戴他；就连斯蒂甘德，那位爱国的坎特伯雷大主教，也觉得这样做是明智的——’”

hints.zh: 坎特伯雷大主教，英格兰教会里地位最高的神职人员。
hints.en: The Archbishop of Canterbury, the most senior bishop of the English Church.

paragraphs.text: "Found what?" said the Duck.

sentences.text: "Found what?" said the Duck.
sentences.zh: “觉得什么明智？”鸭子问。

paragraphs.text: "Found it," the Mouse replied rather crossly: "of course you know what 'it' means."

sentences.text: "Found it," the Mouse replied rather crossly: "of course you know what 'it' means."
sentences.zh: “觉得它明智，”老鼠有点恼火地回答，“你当然知道‘它’指的是什么。”

paragraphs.text: "I know what 'it' means well enough, when I find a thing," said the Duck: "it's generally a frog or a worm. The question is, what did the archbishop find?"

sentences.text: "I know what 'it' means well enough, when I find a thing," said the Duck: "it's generally a frog or a worm.
sentences.zh: “我找到一样东西的时候，当然知道‘它’是什么意思，”鸭子说，“通常不是青蛙就是虫子。

sentences.text: The question is, what did the archbishop find?"
sentences.zh: 问题是，大主教到底找到了什么？”

paragraphs.text: The Mouse did not notice this question, but hurriedly went on, "'—found it advisable to go with Edgar Atheling to meet William and offer him the crown. William's conduct at first was moderate. But the insolence of his Normans—' How are you getting on now, my dear?" it continued, turning to Alice as it spoke.

sentences.text: The Mouse did not notice this question, but hurriedly went on, "'—found it advisable to go with Edgar Atheling to meet William and offer him the crown.
sentences.zh: 老鼠没有理会这个问题，只顾匆匆往下念：“‘——觉得最好和埃德加·阿瑟林一起去见威廉，把王冠献给他。

sentences.text: William's conduct at first was moderate.
sentences.zh: 威廉起初的举动还算温和。

sentences.text: But the insolence of his Normans—' How are you getting on now, my dear?" it continued, turning to Alice as it spoke.
sentences.zh: 可是他的诺曼人傲慢无礼——’ 你现在觉得怎么样，亲爱的？”它说着转向爱丽丝，接着问道。

paragraphs.text: "As wet as ever," said Alice in a melancholy tone: "it doesn't seem to dry me at all."

sentences.text: "As wet as ever," said Alice in a melancholy tone: "it doesn't seem to dry me at all."
sentences.zh: “还是跟原来一样湿，”爱丽丝愁闷地说，“看样子它一点也没把我弄干。”

paragraphs.text: "In that case," said the Dodo solemnly, rising to its feet, "I move that the meeting adjourn, for the immediate adoption of more energetic remedies—"

sentences.text: "In that case," said the Dodo solemnly, rising to its feet, "I move that the meeting adjourn, for the immediate adoption of more energetic remedies—"
sentences.zh: “既然这样，”渡渡鸟郑重地站起来说，“我提议会议休会，立刻采取更有力的补救办法——”

hints.zh: 渡渡鸟，会上出面提议办法的鸟。
hints.en: The Dodo, the bird who comes up with a plan for the party.

hints.zh: 休会、暂停（正式的会议用语）。
hints.en: To break off a meeting for a time; a formal, official word.

paragraphs.text: "Speak English!" said the Eaglet. "I don't know the meaning of half those long words, and, what's more, I don't believe you do either!" And the Eaglet bent down its head to hide a smile: some of the other birds tittered audibly.

sentences.text: "Speak English!" said the Eaglet.
sentences.zh: “说人话！”小鹰说。

sentences.text: "I don't know the meaning of half those long words, and, what's more, I don't believe you do either!"
sentences.zh: “那些大词一半我都不知道是什么意思，而且，我看你自己也未必知道！”

sentences.text: And the Eaglet bent down its head to hide a smile: some of the other birds tittered audibly.
sentences.zh: 小鹰低下头去，掩住笑意；另外几只鸟也忍不住笑出了声。

hints.zh: 小鹰，池中的一只鸟，说话直来直去。
hints.en: The Eaglet, a young eagle among the pool birds.

paragraphs.text: "What I was going to say," said the Dodo in an offended tone, "was, that the best thing to get us dry would be a Caucus-race."

sentences.text: "What I was going to say," said the Dodo in an offended tone, "was, that the best thing to get us dry would be a Caucus-race."
sentences.zh: “我刚才要说的是，”渡渡鸟带着受了冒犯的口气说，“要把我们弄干，最好的办法是举办一场会议式赛跑。”

hints.zh: “会议式赛跑”，卡罗尔自造的词，指一种没有固定规则的赛跑。
hints.en: Caucus-race: Carroll's invented name for a race with hardly any rules.

introduction.zh: 老鼠讲起一段英国历史，据说这是它知道的最“干”的东西。可历史里尽是些拗口的大词，鸭子盯住其中一个字穷追不舍，小鹰也越听越不耐烦。
introduction.en: The Mouse begins a piece of English history, which it says is the driest thing it knows. The history is full of long words; the Duck will not let one small word go, and the Eaglet is losing patience.

quiz.question: What did the Duck keep asking about?
options: Who William the Conqueror was.
What the archbishop found.
Why the Mouse was cross.

feedback.zh: 鸭子在第 7 句把问题说到底，追问的是大主教到底“找到了什么”。
feedback.en: In sentence 7 the Duck asks the question plainly: what did the archbishop find?

quiz.question: Why did the Eaglet tell the Dodo to speak English?
options: Because it did not understand the long words.
Because the Dodo was speaking too quietly.
Because it wanted to hear the story from the beginning.

feedback.zh: 第 14 句小鹰说自己不懂那些大词的一半，还怀疑渡渡鸟也不懂，所以要它“说人话”。
feedback.en: In sentence 14 the Eaglet says it does not know half those long words, and doubts the Dodo does either.

grammar.excerpt: I move that the meeting adjourn

focus.zh: move 表示“提议”时，that 从句用动词原形 adjourn，不加 -s，这是虚拟语气。
focus.en: After move meaning 'propose', the that-clause takes the bare verb adjourn, not adjourns: this is the subjunctive.

paragraphs.text: "What is a Caucus-race?" said Alice; not that she wanted much to know, but the Dodo had paused as if it thought that somebody ought to speak, and no one else seemed inclined to say anything.

sentences.text: "What is a Caucus-race?" said Alice; not that she wanted much to know, but the Dodo had paused as if it thought that somebody ought to speak, and no one else seemed inclined to say anything.
sentences.zh: “什么叫会议式赛跑？”爱丽丝问。她并不是真想知道，只是渡渡鸟停在那里，好像觉得总该有人开口，而别人似乎都不打算说话。

paragraphs.text: "Why," said the Dodo, "the best way to explain it is to do it." (And as you might like to try the thing yourself, some winter day, I will tell you how the Dodo managed it.)

sentences.text: "Why," said the Dodo, "the best way to explain it is to do it." (And as you might like to try the thing yourself, some winter day, I will tell you how the Dodo managed it.)
sentences.zh: “这个嘛，”渡渡鸟说，“最好的解释方式就是亲自做一遍。”（你也许想在某个冬日自己试试这件事，所以我来讲讲渡渡鸟是怎么安排的。）

paragraphs.text: First it marked out a race-course, in a sort of circle, ("the exact shape doesn't matter," it said,) and then all the party were placed along the course, here and there. There was no "One two, three, and away," but they began running when they liked, and left off when they liked, so that it was not easy to know when the race was over. However, when they had been running half an hour or so, and were quite dry again, the Dodo suddenly called out, "The race is over!" and they all crowded round it, panting, and asking, "But who has won?"

sentences.text: First it marked out a race-course, in a sort of circle, ("the exact shape doesn't matter," it said,) and then all the party were placed along the course, here and there.
sentences.zh: 它先划出一条跑道，大致是个圆圈（“形状不必太讲究，”它说），然后把大家沿着跑道东一个西一个地安排开。

sentences.text: There was no "One two, three, and away," but they began running when they liked, and left off when they liked, so that it was not easy to know when the race was over.
sentences.zh: 没有“一、二、三，跑！”这样的口令，谁想跑就跑，想停就停，因此很难知道比赛什么时候才算结束。

sentences.text: However, when they had been running half an hour or so, and were quite dry again, the Dodo suddenly called out, "The race is over!" and they all crowded round it, panting, and asking, "But who has won?"
sentences.zh: 不过，等他们跑了大约半个钟头，身上又干透了，渡渡鸟忽然喊道：“比赛结束！”大家喘着气围拢过来，问：“可是谁赢了呢？”

hints.zh: 划出、标出（范围或路线）。
hints.en: Marked out: drew the lines of a track or area.

hints.zh: 东一个西一个，散落在各处。
hints.en: Here and there: scattered about in different places.

hints.zh: “一、二、三，跑！”赛跑时喊的起跑口令。
hints.en: A starting call for a race, like 'one, two, three, go!'

hints.zh: 停下、中断（正在做的事）。
hints.en: Left off: stopped doing something.

paragraphs.text: This question the Dodo could not answer without a great deal of thought, and it sat for a long time with one finger pressed upon its forehead, (the position in which you usually see Shakespeare, in the pictures of him,) while the rest waited in silence. At last the Dodo said, "Everybody has won, and all must have prizes."

sentences.text: This question the Dodo could not answer without a great deal of thought, and it sat for a long time with one finger pressed upon its forehead, (the position in which you usually see Shakespeare, in the pictures of him,) while the rest waited in silence.
sentences.zh: 这个问题渡渡鸟非得好好想一想才能回答。它用手指按住额头，坐了很久（在莎士比亚的画像里，你常看到他摆这个姿势），其余的人都静静地等着。

sentences.text: At last the Dodo said, "Everybody has won, and all must have prizes."
sentences.zh: 最后渡渡鸟说：“每个人都赢了，所以大家都得有奖品。”

hints.zh: 莎士比亚；画像里的他常以手指抵额，一副沉思的模样。
hints.en: Shakespeare, often pictured with one finger pressed to his forehead.

paragraphs.text: "But who is to give the prizes? " quite a chorus of voices asked.

sentences.text: "But who is to give the prizes? " quite a chorus of voices asked.
sentences.zh: “那谁来发奖品呢？”好几个声音齐声问道。

paragraphs.text: "Why, she, of course," said the Dodo, pointing to Alice with one finger; and the whole party at once crowded round her, calling out in a confused way, "Prizes! Prizes!"

sentences.text: "Why, she, of course," said the Dodo, pointing to Alice with one finger; and the whole party at once crowded round her, calling out in a confused way, "Prizes!
sentences.zh: “当然是这位啦，”渡渡鸟用一根手指指着爱丽丝说。大家立刻围到她身边，七嘴八舌地喊：“奖品！

sentences.text: Prizes!"
sentences.zh: 奖品！”

introduction.zh: 渡渡鸟提议的比赛既没有跑道线，也没有起跑口令：谁想跑就跑，想停就停。那么，这场比赛该在什么时候结束，又该算谁赢呢？
introduction.en: The Dodo's race has no track and no starting signal: anyone may run when they like and stop when they like. So when is the race over, and who is going to be the winner?

quiz.question: How did the runners know when to start and stop?
options: The Dodo shouted a starting signal.
They ran until the circle was complete.
They started and stopped whenever they liked.

feedback.zh: 第 4 句说没有“一、二、三，跑”的口令：想跑就跑，想停就停。
feedback.en: Sentence 4 says there was no starting call: they began running when they liked and left off when they liked.

quiz.question: What did the Dodo say about the winner?
options: Nobody had won, so there were no prizes.
Everybody had won and all must have prizes.
The first runner to stop had won.

feedback.zh: 第 7 句渡渡鸟宣布人人都赢了，所以人人都该有奖。
feedback.en: In sentence 7 the Dodo declares that everybody has won, and all must have prizes.

grammar.excerpt: as if it thought that somebody ought to speak

focus.zh: as if 后接过去式 thought，表示与眼前事实有距离的“好像”，不是过去时间。
focus.en: After as if, the past form thought marks an unreal comparison, not past time: the Dodo does not really think so.

paragraphs.text: Alice had no idea what to do, and in despair she put her hand in her pocket, and pulled out a box of comfits, (luckily the salt water had not got into it,) and handed them round as prizes. There was exactly one a-piece, all round.

sentences.text: Alice had no idea what to do, and in despair she put her hand in her pocket, and pulled out a box of comfits, (luckily the salt water had not got into it,) and handed them round as prizes.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝不知道该怎么办，绝望之中把手伸进口袋，掏出一盒蜜饯糖（幸好海水没有渗进去），把它们当作奖品分发给大家。

sentences.text: There was exactly one a-piece, all round.
sentences.zh: 正好每人都分到一颗。

hints.zh: 糖衣果仁、蜜饯糖，旧时的一种糖果。
hints.en: Comfits: old-fashioned sweets made of nuts or seeds covered in sugar.

hints.zh: 每人一份、每个一颗。
hints.en: A-piece: one for each person.

paragraphs.text: "But she must have a prize herself, you know," said the Mouse.

sentences.text: "But she must have a prize herself, you know," said the Mouse.
sentences.zh: “可是她自己也得有一份奖品呀，”老鼠说。

paragraphs.text: "Of course," the Dodo replied very gravely. "What else have you got in your pocket?" he went on, turning to Alice.

sentences.text: "Of course," the Dodo replied very gravely.
sentences.zh: “当然，”渡渡鸟非常严肃地回答。

sentences.text: "What else have you got in your pocket?" he went on, turning to Alice.
sentences.zh: “你口袋里还有什么别的东西？”它转向爱丽丝，接着问。

paragraphs.text: "Only a thimble," said Alice sadly.

sentences.text: "Only a thimble," said Alice sadly.
sentences.zh: “只有一个顶针，”爱丽丝难过地说。

hints.zh: 顶针，缝纫时套在手指上的小金属套。
hints.en: A thimble, the small metal cap worn on a finger when sewing.

paragraphs.text: "Hand it over here," said the Dodo.

sentences.text: "Hand it over here," said the Dodo.
sentences.zh: “把它交到这里来，”渡渡鸟说。

paragraphs.text: Then they all crowded round her once more, while the Dodo solemnly presented the thimble, saying, "We beg your acceptance of this elegant thimble;" and, when it had finished this short speech, they all cheered.

sentences.text: Then they all crowded round her once more, while the Dodo solemnly presented the thimble, saying, "We beg your acceptance of this elegant thimble;" and, when it had finished this short speech, they all cheered.
sentences.zh: 于是大家又围到她身边，渡渡鸟郑重地把顶针授予她，说：“我们恳请您收下这枚精致的顶针。”它这段简短的话一说完，大家就欢呼起来。

hints.zh: 敬请收下，极为客气的正式说法。
hints.en: Beg your acceptance: a very formal way of saying 'please accept this'.

paragraphs.text: Alice thought the whole thing very absurd, but they all looked so grave that she did not dare to laugh; and as she could not think of anything to say, she simply bowed, and took the thimble, looking as solemn as she could.

sentences.text: Alice thought the whole thing very absurd, but they all looked so grave that she did not dare to laugh; and as she could not think of anything to say, she simply bowed, and took the thimble, looking as solemn as she could.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝觉得整件事荒唐极了，可是大家的神情都那么严肃，她不敢笑；她又想不出该说什么，只好鞠了一躬，接过顶针，尽量装出一副严肃的样子。

paragraphs.text: The next thing was to eat the comfits: this caused some noise and confusion, as the large birds complained that they could not taste theirs, and the small ones choked and had to be patted on the back. However, it was over at last, and they sat down again in a ring, and begged the Mouse to tell them something more.

sentences.text: The next thing was to eat the comfits: this caused some noise and confusion, as the large birds complained that they could not taste theirs, and the small ones choked and had to be patted on the back.
sentences.zh: 接下来是吃掉蜜饯糖：这下引起了一阵吵闹和混乱，因为大鸟抱怨说根本尝不出味道，小鸟则噎住了，得别人拍背才行。

sentences.text: However, it was over at last, and they sat down again in a ring, and begged the Mouse to tell them something more.
sentences.zh: 不过，这事总算过去了。大家又重新围坐成一圈，请老鼠再讲点什么。

hints.zh: 在背上拍一拍，这里指噎住时给人顺气。
hints.en: Patted on the back, the usual help for someone who is choking.

paragraphs.text: "You promised to tell me your history, you know," said Alice, "and why it is you hate—C and D," she added in a whisper, half afraid that it would be offended again.

sentences.text: "You promised to tell me your history, you know," said Alice, "and why it is you hate—C and D," she added in a whisper, half afraid that it would be offended again.
sentences.zh: “你知道，你答应过要讲你的经历，”爱丽丝说，“还有你为什么恨——C 和 D，”她压低声音补了一句，生怕又惹它生气。

hints.zh: 指猫和狗（cat 和 dog）；老鼠先前只肯用首字母说，爱丽丝也不敢明说。
hints.en: C and D stand for cat and dog, which the Mouse would not name aloud.

paragraphs.text: "Mine is a long and a sad tale!" said the Mouse, turning to Alice, and sighing.

sentences.text: "Mine is a long and a sad tale!" said the Mouse, turning to Alice, and sighing.
sentences.zh: “我的故事又长又伤心！”老鼠转向爱丽丝，叹了口气说。

introduction.zh: 奖品得由爱丽丝来发。可她口袋里只有一盒蜜饯糖，数来数去刚好每人一颗。这时大家又说，发奖的人自己也得有一份奖品才行。
introduction.en: Alice has to hand out the prizes, but all she has in her pocket is a box of comfits — just one for each animal. Then the party says that the one who gives the prizes needs a prize too.

quiz.question: What did Alice hand out as prizes?
options: Comfits from her pocket.
Small cakes from a box.
Flowers picked on the bank.

feedback.zh: 第 1 句写她从口袋里掏出一盒 comfits（蜜饯糖），当作奖品一人一颗发下去。
feedback.en: In sentence 1 Alice pulls a box of comfits out of her pocket and hands them round as prizes.

quiz.question: How did Alice behave when she was given the thimble?
options: She refused to take it.
She bowed and took it solemnly.
She laughed at the whole ceremony.

feedback.zh: 第 9 句说她觉得荒唐却不敢笑，只好鞠躬、接过顶针，还尽量装得同样严肃。
feedback.en: Sentence 9 shows her bowing, taking the thimble and looking as solemn as she could.

grammar.excerpt: they all looked so grave that she did not dare to laugh

focus.zh: so 修饰形容词 grave，后面的 that 引出结果：他们严肃到爱丽丝不敢笑。
focus.en: So before the adjective grave, with that introducing the result: their seriousness was such that Alice did not dare to laugh.

paragraphs.text: "It is a long tail, certainly," said Alice, looking down with wonder at the Mouse's tail; "But why do you call it sad?" And she kept on puzzling about it while the Mouse was speaking, so that her idea of the tale was something like this:—— "Fury said to

sentences.text: "It is a long tail, certainly," said Alice, looking down with wonder at the Mouse's tail; "But why do you call it sad?"
sentences.zh: “尾巴确实很长，”爱丽丝说着，惊讶地低头看着老鼠的尾巴，“可你为什么说它伤心呢？”

sentences.text: And she kept on puzzling about it while the Mouse was speaking, so that her idea of the tale was something like this:—— "Fury said to
sentences.zh: 老鼠讲的时候，她一直在琢磨这件事，所以她听到的故事大致是这样的：—— “弗瑞对

hints.zh: 尾巴；与 tale（故事）同音，爱丽丝把 tale 听成了 tail。
hints.en: Tail, which sounds like tale: Alice has taken the Mouse's 'tale' for a 'tail'.

hints.zh: 弗瑞，诗里那条狗的名字；fury 本义是“狂怒”。
hints.en: Fury, the name of the dog in the poem; the word itself means 'rage'.

paragraphs.text: a mouse, That he met in the house, 'Let us both go to law: I will prosecute you.— Come, I'll take no denial; We must have a trial: For really this morning I've nothing to do.' Said the mouse to the cur, 'Such a trial, dear sir, With no jury or judge, would be wasting our breath.' 'I'll be judge. I'll be jury,' Said cunning old Fury; 'I'll try the whole cause, and condemn you to death.''

sentences.text: a mouse, That he met in the house, 'Let us both go to law: I will prosecute you.— Come, I'll take no denial; We must have a trial: For really this morning I've nothing to do.' Said the mouse to the cur, 'Such a trial, dear sir, With no jury or judge, would be wasting our breath.' 'I'll be judge.
sentences.zh: 一只老鼠——他在屋里遇见的那只——‘咱们俩去打官司吧：我要控告你。——来吧，我不许你推辞；我们非得审一场：因为今天早上我实在无事可做。’老鼠对那条恶狗说：‘这样的审判，亲爱的先生，既没有陪审团也没有法官，只是白费口舌。’‘我来当法官。

sentences.text: I'll be jury,' Said cunning old Fury; 'I'll try the whole cause, and condemn you to death.''
sentences.zh: 我来当陪审团，’狡猾的老弗瑞说，‘这案子我全审了，判你死刑。’”

hints.zh: 恶狗、杂种狗（带轻蔑意味）。
hints.en: Cur: a contemptuous word for a dog, especially a mongrel.

hints.zh: 案子、诉讼（法律用语），不是“原因”。
hints.en: Cause here means a law case, not 'a reason'.

paragraphs.text: "You are not attending!" said the Mouse to Alice, severely. "What are you thinking of?" "I beg your pardon," said Alice very humbly: "you had got to the fifth bend, I think?"

sentences.text: "You are not attending!" said the Mouse to Alice, severely.
sentences.zh: “你没在听！”老鼠严厉地对爱丽丝说。

sentences.text: "What are you thinking of?"
sentences.zh: “你在想什么？”

sentences.text: "I beg your pardon," said Alice very humbly: "you had got to the fifth bend, I think?"
sentences.zh: “对不起，”爱丽丝非常谦恭地说，“我想，你刚才讲到第五个弯了吧？”

paragraphs.text: "I had not!" cried the Mouse, sharply and very angrily.

sentences.text: "I had not!" cried the Mouse, sharply and very angrily.
sentences.zh: “我没有！”老鼠又尖又怒地叫道。

paragraphs.text: "A knot!" said Alice, always ready to make herself useful, and looking anxiously about her. "Oh, do let me help to undo it!"

sentences.text: "A knot!" said Alice, always ready to make herself useful, and looking anxiously about her.
sentences.zh: “一个结！”爱丽丝说。她总乐意帮上点忙，一边还焦急地四下张望。

sentences.text: "Oh, do let me help to undo it!"
sentences.zh: “哦，让我帮你把它解开吧！”

hints.zh: 绳结；与 not 同音，爱丽丝把老鼠的“我没有”听成了“一个结”。
hints.en: Knot, which sounds like not: Alice hears 'I had not' as 'a knot'.

paragraphs.text: "I shall do nothing of the sort," said the Mouse, getting up and walking away. "You insult me by talking such nonsense!"

sentences.text: "I shall do nothing of the sort," said the Mouse, getting up and walking away.
sentences.zh: “我绝不会做这种事，”老鼠说着站起身走开了。

sentences.text: "You insult me by talking such nonsense!"
sentences.zh: “你说这种胡话，是在侮辱我！”

hints.target: I shall do nothing of the sort
hints.zh: 我绝不会做那种事，断然拒绝的说法。
hints.en: I shall do nothing of the sort: a firm, rather stiff refusal.

paragraphs.text: "I didn't mean it!" pleaded poor Alice. "But you're so easily offended, you know!"

sentences.text: "I didn't mean it!" pleaded poor Alice.
sentences.zh: “我不是那个意思！”可怜的爱丽丝哀求道。

sentences.text: "But you're so easily offended, you know!"
sentences.zh: “可你也太容易生气了，你知道的！”

paragraphs.text: The Mouse only growled in reply.

sentences.text: The Mouse only growled in reply.
sentences.zh: 老鼠只低吼了一声作为回答。

paragraphs.text: "Please come back, and finish your story!" Alice called after it; and the others all joined in chorus, "Yes, please do!" but the Mouse only shook its head impatiently, and walked a little quicker.

sentences.text: "Please come back, and finish your story!"
sentences.zh: “请回来，把故事讲完吧！”

sentences.text: Alice called after it; and the others all joined in chorus, "Yes, please do!" but the Mouse only shook its head impatiently, and walked a little quicker.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝在它身后喊道；其他人也齐声附和：“对，请回来吧！”可老鼠只是不耐烦地摇摇头，走得更快了些。

introduction.zh: 老鼠说自己的故事又长又伤心，爱丽丝却低头盯着它那条长尾巴，怎么也想不通“长”在哪里。故事讲到一半，她终于忍不住插了嘴。
introduction.en: The Mouse calls its story long and sad, but Alice keeps looking at its long tail and cannot see what is sad about it. Halfway through, she can no longer keep quiet.

quiz.question: What did Alice think the Mouse meant by 'a long and sad tale'?
options: A sad song about a mouse and a dog.
A long story about its life.
A long tail, which she could not see as sad.

feedback.zh: 第 1 句爱丽丝看着老鼠的尾巴，问它为什么说这故事伤心——她把 tale（故事）听成了 tail（尾巴）。
feedback.en: In sentence 1 Alice looks at the Mouse's tail and asks why it calls it sad: she has heard tale as tail.

quiz.question: What did Alice offer to do when the Mouse cried 'I had not!'?
options: To help undo the knot she thought it meant.
To fetch the Mouse a cup of water.
To finish the story herself.

feedback.zh: 第 8 句爱丽丝说“让我帮你把它解开吧”，她以为老鼠说的是打了结的尾巴。
feedback.en: In sentence 8 she says 'do let me help to undo it', taking 'not' for a knot in the tail.

grammar.excerpt: you had got to the fifth bend

focus.zh: had got 是过去完成时，指在她开口打断之前，老鼠已经讲到了哪里。
focus.en: Had got is past perfect: it marks the point the Mouse had already reached before Alice spoke.

paragraphs.text: "What a pity it wouldn't stay!" sighed the Lory, as soon as it was quite out of sight; and an old Crab took the opportunity of saying to her daughter, "Ah, my dear! Let this be a lesson to you never to lose your temper!" "Hold your tongue, Ma!" said the young Crab, a little snappishly. "You're enough to try the patience of an oyster!"

sentences.text: "What a pity it wouldn't stay!" sighed the Lory, as soon as it was quite out of sight; and an old Crab took the opportunity of saying to her daughter, "Ah, my dear!
sentences.zh: “它不肯留下，多可惜呀！”老鼠刚一走远，鹦鹉就叹道。一只老螃蟹趁机对女儿说：“唉，我的宝贝！

sentences.text: Let this be a lesson to you never to lose your temper!"
sentences.zh: 你就记住这个教训：千万别发脾气！”

sentences.text: "Hold your tongue, Ma!" said the young Crab, a little snappishly.
sentences.zh: “住嘴吧，妈！”小螃蟹有点没好气地说。

sentences.text: "You're enough to try the patience of an oyster!"
sentences.zh: “你简直能把牡蛎都惹烦了！”

hints.zh: 发脾气、动怒。
hints.en: Lose your temper: become angry.

hints.target: try the patience of an oyster
hints.zh: 连牡蛎都能被你惹烦——夸张说法，意思是“你太让人受不了了”。
hints.en: An exaggeration: you would try even an oyster's patience, though an oyster has none.

paragraphs.text: "I wish I had our Dinah here, I know I do! " said Alice aloud, addressing nobody in particular. "She'd soon fetch it back!"

sentences.text: "I wish I had our Dinah here, I know I do! " said Alice aloud, addressing nobody in particular.
sentences.zh: “我真希望咱们的黛娜在这儿，真的！”爱丽丝大声说，并不是特意对谁讲。

sentences.text: "She'd soon fetch it back!"
sentences.zh: “她很快就能把它追回来！”

hints.zh: 黛娜，爱丽丝家里的猫。
hints.en: Dinah, Alice's cat at home.

paragraphs.text: "And who is Dinah, if I might venture to ask the question?" said the Lory.

sentences.text: "And who is Dinah, if I might venture to ask the question?" said the Lory.
sentences.zh: “请问，黛娜是谁？”鹦鹉壮着胆子问了一句。

paragraphs.text: Alice replied eagerly, for she was always ready to talk about her pet: "Dinah's our cat. And she's such a capital one for catching mice, you can't think! And oh, I wish you could see her after the birds! Why, she'll eat a little bird as soon as look at it!"

sentences.text: Alice replied eagerly, for she was always ready to talk about her pet: "Dinah's our cat.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝热切地回答，因为她总乐意谈自己的宠物：“黛娜是我们的猫。

sentences.text: And she's such a capital one for catching mice, you can't think!
sentences.zh: 她抓老鼠可厉害了，你简直想象不到！

sentences.text: And oh, I wish you could see her after the birds!
sentences.zh: 哦，我真希望你能看看她追鸟的样子！

sentences.text: Why, she'll eat a little bird as soon as look at it!"
sentences.zh: 嗨，她看一眼小鸟就能把它吃掉！”

hints.zh: 极好的、顶呱呱的（口语，不是“首都”）。
hints.en: Capital here means excellent, not 'a capital city'.

hints.zh: 追鸟；after 在这里是“追赶、追捕”。
hints.en: After the birds: chasing the birds; after means 'in pursuit of'.

paragraphs.text: This speech caused a remarkable sensation among the party. Some of the birds hurried off at once: one old Magpie began wrapping itself up very carefully, remarking, "I really must be getting home; the night-air doesn't suit my throat!" and a Canary called out in a trembling voice to its children, "Come away, my dears! It's high time you were all in bed!" On various pretexts they all moved off, and Alice was soon left alone.

sentences.text: This speech caused a remarkable sensation among the party.
sentences.zh: 这番话在众位中间引起了一阵不小的骚动。

sentences.text: Some of the birds hurried off at once: one old Magpie began wrapping itself up very carefully, remarking, "I really must be getting home; the night-air doesn't suit my throat!" and a Canary called out in a trembling voice to its children, "Come away, my dears!
sentences.zh: 有些鸟立刻匆匆离开了：一只老喜鹊开始仔细地把自己裹起来，还说：“我真得回家了，夜风对我的嗓子不好！”一只金丝雀用发颤的声音对孩子们喊：“走吧，宝贝们！

sentences.text: It's high time you were all in bed!"
sentences.zh: 你们早该上床睡觉了！”

sentences.text: On various pretexts they all moved off, and Alice was soon left alone.
sentences.zh: 大家找出种种借口陆续走开，很快岸上就只剩下爱丽丝一个人了。

hints.zh: 借口、托词。
hints.en: Pretexts: false reasons given to hide the real one.

introduction.zh: 老鼠走了，大家还在议论它为什么不肯留下。爱丽丝想起家里的猫黛娜，忍不住夸起她来——可听众里有一半是鸟。
introduction.en: The Mouse has gone, and the others are still wondering why it would not stay. Alice thinks of Dinah, her cat at home, and cannot resist praising her — though half of her listeners are birds.

quiz.question: Why did the birds hurry away after Alice's speech?
options: Alice's cat was famous for catching birds.
They wanted to bring the Mouse back.
Dinah was waiting for them by the water.

feedback.zh: 第 11 句爱丽丝说黛娜看一眼小鸟就能把它吃掉，所以鸟们听完就急着告辞。
feedback.en: In sentence 11 Alice says Dinah would eat a little bird as soon as look at it, so the birds hurry off.

quiz.question: What did the old Crab tell her daughter?
options: To stay away from cats.
Never to lose her temper.
To be polite to Alice.

feedback.zh: 第 2 句老螃蟹让女儿记住教训：永远别发脾气。
feedback.en: Sentence 2 has the old Crab telling her daughter never to lose her temper.

grammar.excerpt: she's such a capital one for catching mice

focus.zh: such 后接 a + 形容词 + 名词，强调黛娜“这样”出色；one 代替 cat。
focus.en: Such comes before a + adjective + noun to stress how good the cat is; one stands for cat.

paragraphs.text: "I wish I hadn't mentioned Dinah!" she said to herself in a melancholy tone. "Nobody seems to like her, down here, and I'm sure she's the best cat in the world! Oh, my dear Dinah! I wonder if I shall ever see you any more!" And here poor Alice began to cry again, for she felt very lonely and low-spirited. In a little while, however, she again heard a little pattering of footsteps in the distance, and she looked up eagerly, half hoping that the Mouse had changed his mind, and was coming back to finish his story.

sentences.text: "I wish I hadn't mentioned Dinah!" she said to herself in a melancholy tone.
sentences.zh: “真希望我没提黛娜！”她闷闷不乐地自言自语。

sentences.text: "Nobody seems to like her, down here, and I'm sure she's the best cat in the world!
sentences.zh: “这下面的人好像都不喜欢她，可我敢说，她是世界上最好的猫！

sentences.text: Oh, my dear Dinah!
sentences.zh: 哦，我亲爱的黛娜！

sentences.text: I wonder if I shall ever see you any more!"
sentences.zh: 我不知道还能不能再见到你！”

sentences.text: And here poor Alice began to cry again, for she felt very lonely and low-spirited.
sentences.zh: 说到这里，可怜的爱丽丝又哭了起来，因为她觉得非常孤单，情绪低落。

sentences.text: In a little while, however, she again heard a little pattering of footsteps in the distance, and she looked up eagerly, half hoping that the Mouse had changed his mind, and was coming back to finish his story.
sentences.zh: 可是过了一会儿，她又听见远处传来一阵细碎的脚步声。她急切地抬起头，心里半是希望老鼠改了主意，回来把故事讲完。

hints.zh: 情绪低落、提不起精神。
hints.en: Low-spirited: sad and without energy.

hints.zh: （轻而密的）啪嗒声，这里指细碎的脚步声。
hints.en: Pattering: a light, quick series of taps, here of little feet.

introduction.zh: 大家都走了，岸边只剩下爱丽丝一个人。她开始怀疑自己，也格外想念家里的猫。就在这时，远处又传来一阵细碎的脚步声。
introduction.en: Everyone has gone, and Alice is alone on the bank. She begins to doubt herself and misses the cat she left at home. Then, in the distance, she hears a small pattering of feet again.

quiz.question: How did Alice feel after the others left?
options: Lonely and low-spirited.
Angry with the Mouse.
Pleased to be alone at last.

feedback.zh: 第 5 句说她又哭了起来，因为觉得孤单、提不起精神。
feedback.en: Sentence 5 says she began to cry again because she felt very lonely and low-spirited.

quiz.question: What did Alice hope when she heard footsteps again?
options: That the Mouse had come back to finish its story.
That her sister had come to find her.
That the Dodo was bringing her prize.

feedback.zh: 第 6 句说她半是盼着老鼠改了主意，正走回来。
feedback.en: Sentence 6 says she was half hoping the Mouse had changed its mind and was coming back.

grammar.excerpt: I wish I hadn't mentioned Dinah!

focus.zh: wish 后用 had + 过去分词，表示对已经发生的事后悔——她其实已经把黛娜说了出来。
focus.en: Wish with had + past participle expresses regret about something already done: she has mentioned Dinah.

title.en: The Rabbit Sends in a Little Bill

paragraphs.text: It was the White Rabbit, trotting slowly back again, and looking anxiously about as it went, as if it had lost something; and she heard it muttering to itself, "The Duchess! The Duchess! Oh my dear paws! Oh my fur and whiskers! She'll get me executed, as sure as ferrets are ferrets! Where can I have dropped them, I wonder?" Alice guessed in a moment that it was looking for the fan and the pair of white kid gloves, and she very good-naturedly began hunting about for them, but they were nowhere to be seen—everything seemed to have changed since her swim in the pool, and the great hall, with the glass table and the little door, had vanished completely.

sentences.text: It was the White Rabbit, trotting slowly back again, and looking anxiously about as it went, as if it had lost something; and she heard it muttering to itself, "The Duchess!
sentences.zh: 原来是那只白兔，正慢慢地小跑回来，一边跑一边焦急地东张西望，像是丢了什么东西；她还听见它自言自语地嘟囔：“公爵夫人！

sentences.text: The Duchess!
sentences.zh: 公爵夫人！

sentences.text: Oh my dear paws!
sentences.zh: 哦，我可怜的爪子！

sentences.text: Oh my fur and whiskers!
sentences.zh: 哦，我的皮毛和胡须！

sentences.text: She'll get me executed, as sure as ferrets are ferrets!
sentences.zh: 她一定会把我砍头的，就像雪貂终归是雪貂一样千真万确！

sentences.text: Where can I have dropped them, I wonder?"
sentences.zh: 我到底能把它们掉在哪儿了呢？”

sentences.text: Alice guessed in a moment that it was looking for the fan and the pair of white kid gloves, and she very good-naturedly began hunting about for them, but they were nowhere to be seen—everything seemed to have changed since her swim in the pool, and the great hall, with the glass table and the little door, had vanished completely.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝立刻猜出，它是在找那把扇子和那双白色的小山羊皮手套，于是好心地帮它四处找起来。可哪儿都看不见——自从在池子里游过泳之后，一切好像都变了，那座带玻璃桌子和一扇小门的大厅也完全消失了。

hints.zh: 白兔，揣着怀表、总在赶时间的那只兔子。
hints.en: The White Rabbit, the waistcoat-wearing rabbit who is always in a hurry.

hints.zh: 公爵夫人，白兔非常惧怕的贵妇。
hints.en: The Duchess, a noblewoman the White Rabbit is badly afraid of.

hints.target: as sure as ferrets are ferrets
hints.zh: 像雪貂就是雪貂一样确凿——白兔的口头强调，意思是“千真万确”。
hints.en: As sure as ferrets are ferrets: a fixed phrase meaning 'absolutely certain'.

hints.zh: 爱丽丝，故事的女主角。
hints.en: Alice, the girl at the centre of the story.

hints.zh: 小山羊皮手套；这里的 kid 指小山羊皮，不是“小孩”。
hints.en: Kid gloves are gloves made of soft goatskin; kid here is the leather, not a child.

paragraphs.text: Very soon the rabbit noticed Alice, as she went hunting about, and called out to her in an angry tone, "Why, Mary Ann, what are you doing out here? Run home this moment, and fetch me a pair of gloves and a fan! Quick, now!" And Alice was so much frightened that she ran off at once in the direction it pointed to, without trying to explain the mistake that it had made.

sentences.text: Very soon the rabbit noticed Alice, as she went hunting about, and called out to her in an angry tone, "Why, Mary Ann, what are you doing out here?
sentences.zh: 没过多久，白兔就注意到了正在四处寻找的爱丽丝，生气地冲她喊道：“喂，玛丽·安，你跑到这儿来干什么？

sentences.text: Run home this moment, and fetch me a pair of gloves and a fan!
sentences.zh: 马上回家去，给我拿一副手套和一把扇子来！

sentences.text: Quick, now!"
sentences.zh: 快点，这就去！”

sentences.text: And Alice was so much frightened that she ran off at once in the direction it pointed to, without trying to explain the mistake that it had made.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝吓得要命，立刻朝它指的方向跑去，根本没想解释它认错了人。

hints.zh: 玛丽·安，白兔家女仆的名字；白兔把爱丽丝当成了她。
hints.en: Mary Ann, the name of the Rabbit's housemaid, whom he takes Alice to be.

introduction.zh: 白兔一路小跑回来，嘴里念叨着公爵夫人和砍头，像是在找什么要紧东西。爱丽丝好心帮忙，白兔一看见她，却用命令的口气喊了起来。它把她当成了谁？
introduction.en: The White Rabbit trots back, muttering about the Duchess and the axe. Alice tries to help him find what he has lost, but the Rabbit mistakes her for someone else and gives her an order. Who does he think she is?

quiz.question: Why does the White Rabbit keep saying the Duchess's name?
options: He is looking for the Duchess's house.
He wants to invite the Duchess to tea.
He is afraid the Duchess will have him executed.

feedback.zh: 白兔念叨“她一定会把我砍头”，怕的是公爵夫人惩罚它，所以急得直叫。
feedback.en: The Rabbit repeats 'She'll get me executed' — he is afraid of what the Duchess will do to him.

quiz.question: What does Alice do when the Rabbit shouts at her?
options: She explains that he has made a mistake.
She runs off to fetch the gloves and the fan.
She sits down and starts to cry.

feedback.zh: 她吓得要命，顾不上解释，就朝白兔指的方向跑去拿手套和扇子。
feedback.en: She is too frightened to explain and simply runs off the way the Rabbit points.

grammar.excerpt: she heard it muttering to itself

focus.zh: heard it muttering 是 hear + 宾语 + -ing：她听见时，嘟囔声已经在进行。
focus.en: Heard it muttering is hear + object + -ing: the muttering was already going on when she caught it.

paragraphs.text: "He took me for his housemaid," she said to herself as she ran. "How surprised he'll be when he finds out who I am! But I'd better take him his fan and gloves—that is, if I can find them." As she said this, she came upon a neat little house, on the door of which was a bright brass plate with the name "W. RABBIT" engraved upon it. She went in without knocking, and hurried upstairs, in great fear lest she should meet the real Mary Ann, and be turned out of the house before she had found the fan and gloves.

sentences.text: "He took me for his housemaid," she said to herself as she ran.
sentences.zh: “他把我当成他家的女仆了。”她一边跑一边自言自语。

sentences.text: "How surprised he'll be when he finds out who I am!
sentences.zh: “等他弄明白我是谁，准会大吃一惊！

sentences.text: But I'd better take him his fan and gloves—that is, if I can find them."
sentences.zh: 不过我还是把他的扇子和手套送去吧——前提是我找得到。”

sentences.text: As she said this, she came upon a neat little house, on the door of which was a bright brass plate with the name "W. RABBIT" engraved upon it.
sentences.zh: 说着说着，她来到一栋整洁的小房子前，门上钉着一块锃亮的黄铜门牌，上面刻着“白兔”的名字。

sentences.text: She went in without knocking, and hurried upstairs, in great fear lest she should meet the real Mary Ann, and be turned out of the house before she had found the fan and gloves.
sentences.zh: 她没敲门就进去了，急匆匆地上楼，心里非常害怕会碰见真正的玛丽·安，还没找到扇子和手套就被赶出屋子。

hints.zh: 偶然发现、碰上；不是“走到……上面”。
hints.en: Came upon means 'found by chance', not 'walked on top of'.

hints.zh: 以免、生怕；书面旧用法，后面常跟 should。
hints.en: Lest means 'for fear that'; it is old-fashioned and often followed by should.

paragraphs.text: "How queer it seems," Alice said to herself, "to be going messages for a rabbit! I suppose Dinah'll be sending me on messages next!" And she began fancying the sort of thing that would happen: "'Miss Alice! Come here directly, and get ready for your walk!' 'Coming in a minute, nurse! But I've got to watch this mouse-hole till Dinah comes back, and see that the mouse doesn't get out.' Only I don't think," Alice went on, "that they'd let Dinah stop in the house if it began ordering people about like that!"

sentences.text: "How queer it seems," Alice said to herself, "to be going messages for a rabbit!
sentences.zh: “这事儿真古怪，”爱丽丝自言自语，“居然给一只兔子跑腿送东西！

sentences.text: I suppose Dinah'll be sending me on messages next!"
sentences.zh: 我看下一回就该轮到黛娜打发我去送信了！”

sentences.text: And she began fancying the sort of thing that would happen: "'Miss Alice!
sentences.zh: 她开始想象那会是什么情形：“‘爱丽丝小姐！

sentences.text: Come here directly, and get ready for your walk!' 'Coming in a minute, nurse!
sentences.zh: 马上过来，准备去散步！’‘就来，保姆！

sentences.text: But I've got to watch this mouse-hole till Dinah comes back, and see that the mouse doesn't get out.' Only I don't think," Alice went on, "that they'd let Dinah stop in the house if it began ordering people about like that!"
sentences.zh: 可我得守着这个老鼠洞，等黛娜回来，还得看着别让老鼠跑出去。’只不过我觉得，”爱丽丝接着说，“要是黛娜也这样对人呼来喝去，他们大概不会让它留在家里！”

hints.zh: 跑腿送信、替人办事；旧式说法，相当于 running errands。
hints.en: Going messages is an old way of saying 'running errands'.

hints.zh: 黛娜，爱丽丝的猫。
hints.en: Dinah, Alice's cat.

hints.zh: 老鼠洞；爱丽丝想象自己像猫一样守在洞边。
hints.en: A mouse-hole: in her daydream Alice guards it as a cat would.

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝一边跑一边想：给一只兔子跑腿，这事可真够古怪。她果然找到一栋小房子，门上钉着刻了名字的黄铜牌。屋里等着她的，会是那个真正的女仆吗？
introduction.en: Running along, Alice wonders how strange it is to be sent on messages by a rabbit. She finds a neat little house with a brass plate on the door. Will the real housemaid be waiting inside?

quiz.question: What is written on the brass plate on the door?
options: DRINK ME
MARY ANN
W. RABBIT

feedback.zh: 黄铜牌上刻着“W. RABBIT”，可见这栋小房子正是白兔的家。
feedback.en: The plate reads 'W. RABBIT', so the little house belongs to the Rabbit.

quiz.question: Why does Alice hurry upstairs without knocking?
options: She is looking for her cat Dinah.
She wants to meet the real Mary Ann.
She hopes to find the fan and gloves before the real Mary Ann turns her out.

feedback.zh: 她怕撞见真正的玛丽·安，还没找到东西就被赶出去，所以悄悄上楼。
feedback.en: She slips in because she fears the real Mary Ann will throw her out before she finds the fan and gloves.

grammar.excerpt: on the door of which was a bright brass plate

focus.zh: on the door of which 是“介词 + 关系代词”，先行词是 house；从句主语 brass plate 放在 was 后面。
focus.en: On the door of which is a preposition plus relative pronoun; the clause's subject, a bright brass plate, follows was.

paragraphs.text: By this time she had found her way into a tidy little room with a table in the window, and on it (as she had hoped) a fan and two or three pairs of tiny white kid gloves: she took up the fan and a pair of the gloves, and was just going to leave the room, when her eye fell upon a little bottle that stood near the looking-glass. There was no label this time with the words "DRINK ME," but nevertheless she uncorked it and put it to her lips. "I know something interesting is sure to happen," she said to herself, "whenever I eat or drink anything; so I'll just see what this bottle does. I do hope it'll make me grow large again, for really I'm quite tired of being such a tiny little thing!"

sentences.text: By this time she had found her way into a tidy little room with a table in the window, and on it (as she had hoped) a fan and two or three pairs of tiny white kid gloves: she took up the fan and a pair of the gloves, and was just going to leave the room, when her eye fell upon a little bottle that stood near the looking-glass.
sentences.zh: 这时，她已经走进一间整洁的小房间，窗边有张桌子，桌上（正如她所希望的）放着一把扇子和两三双小巧的白色小山羊皮手套。她拿起扇子和一双手套，正要离开房间，目光却落在镜子旁的一只小瓶子上。

sentences.text: There was no label this time with the words "DRINK ME," but nevertheless she uncorked it and put it to her lips.
sentences.zh: 这一次瓶子上没有写着“喝我”的标签，可她还是拔开瓶塞，把瓶子凑到嘴边。

sentences.text: "I know something interesting is sure to happen," she said to herself, "whenever I eat or drink anything; so I'll just see what this bottle does.
sentences.zh: “我知道，只要我吃点或喝点什么，准会有有趣的事发生，”她自言自语，“那我就看看这瓶东西会怎么样。

sentences.text: I do hope it'll make me grow large again, for really I'm quite tired of being such a tiny little thing!"
sentences.zh: 我真希望它能让我重新变大，说真的，我已经很厌倦做这么个小不点儿了！”

hints.zh: 镜子；维多利亚时代的旧说法，现在多说 mirror。
hints.en: A looking-glass is a mirror; the word is old-fashioned now.

hints.zh: “喝我”，上一章那只瓶子上的标签；这一瓶什么都没有。
hints.en: 'DRINK ME' was the label on the bottle in the last chapter; this bottle has none.

paragraphs.text: It did so indeed, and much sooner than she had expected: before she had drunk half the bottle, she found her head pressing against the ceiling, and had to stoop to save her neck from being broken. She hastily put down the bottle, saying to herself, "That's quite enough—I hope I shan't grow any more—As it is, I can't get out at the door—I do wish I hadn't drunk quite so much!"

sentences.text: It did so indeed, and much sooner than she had expected: before she had drunk half the bottle, she found her head pressing against the ceiling, and had to stoop to save her neck from being broken.
sentences.zh: 它果然起了作用，而且比她预料的快得多：还没喝到半瓶，她就发现自己的头顶住了天花板，只好弯下腰，免得把脖子折断。

sentences.text: She hastily put down the bottle, saying to herself, "That's quite enough—I hope I shan't grow any more—As it is, I can't get out at the door—I do wish I hadn't drunk quite so much!"
sentences.zh: 她赶紧放下瓶子，自言自语道：“够了——希望我不会再长了——可就算这样，我也出不了门——真希望我没喝那么多！”

paragraphs.text: Alas! it was too late to wish that! She went on growing, and growing, and very soon had to kneel down on the floor: in another minute there was not even room for this, and she tried the effect of lying down with one elbow against the door, and the other arm curled round her head. Still she went on growing, and, as a last resource, she put one arm out of the window, and one foot up the chimney, and said to herself, "Now I can do no more, whatever happens. What will become of me?"

sentences.text: Alas! it was too late to wish that!
sentences.zh: 唉！现在后悔已经太晚了！

sentences.text: She went on growing, and growing, and very soon had to kneel down on the floor: in another minute there was not even room for this, and she tried the effect of lying down with one elbow against the door, and the other arm curled round her head.
sentences.zh: 她不停地长啊长，很快就只能跪在地板上；再过一分钟，连跪的地方也没有了，她便试着躺下来，一只胳膊肘抵着门，另一条胳膊蜷在头边。

sentences.text: Still she went on growing, and, as a last resource, she put one arm out of the window, and one foot up the chimney, and said to herself, "Now I can do no more, whatever happens.
sentences.zh: 她还在继续长，实在没有别的办法了，只好把一只胳膊伸出窗外，把一只脚伸进烟囱，自言自语道：“现在我再也做不了什么了，不管发生什么。

sentences.text: What will become of me?"
sentences.zh: 我会变成什么样呢？”

hints.zh: 作为最后一招、实在没别的办法时；相当于 as a last resort。
hints.en: As a last resource means 'as a final resort', when nothing else is left.

introduction.zh: 小房间里，爱丽丝找到了扇子和手套，还发现一瓶没有标签的饮料。她太想变回原来的大小，仰头就喝。这一次，身体会照她希望的那样变吗？
introduction.en: In a tidy little room Alice finds the fan and gloves, and a bottle with no label at all. She is tired of being tiny, so she drinks. Will her body do what she hopes this time?

quiz.question: Why does Alice drink from the bottle although it has no label?
options: She is very thirsty after her long run.
She believes something interesting always happens when she eats or drinks.
She wants to test whether it is poison.

feedback.zh: 她说“只要我吃点或喝点什么，准会有有趣的事发生”，于是想看看这瓶东西的效果。
feedback.en: She says something interesting always happens when she eats or drinks, so she tries the bottle.

quiz.question: What happens to Alice soon after she drinks?
options: Her head is pressed against the ceiling.
The bottle turns into a fan.
She shrinks to the size of a mouse.

feedback.zh: 还没喝到半瓶，她的头顶就抵住了天花板，只好弯腰，免得折断脖子。
feedback.en: Before half the bottle is gone her head presses the ceiling, and she has to stoop.

grammar.excerpt: I do hope it'll make me grow large again

focus.zh: do hope 是 do + 动词原形表强调，意思是“真的希望”，不是疑问或否定。
focus.en: Do hope uses do + base verb for emphasis: she really hopes it, and this is neither a question nor a negative.

paragraphs.text: Luckily for Alice, the little magic bottle had now had its full effect, and she grew no larger: still it was very uncomfortable, and as there seemed to be no sort of chance of her ever getting out of the room again, no wonder she felt unhappy.

sentences.text: Luckily for Alice, the little magic bottle had now had its full effect, and she grew no larger: still it was very uncomfortable, and as there seemed to be no sort of chance of her ever getting out of the room again, no wonder she felt unhappy.
sentences.zh: 幸亏如此，小魔法瓶这时已经发挥完了效力，她不再长大了；可她还是很不舒服，而且看来再也没有机会走出这间屋子，难怪她觉得不快乐。

paragraphs.text: "It was much pleasanter at home," thought poor Alice, "when one wasn't always growing larger and smaller, and being ordered about by mice and rabbits. I almost wish I hadn't gone down that rabbit-hole—and yet—and yet—it's rather curious, you know, this sort of life! I do wonder what can have happened to me! When I used to read fairy-tales, I fancied that kind of thing never happened, and now here I am in the middle of one! There ought to be a book written about me, that there ought! And when I grow up, I'll write one—but I'm grown up now," she added in a sorrowful tone, "at least there's no room to grow up any more here."

sentences.text: "It was much pleasanter at home," thought poor Alice, "when one wasn't always growing larger and smaller, and being ordered about by mice and rabbits.
sentences.zh: “在家里可舒服多了，”可怜的爱丽丝心想，“那时候不用老是变大变小，也不用被老鼠和兔子呼来喝去。

sentences.text: I almost wish I hadn't gone down that rabbit-hole—and yet—and yet—it's rather curious, you know, this sort of life!
sentences.zh: 我几乎希望自己没钻进那个兔子洞——可是——可是——你知道，这种日子还真挺稀奇的！

sentences.text: I do wonder what can have happened to me!
sentences.zh: 我真想知道我到底出了什么事！

sentences.text: When I used to read fairy-tales, I fancied that kind of thing never happened, and now here I am in the middle of one!
sentences.zh: 以前我读童话的时候，总以为那种事根本不会发生，可现在我自己就身处一个童话之中！

sentences.text: There ought to be a book written about me, that there ought!
sentences.zh: 应该有人为我写一本书才对，真该写一本！

sentences.text: And when I grow up, I'll write one—but I'm grown up now," she added in a sorrowful tone, "at least there's no room to grow up any more here."
sentences.zh: 等我长大了，我要自己写一本——可我现在已经长大了，”她伤心地补了一句，“至少在这儿再也没有地方可以长大了。”

paragraphs.text: "But then," thought Alice, "shall I never get any older than I am now? That'll be a comfort, one way—never to be an old woman—but then—always to have lessons to learn! Oh, I shouldn't like that!"

sentences.text: "But then," thought Alice, "shall I never get any older than I am now?
sentences.zh: “可是那样的话，”爱丽丝想，“我是不是永远也不会比现在更老了？

sentences.text: That'll be a comfort, one way—never to be an old woman—but then—always to have lessons to learn!
sentences.zh: 从某方面说，这倒是件安慰——永远不用变成老太婆——可又一想——那样就得永远上课！

sentences.text: Oh, I shouldn't like that!"
sentences.zh: 哦，我可不喜欢这样！”

hints.zh: 从某一方面说、往好处想；不是“一条路”。
hints.en: One way here means 'in one respect' or 'on the bright side', not 'one road'.

paragraphs.text: "Oh, you foolish Alice!" she answered herself. "How can you learn lessons in here? Why, there's hardly room for you, and no room at all for any lesson-books!"

sentences.text: "Oh, you foolish Alice!" she answered herself.
sentences.zh: “哦，你这个傻爱丽丝！”她回答自己。

sentences.text: "How can you learn lessons in here?
sentences.zh: “在这儿你怎么上课呢？

sentences.text: Why, there's hardly room for you, and no room at all for any lesson-books!"
sentences.zh: 瞧，连你都快没地方待了，哪儿还放得下课本！”

paragraphs.text: And so she went on, taking first one side and then the other, and making quite a conversation of it altogether; but after a few minutes she heard a voice outside, and stopped to listen.

sentences.text: And so she went on, taking first one side and then the other, and making quite a conversation of it altogether; but after a few minutes she heard a voice outside, and stopped to listen.
sentences.zh: 就这样，她一会儿替这一边说，一会儿替那一边说，简直把整件事说成了一场对话；可过了几分钟，她听见外面有声音，就停下来听。

hints.target: taking first one side and then the other
hints.zh: 先站这一边、再站那一边；指她自问自答，轮流扮演两边。
hints.en: Taking first one side and then the other: she argues both parts of the conversation herself.

introduction.zh: 瓶子终于不再起作用，可爱丽丝已经把房间塞得满满当当。她开始怀念家里，又为“长大”发愁：要是永远不再变老，是不是就得永远上课？
introduction.en: The bottle has done its work, and Alice now fills the room. She thinks of home and worries about growing up: if she never gets any older, will she have lessons for ever?

quiz.question: Why does Alice feel unhappy in the room?
options: Dinah has not come to find her.
She has lost the fan and the gloves.
She sees no chance of ever getting out of the room.

feedback.zh: 她看不出还有走出房间的可能，所以闷闷不乐。
feedback.en: There seems to be no chance of ever leaving the room, and that makes her unhappy.

quiz.question: What does Alice say she will do when she grows up?
options: Write a book about herself.
Teach Dinah to do tricks.
Go back down the rabbit-hole.

feedback.zh: 她说应该有人为她写本书，等长大了就自己写一本，可随即发现自己已经长大了。
feedback.en: She says a book ought to be written about her and that she will write one — but she is grown up already.

grammar.excerpt: There ought to be a book written about me

focus.zh: ought to 表示“应该”，语气比 should 更书面；这里等于说“该有人为我写本书”。
focus.en: Ought to means 'should' and sounds more formal than should: a book about her ought to exist.

paragraphs.text: "Mary Ann! Mary Ann!" said the voice, "fetch me my gloves this moment!" Then came a little pattering of feet on the stairs. Alice knew it was the Rabbit coming to look for her, and she trembled till she shook the house, quite forgetting that she was now about a thousand times as large as the Rabbit, and had no reason to be afraid of it.

sentences.text: "Mary Ann!
sentences.zh: “玛丽·安！

sentences.text: Mary Ann!" said the voice, "fetch me my gloves this moment!"
sentences.zh: 玛丽·安！”那个声音说，“马上把我的手套拿来！”

sentences.text: Then came a little pattering of feet on the stairs.
sentences.zh: 接着，楼梯上传来一阵轻轻的脚步声。

sentences.text: Alice knew it was the Rabbit coming to look for her, and she trembled till she shook the house, quite forgetting that she was now about a thousand times as large as the Rabbit, and had no reason to be afraid of it.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝知道是白兔来找她，吓得抖个不停，抖得整栋房子都晃了起来，完全忘了自己现在比白兔大了约一千倍，根本没有理由怕它。

paragraphs.text: Presently the Rabbit came up to the door, and tried to open it; but as the door opened inwards, and Alice's elbow was pressed hard against it, that attempt proved a failure. Alice heard it say to itself, "Then I'll go round and get in at the window."

sentences.text: Presently the Rabbit came up to the door, and tried to open it; but as the door opened inwards, and Alice's elbow was pressed hard against it, that attempt proved a failure.
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，白兔来到门口，想推开门；可门是朝里开的，爱丽丝的胳膊肘又死死抵着门，这一试就失败了。

sentences.text: Alice heard it say to itself, "Then I'll go round and get in at the window."
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝听见它自言自语：“那我就绕过去，从窗口爬进来。”

hints.zh: 不久、过了一会儿；不是“目前”。
hints.en: Presently means 'soon' or 'after a moment', not 'at present'.

paragraphs.text: "That you won't!" thought Alice, and, after waiting till she fancied she heard the Rabbit just under the window she suddenly spread out her hand, and made a snatch in the air. She did not get hold of anything, but she heard a little shriek and a fall, and a crash of broken glass, from which she concluded that it was just possible, it had fallen into a cucumber-frame, or something of the sort.

sentences.text: "That you won't!" thought Alice, and, after waiting till she fancied she heard the Rabbit just under the window she suddenly spread out her hand, and made a snatch in the air.
sentences.zh: “你可爬不进来！”爱丽丝心想。她等到觉得白兔就在窗下时，忽然伸出手，在空中猛地一抓。

sentences.text: She did not get hold of anything, but she heard a little shriek and a fall, and a crash of broken glass, from which she concluded that it was just possible, it had fallen into a cucumber-frame, or something of the sort.
sentences.zh: 她什么也没抓到，却听见一声小小的尖叫、一下跌倒的声音，还有玻璃摔碎的响声；她由此推断，它多半是掉进了黄瓜架，或者诸如此类的地方。

hints.zh: 猛地一抓；指伸手去抓，而不是慢慢拿。
hints.en: Made a snatch means 'grabbed quickly at something'.

hints.zh: 黄瓜架：带玻璃罩的低矮菜床，所以掉进去会有碎玻璃声。
hints.en: A cucumber-frame is a low glass-covered bed for growing cucumbers, which is why glass breaks.

paragraphs.text: Next came an angry voice—the Rabbit's—"Pat! Pat! Where are you?" And then a voice she had never heard before, "Sure then I'm here! Digging for apples, yer honour!"

sentences.text: Next came an angry voice—the Rabbit's—"Pat!
sentences.zh: 接着传来一个生气的声音——是白兔的——“帕特！

sentences.text: Pat!
sentences.zh: 帕特！

sentences.text: Where are you?"
sentences.zh: 你在哪儿？”

sentences.text: And then a voice she had never heard before, "Sure then I'm here!
sentences.zh: 然后又响起一个她从未听过的声音：“我在这儿呢，当然啦！

sentences.text: Digging for apples, yer honour!"
sentences.zh: 在挖苹果呢，老爷！”

hints.zh: 帕特，白兔的园丁，说话带浓重的乡下方言。
hints.en: Pat, the Rabbit's gardener, who speaks in a broad country dialect.

hints.zh: “老爷”的乡下口音说法（= your honour），仆人回话时用。
hints.en: Yer honour is a dialect form of 'your honour', used by servants answering a master.

paragraphs.text: "Digging for apples, indeed!" said the Rabbit angrily. "Here! Come and help me out of this!" (Sounds of more broken glass.)

sentences.text: "Digging for apples, indeed!" said the Rabbit angrily.
sentences.zh: “挖苹果，真是的！”白兔生气地说。

sentences.text: "Here!
sentences.zh: “这儿！

sentences.text: Come and help me out of this!" (Sounds of more broken glass.)
sentences.zh: 过来帮我从这堆东西里出来！”（又是一阵玻璃碎裂的声音。）

paragraphs.text: "Now tell me, Pat, what's that in the window?"

sentences.text: "Now tell me, Pat, what's that in the window?"
sentences.zh: “好了，帕特，你告诉我，窗户里那是什么东西？”

paragraphs.text: "Sure, it's an arm, yer honour!" (He pronounced it "arrum.")

sentences.text: "Sure, it's an arm, yer honour!" (He pronounced it "arrum.")
sentences.zh: “老爷，那是一条胳膊！”（他把“胳膊”念成了“胳巴”。）

paragraphs.text: "An arm, you goose! Who ever saw one that size? Why, it fills the whole window!"

sentences.text: "An arm, you goose!
sentences.zh: “一条胳膊，你这傻瓜！

sentences.text: Who ever saw one that size?
sentences.zh: 谁见过那么大的胳膊？

sentences.text: Why, it fills the whole window!"
sentences.zh: 它把整个窗户都塞满了！”

introduction.zh: 门外传来白兔的声音，它想进屋，门却推不开，只好改从窗口进来。爱丽丝守在窗边，等着它靠近。楼下很快响起玻璃碎裂的声音，还有一个陌生的声音在用浓重的乡下方言说话。
introduction.en: The Rabbit's voice comes from the stairs, but the door will not open. Alice decides to guard the window, and her first grab catches nothing. Then a new voice answers, in a strange country dialect.

quiz.question: Why can't the Rabbit open the door?
options: Alice's elbow is pressed hard against it.
Pat is holding the door shut.
The door is locked from the inside.

feedback.zh: 门朝里开，爱丽丝的胳膊肘又死死抵着门，白兔自然推不开。
feedback.en: The door opens inwards and Alice's elbow is pressed hard against it, so it will not move.

quiz.question: What does Alice think has happened after her first grab at the window?
options: The Rabbit has run away through the garden.
The Rabbit has fallen into the pool.
The Rabbit has fallen into a cucumber-frame.

feedback.zh: 她听见尖叫、跌倒和玻璃碎裂声，便猜到它掉进了黄瓜架的玻璃罩里。
feedback.en: A shriek, a fall and breaking glass tell her the Rabbit has landed in a cucumber-frame.

grammar.excerpt: about a thousand times as large as the Rabbit

focus.zh: as large as 是同级比较，前面加 a thousand times 表示倍数：大到白兔的一千倍。
focus.en: As large as compares two things as equal; a thousand times in front makes it a multiple.

paragraphs.text: "Sure, it does, yer honour: but it's an arm for all that."

sentences.text: "Sure, it does, yer honour: but it's an arm for all that."
sentences.zh: “老爷，可不是嘛：可它就是一条胳膊呀。”

paragraphs.text: "Well, it's got no business there, at any rate: go and take it away!"

sentences.text: "Well, it's got no business there, at any rate: go and take it away!"
sentences.zh: “好吧，不管怎么说，它不该待在那儿：去把它弄走！”

hints.zh: 不管怎样、无论如何；用来把话拉回重点。
hints.en: At any rate means 'in any case' or 'anyway'.

paragraphs.text: There was a long silence after this, and Alice could only hear whispers now and then; such as, "Sure, I don't like it, yer honour, at all, at all!" "Do as I tell you, you coward!" and at last she spread out her hand again, and made another snatch in the air. This time there were two little shrieks, and more sounds of broken glass. "What a number of cucumber frames there must be!" thought Alice. "I wonder what they'll do next! As for pulling me out of the window, I only wish they could! I'm sure I don't want to stay in here any longer!"

sentences.text: There was a long silence after this, and Alice could only hear whispers now and then; such as, "Sure, I don't like it, yer honour, at all, at all!"
sentences.zh: 之后是一阵长长的沉默，爱丽丝只能偶尔听见几句耳语，比如：“老爷，我可真不喜欢这东西，一点儿也不喜欢！”

sentences.text: "Do as I tell you, you coward!" and at last she spread out her hand again, and made another snatch in the air.
sentences.zh: “照我说的做，你这胆小鬼！”最后，她又伸出手，在空中抓了一把。

sentences.text: This time there were two little shrieks, and more sounds of broken glass.
sentences.zh: 这一回响起了两声尖叫，还有更多玻璃破碎的声音。

sentences.text: "What a number of cucumber frames there must be!" thought Alice.
sentences.zh: “这地方的黄瓜架可真多呀！”爱丽丝心想。

sentences.text: "I wonder what they'll do next!
sentences.zh: “我倒想知道他们下一步要干什么！

sentences.text: As for pulling me out of the window, I only wish they could!
sentences.zh: 至于把我从窗口拉出去，我巴不得他们能办到！

sentences.text: I'm sure I don't want to stay in here any longer!"
sentences.zh: 我敢说，我一刻也不想再待在这儿了！”

paragraphs.text: She waited for some time without hearing anything more: at last came a rumbling of little cart-wheels, and the sound of a good many voices all talking together: she made out the words: "Where's the other ladder?—Why, I hadn't to bring but one; Bill's got the other—Bill! fetch it here, lad!—Here, put 'em up at this corner—No, tie 'em together first—they don't reach half high enough yet—Oh! they'll do well enough; don't be particular—Here, Bill! catch hold of this rope—Will the roof bear?—Mind that loose slate—Oh, it's coming down! Heads below!" (a loud crash)—"Now, who did that?—It was Bill, I fancy—Who's to go down the chimney?—Nay, I shan't! You do it!—That I won't, then!—Bill's got to go down—Here, Bill! the master says you've got to go down the chimney!"

sentences.text: She waited for some time without hearing anything more: at last came a rumbling of little cart-wheels, and the sound of a good many voices all talking together: she made out the words: "Where's the other ladder?—Why, I hadn't to bring but one; Bill's got the other—Bill! fetch it here, lad!—Here, put 'em up at this corner—No, tie 'em together first—they don't reach half high enough yet—Oh! they'll do well enough; don't be particular—Here, Bill! catch hold of this rope—Will the roof bear?—Mind that loose slate—Oh, it's coming down!
sentences.zh: 她等了一会儿，没再听见什么动静；最后传来小车轮子滚动的声音，还有许多人的声音一起说话。她听出了这些话：“另一架梯子在哪儿？——咦，我只带了一架来；比尔拿着另一架——比尔！把它拿到这儿来，小子！——来，把它架在这个角上——不行，先把它们绑在一起——还不够一半高呢——哦！这样就够好了，别那么讲究——来，比尔！抓住这根绳子——屋顶受得住吗？——当心那块松动的石板——哦，它要掉下来了！

sentences.text: Heads below!" (a loud crash)—"Now, who did that?—It was Bill, I fancy—Who's to go down the chimney?—Nay, I shan't!
sentences.zh: 下面的人小心！”（哗啦一声巨响）——“是谁干的？——我看是比尔——谁下去烟囱？——不，我不去！

sentences.text: You do it!—That I won't, then!—Bill's got to go down—Here, Bill! the master says you've got to go down the chimney!"
sentences.zh: 你去！——那我才不去呢！——比尔得下去——来，比尔！主人说叫你下烟囱！”

hints.zh: 辨认出、听清楚；不是“做出”。
hints.en: Made out means 'managed to hear or understand', not 'produced'.

hints.zh: 比尔，白兔的帮手，一只小壁虎。
hints.en: Bill, one of the Rabbit's helpers, a small lizard.

introduction.zh: 窗口那条胳膊谁也搬不动，外面的人只好搬来梯子，围着房子七嘴八舌地商量。商量到后来，谁都不愿意揽下那件差事。他们最后打算派谁去？
introduction.en: Nobody can move the arm in the window, so the crowd outside brings ladders and argues about what to do. In the end they agree on one plan: a small animal must go down the chimney. Who is chosen?

quiz.question: What do the voices outside finally decide to do?
options: Burn the house down at once.
Send Bill down the chimney.
Pull the arm out with a rope.

feedback.zh: 众人商量到最后，一致认定“比尔得下去”，还喊他主人的命令来压他。
feedback.en: After all the arguing the crowd agrees that Bill must go down the chimney.

quiz.question: What does Alice wish while she waits?
options: That they could pull her out of the window.
That she had a ladder of her own.
That the crowd would go away.

feedback.zh: 她说“至于把我从窗口拉出去，我巴不得他们能办到”，因为她一刻也不想再待在里面。
feedback.en: She says she only wishes they could pull her out of the window, as she hates being stuck inside.

grammar.excerpt: I wonder what they'll do next

focus.zh: wonder 后接 what 从句，从句用陈述语序：what they'll do，而不是 what will they do。
focus.en: Wonder takes a wh-clause in statement order: what they'll do, not what will they do.

paragraphs.text: "Oh! so Bill's got to come down the chimney, has he?" said Alice to herself. "Why, they seem to put everything upon Bill! I wouldn't be in Bill's place for a good deal: this fireplace is narrow, to be sure; but I think I can kick a little!"

sentences.text: "Oh! so Bill's got to come down the chimney, has he?" said Alice to herself.
sentences.zh: “哦！这么说比尔得下烟囱，是吗？”爱丽丝自言自语。

sentences.text: "Why, they seem to put everything upon Bill!
sentences.zh: “哼，他们好像什么事都往比尔身上推！

sentences.text: I wouldn't be in Bill's place for a good deal: this fireplace is narrow, to be sure; but I think I can kick a little!"
sentences.zh: 给我一大笔钱我也不愿站在比尔的位置上：这壁炉确实窄；不过我想我还是能踢上一脚的！”

hints.zh: 把什么事都推给比尔；put upon 这里指“把活儿推给某人”。
hints.en: Put everything upon Bill means 'load every job onto Bill'.

paragraphs.text: She drew her foot as far down the chimney as she could, and waited till she heard a little animal (she couldn't guess of what sort it was) scratching and scrambling about in the chimney close above her: then, saying to herself, "This is Bill," she gave one sharp kick, and waited to see what would happen next.

sentences.text: She drew her foot as far down the chimney as she could, and waited till she heard a little animal (she couldn't guess of what sort it was) scratching and scrambling about in the chimney close above her: then, saying to herself, "This is Bill," she gave one sharp kick, and waited to see what would happen next.
sentences.zh: 她尽量把脚往烟囱下面伸，等着听见一只小动物（她猜不出是什么动物）在她头顶上方的烟囱里又抓又爬；然后，她对自己说了句“这就是比尔”，猛地踢了一脚，等着看会发生什么。

paragraphs.text: The first thing she heard was a general chorus of "There goes Bill!" then the Rabbit's voice alone—"Catch him, you by the hedge!" then silence, and then another confusion of voices—"Hold up his head—Brandy now—Don't choke him— How was it, old fellow? What happened to you? Tell us all about it!"

sentences.text: The first thing she heard was a general chorus of "There goes Bill!" then the Rabbit's voice alone—"Catch him, you by the hedge!" then silence, and then another confusion of voices—"Hold up his head—Brandy now—Don't choke him— How was it, old fellow?
sentences.zh: 她首先听到的是一片齐声的喊叫：“比尔上去了！”接着只有白兔的声音——“接住他，你这树篱边的家伙！”然后是一片安静，接着又是一片乱糟糟的声音——“扶住他的头——快拿白兰地——别让他噎着——怎么回事，老伙计？

sentences.text: What happened to you?
sentences.zh: 你遇到什么了？

sentences.text: Tell us all about it!"
sentences.zh: 快跟我们说说！”

hints.zh: 白兰地；当时被当作提神醒脑的药，给昏过去的人喝。
hints.en: Brandy, then used as a reviving medicine for someone who has fainted.

paragraphs.text: Last came a little feeble, squeaking voice, ("That's Bill," thought Alice,) "Well, I hardly know—No more, thank ye; I'm better now—but I'm a deal too flustered to tell you—all I know is, something comes at me like a Jack-in-the-box, and up I goes like a sky-rocket!"

sentences.text: Last came a little feeble, squeaking voice, ("That's Bill," thought Alice,) "Well, I hardly know—No more, thank ye; I'm better now—but I'm a deal too flustered to tell you—all I know is, something comes at me like a Jack-in-the-box, and up I goes like a sky-rocket!"
sentences.zh: 最后传来一个微弱尖细的声音，（“那是比尔。”爱丽丝心想，）“嗯，我也说不清——不喝了，谢谢你；我现在好些了——可我实在慌得厉害，说不清楚——我只知道，有个东西像玩偶匣里的弹簧小人一样朝我冲过来，我就嗖地一下飞了上去，像支冲天炮！”

hints.zh: 玩偶匣：一打开盖子就弹出小人的玩具；比尔拿它比喻突然冲上来的东西。
hints.en: A Jack-in-the-box is a toy figure that springs out when the lid opens; Bill compares it to what rushed at him.

hints.zh: a deal 表示“很、非常”：慌得实在太厉害，不是“一笔交易”。
hints.en: A deal here means 'very much': he is far too flustered to explain, with no bargain involved.

paragraphs.text: "So you did, old fellow!" said the others.

sentences.text: "So you did, old fellow!" said the others.
sentences.zh: “你确实飞上去了，老伙计！”其他人说。

paragraphs.text: "We must burn the house down!" said the Rabbit's voice; and Alice called out as loud as she could, "If you do, I'll set Dinah at you!"

sentences.text: "We must burn the house down!" said the Rabbit's voice; and Alice called out as loud as she could, "If you do, I'll set Dinah at you!"
sentences.zh: “我们得把房子烧掉！”白兔的声音说；爱丽丝用尽力气喊道：“你们要是敢，我就放黛娜来咬你们！”

hints.zh: 放黛娜去咬你；set a dog at someone 就是放狗去追咬某人。
hints.en: Set Dinah at you: to set a dog at someone is to send it to attack them.

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝把脚伸进烟囱，等着那个小东西爬近。外面的人一听动静就乱了套，喊声、脚步声和追问响成一片。他们还会想出什么办法来对付屋里的大家伙？
introduction.en: Alice stretches her foot down the chimney and waits for the small animal to come closer. Outside, the crowd panics at the noise: brandy is fetched, advice is shouted, and someone mentions burning the house. What will they try next?

quiz.question: What does Alice do when she hears the animal in the chimney?
options: She climbs up the chimney herself.
She calls Dinah to come and help.
She gives one sharp kick.

feedback.zh: 她听见小动物在头顶上方又抓又爬，说了句“这就是比尔”，就狠狠踢了一脚。
feedback.en: Hearing the animal scramble above her, she says 'This is Bill' and gives one sharp kick.

quiz.question: What does the Rabbit suggest when Alice cannot be moved?
options: Burning the house down.
Fetching a much longer ladder.
Sending for the Duchess.

feedback.zh: 白兔喊道“我们得把房子烧掉”，爱丽丝则回敬说要放黛娜去咬他们。
feedback.en: The Rabbit shouts 'We must burn the house down!', and Alice answers with a threat about Dinah.

grammar.excerpt: so Bill's got to come down the chimney

focus.zh: 's got to 就是 has got to，表示“不得不、必须”；这里爱丽丝在复述外面人的结论。
focus.en: 'S got to is has got to, meaning 'must'; Alice is repeating the crowd's decision.

paragraphs.text: There was a dead silence instantly, and Alice thought to herself, "I wonder what they will do next! If they had any sense, they'd take the roof off." After a minute or two, they began moving about again, and Alice heard the Rabbit say, "A barrowful will do, to begin with."

sentences.text: There was a dead silence instantly, and Alice thought to herself, "I wonder what they will do next!
sentences.zh: 外面立刻一片死寂，爱丽丝心想：“我倒想知道他们下一步要干什么！

sentences.text: If they had any sense, they'd take the roof off."
sentences.zh: 他们要是有点脑子，就该把屋顶掀掉。”

sentences.text: After a minute or two, they began moving about again, and Alice heard the Rabbit say, "A barrowful will do, to begin with."
sentences.zh: 过了一两分钟，他们又开始走动起来，爱丽丝听见白兔说：“先来一独轮车就够了。”

hints.zh: 一独轮车（的量）；barrow 指手推的独轮车。
hints.en: A barrowful is as much as a wheelbarrow holds.

paragraphs.text: "A barrowful of what?" thought Alice; but she had not long to doubt, for the next moment a shower of little pebbles came rattling in at the window, and some of them hit her in the face. "I'll put a stop to this," she said to herself, and shouted out, "You'd better not do that again!" which produced another dead silence.

sentences.text: "A barrowful of what?" thought Alice; but she had not long to doubt, for the next moment a shower of little pebbles came rattling in at the window, and some of them hit her in the face.
sentences.zh: “一独轮车什么？”爱丽丝想；不过她没疑惑多久，因为紧接着就有一阵小石子从窗口哗啦啦地飞进来，有几颗还打在她脸上。

sentences.text: "I'll put a stop to this," she said to herself, and shouted out, "You'd better not do that again!" which produced another dead silence.
sentences.zh: “我得把这事制止住。”她自言自语，然后大声喊道：“你们最好别再扔了！”这句话又换来一片死寂。

hints.zh: 把这件事制止住；不是“停下来放东西”。
hints.en: Put a stop to this means 'end this', not 'stop to put something down'.

paragraphs.text: Alice noticed with some surprise that the pebbles were all turning into little cakes as they lay on the floor, and a bright idea came into her head. "If I eat one of these cakes," she thought, "it's sure to make some change in my size; and as it can't possibly make me larger, it must make me smaller, I suppose."

sentences.text: Alice noticed with some surprise that the pebbles were all turning into little cakes as they lay on the floor, and a bright idea came into her head.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝有些惊讶地发现，那些石子落在地上，全都变成了小蛋糕；她脑子里忽然闪过一个好主意。

sentences.text: "If I eat one of these cakes," she thought, "it's sure to make some change in my size; and as it can't possibly make me larger, it must make me smaller, I suppose."
sentences.zh: “要是我吃一块这样的蛋糕，”她想，“它一定会让我的身体发生变化；既然它不可能让我变得更大，那我想，它准会让我变小。”

paragraphs.text: So she swallowed one of the cakes, and was delighted to find that she began shrinking directly. As soon as she was small enough to get through the door, she ran out of the house, and found quite a crowd of little animals and birds waiting outside. The poor little Lizard, Bill, was in the middle, being held up by two guinea-pigs, who were giving it something out of a bottle. They all made a rush at Alice the moment she appeared; but she ran off as hard as she could, and soon found herself safe in a thick wood.

sentences.text: So she swallowed one of the cakes, and was delighted to find that she began shrinking directly.
sentences.zh: 于是她吞下一块蛋糕，高兴地发现自己立刻开始缩小。

sentences.text: As soon as she was small enough to get through the door, she ran out of the house, and found quite a crowd of little animals and birds waiting outside.
sentences.zh: 等她小到能从门口出去时，她就跑出房子，看见外面等着好大一群小动物和鸟。

sentences.text: The poor little Lizard, Bill, was in the middle, being held up by two guinea-pigs, who were giving it something out of a bottle.
sentences.zh: 可怜的小蜥蜴比尔在正中间，被两只豚鼠扶着，它们正从瓶子里喂它什么东西。

sentences.text: They all made a rush at Alice the moment she appeared; but she ran off as hard as she could, and soon found herself safe in a thick wood.
sentences.zh: 她一出现，他们全都朝她冲过来；可她拼命地跑，很快就发现自己安全地待在一片茂密的树林里。

hints.zh: 豚鼠，也叫荷兰猪；这里是被叫来帮忙的小动物。
hints.en: Guinea-pigs, small rodents called in to help hold Bill up.

introduction.zh: 窗外安静了一会儿，紧接着飞进来一阵小石子，有几颗打在她脸上。落在地上的石头瞧着不太对劲。爱丽丝盯着它们，忽然想到一个也许能让她脱身的办法。
introduction.en: The window goes quiet, then a shower of little pebbles rattles in and some hit Alice in the face. Strangely, the pebbles change as they lie on the floor. Looking at them, Alice gets an idea that might set her free.

quiz.question: What happens to the pebbles that come through the window?
options: They turn into mushrooms.
They vanish as soon as they land.
They turn into little cakes on the floor.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝惊讶地看见，石子落地后全都变成了小蛋糕。
feedback.en: Alice notices with surprise that the pebbles on the floor turn into little cakes.

quiz.question: Why does Alice eat one of the cakes?
options: She wants to grow big enough to frighten the crowd.
She is hungry after shouting at the crowd.
She expects it to change her size and make her smaller.

feedback.zh: 她推断蛋糕一定会改变身材，既然不能变大，那就只能变小，于是吞了一块。
feedback.en: She reasons that a cake must change her size; as it cannot make her larger, it must make her smaller.

grammar.excerpt: If I eat one of these cakes

focus.zh: if 从句用一般现在时 eat，主句说她预期的结果；这里她在推算吃下蛋糕的后果。
focus.en: The if-clause uses the present tense eat, and the main clause gives the result she expects.

paragraphs.text: "The first thing I've got to do," said Alice to herself, as she wandered about in the wood, "is to grow to my right size again; and the second thing is to find my way into that lovely garden. I think that will be the best plan."

sentences.text: "The first thing I've got to do," said Alice to herself, as she wandered about in the wood, "is to grow to my right size again; and the second thing is to find my way into that lovely garden.
sentences.zh: “我首先要做的，”爱丽丝在树林里游荡时自言自语，“是重新长回我该有的大小；第二件事，是找到路，走进那座可爱的花园。

sentences.text: I think that will be the best plan."
sentences.zh: 我想这是最好的办法。”

paragraphs.text: It sounded an excellent plan, no doubt, and very neatly and simply arranged; the only difficulty was, that she had not the smallest idea how to set about it; and while she was peering about anxiously among the trees, a little sharp bark just over her head made her look up in a great hurry.

sentences.text: It sounded an excellent plan, no doubt, and very neatly and simply arranged; the only difficulty was, that she had not the smallest idea how to set about it; and while she was peering about anxiously among the trees, a little sharp bark just over her head made her look up in a great hurry.
sentences.zh: 这计划听上去好极了，毫无疑问，安排得又干净又简单；唯一的难处是，她完全不知道该怎么着手；她正焦急地在树间张望，忽然头顶上方传来一声尖细的叫声，她连忙抬起头。

hints.zh: 着手去做、开始动手；set about 后面接要做的事。
hints.en: To set about it means 'to begin doing it'.

paragraphs.text: An enormous puppy was looking down at her with large round eyes, and feebly stretching out one paw, trying to touch her. "Poor little thing!" said Alice, in a coaxing tone, and she tried hard to whistle to it; but she was terribly frightened all the time at the thought that it might be hungry, in which case it would be very likely to eat her up in spite of all her coaxing.

sentences.text: An enormous puppy was looking down at her with large round eyes, and feebly stretching out one paw, trying to touch her.
sentences.zh: 一只巨大的小狗正用圆圆的大眼睛低头看着她，还虚弱地伸出一只爪子，想碰碰她。

sentences.text: "Poor little thing!" said Alice, in a coaxing tone, and she tried hard to whistle to it; but she was terribly frightened all the time at the thought that it might be hungry, in which case it would be very likely to eat her up in spite of all her coaxing.
sentences.zh: “可怜的小东西！”爱丽丝用哄劝的语气说，还使劲想对它吹口哨；可她一直害怕得要命，生怕它饿了，真要是那样，那它多半会不顾她怎么哄，把她吃掉。

hints.zh: 小狗、狗崽；这里是一只体型大得吓人的狗崽。
hints.en: A puppy here is a dog so young that its size is startling.

hints.zh: 要是那样的话；承接前面的假设，说明随之而来的结果。
hints.en: In which case means 'if that were so', pointing to the result of the guess.

paragraphs.text: Hardly knowing what she did, she picked up a little bit of stick, and held it out to the puppy; whereupon the puppy jumped into the air off all its feet at once, with a yelp of delight, and rushed at the stick, and made believe to worry it; then Alice dodged behind a great thistle, to keep herself from being run over; and the moment she appeared on the other side, the puppy made another rush at the stick, and tumbled head over heels in its hurry to get hold of it: then Alice, thinking it was very like having a game of play with a carthorse, and expecting every moment to be trampled under its feet, ran round the thistle again; then the puppy began a series of short charges at the stick, running a very little way forwards each time and a long way back, and barking hoarsely all the while, till at last it sat down a good way off, panting, with its tongue hanging out of its mouth, and its great eyes half shut. This seemed to Alice a good opportunity for making her escape, so she set off at once, and ran till she was quite tired and out of breath, and till the puppy's bark sounded quite faint in the distance.

sentences.text: Hardly knowing what she did, she picked up a little bit of stick, and held it out to the puppy; whereupon the puppy jumped into the air off all its feet at once, with a yelp of delight, and rushed at the stick, and made believe to worry it; then Alice dodged behind a great thistle, to keep herself from being run over; and the moment she appeared on the other side, the puppy made another rush at the stick, and tumbled head over heels in its hurry to get hold of it: then Alice, thinking it was very like having a game of play with a carthorse, and expecting every moment to be trampled under its feet, ran round the thistle again; then the puppy began a series of short charges at the stick, running a very little way forwards each time and a long way back, and barking hoarsely all the while, till at last it sat down a good way off, panting, with its tongue hanging out of its mouth, and its great eyes half shut.
sentences.zh: 她几乎不知道自己在做什么，捡起一小根树枝，伸到小狗面前；小狗立刻四脚一齐跳起，欢喜地叫了一声，扑向树枝，假装撕咬起来；爱丽丝躲到一棵大蓟后面，免得被它撞倒；她刚在另一边露面，小狗又朝树枝冲过来，急急忙忙地翻了个跟头；爱丽丝觉得这简直像在跟一匹拉车的马玩耍，随时都可能被它踩在脚下，便又绕着大蓟跑；小狗开始一次次短促地扑向树枝，每次往前跑一点点，又退回去老远，一边跑一边沙哑地叫着，最后它在老远的地方坐下来，伸着舌头直喘气，大眼睛半睁半闭。

sentences.text: This seemed to Alice a good opportunity for making her escape, so she set off at once, and ran till she was quite tired and out of breath, and till the puppy's bark sounded quite faint in the distance.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝觉得这是个逃走的好机会，于是立刻动身，一直跑到又累又喘，直到小狗的叫声在远处变得十分微弱。

introduction.zh: 逃进树林，爱丽丝给自己定了两件事：先变回原来的大小，再找到进那座可爱花园的路。可她还没想好怎么做，头顶忽然传来一声尖细的叫声。
introduction.en: Safe in the wood, Alice sets herself two tasks: grow back to her right size, and find her way into the lovely garden. Before she can plan how, a sharp little bark sounds just above her head.

quiz.question: What two things does Alice decide she must do?
options: Find food and then sleep in the wood.
Grow back to her right size and find the garden.
Find Dinah and go back home.

feedback.zh: 她给自己定下两件事：先长回原来的大小，再找到进那座花园的路。
feedback.en: She sets herself two tasks: grow back to her right size, then find the way into the garden.

quiz.question: Why is Alice frightened of the puppy while she speaks kindly to it?
options: It might be hungry and eat her up.
It belongs to the White Rabbit.
It barks too loudly for her ears.

feedback.zh: 她一边哄它，一边怕它饿了——真是那样，再哄也没用，它很可能把她吃掉。
feedback.en: She coaxes it, yet fears that a hungry puppy would eat her in spite of all her coaxing.

grammar.excerpt: she had not the smallest idea how to set about it

focus.zh: how to set about it 是“疑问词 + 不定式”，说明她“不知道该怎么着手”这件事。
focus.en: How to set about it is a wh-word plus infinitive, telling us what she has no idea about.
