paragraphs.text: "And yet what a dear little puppy it was!" said Alice, as she leant against a buttercup to rest herself, and fanned herself with one of the leaves: "I should have liked teaching it tricks very much, if—if I'd only been the right size to do it! Oh dear! I 'd nearly forgotten that I've got to grow up again! Let me see—how is it to be managed? I suppose I ought to eat or drink something or other; but the great question is, what?"

sentences.text: "And yet what a dear little puppy it was!" said Alice, as she leant against a buttercup to rest herself, and fanned herself with one of the leaves: "I should have liked teaching it tricks very much, if—if I'd only been the right size to do it!
sentences.zh: “可它真是只可爱的小狗啊！”爱丽丝靠着一株毛茛歇脚，用一片叶子扇着风说，“我真愿意教它几套把戏，要是——要是我有合适的大小来教它就好了！

sentences.text: Oh dear!
sentences.zh: 哎呀！

sentences.text: I 'd nearly forgotten that I've got to grow up again!
sentences.zh: 我差点忘了，我还得重新长大呢！

sentences.text: Let me see—how is it to be managed?
sentences.zh: 让我想想——这该怎么才能办到呢？

sentences.text: I suppose I ought to eat or drink something or other; but the great question is, what?"
sentences.zh: 我想我总得吃点或喝点什么才行；可最大的问题是，吃什么、喝什么？”

hints.zh: 毛茛，开黄花的小野草；她得靠着一株才歇得住，可见自己有多小。
hints.en: A buttercup, a small yellow wild flower; she can lean on one, which shows how tiny she is.

hints.zh: manage 这里不是“管理”，而是“设法做到”：这事该怎么办呢？
hints.en: Managed here means 'brought about', not 'run or controlled': how is it to be done?

paragraphs.text: The great question certainly was, what? Alice looked all round her at the flowers and the blades of grass, but she could not see anything that looked like the right thing to eat or drink under the circumstances. There was a large mushroom growing near her, about the same height as herself; and when she had looked under it, and on both sides of it, and behind it, it occurred to her that she might as well look and see what was on the top of it.

sentences.text: The great question certainly was, what?
sentences.zh: 最大的问题确实是，什么？

sentences.text: Alice looked all round her at the flowers and the blades of grass, but she could not see anything that looked like the right thing to eat or drink under the circumstances.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝环顾四周的花和草叶，可在这种情形下，她看不出有什么东西像是能吃的或能喝的。

sentences.text: There was a large mushroom growing near her, about the same height as herself; and when she had looked under it, and on both sides of it, and behind it, it occurred to her that she might as well look and see what was on the top of it.
sentences.zh: 她身旁长着一朵大蘑菇，差不多和她一样高；她往蘑菇底下看过，两边看过，后面也看过，这才想到，不妨也看看蘑菇上面有什么。

paragraphs.text: She stretched herself up on tiptoe, and peeped over the edge of the mushroom, and her eyes immediately met those of a large blue caterpillar, that was sitting on the top with its arms folded, quietly smoking a long hookah, and taking not the smallest notice of her or of anything else.

sentences.text: She stretched herself up on tiptoe, and peeped over the edge of the mushroom, and her eyes immediately met those of a large blue caterpillar, that was sitting on the top with its arms folded, quietly smoking a long hookah, and taking not the smallest notice of her or of anything else.
sentences.zh: 她踮起脚，探身从蘑菇边缘望过去，目光立刻遇到了一只蓝色的大毛毛虫的眼睛。它正盘着胳膊坐在蘑菇顶上，静静地抽着一根长长的水烟筒，对她、对别的一切都毫不在意。

hints.zh: 毛毛虫，这里是一只蓝色的大毛毛虫，坐在蘑菇顶上抽水烟。
hints.en: A caterpillar, here a large blue one sitting on the mushroom and smoking.

hints.zh: 水烟筒：烟气先经过水再吸入口中的长管烟具。
hints.en: A hookah is a long tube pipe in which smoke passes through water before it is breathed in.

introduction.zh: 靠着毛茛休息时，爱丽丝才想起自己还得再长大一次。她四下张望，想找点能吃能喝的东西，最后把目光落在身边那朵大蘑菇上。蘑菇顶上，坐着什么呢？
introduction.en: Resting against a buttercup, Alice remembers that she still has to grow up again. She looks around for something to eat or drink and settles her eyes on a large mushroom beside her. What is sitting on top of it?

quiz.question: What problem is Alice trying to solve?
options: How to teach the puppy some tricks.
How to get back into the lovely garden.
What to eat or drink so that she can grow again.

feedback.zh: 她认定总得吃点或喝点什么才能重新长大，可最大的问题是不知道选什么。
feedback.en: She decides she must eat or drink something, but the great question is what.

quiz.question: What does Alice see on top of the mushroom?
options: A large blue caterpillar smoking a hookah.
The White Rabbit with his watch.
A little cake left by the crowd.

feedback.zh: 蘑菇顶上坐着一只蓝色的大毛毛虫，盘着手臂抽水烟，完全不理她。
feedback.en: On the mushroom sits a large blue caterpillar smoking a hookah, taking no notice of her.

grammar.excerpt: I should have liked teaching it tricks very much, if—if I'd only been the right size to do it

focus.zh: should have liked 与 if I'd been 都是与过去相反的虚拟：她当时并没有合适的大小。
focus.en: Should have liked and if I'd been are past unreal forms: she was not the right size at the time.

paragraphs.text: The Caterpillar and Alice looked at each other for some time in silence: at last the Caterpillar took the hookah out of its mouth, and addressed her in a languid, sleepy voice.

sentences.text: The Caterpillar and Alice looked at each other for some time in silence: at last the Caterpillar took the hookah out of its mouth, and addressed her in a languid, sleepy voice.
sentences.zh: 毛毛虫和爱丽丝一言不发地对看了好一会儿：最后，毛毛虫把水烟筒从嘴里抽出来，用慵懒、困倦的声音跟她说话。

hints.zh: 爱丽丝，本书主角，追着白兔掉进兔子洞的小姑娘。
hints.en: Alice, the girl who followed the White Rabbit down the hole and is the heroine of the book.

hints.zh: 毛毛虫，抽水烟、说话简短生硬，本章一直追问爱丽丝是谁的虫子。
hints.en: The Caterpillar, a hookah-smoking insect who keeps asking Alice who she is.

hints.zh: 水烟筒，一种用长管吸的烟具。
hints.en: A hookah: a water pipe smoked through a long tube.

paragraphs.text: "Who are you?" said the Caterpillar.

sentences.text: "Who are you?" said the Caterpillar.
sentences.zh: “你是谁？”毛毛虫说。

paragraphs.text: This was not an encouraging opening for a conversation. Alice replied, rather shyly, "I—I hardly know, sir, just at present—at least I know who I was when I got up this morning, but I think I must have been changed several times since then."

sentences.text: This was not an encouraging opening for a conversation.
sentences.zh: 这样的开场白，可不太利于谈下去。

sentences.text: Alice replied, rather shyly, "I—I hardly know, sir, just at present—at least I know who I was when I got up this morning, but I think I must have been changed several times since then."
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝相当羞怯地回答：“我——我眼下也说不清，先生——至少今天早上起床的时候，我还知道我是谁；可我想，从那以后我一定已经变过好几回了。”

paragraphs.text: "What do you mean by that?" said the Caterpillar sternly. "Explain yourself!"

sentences.text: "What do you mean by that?" said the Caterpillar sternly.
sentences.zh: “你这话是什么意思？”毛毛虫严厉地说。

sentences.text: "Explain yourself!"
sentences.zh: “把你自己解释清楚！”

hints.zh: 字面是“解释你自己”，通常的意思是“把你的意思说清楚”；毛毛虫故意按字面来理解。
hints.en: Literally 'explain yourself'; the usual meaning is 'make your meaning clear', but the Caterpillar takes it literally.

paragraphs.text: "I can't explain myself, I'm afraid, sir," said Alice, "because I'm not myself, you see."

sentences.text: "I can't explain myself, I'm afraid, sir," said Alice, "because I'm not myself, you see."
sentences.zh: “恐怕我没法解释我自己，先生，”爱丽丝说，“因为你看，我现在不是我自己了。”

paragraphs.text: "I don't see," said the Caterpillar.

sentences.text: "I don't see," said the Caterpillar.
sentences.zh: “我看不出来。”毛毛虫说。

paragraphs.text: "I'm afraid I can't put it more clearly," Alice replied very politely, "for I can't understand it myself to begin with; and being so many different sizes in a day is very confusing."

sentences.text: "I'm afraid I can't put it more clearly," Alice replied very politely, "for I can't understand it myself to begin with; and being so many different sizes in a day is very confusing."
sentences.zh: “恐怕我没法说得更清楚了，”爱丽丝非常有礼貌地回答，“因为这事我自己一开始就弄不明白；一天里变这么多个不同的尺寸，实在太让人糊涂了。”

paragraphs.text: "It isn't," said the Caterpillar.

sentences.text: "It isn't," said the Caterpillar.
sentences.zh: “一点也不糊涂。”毛毛虫说。

paragraphs.text: "Well, perhaps you haven't found it so yet," said Alice; "but when you have to turn into a chrysalis—you will some day, you know—and then after that into a butterfly, I should think you'll feel it a little queer, won't you?"

sentences.text: "Well, perhaps you haven't found it so yet," said Alice; "but when you have to turn into a chrysalis—you will some day, you know—and then after that into a butterfly, I should think you'll feel it a little queer, won't you?"
sentences.zh: “嗯，也许你还没觉得是这样，”爱丽丝说，“不过等你不得不变成蛹的时候——你知道，你总有一天会的——然后再变成蝴蝶，我想你多少会觉得有点别扭吧，是不是？

hints.zh: 蛹，毛毛虫变成蝴蝶之前的形态。
hints.en: A chrysalis: the pupa stage before a caterpillar becomes a butterfly.

paragraphs.text: "Not a bit," said the Caterpillar.

sentences.text: "Not a bit," said the Caterpillar.
sentences.zh: “一点也不。”毛毛虫说。

paragraphs.text: "Well, perhaps your feelings may be different," said Alice; "all I know is, it would feel very queer to me."

sentences.text: "Well, perhaps your feelings may be different," said Alice; "all I know is, it would feel very queer to me."
sentences.zh: “嗯，也许你的感觉跟我不一样，”爱丽丝说，“我只知道，要是换了我，会觉得非常别扭。”

hints.zh: 奇怪的、别扭的；这里指感觉很不自在。
hints.en: Strange or odd; here it means feeling uncomfortable.

paragraphs.text: "You!" said the Caterpillar contemptuously. "Who are you?"

sentences.text: "You!" said the Caterpillar contemptuously.
sentences.zh: “你！”毛毛虫轻蔑地说。

sentences.text: "Who are you?"
sentences.zh: “你是谁？”

paragraphs.text: Which brought them back again to the beginning of the conversation. Alice felt a little irritated at the Caterpillar's making such very short remarks, and she drew herself up and said, very gravely, "I think you ought to tell me who you are, first."

sentences.text: Which brought them back again to the beginning of the conversation.
sentences.zh: 于是他们又回到了这场对话的开头。

sentences.text: Alice felt a little irritated at the Caterpillar's making such very short remarks, and she drew herself up and said, very gravely, "I think you ought to tell me who you are, first."
sentences.zh: 毛毛虫总这样三言两语，爱丽丝有点恼了；她挺直身子，非常严肃地说：“我想，你应该先告诉我你是谁。”

paragraphs.text: "Why?" said the Caterpillar.

sentences.text: "Why?" said the Caterpillar.
sentences.zh: “为什么？”毛毛虫说。

introduction.zh: 蘑菇旁边，爱丽丝遇见一条抽水烟的毛毛虫。它慢吞吞地开口，只问了一句“你是谁？”。可爱丽丝刚变过好几次大小，连自己都答不上来；她越解释，对方好像越不认账。
introduction.en: Beside a mushroom Alice meets a Caterpillar smoking a hookah. It asks her, slowly, who she is. Alice has changed size so often that day that she cannot really answer, and nothing she says seems to satisfy it.

quiz.question: Why can't Alice say who she is?
options: She has changed size several times that day.
She is too frightened to speak.
She has forgotten her own name.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝说，早上起床时她还知道自己是谁，可从那以后一定已经变过好几回，所以现在答不上来。
feedback.en: Alice says she knew who she was that morning but must have changed several times since, so she cannot answer.

quiz.question: What does Alice find irritating about the Caterpillar?
options: It laughs at her size.
It keeps smoking without a word.
It answers only with very short remarks.

feedback.zh: 毛毛虫总用“我看不出来”“一点也不”这样的短话回她，爱丽丝因此有点恼火，才挺直身子反问它。
feedback.en: The Caterpillar answers with short remarks like 'I don't see' and 'Not a bit', which is what irritates Alice.

grammar.excerpt: I think I must have been changed several times since then

focus.zh: must have been changed 是“情态动词 + have + 过去分词”，表示对过去的推测：她认定自己一定已经变过好几回。
focus.en: Must have been changed is a modal with have and a past participle: it shows Alice's firm guess that the change really happened.

paragraphs.text: Here was another puzzling question; and, as Alice could not think of any good reason, and as the Caterpillar seemed to be in a very unpleasant state of mind, she turned away.

sentences.text: Here was another puzzling question; and, as Alice could not think of any good reason, and as the Caterpillar seemed to be in a very unpleasant state of mind, she turned away.
sentences.zh: 这又是一个让人犯难的问题；爱丽丝想不出什么好理由，而毛毛虫似乎心情很不好，于是她转身走开了。

paragraphs.text: "Come back!" the Caterpillar called after her. "I've something important to say!"

sentences.text: "Come back!" the Caterpillar called after her.
sentences.zh: “回来！”毛毛虫在她身后喊。

sentences.text: "I've something important to say!"
sentences.zh: “我有要紧的话要说！”

paragraphs.text: This sounded promising, certainly: Alice turned and came back again.

sentences.text: This sounded promising, certainly: Alice turned and came back again.
sentences.zh: 这话听起来倒确实有希望：爱丽丝转过身，又走了回来。

paragraphs.text: "Keep your temper," said the Caterpillar.

sentences.text: "Keep your temper," said the Caterpillar.
sentences.zh: “沉住气。”毛毛虫说。

hints.zh: 沉住气，别发脾气。
hints.en: Keep your temper: stay calm and do not get angry.

paragraphs.text: "Is that all?" said Alice, swallowing down her anger as well as she could.

sentences.text: "Is that all?" said Alice, swallowing down her anger as well as she could.
sentences.zh: “就这些？”爱丽丝说，尽力把怒气咽下去。

hints.zh: 把（怒气）咽下去，强忍下去。
hints.en: Swallowing down: forcing her anger down and holding it in.

paragraphs.text: "No," said the Caterpillar.

sentences.text: "No," said the Caterpillar.
sentences.zh: “不是。”毛毛虫说。

paragraphs.text: Alice thought she might as well wait, as she had nothing else to do, and perhaps after all it might tell her something worth hearing. For some minutes it puffed away without speaking, but at last it unfolded its arms, took the hookah out of its mouth again, and said, "So you think you're changed, do you?"

sentences.text: Alice thought she might as well wait, as she had nothing else to do, and perhaps after all it might tell her something worth hearing.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝想，反正自己也没别的事可做，不如就等着；说不定它终究会告诉她一些值得一听的事。

sentences.text: For some minutes it puffed away without speaking, but at last it unfolded its arms, took the hookah out of its mouth again, and said, "So you think you're changed, do you?"
sentences.zh: 它一连几分钟只顾喷烟，一声不响；后来终于伸开双臂，又把水烟筒从嘴里取出来，说：“那么，你认为自己变了，是吗？”

paragraphs.text: "I'm afraid I am, sir," said Alice; "I can't remember things as I used—and I don't keep the same size for ten minutes together!"

sentences.text: "I'm afraid I am, sir," said Alice; "I can't remember things as I used—and I don't keep the same size for ten minutes together!"
sentences.zh: “恐怕是这样，先生，”爱丽丝说，“我记不住事情了，不像从前那样——而且我连十分钟都保持不住同一个尺寸！”

paragraphs.text: "Can't remember what things?" said the Caterpillar.

sentences.text: "Can't remember what things?" said the Caterpillar.
sentences.zh: “记不住什么事情？”毛毛虫说。

paragraphs.text: "Well, I've tried to say 'How doth the little busy bee,' but it all came different!" Alice replied in a very melancholy voice.

sentences.text: "Well, I've tried to say 'How doth the little busy bee,' but it all came different!"
sentences.zh: “嗯，我想背‘小小蜜蜂多勤劳’，可背出来全变了样！”

sentences.text: Alice replied in a very melancholy voice.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝用非常忧郁的声音回答。

hints.target: How doth the little busy bee
hints.zh: 《小小蜜蜂多勤劳》，瓦茨的儿童诗，原诗劝孩子勤快；爱丽丝背出来的却是另一套。doth 是古体的 does。
hints.en: The opening of Isaac Watts's poem 'How Doth the Little Busy Bee'; doth is an old form of does.

hints.zh: 忧郁的、伤感的。
hints.en: Sad and low in spirits.

paragraphs.text: "Repeat 'You are old, Father William,'" said the Caterpillar.

sentences.text: "Repeat 'You are old, Father William,'" said the Caterpillar.
sentences.zh: “背一背‘你老了，威廉爸爸’。”毛毛虫说。

hints.zh: 《你老了，威廉爸爸》，一首戏仿诗，原诗劝老人安分，这里的老先生却一个劲儿卖弄本事。
hints.en: A parody of Southey's poem 'The Old Man's Comforts'; this old man boasts instead of preaching.

paragraphs.text: Alice folded her hands, and began:—

sentences.text: Alice folded her hands, and began:—
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝双手交叠，开口念道：——

paragraphs.text: "You are old, Father William," the young man said, "And your hair has become very white; And yet you incessantly stand on your head— Do you think, at your age, it is right?"

sentences.text: "You are old, Father William," the young man said, "And your hair has become very white; And yet you incessantly stand on your head— Do you think, at your age, it is right?"
sentences.zh: “你老了，威廉爸爸，”年轻人说，“你的头发已经白得很；可你还是不停地拿大顶——你觉得，你这把年纪，这样合适吗？”

paragraphs.text: "In my youth," Father William replied to his son, "I feared it might injure the brain; But now that I'm perfectly sure I have none, Why, I do it again and again."

sentences.text: "In my youth," Father William replied to his son, "I feared it might injure the brain; But now that I'm perfectly sure I have none, Why, I do it again and again."
sentences.zh: “我年轻的时候，”威廉爸爸回答儿子，“也怕这样会伤到脑子；可如今我确信自己压根没有脑子，所以嘛，我就一遍又一遍地做。”

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝转身要走，毛毛虫却在背后叫住她，说有话要讲。她回来等着，等到的却只有一句“沉住气”。这条虫子到底要说什么？
introduction.en: Alice turns to leave, but the Caterpillar calls her back: it has something important to say. She comes back and waits, and what she gets is 'Keep your temper'. What is the creature really after?

quiz.question: Why does Alice decide to wait?
options: She has nothing else to do and hopes to hear something worth hearing.
She is afraid to walk away from the mushroom.
The Caterpillar offers her a share of the hookah.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝想，反正没别的事可做，不如等等，说不定它终究会说些值得一听的话。
feedback.en: Alice waits because she has nothing else to do and hopes the Caterpillar may yet say something worth hearing.

quiz.question: What is the important thing the Caterpillar has to say?
options: That Alice should keep her temper.
That Alice should recite a poem.
That Alice should eat the mushroom.

feedback.zh: 毛毛虫叫住她，郑重说出的要紧话只有一句：“沉住气。”爱丽丝忍不住反问“就这些？”。
feedback.en: The Caterpillar calls her back only to say 'Keep your temper', and Alice asks whether that is all.

grammar.excerpt: Alice thought she might as well wait

focus.zh: might as well 后接动词原形，意思是“反正没别的可做，不如……”，本句说她索性等着。
focus.en: Might as well plus a bare verb means 'there is no better reason not to, so…'; here Alice decides to wait.

paragraphs.text: "You are old," said the youth, "as I mentioned before, And have grown most uncommonly fat; Yet you turned a back-somersault in at the door— Pray, what is the reason of that?"

sentences.text: "You are old," said the youth, "as I mentioned before, And have grown most uncommonly fat; Yet you turned a back-somersault in at the door— Pray, what is the reason of that?"
sentences.zh: “你老了，”年轻人说，“这我先前就说过，而且你胖得实在不寻常；可你进门时还翻了个后空翻——请问，这又是怎么回事？”

hints.zh: 后空翻，向后翻的跟头。
hints.en: A backward somersault.

paragraphs.text: "In my youth," said the sage, as he shook his grey locks, "I kept all my limbs very supple By the use of this ointment—one shilling the box— Allow me to sell you a couple?"

sentences.text: "In my youth," said the sage, as he shook his grey locks, "I kept all my limbs very supple By the use of this ointment—one shilling the box— Allow me to sell you a couple?"
sentences.zh: “我年轻的时候，”长者晃着灰白的头发说，“靠用这种药膏，把四肢保持得非常柔软——一先令一盒——让我卖你两盒好不好？”

hints.zh: 药膏、软膏。
hints.en: A cream or soft medicine rubbed on the skin.

hints.zh: 一先令一盒。先令是英国旧币制里的银币，这里老先生正兜售他的药膏。
hints.en: One shilling a box; a shilling was an old British silver coin, and the old man is trying to sell the ointment.

paragraphs.text: "You are old," said the youth, "and your jaws are too weak For anything tougher than suet; Yet you finished the goose, with the bones and the beak— Pray, how did you manage to do it?"

sentences.text: "You are old," said the youth, "and your jaws are too weak For anything tougher than suet; Yet you finished the goose, with the bones and the beak— Pray, how did you manage to do it?"
sentences.zh: “你老了，”年轻人说，“你的牙床连比板油硬一点的东西都嚼不动；可你把那只鹅连骨头带嘴全吃光了——请问，你是怎么做到的？”

hints.zh: 板油，牛羊腹部的硬脂肪，常用来做布丁。
hints.en: Suet: hard fat from beef or mutton, used in puddings.

paragraphs.text: "In my youth," said his father, "I took to the law, And argued each case with my wife; And the muscular strength, which it gave to my jaw, Has lasted the rest of my life."

sentences.text: "In my youth," said his father, "I took to the law, And argued each case with my wife; And the muscular strength, which it gave to my jaw, Has lasted the rest of my life."
sentences.zh: “我年轻的时候，”他父亲说，“我干上了法律这一行，每桩案子都跟我妻子争辩；而争辩给下颌添的那股力气，一直管了我后半辈子。”

hints.zh: 干起了法律这一行，当了律师。
hints.en: Took to the law: went into the legal profession.

paragraphs.text: "You are old," said the youth; "one would hardly suppose That your eye was as steady as ever; Yet you balanced an eel on the end of your nose— What made you so awfully clever?"

sentences.text: "You are old," said the youth; "one would hardly suppose That your eye was as steady as ever; Yet you balanced an eel on the end of your nose— What made you so awfully clever?"
sentences.zh: “你老了，”年轻人说，“谁也想不到你的眼神还跟从前一样稳；可你却在鼻尖上顶住了一条鳗鱼——你怎么会这么厉害？”

paragraphs.text: "I have answered three questions, and that is enough," Said his father; "don't give yourself airs! Do you think I can listen all day to such stuff? Be off, or I'll kick you down stairs!"

sentences.text: "I have answered three questions, and that is enough," Said his father; "don't give yourself airs!
sentences.zh: “我已经回答了三个问题，这就够了，”他父亲说，“你别摆架子！

sentences.text: Do you think I can listen all day to such stuff?
sentences.zh: 你以为我能整天听这些废话吗？

sentences.text: Be off, or I'll kick you down stairs!"
sentences.zh: 滚开，不然我就把你踢下楼去！”

hints.zh: 摆架子，自以为了不起。
hints.en: Give yourself airs: behave as if you are more important than you are.

paragraphs.text: "That is not said right," said the Caterpillar.

sentences.text: "That is not said right," said the Caterpillar.
sentences.zh: “背得不对。”毛毛虫说。

paragraphs.text: "Not quite right, I'm afraid," said Alice, timidly; "some of the words have got altered."

sentences.text: "Not quite right, I'm afraid," said Alice, timidly; "some of the words have got altered."
sentences.zh: “恐怕是不太对，”爱丽丝怯生生地说，“有些词给改掉了。”

paragraphs.text: "It is wrong from beginning to end," said the Caterpillar decidedly, and there was silence for some minutes.

sentences.text: "It is wrong from beginning to end," said the Caterpillar decidedly, and there was silence for some minutes.
sentences.zh: “从头到尾都错了。”毛毛虫断然说道，随后两人沉默了几分钟。

paragraphs.text: The Caterpillar was the first to speak.

sentences.text: The Caterpillar was the first to speak.
sentences.zh: 毛毛虫先开了口。

paragraphs.text: "What size do you want to be?" it asked.

sentences.text: "What size do you want to be?" it asked.
sentences.zh: “你想变成多大？”它问。

introduction.zh: 毛毛虫要爱丽丝背一首《你老了，威廉爸爸》。她合起双手念起来，可诗里那位老先生越念越离谱：翻跟头、卖药膏、连鹅骨头都嚼了。毛毛虫会怎么说？
introduction.en: The Caterpillar asks Alice to recite 'You are old, Father William'. She folds her hands and begins, and the old man in the poem grows stranger with every verse: somersaults, ointment for sale, a goose eaten bones and all.

quiz.question: What does the Caterpillar think of Alice's recitation?
options: It is wrong from beginning to end.
It is word-perfect.
Only a few words are wrong.

feedback.zh: 毛毛虫听完，断然说这首诗“从头到尾都错了”，随后两人沉默了几分钟。
feedback.en: The Caterpillar says the recitation is wrong from beginning to end, and then there is silence for some minutes.

quiz.question: What does Father William say gave his jaw its strength?
options: Arguing cases in his law years.
Eating goose with the bones.
Standing on his head every day.

feedback.zh: 老威廉说，他年轻时干法律，每桩案子都跟妻子争辩，争辩给下颌添的力气一直管到后半辈子。
feedback.en: Father William says that arguing each case with his wife in his law years gave his jaw a strength that lasted the rest of his life.

grammar.excerpt: And the muscular strength, which it gave to my jaw, Has lasted the rest of my life.

focus.zh: 逗号后的 which 指前面的 the muscular strength，补一句这股力气是争辩练出来的；去掉它，主句照样成立。
focus.en: The which after the comma refers back to the muscular strength and adds a comment; without that clause the main sentence still stands.

paragraphs.text: "Oh, I'm not particular as to size," Alice hastily replied; "only one doesn't like changing so often, you know."

sentences.text: "Oh, I'm not particular as to size," Alice hastily replied; "only one doesn't like changing so often, you know."
sentences.zh: “哦，我对大小倒不讲究，”爱丽丝急忙回答，“只是你也知道，谁都不喜欢这样频繁地变来变去。”

hints.zh: 对……不讲究、不挑剔。
hints.en: Not particular as to: not fussy about.

paragraphs.text: "I don't know," said the Caterpillar.

sentences.text: "I don't know," said the Caterpillar.
sentences.zh: “我不知道。”毛毛虫说。

paragraphs.text: Alice said nothing: she had never been so much contradicted in all her life before, and she felt that she was losing her temper.

sentences.text: Alice said nothing: she had never been so much contradicted in all her life before, and she felt that she was losing her temper.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝什么也没说：她一辈子还没被人这样一次次顶撞过，她觉得自己快要发脾气了。

paragraphs.text: "Are you content now?" said the Caterpillar.

sentences.text: "Are you content now?" said the Caterpillar.
sentences.zh: “你现在满意了吗？”毛毛虫说。

paragraphs.text: "Well, I should like to be a little larger, sir, if you wouldn't mind," said Alice: "three inches is such a wretched height to be."

sentences.text: "Well, I should like to be a little larger, sir, if you wouldn't mind," said Alice: "three inches is such a wretched height to be."
sentences.zh: “嗯，要是你不介意的话，先生，我想再大一点点，”爱丽丝说，“三英寸这个身高实在太可怜了。”

hints.zh: 糟糕的、可怜的；这里形容三英寸这个身高太不像样。
hints.en: Miserable or pitiful; here a wretched height means a very poor one.

paragraphs.text: "It is a very good height indeed!" said the Caterpillar angrily, rearing itself upright as it spoke (it was exactly three inches high).

sentences.text: "It is a very good height indeed!" said the Caterpillar angrily, rearing itself upright as it spoke (it was exactly three inches high).
sentences.zh: “这身高确实好得很！”毛毛虫生气地说，一边说一边把身子直直地立起来（它正好三英寸高）。

hints.zh: 把身子直挺挺地立起来。
hints.en: Rearing itself upright: raising its body straight up.

paragraphs.text: "But I 'm not used to it!" pleaded poor Alice in a piteous tone. And she thought to herself, "I wish the creatures wouldn't be so easily offended."

sentences.text: "But I 'm not used to it!" pleaded poor Alice in a piteous tone.
sentences.zh: “可我还不习惯呀！”可怜的爱丽丝用哀怜的声调恳求道。

sentences.text: And she thought to herself, "I wish the creatures wouldn't be so easily offended."
sentences.zh: 她心里想：“但愿这些家伙别这么容易生气。”

hints.zh: 可怜的、哀怜的，形容声音让人听了心软。
hints.en: Piteous: sad and pitiful, asking for sympathy.

paragraphs.text: "You'll get used to it in time," said the Caterpillar; and it put the hookah into its mouth and began smoking again.

sentences.text: "You'll get used to it in time," said the Caterpillar; and it put the hookah into its mouth and began smoking again.
sentences.zh: “你慢慢就会习惯的。”毛毛虫说，又把水烟筒塞进嘴里，重新抽了起来。

paragraphs.text: This time Alice waited patiently until it chose to speak again. In a minute or two the Caterpillar took the hookah out of its mouth and yawned once or twice, and shook itself. Then it got down off the mushroom, and crawled away into the grass, merely remarking as it went, "One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow shorter."

sentences.text: This time Alice waited patiently until it chose to speak again.
sentences.zh: 这一回，爱丽丝耐心地等着，直到它愿意再开口。

sentences.text: In a minute or two the Caterpillar took the hookah out of its mouth and yawned once or twice, and shook itself.
sentences.zh: 过了一两分钟，毛毛虫把水烟筒从嘴里拿出来，打了一两个哈欠，抖了抖身子。

sentences.text: Then it got down off the mushroom, and crawled away into the grass, merely remarking as it went, "One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow shorter."
sentences.zh: 然后它从蘑菇上下来，爬进草丛，一路只说了句：“一边会让你长高，另一边会让你变矮。”

hints.zh: 说、评论；remark 作动词是“说道”，不是“注意到”。
hints.en: Remarking: saying or commenting; as a verb, remark means 'to say'.

paragraphs.text: "One side of what? The other side of what?" thought Alice to herself.

sentences.text: "One side of what?
sentences.zh: “什么的哪一边？

sentences.text: The other side of what?" thought Alice to herself.
sentences.zh: 那另一边又是什么的另一边呢？”爱丽丝心里想。

paragraphs.text: "Of the mushroom," said the Caterpillar, just as if she had asked it aloud; and in another moment it was out of sight.

sentences.text: "Of the mushroom," said the Caterpillar, just as if she had asked it aloud; and in another moment it was out of sight.
sentences.zh: “蘑菇的。”毛毛虫说，就好像她刚才大声问了出来似的；转眼间它就不见了。

introduction.zh: 毛毛虫问爱丽丝想变成多大。她说三英寸实在太矮，没想到这话正戳中了对方——它自己正好三英寸高。这条被惹恼的虫子会拿她怎么办？
introduction.en: The Caterpillar asks what size Alice would like to be. She says three inches is a wretched height, which happens to be exactly the Caterpillar's own height. So what will the creature give her?

quiz.question: Why does the Caterpillar become angry?
options: Alice refuses to try the mushroom.
Alice laughs at the way he smokes.
Alice calls three inches a wretched height, and that is his own height.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝嫌三英寸太矮，而毛毛虫正好三英寸高，它气得把身子直直立起来反驳。
feedback.en: Alice calls three inches a wretched height, and the Caterpillar, exactly three inches high, rears up angrily to contradict her.

quiz.question: What does the Caterpillar tell Alice about the mushroom?
options: She must eat the whole mushroom at once.
One side makes her taller, the other shorter.
Both sides make her grow taller.

feedback.zh: 毛毛虫爬走时只说：蘑菇一边会让人长高，另一边会让人变矮。
feedback.en: As it crawls away, the Caterpillar says only that one side of the mushroom makes you grow taller and the other shorter.

grammar.excerpt: I wish the creatures wouldn't be so easily offended.

focus.zh: wish 后接 wouldn't + 动词原形，表示希望别人别这么做；本句是爱丽丝盼着这些家伙别动不动就生气。
focus.en: Wish plus wouldn't and a bare verb expresses a wish about someone else's behaviour: Alice wants the creatures not to take offence so easily.

paragraphs.text: Alice remained looking thoughtfully at the mushroom for a minute, trying to make out which were the two sides of it; and, as it was perfectly round, she found this a very difficult question. However, at last she stretched her arms round it as far as they would go, and broke off a bit of the edge with each hand.

sentences.text: Alice remained looking thoughtfully at the mushroom for a minute, trying to make out which were the two sides of it; and, as it was perfectly round, she found this a very difficult question.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝仍待在那儿，若有所思地对着蘑菇看了一会儿，想弄清它的两边到底是哪两边；可蘑菇圆得没有一丝棱角，她觉得这个问题实在太难了。

sentences.text: However, at last she stretched her arms round it as far as they would go, and broke off a bit of the edge with each hand.
sentences.zh: 不过，她最后还是尽量伸长双臂把蘑菇抱住，两手各从边上掰下一小块。

hints.zh: 分辨出、弄清楚。
hints.en: Make out: to work out or tell apart.

paragraphs.text: "And now which is which?" she said to herself, and nibbled a little of the right-hand bit to try the effect: the next moment she felt a violent blow underneath her chin; it had struck her foot!

sentences.text: "And now which is which?" she said to herself, and nibbled a little of the right-hand bit to try the effect: the next moment she felt a violent blow underneath her chin; it had struck her foot!
sentences.zh: “可现在哪块是哪块呢？”她自言自语，又啃了一点右手那块试试效果：转眼间，她感到下巴底下被狠狠撞了一下；原来是她的脚踢到了下巴！

hints.zh: 小口小口地啃。
hints.en: Nibbled: took small bites.

paragraphs.text: She was a good deal frightened by this very sudden change, but she felt that there was no time to be lost, as she was shrinking rapidly; so she set to work at once to eat some of the other bit. Her chin was pressed so closely against her foot, that there was hardly room to open her mouth; but she did it at last, and managed to swallow a morsel of the left-hand bit.

sentences.text: She was a good deal frightened by this very sudden change, but she felt that there was no time to be lost, as she was shrinking rapidly; so she set to work at once to eat some of the other bit.
sentences.zh: 这突如其来的变化把她吓得不轻，可她觉得不能再耽搁了，因为她正在飞快地缩小；于是她立刻动手去吃另一块。

sentences.text: Her chin was pressed so closely against her foot, that there was hardly room to open her mouth; but she did it at last, and managed to swallow a morsel of the left-hand bit.
sentences.zh: 她的下巴紧紧压着脚，几乎没有张嘴的余地；不过她终于张开了嘴，勉强咽下了一小口左手那块。

hints.zh: 很、非常；a good deal frightened 就是“吓得不轻”。
hints.en: A good deal: very much; 'a good deal frightened' means badly frightened.

paragraphs.text: ***** **** ***** "Come, my head's free at last!" said Alice in a tone of delight, which changed into alarm in another moment, when she found that her shoulders were nowhere to be found: all she could see when she looked down, was an immense length of neck, which seemed to rise like a stalk out of a sea of green leaves that lay far below her.

sentences.text: ***** **** ***** "Come, my head's free at last!" said Alice in a tone of delight, which changed into alarm in another moment, when she found that her shoulders were nowhere to be found: all she could see when she looked down, was an immense length of neck, which seemed to rise like a stalk out of a sea of green leaves that lay far below her.
sentences.zh: ***** **** ***** “好啦，我的脑袋总算自由了！”爱丽丝高兴地说；可转眼间，这高兴就变成了惊慌——她发现自己的肩膀不知去向了：低头看去，能看见的只有一段长得不得了的脖子，像根茎秆似的，从远远下方一片绿叶的海洋里升起来。

hints.zh: 植物的茎、秆。
hints.en: Stalk: the stem of a plant.

introduction.zh: 蘑菇圆得看不出哪边是哪边，爱丽丝只好两手各掰下一块。她先啃了右手那块，下巴立刻撞上了脚。她慌忙去啃另一块，只盼这一回能让身子别再缩下去。
introduction.en: The mushroom is so round that Alice cannot tell one side from the other, so she breaks off a piece with each hand. She nibbles the right-hand piece, and her chin hits her foot. She hurries to nibble the other, hoping it will put her right.

quiz.question: Why is it hard for Alice to tell the two sides of the mushroom apart?
options: It is perfectly round.
It is buried in the grass.
It is too small to hold.

feedback.zh: 蘑菇是浑圆的，看不出哪一边算“这一边”，爱丽丝只好两手各掰一块。
feedback.en: The mushroom is perfectly round, so Alice cannot tell which side is which and breaks off a piece with each hand.

quiz.question: What happens just after Alice nibbles the right-hand piece?
options: Her own foot strikes her under the chin.
The mushroom crumbles in her hands.
She grows taller than the trees.

feedback.zh: 她刚啃了右手那块，就感到下巴底下挨了重重一击——原来是自己的脚踢到了下巴。
feedback.en: Right after she nibbles the right-hand piece, something strikes her under the chin: it is her own foot.

grammar.excerpt: Her chin was pressed so closely against her foot, that there was hardly room to open her mouth

focus.zh: so closely ... that 把“下巴贴得那么紧”和结果“几乎张不开嘴”连起来，that 从句讲结果。
focus.en: So closely … that links the tightness of her chin against her foot to the result: there was hardly room to open her mouth.

paragraphs.text: "What can all that green stuff be?" said Alice. "And where have my shoulders got to? And oh, my poor hands, how is it I can't see you?" She was moving them about as she spoke, but no result seemed to follow, except a little shaking among the distant green leaves.

sentences.text: "What can all that green stuff be?" said Alice.
sentences.zh: “那些绿油油的东西到底是什么？”爱丽丝说。

sentences.text: "And where have my shoulders got to?
sentences.zh: “我的肩膀又到哪儿去了？

sentences.text: And oh, my poor hands, how is it I can't see you?"
sentences.zh: 还有，哦，我可怜的手啊，我怎么就看不见你们呢？”

sentences.text: She was moving them about as she spoke, but no result seemed to follow, except a little shaking among the distant green leaves.
sentences.zh: 她说话时正把手来回动着，可除了远处绿叶间一点轻微的晃动，似乎什么反应也没有。

paragraphs.text: As there seemed to be no chance of getting her hands up to her head, she tried to get her head down to them, and was delighted to find that her neck would bend about easily in any direction, like a serpent. She had just succeeded in curving it down into a graceful zigzag, and was going to dive in among the leaves, which she found to be nothing but the tops of the trees under which she had been wandering, when a sharp hiss made her draw back in a hurry: a large pigeon had flown into her face, and was beating her violently with its wings.

sentences.text: As there seemed to be no chance of getting her hands up to her head, she tried to get her head down to them, and was delighted to find that her neck would bend about easily in any direction, like a serpent.
sentences.zh: 看来把手举到脑袋那儿是没指望了，她便试着把脑袋低下去凑手，结果惊喜地发现，她的脖子能像蛇一样，朝任何方向轻松弯来弯去。

sentences.text: She had just succeeded in curving it down into a graceful zigzag, and was going to dive in among the leaves, which she found to be nothing but the tops of the trees under which she had been wandering, when a sharp hiss made her draw back in a hurry: a large pigeon had flown into her face, and was beating her violently with its wings.
sentences.zh: 她刚把脖子弯成一个优美的之字形，正要扎进叶丛——她发现那不过是她刚才在下面游荡的那些树的树梢——这时一声尖利的嘶响吓得她急忙缩回来：一只大鸽子直扑到她脸上，用翅膀狠狠拍打她。

hints.zh: 蛇，尤指大蛇；鸽子正是用它来骂爱丽丝。
hints.en: Serpent: a snake, especially a large one.

hints.zh: 之字形，左右来回折的线。
hints.en: Zigzag: a line that turns sharply from side to side.

paragraphs.text: "Serpent!" screamed the Pigeon.

sentences.text: "Serpent!" screamed the Pigeon.
sentences.zh: “蛇！”鸽子尖叫道。

hints.zh: 鸽子，把爱丽丝当成蛇、拼命护着自己窝里蛋的鸟。
hints.en: The Pigeon, who mistakes Alice for a serpent and is guarding the eggs in its nest.

paragraphs.text: "I'm not a serpent!" said Alice indignantly. "Let me alone!"

sentences.text: "I'm not a serpent!" said Alice indignantly.
sentences.zh: “我不是蛇！”爱丽丝愤愤地说。

sentences.text: "Let me alone!"
sentences.zh: “别碰我！”

paragraphs.text: "Serpent, I say again!" repeated the Pigeon, but in a more subdued tone, and added with a kind of sob, "I've tried every way, and nothing seems to suit them!"

sentences.text: "Serpent, I say again!" repeated the Pigeon, but in a more subdued tone, and added with a kind of sob, "I've tried every way, and nothing seems to suit them!"
sentences.zh: “蛇，我再说一遍！”鸽子重复道，不过语气低了些，又带着一种哽咽补充说，“什么法子我都试过了，可好像怎么都不能让它们满意！”

hints.zh: 压低的、缓和下来的（声音或语气）。
hints.en: Subdued: quieter and less forceful.

paragraphs.text: "I haven't the least idea what you're talking about," said Alice.

sentences.text: "I haven't the least idea what you're talking about," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “我一点儿也听不懂你在说什么。”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "I've tried the roots of trees, and I've tried banks, and I've tried hedges," the Pigeon went on, without attending to her; "but those serpents! There's no pleasing them!"

sentences.text: "I've tried the roots of trees, and I've tried banks, and I've tried hedges," the Pigeon went on, without attending to her; "but those serpents!
sentences.zh: “我试过树根，试过土坡，也试过树篱，”鸽子不理她，只管往下说，“可那些蛇啊！

sentences.text: There's no pleasing them!"
sentences.zh: 怎么都没法让它们称心！”

hints.zh: 河岸、土坡；这里指鸽子试过筑巢的地方。
hints.en: Banks: raised ground along a river; here, places the Pigeon tried to nest.

paragraphs.text: Alice was more and more puzzled, but she thought there was no use in saying anything more till the Pigeon had finished.

sentences.text: Alice was more and more puzzled, but she thought there was no use in saying anything more till the Pigeon had finished.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝越来越糊涂，但她觉得在鸽子说完之前，再多说什么也没用。

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝的脖子变得又长又软，能像蛇一样四处弯。她想低头看看自己的手，却被一只鸽子扑了满脸。鸽子一口咬定她是蛇，根本不听她分辩。她要怎么证明自己不是？
introduction.en: Alice's neck has grown long and bendable, and it twists like a serpent's. When she tries to look down at her hands, a Pigeon flies into her face, certain that she is a serpent and unwilling to hear otherwise.

quiz.question: Why does the Pigeon fly at Alice?
options: It is angry that she has climbed its tree.
It takes her for a serpent coming after its eggs.
It wants the mushroom in her hands.

feedback.zh: 鸽子把爱丽丝长而弯的脖子当成蛇，扑上来用翅膀打她，还一口咬定“蛇！”。
feedback.en: The Pigeon takes her long, bending neck for a serpent, flies at her, and screams 'Serpent!'

quiz.question: What does Alice do when she cannot lift her hands to her head?
options: She calls the Caterpillar for help.
She bends her neck down towards her hands.
She eats more of the mushroom.

feedback.zh: 手举不到头，爱丽丝就试着把头低下去凑手，发现脖子能像蛇一样朝各个方向弯。
feedback.en: When her hands will not reach her head, Alice bends her head down to them and finds her neck bends easily in any direction.

grammar.excerpt: She had just succeeded in curving it down into a graceful zigzag

focus.zh: had just succeeded 是过去完成时，把“刚把脖子弯好”放在鸽子扑来之前；in curving 是介词后接 -ing。
focus.en: Had just succeeded is past perfect, placing the curving of her neck before the pigeon flew at her; in curving is a preposition with an -ing form.

paragraphs.text: "As if it wasn't trouble enough hatching the eggs," said the Pigeon; "but I must be on the look-out for serpents night and day! Why, I haven't had a wink of sleep these three weeks!"

sentences.text: "As if it wasn't trouble enough hatching the eggs," said the Pigeon; "but I must be on the look-out for serpents night and day!
sentences.zh: “光孵蛋就够麻烦了，”鸽子说，“可我还得日夜提防着蛇！

sentences.text: Why, I haven't had a wink of sleep these three weeks!"
sentences.zh: 哎呀，我这三个星期连眼都没合过一下！”

hints.zh: 提防着、留心着。
hints.en: On the look-out for: watching out for.

hints.zh: 一点觉；not had a wink of sleep 就是“一觉没睡”。
hints.en: A wink of sleep: even a moment of sleep.

paragraphs.text: "I'm very sorry you've been annoyed," said Alice, who was beginning to see its meaning.

sentences.text: "I'm very sorry you've been annoyed," said Alice, who was beginning to see its meaning.
sentences.zh: “让你这么烦心，我很抱歉。”爱丽丝说，她开始明白它的意思了。

paragraphs.text: "And just as I'd taken the highest tree in the wood," continued the Pigeon, raising its voice to a shriek, "and just as I was thinking I should be free of them at last, they must needs come wriggling down from the sky! Ugh, Serpent!"

sentences.text: "And just as I'd taken the highest tree in the wood," continued the Pigeon, raising its voice to a shriek, "and just as I was thinking I should be free of them at last, they must needs come wriggling down from the sky!
sentences.zh: “我好不容易占下了林子里最高的那棵树，”鸽子继续说着，把声音尖成了叫喊，“我正想着总算可以摆脱它们了，它们偏偏要从天上扭着身子爬下来！

sentences.text: Ugh, Serpent!"
sentences.zh: 呃，蛇！”

hints.zh: 偏要、硬是；旧式说法，带抱怨的语气。
hints.en: Must needs: had to, of all things; an old phrase with a complaining tone.

paragraphs.text: "But I'm not a serpent, I tell you!" said Alice. "I'm a—— I'm a——"

sentences.text: "But I'm not a serpent, I tell you!" said Alice.
sentences.zh: “可我告诉你，我不是蛇！”爱丽丝说。

sentences.text: "I'm a—— I'm a——"
sentences.zh: “我是一个——我是一个——”

paragraphs.text: "Well! What are you?" said the Pigeon. "I can see you're trying to invent something!"

sentences.text: "Well!
sentences.zh: “好啊！

sentences.text: What are you?" said the Pigeon.
sentences.zh: 那你倒是什么？”鸽子说。

sentences.text: "I can see you're trying to invent something!"
sentences.zh: “我看得出来，你正想编出个什么来！”

paragraphs.text: "I—I'm a little girl," said Alice, rather doubtfully, as she remembered the number of changes she had gone through that day.

sentences.text: "I—I'm a little girl," said Alice, rather doubtfully, as she remembered the number of changes she had gone through that day.
sentences.zh: “我——我是个小姑娘。”爱丽丝说得相当没底气，因为她想起了自己这一天经历过的那么多次变化。

paragraphs.text: "A likely story indeed!" said the Pigeon in a tone of the deepest contempt. "I've seen a good many little girls in my time, but never one with such a neck as that! No, no! You're a serpent; and there's no use denying it. I suppose you'll be telling me next that you never tasted an egg!"

sentences.text: "A likely story indeed!" said the Pigeon in a tone of the deepest contempt.
sentences.zh: “说得倒像真的！”鸽子用极其轻蔑的口气说。

sentences.text: "I've seen a good many little girls in my time, but never one with such a neck as that!
sentences.zh: “我这一辈子见过不少小姑娘，可从来没见过谁长着那样一条脖子！

sentences.text: No, no!
sentences.zh: 不对，不对！

sentences.text: You're a serpent; and there's no use denying it.
sentences.zh: 你就是条蛇；否认也没用。

sentences.text: I suppose you'll be telling me next that you never tasted an egg!"
sentences.zh: 我猜你接下来要说，你从来没尝过蛋！”

hints.zh: 反话：“说得倒像真的！”意思是根本不信。
hints.en: Sarcastic: 'A likely story!' means it does not believe a word of it.

hints.zh: 我这一辈子、我这些年。
hints.en: In my time: in my life, over the years.

paragraphs.text: "I have tasted eggs, certainly," said Alice, who was a very truthful child; "but little girls eat eggs quite as much as serpents do, you know."

sentences.text: "I have tasted eggs, certainly," said Alice, who was a very truthful child; "but little girls eat eggs quite as much as serpents do, you know."
sentences.zh: “我确实尝过蛋，”爱丽丝说，她是个非常诚实的孩子，“可你知道，小姑娘吃蛋跟蛇吃蛋一样多呢。”

paragraphs.text: "I don't believe it," said the Pigeon; "but if they do, why then they're a kind of serpent, that's all I can say."

sentences.text: "I don't believe it," said the Pigeon; "but if they do, why then they're a kind of serpent, that's all I can say."
sentences.zh: “我不信，”鸽子说，“就算她们真吃，那她们也算是一种蛇，我只能这么说。”

introduction.zh: 鸽子越说越激动：为了守住窝里的蛋，它已经三个星期没合眼，而“蛇”总从树上爬下来。爱丽丝想说自己是小姑娘，可话到嘴边又没了底气。这回她能说服它吗？
introduction.en: The Pigeon grows more and more upset: it has not slept for three weeks, guarding its eggs from serpents that keep coming down from the trees. Alice wants to say she is a little girl, but the words come out without much confidence.

quiz.question: Why has the Pigeon had no sleep for three weeks?
options: It has been flying from tree to tree.
It has been arguing with Alice all night.
It has been hatching eggs and watching for serpents night and day.

feedback.zh: 鸽子说，除了孵蛋，它还得日夜提防蛇，所以三个星期没合眼。
feedback.en: Besides hatching the eggs, the Pigeon must watch for serpents day and night, which is why it has not slept for three weeks.

quiz.question: What does the Pigeon refuse to believe?
options: That its tree is the highest in the wood.
That little girls eat eggs.
That Alice's neck can bend.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝说小姑娘吃蛋和蛇一样多，鸽子却说“我不信”，还顺势断定小姑娘也算一种蛇。
feedback.en: Alice says little girls eat eggs as much as serpents do; the Pigeon does not believe it and decides little girls must be a kind of serpent.

grammar.excerpt: I suppose you'll be telling me next that you never tasted an egg!

focus.zh: you'll be telling me 是将来进行时 will be + -ing；这里带讥讽，意思是“你接下来大概要说……”。
focus.en: You'll be telling me is future continuous (will be + -ing), used with a sneer: 'no doubt you'll say next that…'

paragraphs.text: This was such a new idea to Alice, that she was quite silent for a minute or two, which gave the Pigeon the opportunity of adding, "You're looking for eggs, I know that well enough; and what does it matter to me whether you're a little girl or a serpent?"

sentences.text: This was such a new idea to Alice, that she was quite silent for a minute or two, which gave the Pigeon the opportunity of adding, "You're looking for eggs, I know that well enough; and what does it matter to me whether you're a little girl or a serpent?"
sentences.zh: 这想法对爱丽丝来说太新鲜了，她竟一言不发地待了一两分钟，这正好让鸽子有机会补上一句：“你在找蛋，这我清楚得很；你是小姑娘还是蛇，对我又有什么要紧？”

paragraphs.text: "It matters a good deal to me," said Alice hastily; "but I'm not looking for eggs, as it happens; and if I was, I shouldn't want yours: I don't like them raw."

sentences.text: "It matters a good deal to me," said Alice hastily; "but I'm not looking for eggs, as it happens; and if I was, I shouldn't want yours: I don't like them raw."
sentences.zh: “对我来说可要紧得很。”爱丽丝急忙说，“不过碰巧我并不是在找蛋；就算我在找，我也不会要你的蛋：我不喜欢生着吃。”

hints.zh: 碰巧、恰好。
hints.en: As it happens: by chance, actually.

hints.zh: 生的、没煮过的。
hints.en: Raw: not cooked.

paragraphs.text: "Well, be off, then!" said the Pigeon in a sulky tone, as it settled down again into its nest. Alice crouched down among the trees as well as she could, for her neck kept getting entangled among the branches, and every now and then she had to stop and untwist it. After a while she remembered that she still held the pieces of mushroom in her hands, and she set to work very carefully, nibbling first at one and then at the other, and growing sometimes taller and sometimes shorter, until she had succeeded in bringing herself down to her usual height.

sentences.text: "Well, be off, then!" said the Pigeon in a sulky tone, as it settled down again into its nest.
sentences.zh: “好吧，那就走吧！”鸽子闷闷不乐地说，重新落回窝里。

sentences.text: Alice crouched down among the trees as well as she could, for her neck kept getting entangled among the branches, and every now and then she had to stop and untwist it.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝尽量在树间蹲低身子，因为她的脖子老是缠在树枝里，不时得停下来把它解开。

sentences.text: After a while she remembered that she still held the pieces of mushroom in her hands, and she set to work very carefully, nibbling first at one and then at the other, and growing sometimes taller and sometimes shorter, until she had succeeded in bringing herself down to her usual height.
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，她想起手里还拿着那两块蘑菇，于是非常小心地动起手来，先啃一块，再啃另一块，一会儿变高，一会儿变矮，最后终于把自己降回到了平常的身高。

hints.zh: 闷闷不乐、板着脸的。
hints.en: Sulky: silent and bad-tempered.

hints.zh: 缠住、绞在一起。
hints.en: Entangled: twisted and caught in something.

introduction.zh: 鸽子丢下一句“你是小姑娘还是蛇，跟我有什么相干”，转身回窝。爱丽丝却说，这事对她很要紧；而且她并不爱吃生蛋。等她终于想起手里的蘑菇，要回到原来的身高还得先弄清哪一块管用。
introduction.en: The Pigeon mutters that it does not care whether Alice is a little girl or a serpent, and settles back into its nest. Alice says it matters a great deal to her, and that she does not even like raw eggs. Then she remembers the mushroom in her hands.

quiz.question: What does Alice say about the eggs?
options: She is looking for some to take home.
She is not looking for eggs, and would not want them raw.
She would like one of the Pigeon's eggs.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝说，碰巧她并不是在找蛋；就算在找，也不会要它的蛋——她不喜欢生着吃。
feedback.en: Alice says she is not looking for eggs, and would not want the Pigeon's even if she were, because she does not like them raw.

quiz.question: How does Alice get back to her usual height?
options: She nibbles first one piece and then the other.
The Pigeon brings her something to eat.
She eats a whole mushroom in one bite.

feedback.zh: 她想起手里还拿着两块蘑菇，便轮流小口啃，时高时矮，最后降回平常的身高。
feedback.en: She remembers the two pieces of mushroom and nibbles first one and then the other until she is back to her usual height.

grammar.excerpt: and if I was, I shouldn't want yours

focus.zh: if 从句用过去式 was、主句用 shouldn't + 动词原形，说的是与现在相反的假设；口语里 if I was 常代替 if I were。
focus.en: A past-tense if-clause with shouldn't and a bare verb describes an unreal present: 'if I were looking, I wouldn't want yours'; in speech if I was often replaces if I were.

paragraphs.text: It was so long since she had been anything near the right size, that it felt quite strange at first; but she got used to it in a few minutes, and began talking to herself, as usual. "Come, there's half my plan done now! How puzzling all these changes are! I'm never sure what I'm going to be, from one minute to another! However, I've got back to my right size: the next thing is, to get into that beautiful garden—how is that to be done, I wonder?" As she said this, she came suddenly upon an open place, with a little house in it about four feet high. "Whoever lives there," thought Alice, "it'll never do to come upon them this size: why, I should frighten them out of their wits!" So she began nibbling at the right-hand bit again, and did not venture to go near the house till she had brought herself down to nine inches high.

sentences.text: It was so long since she had been anything near the right size, that it felt quite strange at first; but she got used to it in a few minutes, and began talking to herself, as usual.
sentences.zh: 她已经很久没有过接近正常的身高了，所以起初觉得很不习惯；不过几分钟后她就习惯了，又像平常那样自言自语起来。

sentences.text: "Come, there's half my plan done now!
sentences.zh: “好了，我的计划现在已经完成一半了！

sentences.text: How puzzling all these changes are!
sentences.zh: 这些变化可真让人摸不着头脑！

sentences.text: I'm never sure what I'm going to be, from one minute to another!
sentences.zh: 我这一分钟都不知道下一分钟会变成什么样！

sentences.text: However, I've got back to my right size: the next thing is, to get into that beautiful garden—how is that to be done, I wonder?"
sentences.zh: 不过，我已经恢复成原来的大小了：接下来就是进那座美丽的花园——我该怎么进去呢？”

sentences.text: As she said this, she came suddenly upon an open place, with a little house in it about four feet high.
sentences.zh: 说着说着，她忽然来到一片空地上，那里有一座约四英尺高的小房子。

sentences.text: "Whoever lives there," thought Alice, "it'll never do to come upon them this size: why, I should frighten them out of their wits!"
sentences.zh: “不管是谁住在那里，”爱丽丝心想，“以我这么个尺寸出现在人家面前可绝对不行：哎呀，我会把他们吓得魂都没了！”

sentences.text: So she began nibbling at the right-hand bit again, and did not venture to go near the house till she had brought herself down to nine inches high.
sentences.zh: 于是她又开始啃右手那块，一直把自己缩到九英寸高，才敢走近那座房子。

hints.zh: 空地，林中开阔的地方。
hints.en: An open place: a clearing.

hints.zh: 那可不行、绝对使不得。
hints.en: It'll never do: that will not do at all.

hints.target: frighten them out of their wits
hints.zh: 把他们吓得魂飞魄散、不知所措。
hints.en: Frighten them out of their wits: scare them badly.

hints.zh: 敢、壮着胆子（去做）。
hints.en: Venture: dare to go or do something.

hints.zh: 九英寸，约二十三厘米；这比她原来的身高矮得多。
hints.en: Nine inches: about 23 cm, far shorter than her usual height.

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝终于回到原来的身高，计划也算完成了一半。前面就是那座美丽的花园，可空地上那座小房子只有四英尺高。以她现在的个子走过去，会出什么事？
introduction.en: Alice is her right size again, and half of her plan is done. Ahead lies the beautiful garden, but the little house in the clearing is only four feet high. What would happen if she walked up to it as she is?

quiz.question: What does Alice plan to do next?
options: Go back to her sister.
Find the Caterpillar and thank it.
Get into the beautiful garden.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝说，恢复原来的大小只算完成了计划的一半，接下来要进那座美丽的花园。
feedback.en: Alice says getting back to her right size is only half her plan; next she wants to get into the beautiful garden.

quiz.question: Why does Alice stop short of the little house?
options: She is still too big and fears she would frighten whoever lives there.
The house has no door.
She has eaten all of her mushroom.

feedback.zh: 她担心自己这副个子会吓坏屋里的人，于是又啃起右手那块蘑菇，缩到九英寸高才敢靠近。
feedback.en: She is afraid her size would frighten whoever lives there, so she nibbles the right-hand piece down to nine inches before going near.

grammar.excerpt: "Whoever lives there," thought Alice

focus.zh: Whoever 引导的从句作 thought 的内容，意思是“不管谁住在那里”；whoever 相当于 anyone who。
focus.en: Whoever introduces the clause that Alice thinks: it means 'anyone who lives there'.

paragraphs.text: For a minute or two she stood looking at the house, and wondering what to do next, when suddenly a footman in livery came running out of the wood—(she considered him to be a footman because he was in livery: otherwise, judging by his face only, she would have called him a fish)—and rapped loudly at the door with his knuckles. It was opened by another footman in livery, with a round face, and large eyes like a frog; and both footmen, Alice noticed, had powdered hair that curled all over their heads. She felt very curious to know what it was all about, and crept a little way out of the wood to listen.

sentences.text: For a minute or two she stood looking at the house, and wondering what to do next, when suddenly a footman in livery came running out of the wood—(she considered him to be a footman because he was in livery: otherwise, judging by his face only, she would have called him a fish)—and rapped loudly at the door with his knuckles.
sentences.zh: 她站在那儿看着那所房子，看了一两分钟，正想着自己该怎么办，忽然有个穿号衣的男仆从树林里跑了出来——（她认定他是男仆，是因为他穿着号衣；不然单看那张脸，她会把他叫作鱼）——他用指节在门上大声敲了几下。

sentences.text: It was opened by another footman in livery, with a round face, and large eyes like a frog; and both footmen, Alice noticed, had powdered hair that curled all over their heads.
sentences.zh: 开门的是另一个穿号衣的男仆，圆脸，一双像青蛙的大眼睛；爱丽丝注意到，两个男仆的头发都扑了粉，满头卷曲。

sentences.text: She felt very curious to know what it was all about, and crept a little way out of the wood to listen.
sentences.zh: 她非常好奇，想知道这到底是怎么回事，就悄悄从树林里挪出来一点，好听个明白。

hints.zh: 扑了粉的头发；旧时大户人家的仆人常戴扑粉的假发，头发卷曲。
hints.en: Powdered hair: servants in grand houses wore their hair powdered white and curled.

paragraphs.text: The Fish-Footman began by producing from under his arm a great letter, nearly as large as himself, and this he handed over to the other, saying, in a solemn tone, "For the Duchess. An invitation from the Queen to play croquet." The Frog-Footman repeated, in the same solemn tone, only changing the order of the words a little, "From the Queen. An invitation for the Duchess to play croquet."

sentences.text: The Fish-Footman began by producing from under his arm a great letter, nearly as large as himself, and this he handed over to the other, saying, in a solemn tone, "For the Duchess.
sentences.zh: 鱼仆先从腋下拿出一封很大的信，几乎和他自己一样大，然后把它交给另一个仆人，用庄重的口气说：“给公爵夫人的。

sentences.text: An invitation from the Queen to play croquet."
sentences.zh: 王后请她去打槌球。”

sentences.text: The Frog-Footman repeated, in the same solemn tone, only changing the order of the words a little, "From the Queen.
sentences.zh: 蛙仆用同样庄重的口气重复了一遍，只是把词序稍微换了换：“王后来的。

sentences.text: An invitation for the Duchess to play croquet."
sentences.zh: 请公爵夫人去打槌球的邀请。”

hints.zh: 鱼仆，长着鱼脸的仆役，送来这封请柬。
hints.en: The Fish-Footman, a fish-faced servant who brings the invitation.

hints.zh: 公爵夫人，这所房子的女主人。
hints.en: The Duchess, the lady of this house.

hints.zh: 王后，这里指奇境里的红心王后。
hints.en: The Queen: the Queen of Hearts in Wonderland.

hints.zh: 槌球，用木槌把球打过铁圈的草地游戏。
hints.en: Croquet: a lawn game in which players hit balls through hoops with a mallet.

paragraphs.text: Then they both bowed low, and their curls got entangled together.

sentences.text: Then they both bowed low, and their curls got entangled together.
sentences.zh: 然后两人深深鞠了一躬，卷发缠在了一起。

paragraphs.text: Alice laughed so much at this, that she had to run back into the wood for fear of their hearing her; and when she next peeped out the Fish-Footman was gone, and the other was sitting on the ground near the door, staring stupidly up into the sky.

sentences.text: Alice laughed so much at this, that she had to run back into the wood for fear of their hearing her; and when she next peeped out the Fish-Footman was gone, and the other was sitting on the ground near the door, staring stupidly up into the sky.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝看得笑个不停，又怕被他们听见，只好跑回树林里；等她再探头张望时，鱼仆已经走了，另一个仆人坐在门边的地上，呆呆地仰头望着天。

hints.zh: 爱丽丝，本书主角，追着白兔掉进奇境的小女孩。
hints.en: Alice, the girl who followed the White Rabbit into Wonderland.

paragraphs.text: Alice went timidly up to the door, and knocked.

sentences.text: Alice went timidly up to the door, and knocked.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝怯生生地走到门前，敲了敲门。

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝来到一所房子前，正琢磨该怎么办，忽然从树林里跑出一个穿号衣的男仆。开门的是另一个仆人，两人的头发都很古怪。她悄悄探出头去，想听清他们在说什么。
introduction.en: Alice stops in front of a house, wondering what to do, when a footman in livery runs out of the wood. Another footman opens the door, and both have very strange hair. Alice creeps closer to hear what the two of them are saying.

quiz.question: Why does Alice decide that the first visitor must be a footman?
options: Because he knocks loudly with his knuckles.
Because he is wearing livery.
Because his face looks like a fish.

feedback.zh: 原文说，她认定他是男仆，正是因为他“穿号衣”；单看那张脸，她本来会把他当成一条鱼。
feedback.en: The text says she calls him a footman because he is in livery; judging by his face alone, she would have called him a fish.

quiz.question: What happens when the two footmen bow to each other?
options: The door shuts behind them.
Their curls get entangled together.
Their letter falls on the ground.

feedback.zh: 两人深深鞠躬，头上的卷发缠在了一起——爱丽丝正是看到这里才笑出声来。
feedback.en: They bow low and their curls get tangled together, which is why Alice cannot stop laughing.

grammar.excerpt: She felt very curious to know what it was all about

focus.zh: know 后面的 what it was all about 是 wh- 从句，用陈述语序：it was，不能再倒装成 was it。
focus.en: The wh-clause after know keeps statement order: what it was all about, not what was it all about.

paragraphs.text: "There's no sort of use in knocking," said the Footman, "and that for two reasons. First, because I'm on the same side of the door as you are; secondly, because they're making such a noise inside, no one could possibly hear you." And certainly there was a most extraordinary noise going on within—a constant howling and sneezing, and every now and then a great crash, as if a dish or kettle had been broken to pieces.

sentences.text: "There's no sort of use in knocking," said the Footman, "and that for two reasons.
sentences.zh: “敲门根本没用，”仆人说，“原因有两个。

sentences.text: First, because I'm on the same side of the door as you are; secondly, because they're making such a noise inside, no one could possibly hear you."
sentences.zh: 第一，因为我和你一样，都站在门的这一边；第二，因为里面吵得那么厉害，根本没人听得见你。”

sentences.text: And certainly there was a most extraordinary noise going on within—a constant howling and sneezing, and every now and then a great crash, as if a dish or kettle had been broken to pieces.
sentences.zh: 屋里的确传出一阵极不寻常的响动——不停地嚎叫和打喷嚏，时不时还有砰的一声巨响，像是盘子或水壶被摔得粉碎。

hints.zh: 一点用也没有；no sort of 加强否定。
hints.en: No sort of use: not any use at all; no sort of makes the negative stronger.

hints.zh: 摔成碎片；to pieces 表示碎成小块。
hints.en: Broken to pieces: smashed into small bits.

paragraphs.text: "Please, then," said Alice, "how am I to get in?"

sentences.text: "Please, then," said Alice, "how am I to get in?"
sentences.zh: “那么请问，”爱丽丝说，“我该怎么进去呢？”

paragraphs.text: "There might be some sense in your knocking," the Footman went on, without attending to her, "if we had the door between us. For instance, if you were inside, you might knock, and I could let you out, you know." He was looking up into the sky all the time he was speaking, and this Alice thought decidedly uncivil. "But perhaps he can't help it," she said to herself; "his eyes are so very nearly at the top of his head. But at any rate he might answer questions.—How am I to get in?" she repeated, aloud.

sentences.text: "There might be some sense in your knocking," the Footman went on, without attending to her, "if we had the door between us.
sentences.zh: “你敲门也许还有点道理，”仆人并不理会她，接着说，“前提是我们中间隔着这扇门。

sentences.text: For instance, if you were inside, you might knock, and I could let you out, you know."
sentences.zh: 比如说，要是你在里面，你敲敲门，我就可以放你出来，你懂吧。”

sentences.text: He was looking up into the sky all the time he was speaking, and this Alice thought decidedly uncivil.
sentences.zh: 他说话的时候一直仰头望着天，爱丽丝觉得这实在太没礼貌。

sentences.text: "But perhaps he can't help it," she said to herself; "his eyes are so very nearly at the top of his head.
sentences.zh: “不过也许他也没办法，”她自言自语，“他的眼睛长得实在太靠头顶了。

sentences.text: But at any rate he might answer questions.—How am I to get in?" she repeated, aloud.
sentences.zh: 可不管怎样，他总该回答人家的问题吧。——我该怎么进去？”她大声重复了一遍。

hints.zh: decidedly 是“确实、明显”，uncivil 是“没礼貌”，合起来是“实在太无礼”。
hints.en: Decidedly uncivil: decidedly means clearly, uncivil means rude.

paragraphs.text: "I shall sit here," the Footman remarked, "till to-morrow——"

sentences.text: "I shall sit here," the Footman remarked, "till to-morrow——"
sentences.zh: “我就坐在这儿，”仆人说道，“一直坐到明天——”

paragraphs.text: At this moment the door of the house opened, and a large plate came skimming out, straight at the Footman's head: it just grazed his nose, and broke to pieces against one of the trees behind him.

sentences.text: At this moment the door of the house opened, and a large plate came skimming out, straight at the Footman's head: it just grazed his nose, and broke to pieces against one of the trees behind him.
sentences.zh: 这时房子的门开了，一只大盘子飞掠而出，直冲仆人的脑袋：盘子只是擦过他的鼻子，撞在他身后的一棵树上，摔成了碎片。

hints.zh: 擦过、蹭到；这里盘子只是擦过他的鼻子，并没有打中。
hints.en: Grazed: touched or scraped lightly in passing.

paragraphs.text: "——or next day, maybe," the Footman continued in the same tone, exactly as if nothing had happened.

sentences.text: "——or next day, maybe," the Footman continued in the same tone, exactly as if nothing had happened.
sentences.zh: “——或者也许是后天，”仆人用同样的口气接着说，就好像什么事都没发生。

paragraphs.text: "How am I to get in?" asked Alice again, in a louder tone.

sentences.text: "How am I to get in?" asked Alice again, in a louder tone.
sentences.zh: “我该怎么进去？”爱丽丝又问了一遍，声音更大了。

paragraphs.text: "Are you to get in at all?" said the Footman. "That's the first question, you know."

sentences.text: "Are you to get in at all?" said the Footman.
sentences.zh: “你究竟该不该进去呢？”仆人说。

sentences.text: "That's the first question, you know."
sentences.zh: “这才是第一个问题，你懂吧。”

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝在门上敲了几下，仆人却说敲门一点用也没有，理由有两个。她问自己该怎么进去，仆人讲起门内门外的道理，眼睛一直望着天。就在这时，门里飞出一只盘子。
introduction.en: Alice knocks, but the footman says knocking is no use at all, and gives two reasons. She asks how she is to get in, and he explains about doors and sides while staring at the sky. Then something comes flying out of the house.

quiz.question: Why does the Footman say there is no use in knocking?
options: He is on the same side of the door, and the noise inside is too loud.
The door is locked and the key has been lost.
Alice is knocking much too quietly.

feedback.zh: 他给出两个理由：两人都在门的同一侧；屋里太吵，没人听得见敲门声。
feedback.en: He gives two reasons: they are on the same side of the door, and the noise inside would drown any knocking.

quiz.question: What does the Footman do while Alice is asking her questions?
options: He keeps looking up into the sky.
He runs off into the wood.
He opens the door and lets her in.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝注意到，他说话时一直仰头看天，她觉得这实在太没礼貌。
feedback.en: Alice notices that he stares at the sky the whole time he is speaking, which she thinks decidedly uncivil.

grammar.excerpt: how am I to get in

focus.zh: be to do 表示按安排“该、要”做某事；am I to get in 是疑问语序，be 提到了主语 I 前面。
focus.en: Be to do means what is arranged or expected; in the question, am comes before the subject I.

paragraphs.text: It was, no doubt: only Alice did not like to be told so. "It's really dreadful," she muttered to herself, "the way all the creatures argue. It's enough to drive one crazy!"

sentences.text: It was, no doubt: only Alice did not like to be told so.
sentences.zh: 那当然没错：只是爱丽丝不喜欢被人这么说。

sentences.text: "It's really dreadful," she muttered to herself, "the way all the creatures argue.
sentences.zh: “真是要命，”她低声嘟囔，“这里所有的家伙都这么爱争辩。

sentences.text: It's enough to drive one crazy!"
sentences.zh: 简直能把人逼疯！”

hints.zh: 把人逼疯；drive sb crazy 是“让某人受不了”。
hints.en: Drive one crazy: make someone lose patience completely.

paragraphs.text: The Footman seemed to think this a good opportunity for repeating his remark, with variations. "I shall sit here," he said, "on and off, for days and days."

sentences.text: The Footman seemed to think this a good opportunity for repeating his remark, with variations.
sentences.zh: 仆人似乎觉得这是个好机会，可以把他的话换个说法再说一遍。

sentences.text: "I shall sit here," he said, "on and off, for days and days."
sentences.zh: “我就坐在这儿，”他说，“断断续续地，一坐就是好些天。”

hints.zh: 断断续续地，时来时不来。
hints.en: On and off: for a while, then not, then again.

paragraphs.text: "But what am I to do?" said Alice.

sentences.text: "But what am I to do?" said Alice.
sentences.zh: “可我该怎么办呢？”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "Anything you like," said the Footman, and began whistling.

sentences.text: "Anything you like," said the Footman, and began whistling.
sentences.zh: “随你便，”仆人说，然后吹起了口哨。

paragraphs.text: "Oh, there's no use in talking to him," said Alice desperately: "he's perfectly idiotic!" And she opened the door and went in.

sentences.text: "Oh, there's no use in talking to him," said Alice desperately: "he's perfectly idiotic!"
sentences.zh: “唉，跟他说什么都没用，”爱丽丝绝望地说，“他简直是个白痴！”

sentences.text: And she opened the door and went in.
sentences.zh: 于是她推开门走了进去。

paragraphs.text: The door led right into a large kitchen, which was full of smoke from one end to the other: the Duchess was sitting on a three-legged stool in the middle, nursing a baby; the cook was leaning over the fire, stirring a large cauldron which seemed to be full of soup. "There's certainly too much pepper in that soup!" Alice said to herself, as well as she could for sneezing.

sentences.text: The door led right into a large kitchen, which was full of smoke from one end to the other: the Duchess was sitting on a three-legged stool in the middle, nursing a baby; the cook was leaning over the fire, stirring a large cauldron which seemed to be full of soup.
sentences.zh: 门一开就通向一间大厨房，里面从头到尾都是烟：公爵夫人坐在中间一张三条腿的凳子上，怀里抱着个婴儿；厨娘正俯在炉火上，搅着一口大锅，锅里似乎装满了汤。

sentences.text: "There's certainly too much pepper in that soup!"
sentences.zh: “那锅汤里放的胡椒实在太多了！”

sentences.text: Alice said to herself, as well as she could for sneezing.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝一边打喷嚏一边自言自语，尽可能把话说清楚。

paragraphs.text: There was certainly too much of it in the air. Even the Duchess sneezed occasionally; and as for the baby, it was sneezing and howling alternately without a moment's pause. The only two creatures in the kitchen that did not sneeze, were the cook, and a large cat which was sitting on the hearth and grinning from ear to ear.

sentences.text: There was certainly too much of it in the air.
sentences.zh: 空气里的胡椒也实在太多了。

sentences.text: Even the Duchess sneezed occasionally; and as for the baby, it was sneezing and howling alternately without a moment's pause.
sentences.zh: 连公爵夫人也时不时打个喷嚏；至于那个婴儿，更是一刻不停地又打喷嚏又嚎叫，轮着来。

sentences.text: The only two creatures in the kitchen that did not sneeze, were the cook, and a large cat which was sitting on the hearth and grinning from ear to ear.
sentences.zh: 厨房里只有两个活物不打喷嚏：一个是厨娘，另一个是只大猫，它坐在壁炉前，咧着嘴笑到耳朵根。

hints.zh: 咧着嘴笑得合不拢，笑到耳朵根。

paragraphs.text: "Please would you tell me," said Alice, a little timidly, for she was not quite sure whether it was good manners for her to speak first, "why your cat grins like that?"

sentences.text: "Please would you tell me," said Alice, a little timidly, for she was not quite sure whether it was good manners for her to speak first, "why your cat grins like that?"
sentences.zh: “请问你能不能告诉我，”爱丽丝有点胆怯地说，因为她不太确定自己先开口是否合乎礼数，“你的猫为什么那样笑呢？”

sentences.text: "It's a Cheshire cat," said the Duchess, "and that's why.
sentences.zh: “那是柴郡猫，”公爵夫人说，“所以就那样笑。

sentences.text: Pig!"

hints.en: Pig! The Duchess is calling the baby a pig, not Alice.

sentences.text: She said the last word with such sudden violence that Alice quite jumped; but she saw in another moment that it was addressed to the baby, and not to her, so she took courage, and went on again:—
sentences.zh: 最后那个字说得那么突兀凶狠，把爱丽丝吓了一跳；可她随即看出，那话是对婴儿说的，不是冲她，于是她鼓起勇气，又接着说：——

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝推门进去，满屋都是胡椒味，呛得人人打喷嚏。厨房里坐着一位公爵夫人，怀里抱着个哭闹的婴儿；壁炉前还有一只大猫，咧着嘴笑个不停。她鼓起勇气，问起那只猫。
introduction.en: Alice pushes the door open and finds the room thick with pepper; everyone is sneezing. In the kitchen sit a Duchess with a crying baby and a large cat grinning by the fire. Alice plucks up courage and asks about the cat.

quiz.question: Why is everyone in the kitchen sneezing?
options: The fire is giving out thick smoke.
The baby has caught a bad cold.
There is too much pepper in the air.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝先发现汤里胡椒太多，接着发现空气里也全是胡椒，连公爵夫人都在打喷嚏。
feedback.en: Alice finds too much pepper in the soup, and then in the air itself: even the Duchess sneezes.

quiz.question: Who is the Duchess speaking to when she says 'Pig!'?
options: The cook.
Alice.
The baby.

feedback.zh: 那声“猪”来得突然，爱丽丝吓了一跳，但随即看出那是对婴儿说的，不是在骂她。
feedback.en: The word comes so violently that Alice jumps, but she soon sees it was addressed to the baby, not to her.

grammar.excerpt: she was not quite sure whether it was good manners for her to speak first

focus.en: The whether-clause is the object of sure and keeps statement order: whether it was good manners for her to speak first.

sentences.text: "I didn't know that Cheshire cats always grinned; in fact, I didn't know that cats could grin."

sentences.zh: “它们都会，”公爵夫人说，“而且大多数还真的会笑。”

sentences.text: "I don't know of any that do," Alice said very politely, feeling quite pleased to have got into a conversation.

paragraphs.text: Alice did not at all like the tone of this remark, and thought it would be as well to introduce some other subject of conversation.
