sentences.text: Alice did not at all like the tone of this remark, and thought it would be as well to introduce some other subject of conversation.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝一点也不喜欢这句话的口气，觉得还是换个话题为好。

sentences.text: While she was trying to fix on one, the cook took the cauldron of soup off the fire, and at once set to work throwing everything within her reach at the Duchess and the baby—the fire-irons came first; then followed a shower of saucepans, plates, and dishes.
sentences.zh: 她正琢磨着挑个什么话题，厨娘把一大锅汤从火上端了下来，马上动手把够得着的东西一件件朝公爵夫人和婴儿扔过去——先飞过来的是火炉用具，接着是雨点般的炖锅、盘子和碟子。

sentences.text: The Duchess took no notice of them even when they hit her; and the baby was howling so much already, that it was quite impossible to say whether the blows hurt it or not.
sentences.zh: 公爵夫人连被砸中了也毫不在意；那婴儿本来就嚎得厉害，实在说不清这些打击有没有弄疼它。

hints.zh: 选定一个（话题）；fix on 是“确定、挑定”。
hints.en: Fix on one: settle on or choose one subject.

hints.zh: 火炉用具，火钳、火铲一类。
hints.en: Fire-irons: the poker, shovel and tongs used at a fire.

paragraphs.text: "Oh, please mind what you're doing!" cried Alice, jumping up and down in an agony of terror. "Oh, there goes his precious nose!" as an unusually large saucepan flew close by it, and very nearly carried it off.

sentences.text: "Oh, please mind what you're doing!" cried Alice, jumping up and down in an agony of terror.
sentences.zh: “哎呀，请你当心点！”爱丽丝大叫，吓得直跳脚。

sentences.text: "Oh, there goes his precious nose!" as an unusually large saucepan flew close by it, and very nearly carried it off.
sentences.zh: “哎呀，他那只宝贝鼻子要没了！”这时一只特别大的炖锅从鼻子旁边飞过，差一点就把它削掉了。

paragraphs.text: "If everybody minded their own business," the Duchess said in a hoarse growl, "the world would go round a deal faster than it does."

sentences.text: "If everybody minded their own business," the Duchess said in a hoarse growl, "the world would go round a deal faster than it does."
sentences.zh: “要是人人都管好自己的事，”公爵夫人用沙哑的嗓音低吼，“这世界转起来会比现在快得多。”

hints.zh: a deal 修饰比较级，表示“……得多”；a deal faster 就是“快得多”。
hints.en: A deal faster: a deal makes a comparative stronger, so much faster.

paragraphs.text: "Which would not be an advantage," said Alice, who felt very glad to get an opportunity of showing off a little of her knowledge. "Just think what work it would make with the day and night! You see the earth takes twenty-four hours to turn round on its axis——"

sentences.text: "Which would not be an advantage," said Alice, who felt very glad to get an opportunity of showing off a little of her knowledge.
sentences.zh: “那可不是什么好事，”爱丽丝说，她很高兴有机会卖弄一点自己的知识。

sentences.text: "Just think what work it would make with the day and night!
sentences.zh: “你想想，那会把白天和黑夜弄成什么样！

sentences.text: You see the earth takes twenty-four hours to turn round on its axis——"
sentences.zh: 你要知道，地球自转一圈要二十四小时——”

introduction.zh: 公爵夫人说话很不客气，爱丽丝只想赶紧换个话题。还没等她找到话头，厨娘就把汤锅端下火，开始把厨房里的东西一件件扔出去。爱丽丝吓得直跳脚——这一顿乱扔，要扔到什么时候？
introduction.en: The Duchess is rude, and Alice is only too glad to change the subject. Before she can think of one, the cook takes the soup off the fire and starts throwing everything she can reach. Alice watches in horror, jumping up and down.

quiz.question: What does the cook do with the cauldron of soup?
options: She pours a bowl of it for Alice.
She takes it off the fire and begins throwing things at the Duchess and the baby.
She throws the soup out of the window.

feedback.zh: 厨娘把汤锅端下火，随即把够得着的东西一件件朝公爵夫人和婴儿扔过去，先扔的是火炉用具。
feedback.en: The cook lifts the cauldron off the fire and starts throwing everything within reach at the Duchess and the baby.

quiz.question: How does the Duchess react when the things hit her?
options: She hides behind Alice.
She takes no notice at all.
She orders the cook out of the kitchen.

feedback.zh: 原文说她即使被砸中也不理会；婴儿本来就嚎得厉害，根本说不清有没有被砸疼。
feedback.en: The text says she takes no notice even when they hit her, and the baby is howling too much to tell whether it is hurt.

grammar.excerpt: If everybody minded their own business," the Duchess said in a hoarse growl, "the world would go round a deal faster than it does.

focus.zh: if 从句用过去式 minded，主句用 would + 原形；说的是与现在相反的假设，不是过去的事。
focus.en: The if-clause uses the past form minded and the main clause uses would + base form; this is a hypothetical, not a past event.

paragraphs.text: "Talking of axes," said the Duchess, "chop off her head!"

sentences.text: "Talking of axes," said the Duchess, "chop off her head!"
sentences.zh: “说到斧头，”公爵夫人说，“把她的头砍下来！”

hints.zh: axe（斧头）的复数 axes 与 axis（轴）的复数 axes 拼写相同；公爵夫人把“轴”听成了“斧头”。
hints.en: Axes is both the plural of axe and of axis; the Duchess hears axis as axe.

paragraphs.text: Alice glanced rather anxiously at the cook, to see if she meant to take the hint; but the cook was busily stirring the soup, and seemed not to be listening, so she went on again: "Twenty-four hours, I think; or is it twelve? I——"

sentences.text: Alice glanced rather anxiously at the cook, to see if she meant to take the hint; but the cook was busily stirring the soup, and seemed not to be listening, so she went on again: "Twenty-four hours, I think; or is it twelve?
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝相当紧张地瞟了厨娘一眼，看她是不是打算照这话去做；可厨娘正忙着搅汤，好像根本没在听，于是她又说下去：“我想是二十四小时吧；要么是十二小时？

paragraphs.text: "Oh, don't bother me," said the Duchess; "I never could abide figures!" And with that she began nursing her child again, singing a sort of lullaby to it as she did so, and giving it a violent shake at the end of every line :—

sentences.text: "Oh, don't bother me," said the Duchess; "I never could abide figures!"
sentences.zh: “唉，别来烦我，”公爵夫人说，“我这辈子都受不了数字！”

sentences.text: And with that she began nursing her child again, singing a sort of lullaby to it as she did so, and giving it a violent shake at the end of every line :—
sentences.zh: 说完她又抱起孩子哄起来，一边哄一边唱着一支像是摇篮曲的东西，每唱完一行就把孩子狠狠摇一下：——

hints.zh: 忍受、容忍；这里她说自己从来受不了数字，不是“遵守”。
hints.en: Abide: here it means to put up with; she cannot stand figures.

paragraphs.text: "Speak roughly to your little boy. And beat him when he sneezes: He only does it to annoy, Because he knows it teases."

sentences.text: "Speak roughly to your little boy.
sentences.zh: “对小男孩要粗声粗气地说话。

sentences.text: And beat him when he sneezes: He only does it to annoy, Because he knows it teases."
sentences.zh: 他打喷嚏就揍他一顿：他打喷嚏只为惹你生气，因为他知道这招气人。”

paragraphs.text: Chorus.

sentences.text: Chorus.
sentences.zh: 合唱。

hints.zh: 副歌，歌里大家一起跟着唱的那一段。
hints.en: Chorus: the part of a song that everyone sings together.

paragraphs.text: (In which the cook and the baby joined):—

sentences.text: (In which the cook and the baby joined):—
sentences.zh: （这一段厨娘和婴儿也一起唱）：——

paragraphs.text: "Wow! wow! wow!"

sentences.text: "Wow! wow! wow!"

paragraphs.text: While the Duchess sang the second verse of the song, she kept tossing the baby violently up and down, and the poor little thing howled so, that Alice could hardly hear the words:—

sentences.text: While the Duchess sang the second verse of the song, she kept tossing the baby violently up and down, and the poor little thing howled so, that Alice could hardly hear the words:—
sentences.zh: 公爵夫人唱第二段的时候，不停地把婴儿狠狠地往上抛又接住，那可怜的小东西嚎得太响，爱丽丝几乎听不清歌词：——

paragraphs.text: "I speak severely to my boy, I beat him when he sneezes; For he can thoroughly enjoy The pepper when he pleases!"

sentences.text: "I speak severely to my boy, I beat him when he sneezes; For he can thoroughly enjoy The pepper when he pleases!"
sentences.zh: “我对我家男孩说话很凶，他打喷嚏我就揍他；因为只要他乐意，就能把胡椒吃个痛快！”

paragraphs.text: Chorus.

sentences.text: Chorus.
sentences.zh: 合唱。

paragraphs.text: "Wow! wow! wow!"

sentences.text: "Wow! wow! wow!"

paragraphs.text: "Here! you may nurse it a bit, if you like!" the Duchess said to Alice, flinging the baby at her as she spoke. "I must go and get ready to play croquet with the Queen," and she hurried out of the room. The cook threw a frying-pan after her as she went, but it just missed her.

sentences.text: "Here! you may nurse it a bit, if you like!" the Duchess said to Alice, flinging the baby at her as she spoke.
sentences.zh: “喏！你要是愿意，就抱它一会儿！”公爵夫人对爱丽丝说，一边说一边把孩子朝她扔了过去。

sentences.text: "I must go and get ready to play croquet with the Queen," and she hurried out of the room.
sentences.zh: “我得去准备准备，好跟王后打槌球。”说完她就匆匆出了房间。

sentences.text: The cook threw a frying-pan after her as she went, but it just missed her.
sentences.zh: 她走的时候，厨娘朝她背后扔了一只煎锅，只差一点就打中她。

introduction.zh: 公爵夫人忽然喊了一声砍头，随即又抱起孩子，唱起一支古怪的摇篮曲，每唱完一行就把婴儿狠狠摇一下。厨娘和婴儿也跟着唱起副歌。爱丽丝站在一旁，不知道该不该开口。
introduction.en: The Duchess suddenly calls for someone's head, then takes her baby and sings a strange lullaby, shaking the child hard at the end of every line. The cook and the baby join in the chorus. Alice stands by, unsure whether to speak.

quiz.question: What does the Duchess do at the end of every line of her song?
options: She gives the baby a violent shake.
She throws a plate at the cook.
She stops to sneeze.

feedback.zh: 她一边唱一边摇孩子，每唱完一行就狠狠摇一下。
feedback.en: She sings to the child and gives it a violent shake at the end of every line.

quiz.question: Who joins in the chorus?
options: The cook and the baby.
Alice and the cook.
The Duchess alone.

feedback.zh: 原文括号里写明，副歌由厨娘和婴儿一起唱。
feedback.en: The stage direction in brackets says that the cook and the baby joined in the chorus.

grammar.excerpt: she kept tossing the baby violently up and down

focus.zh: kept 后面接“宾语 + -ing”：kept tossing the baby，表示一遍又一遍地抛。
focus.en: Keep takes an object plus -ing: kept tossing the baby means she did it again and again.

paragraphs.text: Alice caught the baby with some difficulty, as it was a queer-shaped little creature, and held out its arms and legs in all directions, "just like a star-fish," thought Alice. The poor little thing was snorting like a steam-engine when she caught it, and kept doubling itself up and straightening itself out again, so that altogether, for the first minute or two, it was as much as she could do to hold it.

sentences.text: Alice caught the baby with some difficulty, as it was a queer-shaped little creature, and held out its arms and legs in all directions, "just like a star-fish," thought Alice.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝费了点劲才接住婴儿，因为那是个形状古怪的小东西，手脚朝四面八方伸着；“活像一只海星，”爱丽丝心想。

sentences.text: The poor little thing was snorting like a steam-engine when she caught it, and kept doubling itself up and straightening itself out again, so that altogether, for the first minute or two, it was as much as she could do to hold it.
sentences.zh: 她接住它的时候，那可怜的小东西像蒸汽机一样呼哧呼哧地喷着气，一会儿把自己缩成一团，一会儿又伸直开来，所以头一两分钟里，她几乎拼尽全力才抱得住它。

hints.target: as much as she could do to hold it
hints.zh: 她几乎用尽全力才抱得住；as much as one can do 是“勉强做到”。
hints.en: As much as she could do to hold it: she could just manage to hold it.

paragraphs.text: As soon as she had made out the proper way of nursing it, (which was to twist it up into a sort of knot, and then keep tight hold of its right ear and left foot, so as to prevent its undoing itself,) she carried it out into the open air. "If I don't take this child away with me," thought Alice, "they're sure to kill it in a day or two: wouldn't it be murder to leave it behind?" She said the last words out loud, and the little thing grunted in reply (it had left off sneezing by this time). "Don't grunt," said Alice; "that's not at all a proper way of expressing yourself."

sentences.text: As soon as she had made out the proper way of nursing it, (which was to twist it up into a sort of knot, and then keep tight hold of its right ear and left foot, so as to prevent its undoing itself,) she carried it out into the open air.
sentences.zh: 她刚弄清楚该怎么抱它——就是把它扭成一个结，然后紧紧抓住它的右耳和左脚，免得它自己散开——就把它抱到了户外。

sentences.text: "If I don't take this child away with me," thought Alice, "they're sure to kill it in a day or two: wouldn't it be murder to leave it behind?"
sentences.zh: “我要是不把这孩子带走，”爱丽丝心想，“他们一两天内肯定会把它弄死：把它丢在这儿，不就是谋杀吗？”

sentences.text: She said the last words out loud, and the little thing grunted in reply (it had left off sneezing by this time).
sentences.zh: 最后那句话她大声说了出来，那小东西哼了一声算作回答（这时候它已经不打喷嚏了）。

sentences.text: "Don't grunt," said Alice; "that's not at all a proper way of expressing yourself."
sentences.zh: “别哼哼，”爱丽丝说，“那根本不是好好说话的样子。”

hints.zh: 弄明白、想出；make out 在这里是“搞清楚”。
hints.en: Made out: worked out or understood.

hints.zh: 停止；leave off doing 是“不再做某事”。
hints.en: Left off: stopped doing something.

paragraphs.text: The baby grunted again, and Alice looked very anxiously into its face to see what was the matter with it. There could be no doubt that it had a very turn-up nose, much more like a snout than a real nose; also its eyes were getting extremely small for a baby: altogether Alice did not like the look of the thing at all. "But perhaps it was only sobbing," she thought, and looked into its eyes again, to see if there were any tears.

sentences.text: The baby grunted again, and Alice looked very anxiously into its face to see what was the matter with it.
sentences.zh: 婴儿又哼了一声，爱丽丝非常担心地看它的脸，想知道它怎么了。

sentences.text: There could be no doubt that it had a very turn-up nose, much more like a snout than a real nose; also its eyes were getting extremely small for a baby: altogether Alice did not like the look of the thing at all.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，它长着一个很翘的鼻子，比起鼻子更像猪嘴；而且对一个婴儿来说，它的眼睛也变得越来越小：总之，爱丽丝一点也不喜欢这东西的模样。

sentences.text: "But perhaps it was only sobbing," she thought, and looked into its eyes again, to see if there were any tears.
sentences.zh: “不过也许它只是在抽泣，”她想，于是又看了看它的眼睛，看有没有眼泪。

hints.zh: 猪、狗等动物的长鼻子、口鼻部。
hints.en: Snout: the long nose of a pig or a dog.

introduction.zh: 一个模样古怪的婴儿落进爱丽丝怀里：它手脚乱伸，像蒸汽机一样喷着气，还不停地缩成一团又伸直。她好不容易找到一个抱稳的法子，抱着它走到屋外。这孩子到底怎么了？
introduction.en: A strange-shaped baby lands in Alice's arms: it sticks out its arms and legs, snorts like a steam engine and keeps curling up and stretching out again. She works out a way to hold it and carries it outside. What is wrong with the child?

quiz.question: Why does Alice decide to take the child away with her?
options: The Duchess asks her to keep it for ever.
She wants a child to play with at home.
She believes the others will kill it in a day or two.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝心想，要是把它留下，他们一两天内准会把它弄死，那简直就是谋杀。
feedback.en: Alice thinks that if she leaves it behind, the others are sure to kill it in a day or two.

quiz.question: How does Alice find a way to hold the baby?
options: She asks the cook to tie it up for her.
She wraps it in her apron and carries it on her back.
She twists it into a knot and holds its right ear and left foot.

feedback.zh: 她把孩子扭成一个结，再抓紧右耳和左脚，免得它自己散开。
feedback.en: She twists it into a sort of knot and holds tight to its right ear and left foot so that it cannot come undone.

grammar.excerpt: As soon as she had made out the proper way of nursing it

focus.zh: as soon as 引导时间从句，讲先发生的事；主句 she carried it out 是随后发生的动作。
focus.en: As soon as introduces the earlier action; the main clause, she carried it out, comes second in time.

paragraphs.text: No, there were no tears. "If you're going to turn into a pig, my dear," said Alice, seriously, "I'll have nothing more to do with you. Mind now!" The poor little thing sobbed again (or grunted, it was impossible to say which), and they went on for some while in silence.

sentences.text: No, there were no tears.
sentences.zh: 没有，一滴眼泪也没有。

sentences.text: "If you're going to turn into a pig, my dear," said Alice, seriously, "I'll have nothing more to do with you.
sentences.zh: “亲爱的，你要是打算变成猪，”爱丽丝认真地说，“那我就不再管你了。

sentences.text: Mind now!"
sentences.zh: 你可听好了！”

sentences.text: The poor little thing sobbed again (or grunted, it was impossible to say which), and they went on for some while in silence.
sentences.zh: 那可怜的小东西又抽泣了一声（也可能是哼了一声，实在分不清），他们就这样默默地走了一阵。

paragraphs.text: Alice was just beginning to think to herself, "Now, what am I to do with this creature when I get it home?" when it grunted again, so violently, that she looked down into its face in some alarm. This time there could be no mistake about it: it was neither more nor less than a pig, and she felt that it would be quite absurd for her to carry it any further.

sentences.text: Alice was just beginning to think to herself, "Now, what am I to do with this creature when I get it home?" when it grunted again, so violently, that she looked down into its face in some alarm.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝刚在心里琢磨：“等我把这东西带回家，拿它怎么办呢？”它又哼了一声，哼得那么用力，她有点惊慌地低头去看它的脸。

sentences.text: This time there could be no mistake about it: it was neither more nor less than a pig, and she felt that it would be quite absurd for her to carry it any further.
sentences.zh: 这一回绝不会看错了：它完完全全就是一头猪，她觉得再抱着它往前走实在太荒唐了。

hints.zh: 不多不少正是，简直就是。
hints.en: Neither more nor less than: exactly, and nothing else.

paragraphs.text: So she set the little creature down, and felt quite relieved to see it trot away quietly into the wood. "If it had grown up," she said to herself, "it would have made a dreadfully ugly child: but it makes rather a handsome pig, I think." And she began thinking over other children she knew, who might do very well as pigs, and was just saying to herself, "if one only knew the right way to change them——" when she was a little startled by seeing the Cheshire Cat sitting on a bough of a tree a few yards off.

sentences.text: So she set the little creature down, and felt quite relieved to see it trot away quietly into the wood.
sentences.zh: 于是她把那小东西放到地上，看它安安静静地小跑进树林，心里松了一口气。

sentences.text: "If it had grown up," she said to herself, "it would have made a dreadfully ugly child: but it makes rather a handsome pig, I think."
sentences.zh: “它要是长大，”她自言自语，“会变成一个丑得吓人的孩子；不过我觉得，它倒是一头挺漂亮的猪。”

sentences.text: And she began thinking over other children she knew, who might do very well as pigs, and was just saying to herself, "if one only knew the right way to change them——" when she was a little startled by seeing the Cheshire Cat sitting on a bough of a tree a few yards off.
sentences.zh: 她开始想起自己认识的别的孩子，觉得他们变成猪大概也不错，正自言自语着“要是有人知道该怎么变就好了——”，忽然看见柴郡猫坐在几码外的一根树枝上，倒让她吃了一惊。

hints.zh: 大树枝；bough 多指树的主枝。
hints.en: Bough: a large branch of a tree.

paragraphs.text: The Cat only grinned when it saw Alice. It looked good-natured, she thought: still it had very long claws and a great many teeth, so she felt that it ought to be treated with respect.

sentences.text: The Cat only grinned when it saw Alice.
sentences.zh: 那猫看见爱丽丝，只是咧嘴笑了笑。

sentences.text: It looked good-natured, she thought: still it had very long claws and a great many teeth, so she felt that it ought to be treated with respect.
sentences.zh: 她想，它看上去脾气不错；可它爪子很长，牙齿也很多，所以她觉得还是得敬着它一点。

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝抱着孩子穿过树林，越看越觉得不对劲：那张脸怎么看都不像个正常的婴儿。她认真地对它说了几句话，回答她的却只是一声哼哼。她还能把它带回自己家吗？
introduction.en: Alice carries the child through the wood and cannot shake the feeling that something is wrong with its face. She speaks to it seriously, and gets a grunt for an answer. Can she still take it home with her?

quiz.question: What makes Alice certain that the creature is really a pig?
options: It runs away from her on four short legs.
It grunts so violently that she looks into its face in alarm.
The Duchess shouts after her that it is a pig.

feedback.zh: 它又一次哼哼，爱丽丝低头细看，这一回再不会看错：它完完全全就是一头猪。
feedback.en: It grunts again, and when she looks into its face there can be no mistake: it is neither more nor less than a pig.

quiz.question: What does Alice think of the pig as she sets it down?
options: It ought to be taken back to the Duchess.
It makes rather a handsome pig.
It will never survive in the wood.

paragraphs.text: "Cheshire Puss," she began, rather timidly, as she did not at all know whether it would like the name: however, it only grinned a little wider. "Come, it's pleased so far," thought Alice, and she went on, "Would you tell me, please, which way I ought to go from here?"

sentences.text: "Come, it's pleased so far," thought Alice, and she went on, "Would you tell me, please, which way I ought to go from here?"

paragraphs.text: "I don't much care where——" said Alice.

sentences.text: "What sort of people live about here?"

sentences.text: "In that direction," the Cat said, waving its right paw round, "lives a Hatter: and in that direction," waving the other paw, "lives a March Hare.

sentences.text: Visit either you like: they're both mad."

sentences.text: "How do you know I'm mad?" said Alice.

sentences.zh: “你一定是疯的，”猫说，“不然你就不会到这儿来了。”

sentences.text: Alice didn't think that proved it at all; however, she went on: "And how do you know that you're mad?"
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝认为这根本证明不了什么；不过她还是接着问：“那你怎么知道自己疯了呢？”

introduction.zh: 柴郡猫又出现了，蹲在树枝上冲爱丽丝笑。她客客气气地问，自己该往哪边走；猫说，这要看她想去哪儿。她说不清自己到底想去哪儿——猫会给她指一条什么样的路呢？
introduction.en: The Cheshire Cat is back, grinning from a branch. Alice politely asks which way she should go, and the Cat says that depends on where she wants to get to. She is not sure, so what answer will she get?

quiz.question: What does the Cat say when Alice asks which way she ought to go?
options: It depends on where she wants to get to.
She should follow the March Hare.
She should go back the way she came.

feedback.zh: 猫说，这要看她想到哪儿去；她说不清目的地，猫便说走哪条路都无所谓。
feedback.en: The Cat says it depends on where she wants to get to; when she cannot say, he answers that any way will do.

quiz.question: Why does the Cat say Alice must be mad?
options: Because she keeps talking to a cat in a tree.
Because she has come here, where everyone is mad.
Because she cannot remember her own name.

feedback.zh: 猫说“你一定是疯的，不然你就不会到这儿来了”，把“来这儿”当成发疯的证据。
feedback.en: He says she must be mad, or she would not have come here, treating her arrival as the proof.

grammar.excerpt: or you wouldn't have come here

focus.zh: wouldn't have come 是“情态动词 + have + 过去分词”，对过去作相反的推断：既然你来了，就说明你疯了。
focus.en: Wouldn't have come is modal + have + past participle: it draws a conclusion about the past that is contrary to fact.

paragraphs.text: "Well, then," the Cat went on, "you see a dog growls when it's angry, and wags its tail when it's pleased. Now I growl when I'm pleased, and wag my tail when I'm angry. Therefore I'm mad."

sentences.text: "Well, then," the Cat went on, "you see a dog growls when it's angry, and wags its tail when it's pleased.
sentences.zh: “那好，”猫接着说，“你瞧，狗生气的时候就低吼，高兴的时候就摇尾巴。

sentences.text: Now I growl when I'm pleased, and wag my tail when I'm angry.

hints.en: Purring: the soft sound a happy cat makes, which Alice says is not a growl.

sentences.text: "I should like it very much," said Alice, "but I haven't been invited yet."
sentences.zh: “我很想去，”爱丽丝说，“可还没人请我呢。”

sentences.zh: “你会在那儿见到我的，”猫说，然后就消失了。

paragraphs.text: Alice was not much surprised at this, she was getting so well used to queer things happening. While she was still looking at the place where it had been, it suddenly appeared again.

sentences.text: Alice was not much surprised at this, she was getting so well used to queer things happening.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝对此并不太吃惊，她已经很习惯这种古怪的事了。

sentences.zh: 她还在望着它刚才待过的地方，它忽然又出现了。

sentences.zh: “顺便问一句，那个婴儿后来怎么样了？”猫说。

sentences.zh: “我差点忘了问。”

sentences.text: "I've seen hatters before," she said to herself: "the March Hare will be much the most interesting, and perhaps as this is May it won't be raving mad—at least not so mad as it was in March."

sentences.zh: 她正说着，抬头一看，那猫又在那儿了，坐在一根树枝上。

sentences.text: "I said pig," replied Alice; "and I wish you wouldn't keep appearing and vanishing so suddenly: you make one quite giddy."

introduction.zh: 猫说这里人人都疯了，连爱丽丝也不例外，还举出狗的例子，证明自己疯得有道理。爱丽丝觉得这说法根本站不住脚。说着说着，猫问起那个婴儿的下落，随后又一次不见了。
introduction.en: The Cat says everyone here is mad, Alice included, and uses a dog to prove that he is mad too. Alice does not think much of the argument. Then he asks what became of the baby, and disappears again.

quiz.question: How does the Cat prove that he is mad?
options: He forgets where he lives and who he is.
He vanishes whenever someone speaks to him.
He growls when he is pleased and wags his tail when he is angry.

feedback.zh: 狗生气时低吼、高兴时摇尾；猫说自己正好相反，所以是疯的。
feedback.en: Dogs growl when angry and wag their tails when pleased; the Cat does the opposite, so he calls himself mad.

quiz.question: What does the Cat ask about when it comes back?
options: What became of the baby.
Where Alice is going to sleep.
Whether Alice can play croquet.

feedback.zh: 它一回来就问“那个婴儿后来怎么样了”，还说自己差点忘了问。
feedback.en: He comes back to ask what became of the baby, and admits he had nearly forgotten to ask.

grammar.excerpt: I haven't been invited yet

focus.zh: have been + 过去分词是现在完成时的被动：她“还没有被邀请”，说的正是此刻的状况。
focus.en: Have been + past participle is the present perfect passive: she has not been invited, and that is still true now.

paragraphs.text: "All right," said the Cat; and this time it vanished quite slowly, beginning with the end of the tail, and ending with the grin, which remained some time after the rest of it had gone.

sentences.text: "All right," said the Cat; and this time it vanished quite slowly, beginning with the end of the tail, and ending with the grin, which remained some time after the rest of it had gone.

sentences.text: "Well!
sentences.zh: “哎呀！

sentences.text: I've often seen a cat without a grin," thought Alice; "but a grin without a cat!

sentences.text: It's the most curious thing I ever saw in all my life!"
sentences.zh: 这是我一辈子见过的最奇怪的东西！”

paragraphs.text: She had not gone much farther before she came in sight of the house of the March Hare: she thought it must be the right house, because the chimneys were shaped like ears and the roof was thatched with fur. It was so large a house, that she did not like to go nearer till she had nibbled some more of the left-hand bit of mushroom, and raised herself to about two feet high: even then she walked up towards it rather timidly, saying to herself, "Suppose it should be raving mad after all! I almost wish I'd gone to see the Hatter instead!"

sentences.text: She had not gone much farther before she came in sight of the house of the March Hare: she thought it must be the right house, because the chimneys were shaped like ears and the roof was thatched with fur.

sentences.text: It was so large a house, that she did not like to go nearer till she had nibbled some more of the left-hand bit of mushroom, and raised herself to about two feet high: even then she walked up towards it rather timidly, saying to herself, "Suppose it should be raving mad after all!
sentences.zh: 那房子那么大，她不敢再走近，先又啃了一点左手那块蘑菇，把自己长到大约两英尺高；即便这样，她还是相当胆怯地朝它走去，一边自言自语：“万一它真的疯得厉害呢！

sentences.zh: 我几乎有点后悔，还不如去看帽匠呢！”

hints.en: The left-hand bit of mushroom: the piece Alice nibbles to change her size.

introduction.zh: 这一回，猫消失得很慢：先从尾巴尖不见，最后才轮到那个笑容，笑了好一会儿才散去。爱丽丝从没见过这样的事。她继续往前走，来到三月兔的房子前，那房子大得让她不敢靠近。
introduction.en: This time the Cat vanishes slowly, tail first, and the grin stays behind after the rest of him is gone. Alice has never seen anything like it. She walks on and reaches the March Hare's house, which is far too big to approach.

quiz.question: In what order does the Cat vanish this time?
options: From the grin to the end of the tail.
From the end of the tail to the grin.
All at once, without leaving anything behind.

feedback.en: It begins with the end of the tail and ends with the grin, which stays for a while after the rest has gone.

quiz.question: Why does Alice think the March Hare's house must be the right one?

The Cat is waiting for her at the door.
Its chimneys are shaped like ears and its roof is thatched with fur.

grammar.excerpt: the grin, which remained some time after the rest of it had gone

focus.en: The comma before which marks a non-restrictive clause: it adds a comment about the grin instead of identifying it.

"Very uncomfortable for the Dormouse," thought Alice; "only, as it's asleep, I suppose it doesn't mind."

sentences.text: There was a table set out under a tree in front of the house, and the March Hare and the Hatter were having tea at it: a Dormouse was sitting between them, fast asleep, and the other two were using it as a cushion, resting their elbows on it, and talking over its head.

sentences.zh: “我没看见有什么葡萄酒。”她说。

paragraphs.text: "There isn't any," said the March Hare.

sentences.text: "There isn't any," said the March Hare.
sentences.zh: “本来就没有。”三月兔说。

paragraphs.text: "Then it wasn't very civil of you to offer it," said Alice angrily.

sentences.text: "Then it wasn't very civil of you to offer it," said Alice angrily.
sentences.zh: “那你请我喝葡萄酒可不太礼貌。”爱丽丝生气地说。

paragraphs.text: "It wasn't very civil of you to sit down without being invited," said the March Hare.

sentences.text: "It wasn't very civil of you to sit down without being invited," said the March Hare.
sentences.zh: “没人请你你就坐下，可也不太礼貌。”三月兔说。

paragraphs.text: "I didn't know it was your table," said Alice; "it's laid for a great many more than three."

sentences.text: "I didn't know it was your table," said Alice; "it's laid for a great many more than three."
sentences.zh: “我不知道这是你的桌子，”爱丽丝说，“这桌子摆的位子，可远远不止三个人。”

paragraphs.text: "Your hair wants cutting," said the Hatter. He had been looking at Alice for some time with great curiosity, and this was his first speech.

sentences.text: "Your hair wants cutting," said the Hatter.
sentences.zh: “你的头发该剪了。”帽匠说。

sentences.text: He had been looking at Alice for some time with great curiosity, and this was his first speech.
sentences.zh: 他带着极大的好奇打量了爱丽丝好一会儿，这是他开口说的第一句话。

hints.zh: 英国说法，等于 needs cutting，意思是“该剪了”。
hints.en: A British use of want: 'wants cutting' means 'needs cutting'.

paragraphs.text: "You should learn not to make personal remarks," Alice said with some severity: "it's very rude."

sentences.text: "You should learn not to make personal remarks," Alice said with some severity: "it's very rude."
sentences.zh: “你该学会不要对别人评头论足，”爱丽丝有些严厉地说，“这很不礼貌。”

hints.zh: 议论别人外貌或私事的评论，通常被认为不礼貌。
hints.en: Comments about someone's appearance or private life, usually thought rude.

paragraphs.text: The Hatter opened his eyes very wide on hearing this; but all he said was, "Why is a raven like a writing-desk?"

sentences.text: The Hatter opened his eyes very wide on hearing this; but all he said was, "Why is a raven like a writing-desk?"
sentences.zh: 帽匠听了这话，把眼睛睁得大大的；可他只说了句：“为什么乌鸦像写字台？”

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝走到房子前，看见树下摆着一张很大的茶桌。三月兔、帽匠和一只睡鼠挤在桌子的一角，一见她来就齐声喊“没地方了！”。可桌上明明空着一大片——他们为什么这么说？
introduction.en: Alice comes to a house and finds a big tea table under a tree. The March Hare, the Hatter and the Dormouse are squeezed into one corner, and they shout that there is no room. Yet most of the table is empty. Why do they say that?

quiz.question: What is strange about the table when Alice arrives?
options: It is set for a party of thirty.
It is too small for three people.
It is large, yet the three sit crowded in one corner.

feedback.zh: 桌子很大，可三月兔、帽匠和睡鼠偏挤在一角，还冲爱丽丝喊没地方。
feedback.en: The table is large, but the three are crowded into one corner and still shout that there is no room.

quiz.question: Why does Alice call the March Hare impolite?
options: He offers her wine that does not exist.
He sits in the only arm-chair.
He refuses to pour her any tea.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝看遍桌子也没找到酒，三月兔承认本来就没有，她便说这样请客不礼貌。
feedback.en: Alice looks round, sees no wine and says so; when the March Hare admits there is none, she calls the offer uncivil.

grammar.excerpt: He had been looking at Alice for some time with great curiosity

focus.zh: had been looking 是过去完成进行时：从更早一直看到这一刻，强调已经持续了一阵。
focus.en: Had been looking is past perfect continuous: the looking went on for some time up to that moment.

paragraphs.text: "Come, we shall have some fun now!" thought Alice. "I'm glad they've begun asking riddles.—I believe I can guess that," she added aloud.

sentences.text: "Come, we shall have some fun now!" thought Alice.
sentences.zh: “好啊，这下可有得玩了！”爱丽丝想。

sentences.text: "I'm glad they've begun asking riddles.—I believe I can guess that," she added aloud.
sentences.zh: “我很高兴他们开始出谜语了。——我相信我能猜出来。”她大声补了一句。

paragraphs.text: "Do you mean that you think you can find out the answer to it?" said the March Hare.

sentences.text: "Do you mean that you think you can find out the answer to it?" said the March Hare.
sentences.zh: “你的意思是，你认为你能找出答案？”三月兔说。

paragraphs.text: "Exactly so," said Alice.

sentences.text: "Exactly so," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “正是。”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "Then you should say what you mean," the March Hare went on.

sentences.text: "Then you should say what you mean," the March Hare went on.
sentences.zh: “那你就该说出你的意思。”三月兔接着说。

paragraphs.text: "I do," Alice hastily replied; "at least—at least I mean what I say—that's the same thing, you know."

sentences.text: "I do," Alice hastily replied; "at least—at least I mean what I say—that's the same thing, you know."
sentences.zh: “我是这样啊，”爱丽丝急忙答道，“至少——至少我说什么就是什么意思——你知道，这是一回事。”

paragraphs.text: "Not the same thing a bit!" said the Hatter. "Why, you might just as well say that 'I see what I eat' is the same thing as 'I eat what I see'!"

sentences.text: "Not the same thing a bit!" said the Hatter.
sentences.zh: “根本不是一回事！”帽匠说。

sentences.text: "Why, you might just as well say that 'I see what I eat' is the same thing as 'I eat what I see'!"
sentences.zh: “哎呀，你倒不如说，‘我看见我吃的东西’跟‘我吃我看见的东西’是一回事！”

paragraphs.text: "You might just as well say," added the March Hare, "that 'I like what I get' is the same thing as 'I get what I like'!"

sentences.text: "You might just as well say," added the March Hare, "that 'I like what I get' is the same thing as 'I get what I like'!"
sentences.zh: “你倒不如说，”三月兔补充道，“‘我喜欢我得到的东西’跟‘我得到我喜欢的东西’是一回事！”

paragraphs.text: "You might just as well say," added the Dormouse, who seemed to be talking in his sleep, "that 'I breathe when I sleep' is the same thing as 'I sleep when I breathe'!"

sentences.text: "You might just as well say," added the Dormouse, who seemed to be talking in his sleep, "that 'I breathe when I sleep' is the same thing as 'I sleep when I breathe'!"
sentences.zh: “你倒不如说，”睡鼠补充道，它像是在说梦话，“‘我睡觉时呼吸’跟‘我呼吸时睡觉’是一回事！”

paragraphs.text: "It is the same thing with you," said the Hatter, and here the conversation dropped, and the party sat silent for a minute, while Alice thought over all she could remember about ravens and writing-desks, which wasn't much.

sentences.text: "It is the same thing with you," said the Hatter, and here the conversation dropped, and the party sat silent for a minute, while Alice thought over all she could remember about ravens and writing-desks, which wasn't much.
sentences.zh: “对你来说就是一回事。”帽匠说。说到这里，谈话断了，大家沉默了一分钟；爱丽丝把脑子里记得的关于乌鸦和写字台的事都想了一遍——可惜并不多。

hints.zh: 谈话中断了、说不下去了。
hints.en: 'The conversation dropped' means the talk simply stopped.

hints.zh: 这里指在场的一伙人，不是“聚会”。
hints.en: Here 'party' means the group of people present, not a celebration.

paragraphs.text: The Hatter was the first to break the silence. "What day of the month is it?" he said, turning to Alice: he had taken his watch out of his pocket, and was looking at it uneasily, shaking it every now and then, and holding it to his ear.

sentences.text: The Hatter was the first to break the silence.
sentences.zh: 帽匠第一个打破了沉默。

sentences.text: "What day of the month is it?" he said, turning to Alice: he had taken his watch out of his pocket, and was looking at it uneasily, shaking it every now and then, and holding it to his ear.
sentences.zh: “今天几号？”他转向爱丽丝说。他已经把怀表从口袋里掏了出来，不安地瞧着它，不时摇一摇，又贴到耳边听。

paragraphs.text: Alice considered a little, and said, "The fourth."

sentences.text: Alice considered a little, and said, "The fourth."
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝想了想，说：“四号。”

introduction.zh: 帽匠出了一个关于乌鸦和写字台的怪谜语，爱丽丝以为自己终于等到好玩的时刻。可三月兔紧接着追问她“说”和“想”的区别，她越解释越绕。你能跟上他们的逻辑吗？
introduction.en: The Hatter asks a riddle, and Alice thinks the fun is about to begin. But the March Hare starts asking what she means by what she says, and every answer leads her deeper into a tangle. Can you follow their logic?

quiz.question: Why does Alice think she has answered the March Hare?
options: She has guessed the riddle.
She has stopped listening to him.
She believes saying what you mean and meaning what you say are the same.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝认为“说出你的意思”和“说话算话”是一回事，所以觉得自己已经答上了。
feedback.en: Alice thinks saying what you mean and meaning what you say are the same thing, so she believes she has answered.

quiz.question: What does the Hatter do with his watch while he asks Alice the date?
options: He hands it to the March Hare.
He puts it back in his pocket.
He shakes it and holds it to his ear.

feedback.zh: 帽匠一边问日期，一边不安地看表、不时摇晃，还贴到耳边听。
feedback.en: As he asks the date, the Hatter looks at the watch uneasily, shakes it and holds it to his ear.

grammar.excerpt: you might just as well say that 'I see what I eat' is the same thing as 'I eat what I see'!

focus.zh: might just as well 后接动词原形，意思是“倒不如说”，帽匠用它来反讽爱丽丝的说法。
focus.en: Might just as well + verb means 'you could equally say'; the Hatter uses it to mock Alice's logic.

paragraphs.text: "Two days wrong!" sighed the Hatter. "I told you butter wouldn't suit the works!" he added, looking angrily at the March Hare.

sentences.text: "Two days wrong!" sighed the Hatter.
sentences.zh: “慢了两天！”帽匠叹着气说。

sentences.text: "I told you butter wouldn't suit the works!" he added, looking angrily at the March Hare.
sentences.zh: “我跟你说过，黄油不适合机芯！”他补了一句，气冲冲地看着三月兔。

hints.zh: 机芯，钟表内部的机械装置。
hints.en: The works: the moving parts inside a clock or watch.

paragraphs.text: "It was the best butter," the March Hare meekly replied.

sentences.text: "It was the best butter," the March Hare meekly replied.
sentences.zh: “那可是最好的黄油。”三月兔温顺地回答。

paragraphs.text: "Yes, but some crumbs must have got in as well," the Hatter grumbled: "you shouldn't have put it in with the bread-knife."

sentences.text: "Yes, but some crumbs must have got in as well," the Hatter grumbled: "you shouldn't have put it in with the bread-knife."
sentences.zh: “是啊，可一定还掉进去一些面包屑，”帽匠嘟囔道，“你不该用面包刀把它抹进去。”

paragraphs.text: The March Hare took the watch and looked at it gloomily: then he dipped it into his cup of tea, and looked at it again: but he could think of nothing better to say than his first remark, "It was the best butter, you know."

sentences.text: The March Hare took the watch and looked at it gloomily: then he dipped it into his cup of tea, and looked at it again: but he could think of nothing better to say than his first remark, "It was the best butter, you know."
sentences.zh: 三月兔接过怀表，愁闷地看了看；然后把它浸到自己的茶杯里，又看了看；可他想不出比头一句更好的话，只能说：“你知道，那可是最好的黄油。”

paragraphs.text: Alice had been looking over his shoulder with some curiosity. "What a funny watch!" she remarked. "It tells the day of the month, and doesn't tell what o'clock it is!"

sentences.text: Alice had been looking over his shoulder with some curiosity.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝一直带着几分好奇，从他的肩膀后面看着。

sentences.text: "What a funny watch!" she remarked.
sentences.zh: “这表真奇怪！”她说。

sentences.text: "It tells the day of the month, and doesn't tell what o'clock it is!"
sentences.zh: “它报日期，却不报几点钟！”

paragraphs.text: "Why should it?" muttered the Hatter. "Does your watch tell you what year it is?"

sentences.text: "Why should it?" muttered the Hatter.
sentences.zh: “它为什么要报？”帽匠咕哝道。

sentences.text: "Does your watch tell you what year it is?"
sentences.zh: “你的表会告诉你今年是哪一年吗？”

paragraphs.text: "Of course not," Alice replied very readily: "but that's because it stays the same year for such a long time together."

sentences.text: "Of course not," Alice replied very readily: "but that's because it stays the same year for such a long time together."
sentences.zh: “当然不会，”爱丽丝不假思索地回答，“可那是因为一年要过很久才换一次啊。”

paragraphs.text: "Which is just the case with mine," said the Hatter.

sentences.text: "Which is just the case with mine," said the Hatter.
sentences.zh: “我的表正是这种情况。”帽匠说。

paragraphs.text: Alice felt dreadfully puzzled. The Hatter's remark seemed to her to have no sort of meaning in it, and yet it was certainly English. "I don't quite understand you," she said, as politely as she could.

sentences.text: Alice felt dreadfully puzzled.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝觉得非常困惑。

sentences.text: The Hatter's remark seemed to her to have no sort of meaning in it, and yet it was certainly English.
sentences.zh: 在她看来，帽匠的话似乎一点意思也没有，可那又确确实实是英语。

sentences.text: "I don't quite understand you," she said, as politely as she could.
sentences.zh: “我不太明白你的意思。”她尽量礼貌地说。

paragraphs.text: "The Dormouse is asleep again," said the Hatter, and he poured a little hot tea on its nose.

sentences.text: "The Dormouse is asleep again," said the Hatter, and he poured a little hot tea on its nose.
sentences.zh: “睡鼠又睡着了。”帽匠说着，往它的鼻子上倒了一点热茶。

paragraphs.text: The Dormouse shook its head impatiently, and said, without opening its eyes, "Of course, of course; just what I was going to remark myself."

sentences.text: The Dormouse shook its head impatiently, and said, without opening its eyes, "Of course, of course; just what I was going to remark myself."
sentences.zh: 睡鼠不耐烦地摇摇头，眼睛也没睁，说：“当然，当然；这正是我本来要说的。”

paragraphs.text: "Have you guessed the riddle yet?" the Hatter said, turning to Alice again.

sentences.text: "Have you guessed the riddle yet?" the Hatter said, turning to Alice again.
sentences.zh: “你猜出那个谜语了吗？”帽匠又转向爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "No, I give it up," Alice replied: "what's the answer?"

sentences.text: "No, I give it up," Alice replied: "what's the answer?"
sentences.zh: “没有，我放弃了，”爱丽丝回答，“答案是什么？”

hints.zh: 放弃（猜谜、尝试），这里指认输、不再猜了。
hints.en: 'I give it up' means 'I stop trying'; Alice gives up on the riddle.

introduction.zh: 帽匠掏出怀表，愁眉苦脸地摇一摇，又贴在耳边听。他说表慢了两天，还怪三月兔往机芯里抹了黄油。爱丽丝凑过去，想看看这只表究竟哪里不对——它真的还能报时吗？
introduction.en: The Hatter pulls out his watch, shakes it and holds it to his ear. It is two days wrong, and he blames the March Hare for putting butter into the works. When Alice looks closer, she wonders what is wrong with it — can it still tell the time?

quiz.question: Why does the Hatter blame the March Hare?
options: The March Hare has broken the watch.
The March Hare put butter in the works of the watch.
The March Hare told him the wrong date.

feedback.zh: 帽匠认定是三月兔把黄油抹进机芯，才害得表慢了两天。
feedback.en: The Hatter is sure that the butter the March Hare put into the works has made the watch two days slow.

quiz.question: What is unusual about the Hatter's watch?
options: It tells the day of the month but not the hour.
It has stopped at six o'clock.
It shows the year but not the month.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝发现这表只报日期，不报钟点，这和普通怀表正好相反。
feedback.en: Alice notices that the watch tells the day of the month but not the time, the opposite of a normal watch.

grammar.excerpt: you shouldn't have put it in with the bread-knife

focus.zh: shouldn't have put 是“情态动词 + have + 过去分词”，责怪对方过去做了某事。
focus.en: Shouldn't have put is modal + have + past participle: it blames someone for a past action.

paragraphs.text: "I haven't the slightest idea," said the Hatter.

sentences.text: "I haven't the slightest idea," said the Hatter.
sentences.zh: “我一点头绪也没有。”帽匠说。

paragraphs.text: "Nor I," said the March Hare.

sentences.text: "Nor I," said the March Hare.
sentences.zh: “我也没有。”三月兔说。

paragraphs.text: Alice sighed wearily. "I think you might do something better with the time," she said, "than wasting it in asking riddles that have no answers."

sentences.text: Alice sighed wearily.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝疲惫地叹了口气。

sentences.text: "I think you might do something better with the time," she said, "than wasting it in asking riddles that have no answers."
sentences.zh: “我觉得你们本可以把时间拿去做点更好的事，”她说，“而不是浪费在出这些没有答案的谜语上。”

paragraphs.text: "If you knew Time as well as I do," said the Hatter, "you wouldn't talk about wasting it. It's him."

sentences.text: "If you knew Time as well as I do," said the Hatter, "you wouldn't talk about wasting it.
sentences.zh: “你要是像我一样了解时间，”帽匠说，“就不会说什么浪费它了。

sentences.text: It's him."
sentences.zh: 时间就是他。”

hints.zh: 时间；帽匠在这里把它当成一位可以交谈、可以得罪的先生。
hints.en: Time; the Hatter speaks of it as a person you can talk to and offend.

paragraphs.text: "I don't know what you mean," said Alice.

sentences.text: "I don't know what you mean," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “我不明白你是什么意思。”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "Of course you don't!" the Hatter said, tossing his head contemptuously. "I dare say you never even spoke to Time!"

sentences.text: "Of course you don't!" the Hatter said, tossing his head contemptuously.
sentences.zh: “你当然不明白！”帽匠轻蔑地一甩头说。

sentences.text: "I dare say you never even spoke to Time!"
sentences.zh: “我敢说你从来没跟时间说过话！”

paragraphs.text: "Perhaps not," Alice cautiously replied: "but I know I have to beat time when I learn music."

sentences.text: "Perhaps not," Alice cautiously replied: "but I know I have to beat time when I learn music."
sentences.zh: “也许没有，”爱丽丝小心地回答，“可我知道，我学音乐的时候得打拍子。”

hints.zh: 打拍子，按节拍用手或脚示意；帽匠却听成了“打时间”。
hints.en: 'Beat time' means to mark the rhythm in music; the Hatter hears it as hitting Time.

paragraphs.text: "Ah! that accounts for it," said the Hatter. "He won't stand beating. Now, if you only kept on good terms with him, he'd do almost anything you liked with the clock. For instance, suppose it were nine o'clock in the morning, just time to begin lessons: you'd only have to whisper a hint to Time, and round goes the clock in a twinkling! Half-past one, time for dinner!"

sentences.text: "Ah! that accounts for it," said the Hatter.
sentences.zh: “啊！这就说得通了。”帽匠说。

sentences.text: "He won't stand beating.
sentences.zh: “他可受不了别人打他。

sentences.text: Now, if you only kept on good terms with him, he'd do almost anything you liked with the clock.
sentences.zh: 你要是跟他处好关系，你想让钟指到几点，它几乎就能指到几点。

sentences.text: For instance, suppose it were nine o'clock in the morning, just time to begin lessons: you'd only have to whisper a hint to Time, and round goes the clock in a twinkling!
sentences.zh: 比如说，假定现在是早上九点，正好该开始上课：你只要跟时间悄悄提一句，一眨眼，钟就转过去了！

sentences.text: Half-past one, time for dinner!"
sentences.zh: 一点半，该吃午饭了！”

hints.zh: 解释了原因，这里指“难怪会这样”。
hints.en: 'That accounts for it' means 'that explains why it is so'.

hints.zh: 跟某人关系好、相处融洽。
hints.en: To be 'on good terms with' someone is to have a friendly relationship with them.

hints.zh: 一眨眼之间，形容极快。
hints.en: 'In a twinkling' means in a very short time, in an instant.

paragraphs.text: ("I only wish it was," the March Hare said to itself in a whisper.)

sentences.text: ("I only wish it was," the March Hare said to itself in a whisper.)
sentences.zh: （“我倒希望真是这样。”三月兔小声自言自语。）

paragraphs.text: "That would be grand, certainly," said Alice thoughtfully: "but then—I shouldn't be hungry for it, you know."

sentences.text: "That would be grand, certainly," said Alice thoughtfully: "but then—I shouldn't be hungry for it, you know."
sentences.zh: “那当然好极了，”爱丽丝若有所思地说，“可是那样一来——你知道，我就不会饿得想吃午饭了。”

paragraphs.text: "Not at first, perhaps," said the Hatter: "but you could keep it to half-past one as long as you liked."

sentences.text: "Not at first, perhaps," said the Hatter: "but you could keep it to half-past one as long as you liked."
sentences.zh: “也许一开始不饿，”帽匠说，“可你可以把时间一直保持在一点半，想保持多久就多久。”

paragraphs.text: "Is that the way you manage?" Alice asked.

sentences.text: "Is that the way you manage?"
sentences.zh: “你们就是这么做的？”

sentences.text: Alice asked.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝问。

paragraphs.text: The Hatter shook his head mournfully. "Not I!" he replied. "We quarrelled last March——just before he went mad, you know——" (pointing with his teaspoon at the March Hare,) "——it was at the great concert given by the Queen of Hearts, and I had to sing 'Twinkle, twinkle, little bat! How I wonder what you're at!'

sentences.text: The Hatter shook his head mournfully.
sentences.zh: 帽匠伤心地摇了摇头。

sentences.text: "Not I!" he replied.
sentences.zh: “我没唱！”他回答。

sentences.text: "We quarrelled last March——just before he went mad, you know——" (pointing with his teaspoon at the March Hare,) "——it was at the great concert given by the Queen of Hearts, and I had to sing 'Twinkle, twinkle, little bat!
sentences.zh: “我们三月里吵了一架——就在他发疯之前，你知道——”他用茶匙指了指三月兔，“——那是在红心王后办的一场大型音乐会上，我不得不唱《一闪一闪，小蝙蝠！

sentences.text: How I wonder what you're at!'
sentences.zh: 我多想知道你在干什么！”

hints.zh: 红心王后，奇境里的统治者，动不动就喊砍头。
hints.en: The Queen of Hearts, the ruler of Wonderland who is always shouting for heads to be cut off.

paragraphs.text: You know the song, perhaps?"

sentences.text: You know the song, perhaps?"
sentences.zh: 你也许知道这首歌吧？”

paragraphs.text: "I've heard something like it," said Alice.

sentences.text: "I've heard something like it," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “我听过类似的。”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "It goes on, you know," the Hatter continued, "in this way:—

sentences.text: "It goes on, you know," the Hatter continued, "in this way:—
sentences.zh: “你知道，它接着往下唱，”帽匠继续说，“是这样——”

paragraphs.text: 'Up above the world you fly, Like a teatray in the sky. Twinkle, twinkle————'"

sentences.text: 'Up above the world you fly, Like a teatray in the sky.
sentences.zh: ‘你飞在世界上方，像天上的一只茶盘。

sentences.text: Twinkle, twinkle————'"
sentences.zh: 一闪一闪——’”

introduction.zh: 帽匠说，时间不是钟表上的刻度，而是一位可以得罪的“先生”。爱丽丝只知道自己学琴时要打拍子，这在她看来再自然不过。两个人说的明明是同一个词，为什么完全对不上？
introduction.en: The Hatter talks about Time as if it were a person who can be offended. Alice only knows that she has to beat time when she learns music. They use the same word, yet they mean completely different things. Why can't they agree?

quiz.question: Why does the Hatter think Alice has never spoken to Time?
options: She says she has wasted her whole day.
She only knows beating time when she learns music.
She cannot read a clock.

feedback.zh: 帽匠把时间当成一个人；爱丽丝却只说自己练琴时得“打拍子”，所以他断定她根本不懂时间。
feedback.en: The Hatter treats Time as a person, so Alice's remark about beating time in music convinces him she knows nothing about it.

quiz.question: What does the Hatter say Time would do for a friend?
options: Give them a new watch.
Turn the clock to any hour they liked.
Make them always hungry.

feedback.zh: 帽匠说，只要跟时间处好关系，想让钟是几点，它几乎就能是几点。
feedback.en: The Hatter says that if you stayed on good terms with Time, the clock would show almost any hour you liked.

grammar.excerpt: if you only kept on good terms with him, he'd do almost anything you liked with the clock.

focus.zh: if you only kept ... he'd do 是第二类条件句：if 从句用过去式，主句用 would + 原形，说与现在相反的假设。
focus.en: If you kept ... he'd do is a second conditional: past tense in the if-clause, would + verb in the main clause, for an unreal present.

title.en: Why the Table Is Always Laid

paragraphs.text: Here the Dormouse shook itself, and began singing in its sleep "Twinkle, twinkle, twinkle, twinkle——" and went on so long that they had to pinch it to make it stop.

sentences.text: Here the Dormouse shook itself, and began singing in its sleep "Twinkle, twinkle, twinkle, twinkle——" and went on so long that they had to pinch it to make it stop.
sentences.zh: 这时睡鼠抖了抖身子，在睡梦中唱起来：“一闪一闪，一闪一闪——”它唱个没完，他们只好掐它一下，让它停下来。

paragraphs.text: "Well, I'd hardly finished the first verse," said the Hatter, "when the Queen bawled out, 'He's murdering the time! Off with his head!'"

sentences.text: "Well, I'd hardly finished the first verse," said the Hatter, "when the Queen bawled out, 'He's murdering the time!
sentences.zh: “我第一段还没唱完，”帽匠说，“王后就嚷起来：‘他在糟蹋时间！

sentences.text: Off with his head!'"
sentences.zh: 砍掉他的头！’”

hints.zh: 糟蹋时间、把时间弄坏；这里是“kill time（消磨时间）”的夸张说法。
hints.en: 'Murdering the time' means ruining time; it plays on the phrase 'kill time'.

paragraphs.text: "How dreadfully savage!" exclaimed Alice.

sentences.text: "How dreadfully savage!" exclaimed Alice.
sentences.zh: “太残暴了！”爱丽丝叫道。

paragraphs.text: "And ever since that," the Hatter went on in a mournful tone, "he won't do a thing I ask! It's always six o'clock now."

sentences.text: "And ever since that," the Hatter went on in a mournful tone, "he won't do a thing I ask!
sentences.zh: “从那以后，”帽匠用悲伤的语调接着说，“我求它做什么，它都不肯做！

sentences.text: It's always six o'clock now."
sentences.zh: 现在永远是六点钟。”

paragraphs.text: A bright idea came into Alice's head. "Is that the reason so many tea-things are put out here?" she asked.

sentences.text: A bright idea came into Alice's head.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝脑子里冒出一个好主意。

sentences.text: "Is that the reason so many tea-things are put out here?" she asked.
sentences.zh: “这就是这里摆着这么多茶具的原因吗？”她问。

hints.zh: 茶具，指茶杯、茶碟、茶壶等一套东西。
hints.en: 'Tea-things' means the cups, saucers, pot and other tea equipment.

paragraphs.text: "Yes, that's it," said the Hatter with a sigh: "it's always tea-time, and we've no time to wash the things between whiles."

sentences.text: "Yes, that's it," said the Hatter with a sigh: "it's always tea-time, and we've no time to wash the things between whiles."
sentences.zh: “对，就是这样，”帽匠叹了口气说，“永远是喝茶时间，我们没空在两次之间洗茶具。”

hints.zh: 在空当里、在两次之间。
hints.en: 'Between whiles' means in the intervals between one thing and another.

paragraphs.text: "Then you keep moving round, I suppose?" said Alice.

sentences.text: "Then you keep moving round, I suppose?" said Alice.
sentences.zh: “那你们就一圈一圈地挪位子，我猜？”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "Exactly so," said the Hatter: "as the things get used up."

sentences.text: "Exactly so," said the Hatter: "as the things get used up."
sentences.zh: “正是，”帽匠说，“随着茶具一套套用脏。”

paragraphs.text: "But when do you come to the beginning again?" Alice ventured to ask.

sentences.text: "But when do you come to the beginning again?"
sentences.zh: “可你们什么时候才绕回开头呢？”

sentences.text: Alice ventured to ask.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝壮着胆子问。

paragraphs.text: "Suppose we change the subject," the March Hare interrupted, yawning. "I'm getting tired of this. I vote the young lady tells us a story."

sentences.text: "Suppose we change the subject," the March Hare interrupted, yawning.
sentences.zh: “咱们换个话题吧。”三月兔打着哈欠插嘴。

sentences.text: "I'm getting tired of this.
sentences.zh: “我听得都腻了。

sentences.text: I vote the young lady tells us a story."
sentences.zh: 我提议让这位小姐给咱们讲个故事。”

hints.zh: 我提议、我建议；vote 这里不是“投票选举”。
hints.en: 'I vote' here means 'I suggest', not voting in an election.

paragraphs.text: "I'm afraid I don't know one," said Alice, rather alarmed at the proposal.

sentences.text: "I'm afraid I don't know one," said Alice, rather alarmed at the proposal.
sentences.zh: “恐怕我一个故事也不会讲。”爱丽丝说，这提议让她有点惊慌。

paragraphs.text: "Then the Dormouse shall!" they both cried. "Wake up, Dormouse!" And they pinched it on both sides at once.

sentences.text: "Then the Dormouse shall!" they both cried.
sentences.zh: “那就让睡鼠讲！”两人一齐喊道。

sentences.text: "Wake up, Dormouse!"
sentences.zh: “醒醒，睡鼠！”

sentences.text: And they pinched it on both sides at once.
sentences.zh: 他们同时从两边掐它。

paragraphs.text: The Dormouse slowly opened his eyes. "I wasn't asleep," he said in a hoarse, feeble voice: "I heard every word you fellows were saying."

sentences.text: The Dormouse slowly opened his eyes.
sentences.zh: 睡鼠慢慢睁开眼睛。

sentences.text: "I wasn't asleep," he said in a hoarse, feeble voice: "I heard every word you fellows were saying."
sentences.zh: “我没睡着，”它用沙哑微弱的声音说，“你们说的每个字我都听见了。”

paragraphs.text: "Tell us a story!" said the March Hare.

sentences.text: "Tell us a story!" said the March Hare.
sentences.zh: “给我们讲个故事！”三月兔说。

paragraphs.text: "Yes, please do!" pleaded Alice.

sentences.text: "Yes, please do!" pleaded Alice.
sentences.zh: “对，讲一个吧！”爱丽丝恳求道。

paragraphs.text: "And be quick about it," added the Hatter, "or you'll be asleep again before it's done."

sentences.text: "And be quick about it," added the Hatter, "or you'll be asleep again before it's done."
sentences.zh: “而且快点讲，”帽匠补了一句，“不然故事还没讲完，你又睡着了。”

introduction.zh: 帽匠说起一件旧事：他曾在红心王后面前唱歌，王后当场喊了一句什么。那声喊之后，他的时间就出了毛病，茶桌上的茶具也一直撤不下去。可一直喝茶，总得有个尽头吧？
introduction.en: The Hatter tells an old story about singing before the Queen and the shout that followed. After that shout, he says, his clock went wrong, and the tea-things on the table are never cleared away. But can a tea party go on for ever?

quiz.question: Why does the Hatter's watch stay at six o'clock?
options: Time will not do anything he asks, after the Queen's shout.
The March Hare has hidden the hands.
It is broken and cannot be mended.

feedback.zh: 帽匠说，自从王后喊“他在糟蹋时间”，时间就再也不肯听他的，于是钟一直停在六点。
feedback.en: Since the Queen shouted that he was murdering the time, Time has refused to do anything the Hatter asks.

quiz.question: Why are so many tea-things set out?
options: The Queen ordered a large tea party.
The Hatter collects cups.
It is always tea-time, so they have no time to wash the things.

feedback.zh: 帽匠解释说，这里永远是喝茶时间，他们根本没空在两次喝茶之间洗茶具。
feedback.en: The Hatter explains that it is always tea-time, so there is never a moment to wash the things between teas.

grammar.excerpt: went on so long that they had to pinch it to make it stop

focus.zh: so ... that 结构：so 修饰 long，that 引出结果——它唱得太久，大家只好掐它。
focus.en: So ... that links the long singing to its result: they had to pinch it to make it stop.

title.en: Three Sisters in a Treacle Well

paragraphs.text: "Once upon a time there were three little sisters," the Dormouse began in a great hurry; "and their names were Elsie, Lacie, and Tillie; and they lived at the bottom of a well——"

sentences.text: "Once upon a time there were three little sisters," the Dormouse began in a great hurry; "and their names were Elsie, Lacie, and Tillie; and they lived at the bottom of a well——"
sentences.zh: “从前有三个小姐妹，”睡鼠急匆匆地开了头，“她们叫埃尔茜、莱茜和蒂莉；她们住在一口井的井底——”

hints.zh: 埃尔茜、莱茜、蒂莉，三个小姐妹的名字。
hints.en: Elsie, Lacie and Tillie: the names of the three little sisters.

paragraphs.text: "What did they live on?" said Alice, who always took a great interest in questions of eating and drinking.

sentences.text: "What did they live on?" said Alice, who always took a great interest in questions of eating and drinking.
sentences.zh: “她们靠什么过活？”爱丽丝说。她对吃喝的事总是很感兴趣。

hints.zh: 靠吃某样东西过活、以某物为主食。
hints.en: 'Live on' means to survive by eating a particular food.

paragraphs.text: "They lived on treacle," said the Dormouse, after thinking a minute or two.

sentences.text: "They lived on treacle," said the Dormouse, after thinking a minute or two.
sentences.zh: “她们靠吃糖浆过活。”睡鼠想了一两分钟才说。

hints.zh: 糖浆，英国说法，指熬糖时剩下的浓稠糖汁。
hints.en: Treacle: a thick dark syrup, a common British sweet food.

paragraphs.text: "They couldn't have done that, you know," Alice gently remarked: "they'd have been ill."

sentences.text: "They couldn't have done that, you know," Alice gently remarked: "they'd have been ill."
sentences.zh: “你知道，她们不可能那样做，”爱丽丝温和地说，“那样她们会生病的。”

paragraphs.text: "So they were," said the Dormouse; "very ill."

sentences.text: "So they were," said the Dormouse; "very ill."
sentences.zh: “她们确实病了，”睡鼠说，“病得很重。”

paragraphs.text: Alice tried a little to fancy to herself what such an extraordinary way of living would be like, but it puzzled her too much, so she went on: "But why did they live at the bottom of a well?"

sentences.text: Alice tried a little to fancy to herself what such an extraordinary way of living would be like, but it puzzled her too much, so she went on: "But why did they live at the bottom of a well?"
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝试着想象那种奇特的生活方式会是什么样，可这让她太糊涂了，于是她接着问：“可她们为什么住在井底呢？”

hints.zh: 在脑子里想象、设想。
hints.en: To 'fancy to herself' is to picture something in her own mind.

paragraphs.text: "Take some more tea," the March Hare said to Alice, very earnestly.

sentences.text: "Take some more tea," the March Hare said to Alice, very earnestly.
sentences.zh: “再喝点茶吧。”三月兔非常诚恳地对爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "I've had nothing yet," Alice replied in an offended tone, "so I can't take more."

sentences.text: "I've had nothing yet," Alice replied in an offended tone, "so I can't take more."
sentences.zh: “我还一口都没喝呢，”爱丽丝不高兴地回答，“所以没法再喝。”

paragraphs.text: "You mean you can't take less," said the Hatter: "it's very easy to take more than nothing."

sentences.text: "You mean you can't take less," said the Hatter: "it's very easy to take more than nothing."
sentences.zh: “你的意思是，你没法喝得更少，”帽匠说，“要想比‘什么也没喝’再多喝一点，那太容易了。”

paragraphs.text: "Nobody asked your opinion," said Alice.

sentences.text: "Nobody asked your opinion," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “没人问你的意见。”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "Who's making personal remarks now?" the Hatter asked triumphantly.

sentences.text: "Who's making personal remarks now?" the Hatter asked triumphantly.
sentences.zh: “现在是谁在议论别人的私事？”帽匠得意地问。

paragraphs.text: Alice did not quite know what to say to this: so she helped herself to some tea and bread-and-butter, and then turned to the Dormouse, and repeated her question. "Why did they live at the bottom of a well?"

sentences.text: Alice did not quite know what to say to this: so she helped herself to some tea and bread-and-butter, and then turned to the Dormouse, and repeated her question.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝不知该怎么接这话，就自己倒了点茶、拿了点黄油面包，然后转向睡鼠，又把问题问了一遍。

sentences.text: "Why did they live at the bottom of a well?"
sentences.zh: “她们为什么住在井底？”

paragraphs.text: The Dormouse again took a minute or two to think about it, and then said, "It was a treacle-well."

sentences.text: The Dormouse again took a minute or two to think about it, and then said, "It was a treacle-well."
sentences.zh: 睡鼠又想了一两分钟，然后说：“那是一口糖浆井。”

hints.zh: 糖浆井，睡鼠故事里生造出来的井，井里装的不是水而是糖浆。
hints.en: A treacle-well: an invented well in the Dormouse's story, filled with treacle instead of water.

paragraphs.text: "There's no such thing!" Alice was beginning very angrily, but the Hatter and the March Hare went "Sh! sh!" and the Dormouse sulkily remarked, "If you can't be civil, you'd better finish the story for yourself."

sentences.text: "There's no such thing!"
sentences.zh: “根本没有这种东西！”

sentences.text: Alice was beginning very angrily, but the Hatter and the March Hare went "Sh! sh!" and the Dormouse sulkily remarked, "If you can't be civil, you'd better finish the story for yourself."
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝正要气冲冲地开口，帽匠和三月兔却“嘘！嘘！”地制止她，睡鼠则闷闷不乐地说：“你要是不讲礼貌，这故事还是你自己讲完吧。”

introduction.zh: 轮到睡鼠讲故事了。它迷迷糊糊地讲起三个住在井底的小姐妹，靠吃糖浆过活。爱丽丝越听越觉得不对：人怎么能只吃糖浆？她们又为什么偏要住在井底？
introduction.en: It is the Dormouse's turn to tell a story. Half asleep, it describes three little sisters who live at the bottom of a well and live on treacle. Alice cannot believe it: how can anyone eat only treacle, and why live down a well?

quiz.question: Why does Alice doubt the Dormouse's story?
options: Three sisters could not live at the bottom of a well.
Living only on treacle would make the sisters ill.
The sisters' names are not real names.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝说，只靠糖浆过活是不可能的，那样三姐妹一定会生病。
feedback.en: Alice says the sisters could not have lived on treacle alone, because they would have been ill.

quiz.question: What does the March Hare do when Alice asks about the well?
options: He offers her more tea.
He wakes the Dormouse.
He answers her question.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝追问井的事，三月兔却不回答，只一个劲儿劝她再喝点茶。
feedback.en: Instead of answering Alice's question about the well, the March Hare earnestly offers her more tea.

grammar.excerpt: they'd have been ill

focus.zh: they'd have been 是 would have + 过去分词，承接上句 couldn't have done：要是真那样，她们早就病了。
focus.en: They'd have been is would have + past participle: it gives the past result of the imagined action in the sentence before.

paragraphs.text: "No, please go on!" Alice said very humbly: "I won't interrupt you again. I dare say there may be one."

sentences.text: "No, please go on!"
sentences.zh: “别，请接着讲！”

sentences.text: Alice said very humbly: "I won't interrupt you again.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝非常谦卑地说，“我不会再打断你了。

sentences.text: I dare say there may be one."
sentences.zh: 我想也许真有那么一口井。”

paragraphs.text: "One, indeed!" said the Dormouse indignantly. However, he consented to go on. "And so these three little sisters—they were learning to draw, you know——"

sentences.text: "One, indeed!" said the Dormouse indignantly.
sentences.zh: “真有，才怪！”睡鼠愤愤地说。

sentences.text: However, he consented to go on.
sentences.zh: 不过，它还是同意继续讲下去。

sentences.text: "And so these three little sisters—they were learning to draw, you know——"
sentences.zh: “于是这三个小姐妹——你知道，她们在学画画——”

hints.zh: 这里既可指“画画”，也可指“从井里打水”，睡鼠故意把两个意思混在一起。
hints.en: 'Draw' can mean 'make a picture' or 'pull water from a well'; the Dormouse plays on both.

paragraphs.text: "What did they draw?" said Alice, quite forgetting her promise.

sentences.text: "What did they draw?" said Alice, quite forgetting her promise.
sentences.zh: “她们画什么？”爱丽丝说，完全忘了自己的保证。

paragraphs.text: "Treacle," said the Dormouse, without considering at all this time.

sentences.text: "Treacle," said the Dormouse, without considering at all this time.
sentences.zh: “糖浆。”睡鼠这次想都没想就回答。

paragraphs.text: "I want a clean cup," interrupted the Hatter: "let's all move one place on."

sentences.text: "I want a clean cup," interrupted the Hatter: "let's all move one place on."
sentences.zh: “我要一个干净的杯子，”帽匠插嘴说，“咱们都往下挪一个位子吧。”

hints.zh: 依次挪到下一个位子。
hints.en: 'Move one place on' means each person moves to the next seat.

paragraphs.text: He moved on as he spoke, and the Dormouse followed him: the March Hare moved into the Dormouse's place, and Alice rather unwillingly took the place of the March Hare. The Hatter was the only one who got any advantage from the change: and Alice was a good deal worse off than before, as the March Hare had just upset the milk-jug into his plate.

sentences.text: He moved on as he spoke, and the Dormouse followed him: the March Hare moved into the Dormouse's place, and Alice rather unwillingly took the place of the March Hare.
sentences.zh: 他边说边挪过去，睡鼠跟着他；三月兔坐到了睡鼠的位子上，爱丽丝则很不情愿地坐到了三月兔的位子上。

sentences.text: The Hatter was the only one who got any advantage from the change: and Alice was a good deal worse off than before, as the March Hare had just upset the milk-jug into his plate.
sentences.zh: 这一换，只有帽匠占了便宜；爱丽丝的处境却比先前糟了不少，因为三月兔刚把牛奶罐打翻在自己的盘子里。

hints.zh: 境况更糟、处境更差。
hints.en: 'Worse off' means in a worse situation than before.

paragraphs.text: Alice did not wish to offend the Dormouse again, so she began very cautiously: "But I don't understand. Where did they draw the treacle from?"

sentences.text: Alice did not wish to offend the Dormouse again, so she began very cautiously: "But I don't understand.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝不想再惹睡鼠不高兴，于是非常小心地开口：“可我不明白。

sentences.text: Where did they draw the treacle from?"
sentences.zh: 她们是从哪儿打糖浆的呢？”

paragraphs.text: "You can draw water out of a water-well," said the Hatter; "so I should think you could draw treacle out of a treacle-well—eh, stupid?"

sentences.text: "You can draw water out of a water-well," said the Hatter; "so I should think you could draw treacle out of a treacle-well—eh, stupid?"
sentences.zh: “你能从水井里打水，”帽匠说，“那我以为你也能从糖浆井里打糖浆——嗯，笨蛋？”

paragraphs.text: "But they were in the well," Alice said to the Dormouse, not choosing to notice this last remark.

sentences.text: "But they were in the well," Alice said to the Dormouse, not choosing to notice this last remark.
sentences.zh: “可她们是在井里呀。”爱丽丝对睡鼠说，故意不去理会他最后那句话。

paragraphs.text: "Of course they were," said the Dormouse,—"well in."

sentences.text: "Of course they were," said the Dormouse,—"well in."
sentences.zh: “她们当然在井里，”睡鼠说，“在井里头。”

hints.zh: 睡鼠把“在井里”说成 well in，语序一颠倒就成了文字游戏。
hints.en: 'Well in' twists the word order of 'in the well' into a joke.

paragraphs.text: This answer so confused poor Alice, that she let the Dormouse go on for some time without interrupting it.

sentences.text: This answer so confused poor Alice, that she let the Dormouse go on for some time without interrupting it.
sentences.zh: 这回答把可怜的爱丽丝弄得太糊涂了，她好一会儿都没打断睡鼠，任它往下讲。

paragraphs.text: "They were learning to draw," the Dormouse went on, yawning and rubbing its eyes, for it was getting very sleepy; "and they drew all manner of things—everything that begins with an M——"

sentences.text: "They were learning to draw," the Dormouse went on, yawning and rubbing its eyes, for it was getting very sleepy; "and they drew all manner of things—everything that begins with an M——"
sentences.zh: “她们在学画画，”睡鼠打着哈欠、揉着眼睛继续讲，因为它越来越困了，“她们画各种各样的东西——凡是开头是 M 的——”

hints.zh: 各种各样的东西。
hints.en: 'All manner of things' means all kinds of things.

paragraphs.text: "Why with an M?" said Alice.

sentences.text: "Why with an M?" said Alice.
sentences.zh: “为什么是 M？”爱丽丝说。

introduction.zh: 睡鼠接着讲三姐妹学画画，可她们画的是糖浆，而且都住在井里。爱丽丝刚想问个明白，帽匠却忽然对桌上的杯子挑起了毛病。这场茶会还能不能好好讲下去？
introduction.en: The Dormouse goes on with the story of the sisters who learn to draw — but they draw treacle, and they live in the well. Alice is just trying to make sense of it when the Hatter starts complaining about the cups. Can the story survive the tea party?

quiz.question: Why does Alice ask where the sisters drew the treacle from?
options: Because the Dormouse refused to answer.
Because the sisters were inside the well.
Because the well had no water in it.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝提醒睡鼠，三姐妹就住在井里，所以她才追问糖浆究竟是从哪儿打上来的。
feedback.en: Alice points out that the sisters were inside the well, which is why she asks where the treacle was drawn from.

quiz.question: What happens after everyone moves one place?
options: Everyone gets a clean cup.
Alice ends up worse off than before.
The Dormouse tells a new story.

feedback.zh: 换位之后只有帽匠得了好处，爱丽丝面前是三月兔打翻的牛奶罐，处境更糟。
feedback.en: Only the Hatter gains from the move; Alice ends up worse off, with the March Hare's spilled milk-jug in front of her.

grammar.excerpt: the March Hare had just upset the milk-jug into his plate

focus.zh: had just upset 是过去完成时：牛奶罐被打翻，发生在爱丽丝换位子之前。
focus.en: Had just upset is past perfect: the spilling happened before Alice took the new place.

paragraphs.text: "Why not?" said the March Hare.

sentences.text: "Why not?" said the March Hare.
sentences.zh: “为什么不能是 M？”三月兔说。

paragraphs.text: Alice was silent.

sentences.text: Alice was silent.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝不说话了。

paragraphs.text: The Dormouse had closed its eyes by this time, and was going off into a doze; but, on being pinched by the Hatter, it woke up again with a little shriek, and went on: "——that begins with an M, such as mouse-traps, and the moon, and memory, and muchness—you know you say things are 'much of a muchness'—did you ever see such a thing as a drawing of a muchness?"

sentences.text: The Dormouse had closed its eyes by this time, and was going off into a doze; but, on being pinched by the Hatter, it woke up again with a little shriek, and went on: "——that begins with an M, such as mouse-traps, and the moon, and memory, and muchness—you know you say things are 'much of a muchness'—did you ever see such a thing as a drawing of a muchness?"
sentences.zh: 这时睡鼠已经闭上了眼睛，正要打瞌睡；可被帽匠一掐，它又尖叫一声醒了过来，接着说：“——开头是 M 的东西，比如捕鼠夹、月亮、记忆，还有‘多’——你知道，人们会说东西‘都差不多’——你见过画出来的‘差不多’这种东西吗？”

hints.zh: “多”这个概念；睡鼠把 much 生造成名词，仿佛它能被画出来。
hints.en: 'Muchness' is an invented noun from 'much', as if 'much' were a thing you could draw.

hints.zh: 习语，意思是“差不多、大同小异”。
hints.en: The idiom 'much of a muchness' means 'very similar, much the same'.

paragraphs.text: "Really, now you ask me," said Alice, very much confused, "I don't think——"

sentences.text: "Really, now you ask me," said Alice, very much confused, "I don't think——"
sentences.zh: “说真的，你这一问，”爱丽丝非常困惑地说，“我觉得——”

paragraphs.text: "Then you shouldn't talk," said the Hatter.

sentences.text: "Then you shouldn't talk," said the Hatter.
sentences.zh: “那你就别说话。”帽匠说。

paragraphs.text: This piece of rudeness was more than Alice could bear: she got up in great disgust, and walked off; the Dormouse fell asleep instantly, and neither of the others took the least notice of her going, though she looked back once or twice, half hoping that they would call after her: the last time she saw them, they were trying to put the Dormouse into the teapot. "At any rate I'll never go there again!" said Alice as she picked her way through the wood. "It's the stupidest tea-party I ever was at in all my life?"

sentences.text: This piece of rudeness was more than Alice could bear: she got up in great disgust, and walked off; the Dormouse fell asleep instantly, and neither of the others took the least notice of her going, though she looked back once or twice, half hoping that they would call after her: the last time she saw them, they were trying to put the Dormouse into the teapot.
sentences.zh: 这份无礼实在让爱丽丝忍无可忍：她非常厌恶地站起来，走了出去；睡鼠立刻睡着了，另外两位对她的离开毫不在意，尽管她回头看了他们一两次，还半希望他们会叫她回去：最后一次看时，他们正试着把睡鼠塞进茶壶里。

sentences.text: "At any rate I'll never go there again!" said Alice as she picked her way through the wood.
sentences.zh: “不管怎么说，我再也不去那儿了！”爱丽丝一边在树林里小心地择路走着，一边说。

sentences.text: "It's the stupidest tea-party I ever was at in all my life?"
sentences.zh: “这是我这辈子参加过的最愚蠢的茶会！”

hints.zh: 小心地选择落脚处往前走。
hints.en: To 'pick your way' is to walk carefully, choosing where to put your feet.

paragraphs.text: Just as she said this, she noticed that one of the trees had a door leading right into it. "That's very curious!" she thought. "But everything's curious to-day. I think I may as well go in at once." And in she went.

sentences.text: Just as she said this, she noticed that one of the trees had a door leading right into it.
sentences.zh: 她正说着，忽然发现其中一棵树上有一扇门，直通树里。

sentences.text: "That's very curious!" she thought.
sentences.zh: “真奇怪！”她想。

sentences.text: "But everything's curious to-day.
sentences.zh: “不过今天什么都奇怪。

sentences.text: I think I may as well go in at once."
sentences.zh: 我想我不如马上进去看看。”

sentences.text: And in she went.
sentences.zh: 于是她走了进去。

paragraphs.text: Once more she found herself in the long hall, and close to the little glass table. "Now, I'll manage better this time," she said to herself, and began by taking the little golden key, and unlocking the door that led into the garden. Then she set to work nibbling at the mushroom (she had kept a piece of it in her pocket) till she was about a foot high: then she walked down the little passage: and then—she found herself at last in the beautiful garden, among the bright flower-beds and the cool fountains.

sentences.text: Once more she found herself in the long hall, and close to the little glass table.
sentences.zh: 她又来到了那个长长的门厅里，靠近那张小玻璃桌。

sentences.text: "Now, I'll manage better this time," she said to herself, and began by taking the little golden key, and unlocking the door that led into the garden.
sentences.zh: “这回我要办得更好些。”她自言自语道，先拿起那把小小的金钥匙，打开了通往花园的门。

sentences.text: Then she set to work nibbling at the mushroom (she had kept a piece of it in her pocket) till she was about a foot high: then she walked down the little passage: and then—she found herself at last in the beautiful garden, among the bright flower-beds and the cool fountains.
sentences.zh: 然后她开始一点一点啃蘑菇（她在口袋里留了一块），一直啃到身子大约一英尺高；接着她走过那条小通道；然后——她终于来到了美丽的花园里，置身于鲜艳的花坛和清凉的喷泉之间。

hints.zh: 开始动手做某事。
hints.en: To 'set to work' is to begin doing something with effort.

introduction.zh: 茶会上的回答越来越短，睡鼠也越睡越沉。爱丽丝起身穿过树林，忽然在一棵树上看见一扇门。门后面，会不会又是那个熟悉的大厅？
introduction.en: The answers at the tea party grow shorter, and the Dormouse sinks back into sleep. Alice gets up and walks away through the wood, where she notices a door in one of the trees. Could it lead back to the hall she knows?

quiz.question: Why does Alice say she will never go back to the tea party?
options: The Hatter's rude reply caps a long, stupid conversation.
She cannot find the way out of the wood.
The tea has gone cold.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝刚说“我觉得——”，帽匠就打断她“那你就别说话”，她终于认定这是最愚蠢的茶会。
feedback.en: When Alice begins 'I don't think—', the Hatter cuts her off with 'Then you shouldn't talk', and she decides the party is the stupidest she has ever seen.

quiz.question: What does Alice notice in the wood?
options: The March Hare following her.
A door in one of the trees.
A glass table under a tree.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝在树林里发现一棵树上有一扇门，门直通树里。
feedback.en: Alice notices that one of the trees has a door leading right into it.

grammar.excerpt: on being pinched by the Hatter, it woke up again with a little shriek

focus.zh: being pinched 是“being + 过去分词”的被动分词短语，放在 on 后表示“一被掐就……”。
focus.en: Being pinched is a passive participle phrase after on: 'as soon as it was pinched'.

paragraphs.text: A large rose-tree stood near the entrance of the garden: the roses growing on it were white, but there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red. Alice thought this a very curious thing, and she went nearer to watch them, and just as she came up to them she heard one of them say, "Look out now. Five! Don't go splashing paint over me like that!"

sentences.text: A large rose-tree stood near the entrance of the garden: the roses growing on it were white, but there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red.
sentences.zh: 花园入口附近立着一棵大玫瑰树：树上开着的玫瑰是白色的，可树旁有三个园丁，正忙着把它们涂成红色。

sentences.text: Alice thought this a very curious thing, and she went nearer to watch them, and just as she came up to them she heard one of them say, "Look out now.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝觉得这事很古怪，就走近些去看；她刚走到他们跟前，就听见其中一个说：“当心点。

sentences.text: Five!
sentences.zh: 五号！

sentences.text: Don't go splashing paint over me like that!"
sentences.zh: 别那么把颜料往我身上泼！”

hints.zh: 爱丽丝，本书主角，追着白兔掉进兔子洞的小姑娘。
hints.en: Alice, the girl who followed the White Rabbit down the hole and is the heroine of the book.

hints.zh: “当心！”“留神！”这里是提醒同伴别把颜料泼过来。
hints.en: 'Watch out!' — a warning to be careful, here about splashing paint.

hints.zh: 五号，园丁们以数字为名，所以后面还有七号、二号。
hints.en: Five: the gardeners are named after numbers, so there is also a Seven and a Two.

paragraphs.text: "I couldn't help it," said Five, in a sulky tone; "Seven jogged my elbow."

sentences.text: "I couldn't help it," said Five, in a sulky tone; "Seven jogged my elbow."
sentences.zh: “我也没办法呀，”五号闷闷不乐地说，“是七号撞了我的胳膊肘。”

hints.zh: 撞了我的胳膊肘，害我手一抖；这是五号推卸责任的借口。
hints.en: Jogged my elbow: knocked my arm so that my hand slipped — Five's excuse for the mess.

paragraphs.text: On which Seven looked up and said, "That's right, Five! Always lay the blame on others!"

sentences.text: On which Seven looked up and said, "That's right, Five!
sentences.zh: 听了这话，七号抬起头说：“说得没错，五号！

sentences.text: Always lay the blame on others!"
sentences.zh: 总把错推到别人身上！”

hints.zh: 把过错推到（别人身上）。
hints.en: Lay the blame on someone: to say that someone else is at fault.

paragraphs.text: "You'd better not talk!" said Five. "I heard the Queen say only yesterday you deserved to be beheaded!"

sentences.text: "You'd better not talk!" said Five.
sentences.zh: “你最好别说话！”五号说。

sentences.text: "I heard the Queen say only yesterday you deserved to be beheaded!"
sentences.zh: “我昨天才听王后说，你该被砍头！”

paragraphs.text: "What for?" said the one who had spoken first.

sentences.text: "What for?" said the one who had spoken first.
sentences.zh: “为什么？”最先开口的那个说。

paragraphs.text: "That's none of your business, Two!" said Seven.

sentences.text: "That's none of your business, Two!" said Seven.
sentences.zh: “这不关你的事，二号！”七号说。

paragraphs.text: "Yes, it is his business!" said Five, "and I'll tell him—it was for bringing the cook tulip-roots instead of onions."

sentences.text: "Yes, it is his business!" said Five, "and I'll tell him—it was for bringing the cook tulip-roots instead of onions."
sentences.zh: “怎么不关他的事！”五号说，“我这就告诉他——就因为他给厨娘拿的是郁金香球根，不是洋葱。”

hints.zh: 郁金香的球根，样子像洋葱；拿它当洋葱做菜，所以厨娘要告状。
hints.en: Tulip bulbs, which look like onions; bringing them instead of onions is what got Two into trouble.

paragraphs.text: Seven flung down his brush, and had just begun, "Well, of all the unjust things—" when his eye chanced to fall upon Alice, as she stood watching them, and he checked himself suddenly: the others looked round also, and all of them bowed low.

sentences.text: Seven flung down his brush, and had just begun, "Well, of all the unjust things—" when his eye chanced to fall upon Alice, as she stood watching them, and he checked himself suddenly: the others looked round also, and all of them bowed low.
sentences.zh: 七号把刷子一扔，刚说出“哼，天底下最不讲理的事——”，就一眼瞥见站在那儿看着他们的爱丽丝，赶紧把话咽了回去；另外两个也回过头来，三个人一齐深深鞠躬。

paragraphs.text: "Would you tell me, please," said Alice, a little timidly, "why you are painting those roses?"

sentences.text: "Would you tell me, please," said Alice, a little timidly, "why you are painting those roses?"
sentences.zh: “请问，”爱丽丝有点胆怯地说，“你们为什么要把那些玫瑰涂成红色？”

introduction.zh: 花园入口附近，三个园丁正忙着把白玫瑰涂成红色，一边涂一边互相埋怨，还提起王后与砍头。爱丽丝走近去看：他们究竟为什么非要把花涂红不可？
introduction.en: At the garden entrance three gardeners are painting white roses red and blaming each other for every splash. Alice steps closer, and hears them mention the Queen and beheading. Why must these roses be red before someone arrives?

quiz.question: What are the three gardeners doing at the rose-tree?
options: Painting the white roses red.
Planting a new red rose-tree.
Cutting the white roses off.
