feedback.zh: 开篇就写三个园丁在玫瑰树旁忙着把白玫瑰涂红，爱丽丝正是被这桩怪事吸引过去的。
feedback.en: The unit opens with the three gardeners busily painting white roses red, which is what draws Alice closer.

quiz.question: What does Five say he heard the Queen say about Seven?
options: That Seven must leave the garden.
That Seven deserved to be beheaded.
That Seven should paint faster.

feedback.zh: 五号说，他昨天亲耳听王后说七号该被砍头，七号因此叫他闭嘴。
feedback.en: Five says he heard the Queen herself say the day before that Seven deserved to be beheaded.

grammar.excerpt: I heard the Queen say only yesterday you deserved to be beheaded

focus.zh: heard 后接宾语 the Queen 和动词原形 say，听见的是整个说话动作；再到 be beheaded 收住。
focus.en: Heard takes the object the Queen plus the bare verb say: she heard the whole act of speaking, and the clause about beheading hangs on say.

paragraphs.text: Five and Seven said nothing, but looked at Two. Two began, in a low voice, "Why, the fact is, you see, Miss, this here ought to have been a red rose-tree, and we put a white one in by mistake; and if the Queen was to find it out, we should all have our heads cut off, you know. So you see, Miss, we're doing our best, afore she comes, to—" At this moment Five, who had been anxiously looking across the garden, called out "The Queen! The Queen!" and the three gardeners instantly threw themselves flat upon their faces. There was a sound of many footsteps, and Alice looked round, eager to see the Queen.

sentences.text: Five and Seven said nothing, but looked at Two.
sentences.zh: 五号和七号没说话，只看着二号。

sentences.text: Two began, in a low voice, "Why, the fact is, you see, Miss, this here ought to have been a red rose-tree, and we put a white one in by mistake; and if the Queen was to find it out, we should all have our heads cut off, you know.
sentences.zh: 二号低声开口：“是这么回事，小姐，您瞧，这儿本来该是一棵红玫瑰树，我们弄错了，栽了一棵白的；要是让王后发现了，我们几个的脑袋就都保不住了，您知道。

sentences.text: So you see, Miss, we're doing our best, afore she comes, to—" At this moment Five, who had been anxiously looking across the garden, called out "The Queen!
sentences.zh: 所以您瞧，小姐，我们趁她还没来，尽量把它——”这时，一直不安地朝花园那头张望的五号喊了起来：“王后！

sentences.text: The Queen!" and the three gardeners instantly threw themselves flat upon their faces.
sentences.zh: 王后！”三个园丁立刻扑倒在地，脸朝下趴着。

sentences.text: There was a sound of many footsteps, and Alice looked round, eager to see the Queen.
sentences.zh: 传来许多人的脚步声，爱丽丝转过头去，急着想看看王后。

hints.zh: 口语里加强语气的说法，相当于 this，带乡下口音。
hints.en: 'This here' is a dialect way of saying this, for emphasis.

hints.zh: 方言里的 before，意思是“在……之前”。
hints.en: Afore is a dialect form of before.

paragraphs.text: First came ten soldiers carrying clubs; these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners: next the ten courtiers; these were ornamented all over with diamonds, and walked two and two, as the soldiers did. After these came the royal children; there were ten of them, and the little dears came jumping merrily along hand in hand, in couples: they were all ornamented with hearts. Next came the guests, mostly Kings and Queens, and among them Alice recognised the White Rabbit: it was talking in a hurried nervous manner, smiling at everything that was said, and went by without noticing her. Then followed the Knave of Hearts, carrying the King's crown on a crimson velvet cushion; and, last of all this grand procession, came THE KING AND QUEEN OF HEARTS.

sentences.text: First came ten soldiers carrying clubs; these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners: next the ten courtiers; these were ornamented all over with diamonds, and walked two and two, as the soldiers did.
sentences.zh: 走在最前面的是十个扛着棍棒的士兵；他们的样子跟那三个园丁一样，都是又长又扁的长方形，手脚长在四个角上；接着是十个朝臣，浑身上下都装饰着方块花色，也像士兵一样两人一排地走。

sentences.text: After these came the royal children; there were ten of them, and the little dears came jumping merrily along hand in hand, in couples: they were all ornamented with hearts.
sentences.zh: 他们后面是王室的孩子，一共十个；这些可爱的小家伙两人一对，手拉着手，欢欢喜喜地蹦跳着过来：他们身上都装饰着红心花色。

sentences.text: Next came the guests, mostly Kings and Queens, and among them Alice recognised the White Rabbit: it was talking in a hurried nervous manner, smiling at everything that was said, and went by without noticing her.
sentences.zh: 再后面是宾客，大多是国王和王后，爱丽丝在里头认出了白兔：它正急急忙忙、紧张兮兮地说着话，别人说什么它都陪笑，从她身边走过时却没注意到她。

sentences.text: Then followed the Knave of Hearts, carrying the King's crown on a crimson velvet cushion; and, last of all this grand procession, came THE KING AND QUEEN OF HEARTS.
sentences.zh: 接着走来的是红心骑士，手里捧着一个深红色天鹅绒垫子，上面放着国王的王冠；这队盛大行列的最后，是红心国王和红心王后。

hints.zh: 白兔，揣着怀表、把爱丽丝引进奇境的那只兔子。
hints.en: The White Rabbit, the rabbit with the watch who first led Alice into Wonderland.

hints.zh: 棍棒；在扑克牌里也指“梅花”花色，这里士兵扛的是棍棒。
hints.en: Clubs: heavy sticks, and also one of the card suits; here the soldiers carry them.

hints.zh: 方块，扑克牌四种花色之一；朝臣身上满是方块花纹。
hints.en: Diamonds, one of the four card suits, patterned all over the courtiers.

hints.target: THE KING AND QUEEN OF HEARTS
hints.zh: 红心国王与红心王后，也就是这副牌的国王和王后，全场的最高主人。
hints.en: The King and Queen of Hearts: the king and queen of this pack of cards, and the rulers here.

introduction.zh: 二号吞吞吐吐地道出原委：这棵树本该是红的。话还没说完，他就慌慌张张地朝花园那头张望，声音也变了。究竟是谁来了，让三个园丁怕成这样？
introduction.en: Two explains, in a low voice, that the rose-tree should have been red. Before he can finish, he is peering anxiously across the garden and his voice changes. Who is coming, and why does the whole garden fall silent at the news?

quiz.question: Why are the gardeners so worried about the rose-tree?
options: It is the wrong colour and the Queen may find out.
It is dying because of the paint.
Alice has seen them stealing roses.

feedback.zh: 二号说这棵树本该是红玫瑰，他们错栽了白的；若是被王后发现，大家的脑袋都保不住。
feedback.en: Two admits the tree should have been red and that they planted a white one by mistake, which would cost them all their heads.

quiz.question: What is strange about the soldiers in the procession?
options: They are oblong and flat, with hands and feet at the corners.
They are all much taller than Alice.
They are dressed all in white.

feedback.zh: 士兵又长又扁，手脚长在四个角上，跟那三个园丁一个形状——他们是纸牌上的人。
feedback.en: The soldiers are oblong and flat with hands and feet at the corners, exactly like the gardeners: they are figures on playing cards.

grammar.excerpt: we should all have our heads cut off

focus.zh: have + 宾语 our heads + 过去分词 cut off，表示“让别人把头砍掉”，动作不是自己做的。
focus.en: Have plus object plus past participle: the heads would be cut off by someone else, not by the gardeners themselves.

paragraphs.text: Alice was rather doubtful whether she ought not to lie down on her face like the three gardeners, but she could not remember ever having heard of such a rule at processions; "and besides, what would be the use of a procession," thought she, "if people had all to lie down on their faces, so that they couldn't see it?" So she stood where she was, and waited.

sentences.text: Alice was rather doubtful whether she ought not to lie down on her face like the three gardeners, but she could not remember ever having heard of such a rule at processions; "and besides, what would be the use of a procession," thought she, "if people had all to lie down on their faces, so that they couldn't see it?"
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝拿不准自己是不是也该像那三个园丁一样趴下，可她记不起听说过游行时有这样的规矩；“再说，要是大家都得趴在地上、看都看不见，”她想，“那游行还有什么意思？”

sentences.text: So she stood where she was, and waited.
sentences.zh: 于是她就站在原地等着。

paragraphs.text: When the procession came opposite to Alice, they all stopped and looked at her, and the Queen said severely, "Who is this?" She said it to the Knave of Hearts, who only bowed and smiled in reply.

sentences.text: When the procession came opposite to Alice, they all stopped and looked at her, and the Queen said severely, "Who is this?"
sentences.zh: 队伍走到爱丽丝对面时，全都停下来看着她，王后严厉地说：“这是谁？”

sentences.text: She said it to the Knave of Hearts, who only bowed and smiled in reply.
sentences.zh: 这句话是问红心骑士的，可它只鞠了一躬，笑着不作声。

hints.zh: 红心骑士，宫廷里听差的牌，替王后传话跑腿。
hints.en: The Knave of Hearts, a court card who waits on the Queen and carries her orders.

paragraphs.text: "Idiot!" said the Queen, tossing her head impatiently; and, turning to Alice, she went on, "What's your name, child?"

sentences.text: "Idiot!" said the Queen, tossing her head impatiently; and, turning to Alice, she went on, "What's your name, child?"
sentences.zh: “白痴！”王后不耐烦地把头一甩，又转向爱丽丝，接着说，“你叫什么名字，孩子？”

hints.zh: 把头一甩，表示不耐烦、瞧不起。
hints.en: Tossing her head: jerking it back in impatience or contempt.

paragraphs.text: "My name is Alice, so please your Majesty," said Alice very politely; but she added, to herself, "Why, they're only a pack of cards, after all. I needn't be afraid of them!"

sentences.text: "My name is Alice, so please your Majesty," said Alice very politely; but she added, to herself, "Why, they're only a pack of cards, after all.
sentences.zh: “我叫爱丽丝，回禀陛下。”爱丽丝非常有礼貌地说；可她心里又补了一句：“咳，他们说到底不过是一副纸牌。

sentences.text: I needn't be afraid of them!"
sentences.zh: 我才不用怕他们呢！”

hints.zh: 陛下，对君主的称呼；“so please your Majesty”是极恭敬的说法。
hints.en: Majesty: the title used for a monarch; 'so please your Majesty' is very formal and respectful.

hints.zh: 一副纸牌。爱丽丝这才想到，眼前这些人不过是牌。
hints.en: A pack of cards; Alice suddenly realises that the whole court is made of cards.

paragraphs.text: "And who are these?" said the Queen, pointing to the three gardeners who were lying round the rose-tree; for you see, as they were lying on their faces, and the pattern on their back was the same as the rest of the pack, she could not tell whether they were gardeners, or soldiers, or courtiers, or three of her own children.

sentences.text: "And who are these?" said the Queen, pointing to the three gardeners who were lying round the rose-tree; for you see, as they were lying on their faces, and the pattern on their back was the same as the rest of the pack, she could not tell whether they were gardeners, or soldiers, or courtiers, or three of her own children.
sentences.zh: “这些又是什么人？”王后指着趴在玫瑰树周围的三个园丁说；你要知道，他们脸朝下趴着，背上的花纹又跟整副牌里其他牌一样，所以她分不清他们是园丁、士兵、朝臣，还是她自己的三个孩子。

paragraphs.text: "How should I know?" said Alice, surprised at her own courage. "It's no business of mine."

sentences.text: "How should I know?" said Alice, surprised at her own courage.
sentences.zh: “我怎么知道？”爱丽丝说，自己也为自己这份胆量吃惊。

sentences.text: "It's no business of mine."
sentences.zh: “这可不关我的事。”

paragraphs.text: The Queen turned crimson with fury, and, after glaring at her for a moment like a wild beast, began screaming, "Off with her head! Off—"

sentences.text: The Queen turned crimson with fury, and, after glaring at her for a moment like a wild beast, began screaming, "Off with her head!
sentences.zh: 王后气得满脸通红，像野兽一样瞪了她一会儿，就尖叫起来：“砍掉她的头！

sentences.text: Off—"

hints.zh: 深红色；turned crimson with fury 指气得满脸通红。
hints.en: Crimson: deep red; 'turned crimson with fury' means her face went red with rage.

paragraphs.text: "Nonsense!" said Alice, very loudly and decidedly, and the Queen was silent.

sentences.text: "Nonsense!" said Alice, very loudly and decidedly, and the Queen was silent.
sentences.zh: “胡说！”爱丽丝非常响亮、非常坚决地说，王后就不作声了。

introduction.zh: 队伍在爱丽丝面前停下，所有目光都落到她身上，王后开口问话。面对这样一群人，她该照规矩趴下，还是站着不动？她心里那点念头，又能撑多久？
introduction.en: The procession stops in front of Alice and every face turns to her. Should she lie face down as the gardeners did, or stay on her feet? The Queen begins to ask questions, and a wrong answer could be expensive.

quiz.question: Why does Alice stay on her feet instead of lying face down?
options: She is too frightened to move.
She has never heard of such a rule at processions.
The gardeners tell her to stay where she is.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝记不起游行时有趴下的规矩，还想：大家都趴着看不见，游行也就没用了。
feedback.en: Alice cannot remember such a rule at processions, and thinks a procession nobody could see would be pointless.

quiz.question: How does Alice answer when the Queen asks who the gardeners are?
options: That they are her friends.
That she does not know and it is no business of hers.
That they are three of the Queen's children.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝干脆回答“我怎么知道”，还说这不关她的事，连自己都为这份胆量吃了一惊。
feedback.en: Alice answers 'How should I know?' and adds that it is no business of hers, surprised at her own courage.

grammar.excerpt: whether she ought not to lie down on her face like the three gardeners

focus.zh: whether 引出她拿不准的“是否该趴下”，作 doubtful 的补充；从句用陈述语序，谓语是 ought not to lie down。
focus.en: Whether introduces the uncertain question she is doubtful about; the clause keeps statement order, and its verb is ought not to lie down.

paragraphs.text: The King laid his hand upon her arm, and timidly said, "Consider, my dear: she is only a child!"

sentences.text: The King laid his hand upon her arm, and timidly said, "Consider, my dear: she is only a child!"
sentences.zh: 国王把手搭在她胳膊上，怯生生地说：“你想想，亲爱的：她不过是个孩子！”

paragraphs.text: The Queen turned angrily away from him, and said to the Knave, "Turn them over!"

sentences.text: The Queen turned angrily away from him, and said to the Knave, "Turn them over!"
sentences.zh: 王后气冲冲地转过身去背对着他，对红心骑士说：“把他们翻过来！”

hints.zh: 把他们翻过来。三个园丁脸朝下趴着，翻过来才看得清是什么牌。
hints.en: Turn them over: the gardeners are lying face down, and only when turned can anyone see which card they are.

paragraphs.text: The Knave did so, very carefully, with one foot.

sentences.text: The Knave did so, very carefully, with one foot.
sentences.zh: 红心骑士照办了，用一只脚，非常小心地把他们翻了过来。

paragraphs.text: "Get up!" said the Queen in a shrill, loud voice, and the three gardeners instantly jumped up, and began bowing to the King, the Queen, the royal children, and everybody else.

sentences.text: "Get up!" said the Queen in a shrill, loud voice, and the three gardeners instantly jumped up, and began bowing to the King, the Queen, the royal children, and everybody else.
sentences.zh: “起来！”王后用又尖又响的声音说，三个园丁立刻跳起来，开始向国王、王后、王室的孩子，还有在场的每个人一一鞠躬。

paragraphs.text: "Leave off that!" screamed the Queen. "You make me giddy." And then, turning to the rose-tree, she went on, "What have you been doing here?"

sentences.text: "Leave off that!" screamed the Queen.
sentences.zh: “别鞠了！”王后尖叫。

sentences.text: "You make me giddy."
sentences.zh: “你把我看得头都晕了。”

sentences.text: And then, turning to the rose-tree, she went on, "What have you been doing here?"
sentences.zh: 然后她转向那棵玫瑰树，接着问：“你们在这儿干了什么？”

paragraphs.text: "May it please your Majesty," said Two, in a very humble tone, going down on one knee as he spoke, "we were trying—"

sentences.text: "May it please your Majesty," said Two, in a very humble tone, going down on one knee as he spoke, "we were trying—"
sentences.zh: “回禀陛下，”二号用极恭顺的口气说，一边说一边单膝跪下，“我们是想——”

hints.zh: “回禀陛下”，旧时下属对君主开口时的恭敬套语，直译是“愿这能使陛下高兴”。
hints.en: 'May it please your Majesty': an old, very humble way of opening a speech to a monarch.

paragraphs.text: "I see!" said the Queen, who had meanwhile been examining the roses. "Off with their heads!" and the procession moved on, three of the soldiers remaining behind to execute the unfortunate gardeners, who ran to Alice for protection.

sentences.text: "I see!" said the Queen, who had meanwhile been examining the roses.
sentences.zh: “我明白了！”王后说——这工夫她一直在查看那些玫瑰。

sentences.text: "Off with their heads!" and the procession moved on, three of the soldiers remaining behind to execute the unfortunate gardeners, who ran to Alice for protection.
sentences.zh: “砍掉他们的头！”队伍继续往前走，只留下三个士兵去处决那几个倒霉的园丁，园丁们却跑到爱丽丝那儿求她保护。

paragraphs.text: "You shan't be beheaded!" said Alice, and she put them into a large flower-pot that stood near. The three soldiers wandered about for a minute or two, looking for them, and then quietly marched off after the others.

sentences.text: "You shan't be beheaded!" said Alice, and she put them into a large flower-pot that stood near.
sentences.zh: “你们不会被砍头的！”爱丽丝说，把他们塞进旁边一个大花盆里。

sentences.text: The three soldiers wandered about for a minute or two, looking for them, and then quietly marched off after the others.
sentences.zh: 那三个士兵四处转了一两分钟，到处找他们，随后就悄悄跟上队伍走了。

hints.zh: shall not 的缩写；这里表示“绝不让你们被砍头”。
hints.en: Shan't is short for shall not; here Alice means she will not let it happen.

paragraphs.text: "Are their heads off?" shouted the Queen.

sentences.text: "Are their heads off?" shouted the Queen.
sentences.zh: “他们的头掉了吗？”王后喊道。

paragraphs.text: "Their heads are gone, if it please your Majesty!" the soldiers shouted in reply.

sentences.text: "Their heads are gone, if it please your Majesty!" the soldiers shouted in reply.
sentences.zh: “他们的头都没了，回禀陛下！”士兵们大声回答。

paragraphs.text: "That's right!" shouted the Queen. "Can you play croquet?"

sentences.text: "That's right!" shouted the Queen.
sentences.zh: “很好！”王后喊道。

sentences.text: "Can you play croquet?"
sentences.zh: “你会打槌球吗？”

hints.zh: 槌球戏，用木槌把球打过草地上的铁环；本书里球和槌都是活物。
hints.en: Croquet: a lawn game in which balls are hit through hoops with mallets; here the balls and mallets are alive.

paragraphs.text: The soldiers were silent, and looked at Alice, as the question was evidently meant for her.

sentences.text: The soldiers were silent, and looked at Alice, as the question was evidently meant for her.
sentences.zh: 士兵们不出声，只看着爱丽丝，因为这个问题显然是问她的。

paragraphs.text: "Yes!" shouted Alice.

sentences.text: "Yes!" shouted Alice.
sentences.zh: “会！”爱丽丝大声说。

paragraphs.text: "Come on, then!" roared the Queen, and Alice joined the procession, wondering very much what would happen next.

sentences.text: "Come on, then!" roared the Queen, and Alice joined the procession, wondering very much what would happen next.
sentences.zh: “那就来吧！”王后吼道。爱丽丝加入了队伍，心里非常想知道接下来会出什么事。

introduction.zh: 王后一声令下，三个园丁被翻了过来，只好跪下答话。可她的问题刚问出口，判决就跟着来了；爱丽丝手边正好有个空花盆。她来得及做什么？
introduction.en: A word from the Queen and the gardeners are turned over and made to kneel. Her question is hardly out before a sentence follows it. Alice has an empty flower-pot nearby, and very little time.

quiz.question: What does the King do when the Queen screams for Alice's head?
options: He reminds her that Alice is only a child.
He quietly leaves the garden.
He orders the soldiers to seize Alice.

feedback.zh: 国王按住王后的手臂，怯生生地提醒她：爱丽丝不过是个孩子。
feedback.en: The King lays a hand on the Queen's arm and timidly reminds her that Alice is only a child.

quiz.question: Where does Alice put the three gardeners?
options: Under the Queen's throne.
Behind the rose-tree.
In a large flower-pot.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝说他们不会被砍头，顺手把三个园丁塞进旁边的大花盆里。
feedback.en: Alice says they shall not be beheaded and pops the three gardeners into a big flower-pot nearby.

grammar.excerpt: What have you been doing here?

focus.zh: have been doing 是现在完成进行时：从过去一直做到现在，王后问的是“你们一直在这儿干什么”。
focus.en: Have been doing is the present perfect continuous: the Queen asks about an action that has been going on up to now.

paragraphs.text: "It's—it's a very fine day!" said a timid voice at her side. She was walking by the White Rabbit, who was peeping anxiously into her face.

sentences.text: "It's—it's a very fine day!" said a timid voice at her side.
sentences.zh: “今天——今天天气真好！”她身边有个怯怯的声音说。

sentences.text: She was walking by the White Rabbit, who was peeping anxiously into her face.
sentences.zh: 走在她旁边的是白兔，它正不安地偷眼打量她的脸。

paragraphs.text: "Very," said Alice:—"where's the Duchess?"

sentences.text: "Very," said Alice:—"where's the Duchess?"
sentences.zh: “是很好，”爱丽丝说，“——公爵夫人在哪儿？”

hints.zh: 公爵夫人，脾气暴躁，前几章在胡椒厨房里出现过。
hints.en: The Duchess, the bad-tempered lady Alice met earlier in the pepper kitchen.

paragraphs.text: "Hush! hush!" said the Rabbit in a low, hurried tone. He looked anxiously over his shoulder as he spoke, and then raised himself upon tiptoe, put his mouth close to her ear, and whispered, "She's under sentence of execution."

sentences.text: "Hush! hush!" said the Rabbit in a low, hurried tone.
sentences.zh: “嘘！嘘！”白兔压低声音、急急忙忙地说。

sentences.text: He looked anxiously over his shoulder as he spoke, and then raised himself upon tiptoe, put his mouth close to her ear, and whispered, "She's under sentence of execution."
sentences.zh: 它一边说一边不安地回头看，然后踮起脚，把嘴凑到她耳边，悄声说：“她被判了死刑。”

hints.zh: 已被判处死刑，只等行刑。
hints.en: Under sentence of execution: condemned to death and waiting to be executed.

paragraphs.text: "What for?" said Alice.

sentences.text: "What for?" said Alice.
sentences.zh: “为什么？”爱丽丝问。

paragraphs.text: "Did you say, 'What a pity!'?" the Rabbit asked.

sentences.text: "Did you say, 'What a pity!'?" the Rabbit asked.
sentences.zh: “你是说‘真可惜’吗？”白兔问。

paragraphs.text: "No, I didn't," said Alice: "I don't think it's at all a pity. I said 'What for?'"

sentences.text: "No, I didn't," said Alice: "I don't think it's at all a pity.
sentences.zh: “不，我没说，”爱丽丝说，“我一点也不觉得可惜。

sentences.text: I said 'What for?'"
sentences.zh: 我说的是‘为什么’。”

paragraphs.text: "She boxed the Queen's ears—" the Rabbit began. Alice gave a little scream of laughter. "Oh, hush!" the Rabbit whispered in a frightened tone. "The Queen will hear you! You see she came rather late, and the Queen said—"

sentences.text: "She boxed the Queen's ears—" the Rabbit began.
sentences.zh: “她打了王后一记耳光——”白兔刚开口。

sentences.text: Alice gave a little scream of laughter.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝忍不住笑出声来。

sentences.text: "Oh, hush!" the Rabbit whispered in a frightened tone.
sentences.zh: “哦，嘘！”白兔害怕地低声说。

sentences.text: "The Queen will hear you!
sentences.zh: “王后会听见你的！

sentences.text: You see she came rather late, and the Queen said—"
sentences.zh: 你知道，她来得晚了些，王后就说——”

hints.zh: 打了王后一记耳光（box someone's ears）。
hints.en: Boxed the Queen's ears: slapped the Queen on the side of the head.

paragraphs.text: "Get to your places!" shouted the Queen in a voice of thunder, and people began running about in all directions, tumbling up against each other: however, they got settled down in a minute or two, and the game began.

sentences.text: "Get to your places!" shouted the Queen in a voice of thunder, and people began running about in all directions, tumbling up against each other: however, they got settled down in a minute or two, and the game began.
sentences.zh: “各就各位！”王后用打雷一样的声音喊，人们便四散跑开，撞成一团；不过一两分钟后大家都站定了，球戏就开始了。

paragraphs.text: Alice thought she had never seen such a curious croquet-ground in her life: it was all ridges and furrows; the croquet-balls were live hedgehogs, and the mallets live flamingoes, and the soldiers had to double themselves up and stand on their hands and feet, to make the arches.

sentences.text: Alice thought she had never seen such a curious croquet-ground in her life: it was all ridges and furrows; the croquet-balls were live hedgehogs, and the mallets live flamingoes, and the soldiers had to double themselves up and stand on their hands and feet, to make the arches.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝想，她一辈子也没见过这么奇怪的槌球场：地上尽是垄和沟；球是活刺猬，球杆是活火烈鸟，士兵们还得弯下身子、手脚撑地，充当球门。

hints.zh: 田垄和沟壑，指地面高低不平。
hints.en: Ridges and furrows: raised strips and deep grooves in the ground.

hints.zh: 火烈鸟，长颈长腿的粉红色水鸟；这里被当作球杆用。
hints.en: Flamingoes: long-necked pink birds, used here as croquet mallets.

introduction.zh: 队伍走着，白兔凑到爱丽丝身边，先没话找话，随后压低声音说出一件可怕的事。她还想再问，王后已经在场地上喊了起来。这场球，到底要怎么打？
introduction.en: As they walk, the White Rabbit sidles up to Alice and then whispers something alarming about the Duchess. Before she can ask more, the Queen's voice booms across the ground. What kind of game is about to begin?

quiz.question: What does the White Rabbit whisper about the Duchess?
options: That she is under sentence of execution.
That she has left the garden.
That she wants to see Alice.

feedback.zh: 白兔凑到她耳边悄声说：公爵夫人已被判了死刑。爱丽丝问“为什么”，它却听成了“真可惜”。
feedback.en: The Rabbit whispers that the Duchess is under sentence of execution, then mistakes Alice's 'What for?' for 'What a pity!'

quiz.question: What is unusual about the croquet-ground?
options: The ground is covered with water.
The arches are made of roses.
The balls are hedgehogs and the mallets are flamingoes.

feedback.zh: 场上球是活刺猬，球杆是活火烈鸟，士兵弯腰撑地充当球门。
feedback.en: On this ground the balls are live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes, and doubled-up soldiers serve as the arches.

grammar.excerpt: she had never seen such a curious croquet-ground in her life

focus.zh: had never seen 是过去完成时：以当时那一刻为界，说在那之前从没见过；never 放在 had 之后。
focus.en: Had never seen is past perfect: at that past moment, she had never seen such a ground before; never comes after had.

paragraphs.text: The chief difficulty Alice found at first was in managing her flamingo: she succeeded in getting its body tucked away, comfortably enough, under her arm, with its legs hanging down, but generally, just as she had got its neck nicely straightened out, and was going to give the hedgehog a blow with its head, it would twist itself round and look up in her face, with such a puzzled expression that she could not help bursting out laughing: and when she had got its head down, and was going to begin again, it was very provoking to find that the hedgehog had unrolled itself, and was in the act of crawling away: besides all this, there was generally a ridge or a furrow in the way wherever she wanted to send the hedgehog to, and, as the doubled-up soldiers were always getting up and walking off to other parts of the ground, Alice soon came to the conclusion that it was a very difficult game indeed.

sentences.text: The chief difficulty Alice found at first was in managing her flamingo: she succeeded in getting its body tucked away, comfortably enough, under her arm, with its legs hanging down, but generally, just as she had got its neck nicely straightened out, and was going to give the hedgehog a blow with its head, it would twist itself round and look up in her face, with such a puzzled expression that she could not help bursting out laughing: and when she had got its head down, and was going to begin again, it was very provoking to find that the hedgehog had unrolled itself, and was in the act of crawling away: besides all this, there was generally a ridge or a furrow in the way wherever she wanted to send the hedgehog to, and, as the doubled-up soldiers were always getting up and walking off to other parts of the ground, Alice soon came to the conclusion that it was a very difficult game indeed.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝起初觉得最难的是摆弄她那只火烈鸟：她总算把鸟身子夹在腋下，倒也还算舒服，两条腿垂下来；可通常她刚把鸟脖子顺直，正要拿鸟头去击刺猬，那鸟就扭过头来，一脸困惑地仰头看她的脸，逗得她忍不住大笑；等她再把鸟头按下去、准备重来时，又气人地发现刺猬已经展开身子，正要爬走；除此之外，不管她想把刺猬往哪儿打，路上总有一道垄或一条沟；而那些弯着腰的士兵又老是直起身走开，到场地别处去了。爱丽丝很快就断定，这游戏实在太难了。

hints.zh: 刺猬，遇险就蜷成一团；本章里被当作槌球。
hints.en: A hedgehog, which rolls itself into a ball; here the hedgehogs are the croquet balls.

hints.zh: 塞好、夹好；她把火烈鸟的身子夹在腋下。
hints.en: Tucked away: pushed neatly out of the way, here under her arm.

hints.zh: 正在……的当口；in the act of crawling away 就是“正要爬走”。
hints.en: In the act of doing something: in the very middle of doing it.

paragraphs.text: The players all played at once without waiting for turns, quarrelling all the while, and fighting for the hedgehogs; and in a very short time the Queen was in a furious passion, and went stamping about, and shouting, "Off with his head!" or "Off with her head!" about once in a minute.

sentences.text: The players all played at once without waiting for turns, quarrelling all the while, and fighting for the hedgehogs; and in a very short time the Queen was in a furious passion, and went stamping about, and shouting, "Off with his head!" or "Off with her head!" about once in a minute.
sentences.zh: 打球的人都不等轮次，一齐动手，从头到尾争争吵吵，为刺猬你抢我夺；没过多久，王后就勃然大怒，跺着脚走来走去，差不多每分钟就喊一次“砍掉他的头！”或者“砍掉她的头！”

hints.zh: 跺着脚走来走去，气急败坏的样子。
hints.en: Stamping about: walking up and down and bringing her feet down hard.

hints.zh: 勃然大怒；in a passion 是旧时说“大发脾气”。
hints.en: In a furious passion: in a violent rage.

paragraphs.text: Alice began to feel very uneasy: to be sure, she had not as yet had any dispute with the Queen, but she knew that it might happen any minute, "and then," thought she, "what would become of me? They're dreadfully fond of beheading people here; the great wonder is, that there's any one left alive!"

sentences.text: Alice began to feel very uneasy: to be sure, she had not as yet had any dispute with the Queen, but she knew that it might happen any minute, "and then," thought she, "what would become of me?
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝开始觉得很不自在：不错，她到现在还没跟王后争执过，可她知道这事随时都可能发生；“到那时候，”她想，“我会怎么样呢？

sentences.text: They're dreadfully fond of beheading people here; the great wonder is, that there's any one left alive!"
sentences.zh: 这儿的人可怕地爱砍人脑袋；奇怪的是，居然还有人活着！”

introduction.zh: 球戏一开始，爱丽丝就发现每样东西都在动：火烈鸟扭头看她，刺猬自己展开身子爬走，球门还挪到别处去了。她该怎么把球打进门？
introduction.en: From the first stroke, nothing on this croquet-ground keeps still: the flamingo twists round to look at her, the hedgehog unrolls and crawls off, and the arches wander away. How can anyone play a game like this?

quiz.question: Why is it so hard for Alice to hit the hedgehog?
options: She has never played croquet before.
The flamingo keeps twisting round and the hedgehog keeps unrolling.
The hedgehogs are too heavy to move.

feedback.zh: 她的火烈鸟老是扭头看她，刺猬又自己展开身子爬走，所以她断定这游戏实在太难。
feedback.en: Her flamingo keeps twisting round to look at her and the hedgehog keeps unrolling and crawling off, so she decides the game is very difficult.

quiz.question: What does the Queen do while the others play?
options: She keeps shouting for heads to be cut off.
She sits quietly and watches.
She orders the game to stop.

feedback.zh: 大家不等轮次乱打一气，没多久王后就勃然大怒，几乎每分钟都喊一次砍头。
feedback.en: The players all strike at once, and soon the Queen is in a fury, shouting for a head about once a minute.

grammar.excerpt: with such a puzzled expression that she could not help bursting out laughing

focus.zh: such a + 形容词 + 名词：such a puzzled expression 指“那样困惑的一副表情”，后面的 that 从句说明结果。
focus.en: Such a plus adjective plus noun: such a puzzled expression, and the that-clause that follows tells you the result.

paragraphs.text: She was looking about for some way of escape, and wondering whether she could get away without being seen, when she noticed a curious appearance in the air: it puzzled her very much at first, but after watching it a minute or two she made it out to be a grin, and she said to herself, "It's the Cheshire Cat: now I shall have somebody to talk to."

sentences.text: She was looking about for some way of escape, and wondering whether she could get away without being seen, when she noticed a curious appearance in the air: it puzzled her very much at first, but after watching it a minute or two she made it out to be a grin, and she said to herself, "It's the Cheshire Cat: now I shall have somebody to talk to."
sentences.zh: 她正四下张望，想找个逃跑的办法，盘算着能不能不被人看见就溜走，忽然注意到空中出现一个怪东西：起初她怎么也弄不明白，可看了一两分钟，她看出那是一个咧嘴的笑，便自言自语说：“是柴郡猫：这下我有个人可以说话了。”

hints.zh: 柴郡猫，会隐身、能只露出一个笑，说话慢条斯理。
hints.en: The Cheshire Cat, which can vanish and leave only its grin, and speaks very coolly.

hints.zh: 咧开嘴的笑；这里先出现的是笑，身子还没出来。
hints.en: A grin: a wide smile; here the smile appears before the body does.

hints.zh: 辨认出、看出（是……）；make out 指费力看清或听懂。
hints.en: Made it out: managed to see what it was; 'make out' means to see or hear with difficulty.

paragraphs.text: "How are you getting on?" said the Cat, as soon as there was mouth enough for it to speak with.

sentences.text: "How are you getting on?" said the Cat, as soon as there was mouth enough for it to speak with.
sentences.zh: “你过得怎么样？”猫说，这时它已经长出足够说话的嘴了。

paragraphs.text: Alice waited till the eyes appeared, and then nodded. "It's no use speaking to it," she thought, "till its ears have come, or at least one of them." In another minute the whole head appeared, and then Alice put down her flamingo, and began an account of the game, feeling very glad she had some one to listen to her. The Cat seemed to think that there was enough of it now in sight, and no more of it appeared.

sentences.text: Alice waited till the eyes appeared, and then nodded.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝等眼睛出现了，才点点头。

sentences.text: "It's no use speaking to it," she thought, "till its ears have come, or at least one of them."
sentences.zh: “跟它说话也没用，”她想，“得等它的耳朵出来，至少出来一只。”

sentences.text: In another minute the whole head appeared, and then Alice put down her flamingo, and began an account of the game, feeling very glad she had some one to listen to her.
sentences.zh: 又过了一分钟，整个头都出现了，爱丽丝这才放下火烈鸟，开始讲起球戏的情形，心里很高兴总算有人听她说话。

sentences.text: The Cat seemed to think that there was enough of it now in sight, and no more of it appeared.
sentences.zh: 猫似乎觉得露出来的已经够多了，再没有多露出一点。

paragraphs.text: "I don't think they play at all fairly," Alice began, in rather a complaining tone, "and they all quarrel so dreadfully one can't hear one's-self speak—and they don't seem to have any rules in particular; at least, if there are, nobody attends to them—and you've no idea how confusing it is all the things being alive; for instance, there's the arch I've got to go through next walking about at the other end of the ground—and I should have croqueted the Queen's hedgehog just now, only it ran away when it saw mine coming!"

sentences.text: "I don't think they play at all fairly," Alice began, in rather a complaining tone, "and they all quarrel so dreadfully one can't hear one's-self speak—and they don't seem to have any rules in particular; at least, if there are, nobody attends to them—and you've no idea how confusing it is all the things being alive; for instance, there's the arch I've got to go through next walking about at the other end of the ground—and I should have croqueted the Queen's hedgehog just now, only it ran away when it saw mine coming!"
sentences.zh: “我觉得他们打得一点也不公道，”爱丽丝用相当抱怨的口气说，“而且大家吵得那么厉害，连自己说什么都听不见——他们好像也没有什么特别的规则；就算有，也没人遵守——你真想不到，什么东西都是活的，有多乱；比方说吧，我下一杆要过的那个球门，这会儿正在场地另一头走来走去——刚才我本该把王后的刺猬打出去的，可它一见我的刺猬过来就跑了！”

hints.zh: 留意、照办；nobody attends to them 就是“没人遵守”。
hints.en: Attends to: pays attention to and obeys; 'nobody attends to them' means nobody follows them.

hints.zh: croquet 作动词：用槌把自己的球打出去，撞走对方的球。
hints.en: Croqueted: used as a verb, to hit your own ball so that it drives another player's ball away.

paragraphs.text: "How do you like the Queen?" said the Cat in a low voice.

sentences.text: "How do you like the Queen?" said the Cat in a low voice.
sentences.zh: “你觉得王后怎么样？”猫低声问。

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝正想找机会溜走，忽然看见半空中浮着一样东西，看了好一会儿才认出那是一个笑。接着，一个熟悉的声音跟她打招呼。这会儿，她能把满肚子委屈说给谁听？
introduction.en: Alice is looking for a way out when something odd appears in the air: it takes her a minute to see that it is a grin. Then a familiar voice greets her. At last she has someone to tell her troubles to.

quiz.question: What does Alice first notice in the air?
options: A pair of ears.
A flamingo flying up.
A grin without a body.

feedback.zh: 她起初弄不明白空中那东西，看了一两分钟才认出是一个咧嘴的笑——柴郡猫先露出了笑。
feedback.en: At first she cannot make out the thing in the air; after a minute or two she sees that it is a grin.

quiz.question: What does Alice complain about to the Cat?
options: That nobody will speak to her.
That the players keep no rules and everything is alive.
That the Queen is unfair to the gardeners.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝抱怨大家不守规则、什么都活着，连她下一杆要过的球门都走到场地另一头去了。
feedback.en: Alice complains that nobody keeps the rules and that everything is alive, down to the arch that has walked to the other end of the ground.

grammar.excerpt: I should have croqueted the Queen's hedgehog just now

focus.zh: should have + 过去分词，说“本来应该做到而没做到”：那一杆她本该把王后的刺猬打出去。
focus.en: Should have plus past participle: she ought to have made that stroke, but did not.

title.en: A Cat May Look at a King

paragraphs.text: "Not at all," said Alice: "she's so extremely—" Just then she noticed that the Queen was close behind her, listening: so she went on, "—likely to win, that it's hardly worth while finishing the game."

sentences.text: "Not at all," said Alice: "she's so extremely—" Just then she noticed that the Queen was close behind her, listening: so she went on, "—likely to win, that it's hardly worth while finishing the game."
sentences.zh: “一点也不喜欢，”爱丽丝说，“她实在太——”就在这时，她发现王后就在她身后不远，正听着，于是她接着说，“——太可能赢了，所以把这场球打完简直没什么意思。”

paragraphs.text: The Queen smiled and passed on.

sentences.text: The Queen smiled and passed on.
sentences.zh: 王后笑了笑，走了过去。

paragraphs.text: "Who are you talking to?" said the King, coming up to Alice, and looking at the Cat's head with great curiosity.

sentences.text: "Who are you talking to?" said the King, coming up to Alice, and looking at the Cat's head with great curiosity.
sentences.zh: “你在跟谁说话？”国王走到爱丽丝跟前说，非常好奇地看着猫的头。

paragraphs.text: "It's a friend of mine—a Cheshire Cat," said Alice: "allow me to introduce it."

sentences.text: "It's a friend of mine—a Cheshire Cat," said Alice: "allow me to introduce it."
sentences.zh: “是我的一个朋友——一只柴郡猫，”爱丽丝说，“请允许我介绍一下。”

paragraphs.text: "I don't like the look of it at all," said the King: "however, it may kiss my hand if it likes."

sentences.text: "I don't like the look of it at all," said the King: "however, it may kiss my hand if it likes."
sentences.zh: “我一点也不喜欢它这副样子，”国王说，“不过，它要是愿意，可以亲我的手。”

paragraphs.text: "I'd rather not," the Cat remarked.

sentences.text: "I'd rather not," the Cat remarked.
sentences.zh: “我还是不亲了。”猫说。

paragraphs.text: "Don't be impertinent," said the King, "and don't look at me like that!" He got behind Alice as he spoke.

sentences.text: "Don't be impertinent," said the King, "and don't look at me like that!"
sentences.zh: “别放肆，”国王说，“也别那样看着我！”

sentences.text: He got behind Alice as he spoke.
sentences.zh: 他一边说一边躲到爱丽丝身后。

hints.zh: 放肆、无礼，对长辈或上位者说话不客气。
hints.en: Impertinent: rude and disrespectful, especially to someone above you.

paragraphs.text: "A cat may look at a king," said Alice. "I've read that in some book, but I don't remember where."

sentences.text: "A cat may look at a king," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “猫也有权看国王。”爱丽丝说。

sentences.text: "I've read that in some book, but I don't remember where."
sentences.zh: “我在哪本书上读到过，可记不得是哪一本了。”

hints.target: A cat may look at a king
hints.zh: 谚语：“猫也有权看国王”，意思是小人物也有看大人物的自由。
hints.en: An old saying: 'A cat may look at a king' — even the humble have a right to look at the great.

paragraphs.text: "Well, it must be removed," said the King very decidedly, and he called to the Queen, who was passing at the moment, "My dear! I wish you would have this cat removed!"

sentences.text: "Well, it must be removed," said the King very decidedly, and he called to the Queen, who was passing at the moment, "My dear!
sentences.zh: “嗯，它必须被弄走。”国王非常坚决地说，又朝正从旁边经过的王后喊，“亲爱的！

sentences.text: I wish you would have this cat removed!"
sentences.zh: 我希望你叫人把这猫弄走！”

hints.zh: 弄走、除掉；王后嘴里的 remove 往往就是“砍头”。
hints.en: Removed: got rid of; in the Queen's mouth it usually means a beheading.

paragraphs.text: The Queen had only one way of settling all difficulties, great or small. "Off with his head!" she said, without even looking round.

sentences.text: The Queen had only one way of settling all difficulties, great or small.
sentences.zh: 王后解决一切难题，不论大小，只有一种办法。

sentences.text: "Off with his head!" she said, without even looking round.
sentences.zh: “砍掉他的头！”她说，连头都没回。

paragraphs.text: "I'll fetch the executioner myself," said the King eagerly, and he hurried off.

sentences.text: "I'll fetch the executioner myself," said the King eagerly, and he hurried off.
sentences.zh: “我亲自去叫刽子手。”国王急切地说，匆匆走了。

hints.zh: 刽子手，专门执行死刑的人。
hints.en: The executioner: the man whose job is to carry out executions.

introduction.zh: 王后从爱丽丝身后走过，国王又盯着半空中的猫头发问。有人嫌它碍眼，有人嫌它无礼，猫却一点也不着急。一句老话，能挡得住王后吗？
introduction.en: The Queen passes close behind Alice, and the King stares at the Cat's head and does not like what he sees. The Cat is not troubled in the least. Can an old saying really protect it from the Queen?

quiz.question: Why does Alice change what she is saying about the Queen?
options: She sees the Queen listening behind her.
The King asks her to be polite.
The Cat warns her.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝正说王后“实在太——”，忽然发现王后就在身后听着，只好改口说“太可能赢了”。
feedback.en: Alice is halfway through 'she's so extremely—' when she notices the Queen listening behind her, and switches to 'likely to win'.

quiz.question: What does the King want done with the Cat?
options: He wants it invited to the palace.
He wants Alice to take it home.
He wants it removed.

feedback.zh: 国王非常坚决地说这猫“必须弄走”，还回头请王后下手。
feedback.en: The King says very decidedly that the Cat must be removed, and calls on the Queen to do it.

grammar.excerpt: I'd rather not

focus.zh: would rather 后接动词原形，I'd 就是 I would；not 单独放在后面，表示“宁可不要”。
focus.en: Would rather takes a bare verb, and I'd is I would; the bare not at the end means 'I would prefer not to'.

paragraphs.text: Alice thought she might as well go back and see how the game was going on, as she heard the Queen's voice in the distance, screaming with passion. She had already heard her sentence three of the players to be executed for having missed their turns, and she did not like the look of things at all, as the game was in such confusion that she never knew whether it was her turn or not. So she went off in search of her hedgehog.

sentences.text: Alice thought she might as well go back and see how the game was going on, as she heard the Queen's voice in the distance, screaming with passion.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝想，不如回去看看球戏进行得怎么样了，因为她听见远处传来王后的声音，正在暴怒地尖叫。

sentences.text: She had already heard her sentence three of the players to be executed for having missed their turns, and she did not like the look of things at all, as the game was in such confusion that she never knew whether it was her turn or not.
sentences.zh: 她已经听见王后判了三个球员死刑，因为他们错过了自己的轮次；她一点也不喜欢眼前的局面，球戏乱得她根本不知道自己该不该上场。

sentences.text: So she went off in search of her hedgehog.
sentences.zh: 于是她走开去找她的刺猬。

paragraphs.text: The hedgehog was engaged in a fight with another hedgehog, which seemed to Alice an excellent opportunity for croqueting one of them with the other: the only difficulty was, that her flamingo was gone across to the other side of the garden, where Alice could see it trying in a helpless sort of way to fly up into a tree.

sentences.text: The hedgehog was engaged in a fight with another hedgehog, which seemed to Alice an excellent opportunity for croqueting one of them with the other: the only difficulty was, that her flamingo was gone across to the other side of the garden, where Alice could see it trying in a helpless sort of way to fly up into a tree.
sentences.zh: 那刺猬正跟另一只刺猬打作一团，爱丽丝觉得这正是拿一只去打另一只的好机会：唯一的难处是，她的火烈鸟跑到花园那头去了，她看得见它正无可奈何地想往树上飞。

hints.target: in a helpless sort of way
hints.zh: 一副无可奈何的样子，想飞又飞不起来。
hints.en: In a helpless sort of way: looking quite unable to manage it.

paragraphs.text: By the time she had caught the flamingo and brought it back, the fight was over, and both the hedgehogs were out of sight: "but it doesn't matter much," thought Alice, "as all the arches are gone from this side of the ground." So she tucked it away under her arm, that it might not escape again, and went back to have a little more conversation with her friend.

sentences.text: By the time she had caught the flamingo and brought it back, the fight was over, and both the hedgehogs were out of sight: "but it doesn't matter much," thought Alice, "as all the arches are gone from this side of the ground."
sentences.zh: 等她抓住火烈鸟、把它带回来，架已经打完了，两只刺猬都不见了踪影；“不过这也没什么要紧，”爱丽丝想，“反正场地这一边的球门都走光了。”

sentences.text: So she tucked it away under her arm, that it might not escape again, and went back to have a little more conversation with her friend.
sentences.zh: 于是她把火烈鸟夹在腋下，免得它再跑掉，然后回去跟她的朋友再聊几句。

hints.zh: 球门，槌球戏里要穿过的拱；这里是弯腰撑地的士兵。
hints.en: The arches: the hoops a croquet ball must pass through, here made by doubled-up soldiers.

hints.zh: 看不见了，不见踪影。
hints.en: Out of sight: no longer visible, gone.

paragraphs.text: When she got back to the Cheshire Cat, she was surprised to find quite a large crowd collected round it: there was a dispute going on between the executioner, the King, and the Queen, who were all talking at once, while all the rest were quite silent, and looked very uncomfortable.

sentences.text: When she got back to the Cheshire Cat, she was surprised to find quite a large crowd collected round it: there was a dispute going on between the executioner, the King, and the Queen, who were all talking at once, while all the rest were quite silent, and looked very uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 她回到柴郡猫那儿，惊讶地发现它周围聚了一大群人：刽子手、国王和王后正在争执，三个人同时开口，其余的人都一声不响，看样子很不自在。

introduction.zh: 球场那头，王后的尖叫声一阵接一阵；爱丽丝的刺猬正跟另一只打成一团，火烈鸟却跑到花园另一头去了。等她回来时，柴郡猫周围已经围了一群人。
introduction.en: The Queen's screaming carries across the ground, Alice's hedgehog is busy fighting another, and her flamingo has wandered to the far side of the garden. When she gets back, a crowd has gathered round the Cat.

quiz.question: Why does Alice go back towards the game?
options: She is looking for the Duchess.
She wants to see how the game is going.
The Queen calls her by name.

feedback.zh: 她听见远处王后在尖叫，想想不如回去看看球戏进行得怎么样。
feedback.en: Hearing the Queen screaming in the distance, she decides she may as well go back and see how the game is going.

quiz.question: Why does it no longer matter that the hedgehogs are gone?
options: All the arches have left this side of the ground.
The Queen has stopped the game.
Alice has found another ball.

feedback.zh: 等她抓回火烈鸟，两只刺猬都不见了；她说反正这一边的球门也全走光了，没什么要紧。
feedback.en: By the time she returns with the flamingo both hedgehogs are gone, and she says it hardly matters since all the arches have left this side.

grammar.excerpt: By the time she had caught the flamingo and brought it back

focus.zh: by the time 引出“等她抓回火烈鸟”这个时间界限，主句讲那之前已结束的事，所以从句用 had caught。
focus.en: By the time marks the deadline; the main clause reports what was already over by then, so the clause uses had caught.

paragraphs.text: The moment Alice appeared, she was appealed to by all three to settle the question, and they repeated their arguments to her, though, as they all spoke at once, she found it very hard to make out exactly what they said.

sentences.text: The moment Alice appeared, she was appealed to by all three to settle the question, and they repeated their arguments to her, though, as they all spoke at once, she found it very hard to make out exactly what they said.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝一出现，三个人都请她来评断这个问题，又各自把理由对她重说了一遍；可他们同时开口，她觉得很难听清他们到底说了什么。

hints.zh: 被（大家）请来评理、求助；appeal to somebody 就是“向某人求助”。
hints.en: Appealed to: asked to decide or help; 'appeal to someone' means to turn to them for a judgement.

paragraphs.text: The executioner's argument was, that you couldn't cut off a head unless there was a body to cut it off from: that he had never had to do such a thing before, and he wasn't going to begin at his time of life.

sentences.text: The executioner's argument was, that you couldn't cut off a head unless there was a body to cut it off from: that he had never had to do such a thing before, and he wasn't going to begin at his time of life.
sentences.zh: 刽子手的理由是：要是没有身子，就没法从身子上砍下头来；他以前从没干过这种事，到了这把年纪也不打算开这个头。

hints.zh: 到了他这把年纪；刽子手以此表示自己老了，不想再开这个头。
hints.en: At his time of life: at his age — the executioner's excuse for not starting now.

paragraphs.text: The King's argument was, that anything that had a head could be beheaded, and that you weren't to talk nonsense.

sentences.text: The King's argument was, that anything that had a head could be beheaded, and that you weren't to talk nonsense.
sentences.zh: 国王的理由是：凡是有头的东西都能砍头，而且不许胡说八道。

paragraphs.text: The Queen's argument was, that if something wasn't done about it in less than no time she'd have everybody executed, all round. (It was this last remark that had made the whole party look so grave and anxious.)

sentences.text: The Queen's argument was, that if something wasn't done about it in less than no time she'd have everybody executed, all round. (It was this last remark that had made the whole party look so grave and anxious.)
sentences.zh: 王后的理由是：要是不能马上把这事办妥，她就把所有人都处死，一个不留。（正是这最后一句话，让在场的人都显得那么严肃不安。）

hints.zh: 夸张说法，意思是“马上、一转眼”。
hints.en: In less than no time: a joking expression meaning 'at once, in no time at all'.

paragraphs.text: Alice could think of nothing else to say but "It belongs to the Duchess: you'd better ask her about it."

sentences.text: Alice could think of nothing else to say but "It belongs to the Duchess: you'd better ask her about it."
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝想不出别的话可说，只好说：“它是公爵夫人的：你最好去问她。”

paragraphs.text: "She's in prison," the Queen said to the executioner: "fetch her here." And the executioner went off like an arrow.

sentences.text: "She's in prison," the Queen said to the executioner: "fetch her here."
sentences.zh: “她在牢里，”王后对刽子手说，“把她带到这儿来。”

sentences.text: And the executioner went off like an arrow.
sentences.zh: 刽子手就像箭一样飞奔而去。

paragraphs.text: The Cat's head began fading away the moment he was gone, and, by the time he had come back with the Duchess, it had entirely disappeared; so the King and the executioner ran wildly up and down looking for it, while the rest of the party went back to the game.

sentences.text: The Cat's head began fading away the moment he was gone, and, by the time he had come back with the Duchess, it had entirely disappeared; so the King and the executioner ran wildly up and down looking for it, while the rest of the party went back to the game.
sentences.zh: 他刚走，猫头就开始渐渐消失；等他带着公爵夫人回来时，猫头已经全不见了；于是国王和刽子手疯了似的跑来跑去到处找，其余的人则回去打球了。

introduction.zh: 刽子手、国王和王后同时开口，各说各的理，都要爱丽丝来评断，可谁的声音也听不清。这颗没有身子的猫头，到底该由谁来砍？
introduction.en: The executioner, the King and the Queen all talk at once and all appeal to Alice, though she can hardly make out a word. A head is there, and no body to cut it from. Who is to settle it?

quiz.question: What is the executioner's reason for not cutting off the Cat's head?
options: The Cat belongs to the Duchess.
He has lost his axe.
There is no body to cut the head off from.

feedback.zh: 刽子手说，没有身子就无从下刀；他这辈子没干过这种事，也不打算现在开头。
feedback.en: The executioner argues that a head cannot be cut off without a body, and that he is not going to start at his time of life.

quiz.question: What does the Queen threaten if the matter is not settled at once?
options: To call the Duchess back to the garden.
To have everybody executed.
To send the King to prison.

feedback.zh: 王后的理由是：再不马上办，她就把所有人统统处死；这句话让全场都严肃不安起来。
feedback.en: The Queen's argument is that if nothing is done at once she will have everybody executed, which is what makes the whole party look grave.

grammar.excerpt: you couldn't cut off a head unless there was a body to cut it off from

focus.zh: unless 等于 if not，引出唯一例外“除非有身子可砍”；从句用一般过去时，跟 couldn't 保持一致。
focus.en: Unless means 'if not': it marks the one exception — no body, no head to cut off — and its past tense matches couldn't.

paragraphs.text: "You can't think how glad I am to see you again, you dear old thing! " said the Duchess, as she tucked her arm affectionately into Alice's, and they walked off together.

sentences.text: "You can't think how glad I am to see you again, you dear old thing! " said the Duchess, as she tucked her arm affectionately into Alice's, and they walked off together.
sentences.zh: “你真想不到我再见你有多高兴，你这亲爱的老东西！”公爵夫人说着，亲热地把胳膊挽进爱丽丝的臂弯，两个人一起走开了。

hints.zh: 爱丽丝，本书主角，追着白兔掉进兔子洞的小姑娘。
hints.en: Alice, the girl who followed the White Rabbit down the hole and is the heroine of the book.

hints.zh: 公爵夫人，脾气古怪的贵妇，不管说什么都要从中找出一条“寓意”。
hints.en: The Duchess, an odd noblewoman who finds a moral in whatever is said.

paragraphs.text: Alice was very glad to find her in such a pleasant temper, and thought to herself that perhaps it was only the pepper that had made her so savage when they met in the kitchen.

sentences.text: Alice was very glad to find her in such a pleasant temper, and thought to herself that perhaps it was only the pepper that had made her so savage when they met in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝很高兴见她脾气这么好，心里想：也许她们在厨房见面时，她那么凶只是因为胡椒。

paragraphs.text: When I'm a Duchess," she said to herself, (not in a very hopeful tone though,) "I won't have any pepper in my kitchen at all. Soup does very well without—Maybe it's always pepper that makes people hot-tempered," she went on, very much pleased at having found out a new kind of rule, "and vinegar that makes them sour—and camomile that makes them bitter—and—and barley-sugar and such things that make children sweet-tempered. I only wish people knew that: then they wouldn't be so stingy about it, you know—"

sentences.text: When I'm a Duchess," she said to herself, (not in a very hopeful tone though,) "I won't have any pepper in my kitchen at all.
sentences.zh: “等我做了公爵夫人，”她自言自语（不过语气并不怎么有指望），“我的厨房里一点儿胡椒都不放。”

sentences.text: Soup does very well without—Maybe it's always pepper that makes people hot-tempered," she went on, very much pleased at having found out a new kind of rule, "and vinegar that makes them sour—and camomile that makes them bitter—and—and barley-sugar and such things that make children sweet-tempered.
sentences.zh: “汤里不放也很好——也许让人脾气火爆的总是胡椒，”她继续说，为自己发现了一条新规律而十分得意，“让人发酸的是醋——让人发苦的是洋甘菊——还有——还有大麦糖之类的东西，让孩子们脾气温和。”

sentences.text: I only wish people knew that: then they wouldn't be so stingy about it, you know—"
sentences.zh: “我真希望人们知道这一点：那样他们就不会在这上头这么吝啬了，你知道——”

hints.zh: 脾气火爆的、容易发火的；temper 指脾气，hot 指火气。
hints.en: Hot-tempered: easily made angry; temper means a person's disposition.

hints.zh: 大麦糖，用大麦糖浆熬成的硬糖，味甜。
hints.en: Barley sugar: a hard, sweet candy made from barley syrup.

paragraphs.text: She had quite forgotten the Duchess by this time, and was a little startled when she heard her voice close to her ear. "You're thinking about something, my dear, and that makes you forget to talk. I can't tell you just now what the moral of that is, but I shall remember it in a bit."

sentences.text: She had quite forgotten the Duchess by this time, and was a little startled when she heard her voice close to her ear.
sentences.zh: 这时她早把公爵夫人忘得干干净净，忽然听见声音就在耳边，倒吓了一跳。

sentences.text: "You're thinking about something, my dear, and that makes you forget to talk.
sentences.zh: “你在想事情呢，亲爱的，一想事就忘了说话。

sentences.text: I can't tell you just now what the moral of that is, but I shall remember it in a bit."
sentences.zh: 这会儿我还说不出这里头的寓意是什么，不过我过一会儿就会想起来的。”

paragraphs.text: "Perhaps it hasn't one," Alice ventured to remark.

sentences.text: "Perhaps it hasn't one," Alice ventured to remark.
sentences.zh: “也许它根本没什么寓意，”爱丽丝壮着胆子说。

paragraphs.text: "Tut, tut, child!" said the Duchess. "Every thing's got a moral, if only you can find it." And she squeezed herself up closer to Alice's side as she spoke.

sentences.text: "Tut, tut, child!" said the Duchess.
sentences.zh: “啧，啧，孩子！”公爵夫人说。

sentences.text: "Every thing's got a moral, if only you can find it."
sentences.zh: “样样东西都有寓意，只要你能找出来。”

sentences.text: And she squeezed herself up closer to Alice's side as she spoke.
sentences.zh: 说着，她把自己挤得更紧，贴到爱丽丝身边。

hints.zh: 啧啧，表示不赞成或嗔怪的口头语。
hints.en: Tut-tut: an old-fashioned sound of mild disapproval.

hints.zh: 寓意、教训；公爵夫人不管说什么都要从中找出一条“寓意”，这是本章反复出现的玩笑。
hints.en: A moral: the lesson drawn from something. The Duchess draws one from everything, which is the running joke of the chapter.

introduction.zh: 球场上，公爵夫人忽然亲热地挽住爱丽丝的胳膊，一口一个“亲爱的老东西”。爱丽丝刚松了口气，就发现这位夫人有个怪毛病：不论说什么，她都要从里头找出一条“寓意”。胡椒、汤、醋，样样都有教训。这些寓意真的站得住脚吗？
introduction.en: On the croquet ground the Duchess takes Alice's arm and calls her a dear old thing. Alice is relieved, until she notices that the Duchess finds a moral in everything, from pepper to soup. Do these morals really hold?

quiz.question: Why does Alice think the Duchess is in a better temper now?
options: Because the pepper is gone.
Because the Duchess has just won a game.
Because Alice has grown taller.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝想，也许她们在厨房见面时她那么凶，只是因为胡椒；眼下没了那股火气，人就和气了。
feedback.en: Alice decides that the pepper was probably what made the Duchess so savage when they met in the kitchen.

quiz.question: What does the Duchess say everything has?
options: A price.
A name.
A moral.

feedback.zh: 公爵夫人说，样样东西都有寓意，只要你能找出来——这是她一路上的口头禅。
feedback.en: The Duchess insists that everything has a moral, if only you can find it.

grammar.excerpt: I only wish people knew that

focus.zh: wish 后面用过去式 knew，说的却是现在：但愿人们知道，可他们并不知道。
focus.en: After wish, knew is a past form about the present: people do not know, and Alice wishes they did.

title.en: A Sharp Chin and a Flamingo

paragraphs.text: Alice did not much like her keeping so close to her: first, because the Duchess was very ugly, and secondly, because she was exactly the right height to rest her chin on Alice's shoulder, and it was an uncomfortably sharp chin. However, she did not like to be rude, so she bore it as well as she could.

sentences.text: Alice did not much like her keeping so close to her: first, because the Duchess was very ugly, and secondly, because she was exactly the right height to rest her chin on Alice's shoulder, and it was an uncomfortably sharp chin.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝不太喜欢她贴得这么近：第一，公爵夫人长得很难看；第二，她的个头正好能把下巴搁在爱丽丝肩上，而那下巴尖得让人难受。

sentences.text: However, she did not like to be rude, so she bore it as well as she could.
sentences.zh: 不过她又不想失礼，只好尽量忍着。

paragraphs.text: "The game's going on rather better now," she said, by way of keeping up the conversation a little.

sentences.text: "The game's going on rather better now," she said, by way of keeping up the conversation a little.
sentences.zh: “现在球赛进行得顺一些了，”她说，算是把话头往下接一接。

paragraphs.text: "'Tis so," said the Duchess: "and the moral of that is—'Oh, 'tis love, 'tis love, that makes the world go round!'"

sentences.text: "'Tis so," said the Duchess: "and the moral of that is—'Oh, 'tis love, 'tis love, that makes the world go round!'"
sentences.zh: “是这样，”公爵夫人说，“这里头的寓意就是——‘哦，是爱，是爱，让世界转个不停！’”

hints.zh: it is 的古旧缩略形式，旧诗和方言里常见。
hints.en: 'Tis: an old contraction of 'it is', still heard in poetry and dialect.

paragraphs.text: "Somebody said," Alice whispered, "that it's done by every body minding their own business!"

sentences.text: "Somebody said," Alice whispered, "that it's done by every body minding their own business!"
sentences.zh: “有人说，”爱丽丝小声说，“那是靠各人管好各人的事！”

hints.zh: 各管各的事，别去多管闲事。
hints.en: Minding their own business: looking after their own affairs and not interfering.

paragraphs.text: "Ah, well! It means much the same thing," said the Duchess, digging her sharp little chin into Alice's shoulder as she added, "and the moral of that is—'Take care of the sense, and the sounds will take care of themselves.'"

sentences.text: "Ah, well!
sentences.zh: “啊，好吧！

sentences.text: It means much the same thing," said the Duchess, digging her sharp little chin into Alice's shoulder as she added, "and the moral of that is—'Take care of the sense, and the sounds will take care of themselves.'"
sentences.zh: 意思差不多是一回事，”公爵夫人说着，把尖尖的小下巴往爱丽丝肩上一顶，又补上一句，“这里头的寓意就是——‘照看好意思，声音自会照看好自己。’”

paragraphs.text: "How fond she is of finding morals in things!" Alice thought to herself.

sentences.text: "How fond she is of finding morals in things!"
sentences.zh: “她多爱从东西里找寓意啊！”

sentences.text: Alice thought to herself.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝心里想。

paragraphs.text: "I dare say you're wondering why I don't put my arm round your waist," the Duchess said after a pause: "the reason is, that I'm doubtful about the temper of your flamingo. Shall I try the experiment?"

sentences.text: "I dare say you're wondering why I don't put my arm round your waist," the Duchess said after a pause: "the reason is, that I'm doubtful about the temper of your flamingo.
sentences.zh: “我敢说你在纳闷，我为什么不搂着你的腰，”公爵夫人停了一下说，“原因是，我对你那只火烈鸟的脾气没把握。

sentences.text: Shall I try the experiment?"
sentences.zh: 要不要试一试？”

hints.zh: 火烈鸟，奇境里被当作槌球杆用的长腿鸟。
hints.en: A flamingo: the long-legged bird used as a croquet mallet in Wonderland.

paragraphs.text: "He might bite," Alice cautiously replied, not feeling at all anxious to have the experiment tried.

sentences.text: "He might bite," Alice cautiously replied, not feeling at all anxious to have the experiment tried.
sentences.zh: “它可能会咬人，”爱丽丝小心地回答，一点也不希望真去试。

paragraphs.text: "Very true," said the Duchess: "flamingoes and mustard both bite. And the moral of that is—'Birds of a feather flock together.'"

sentences.text: "Very true," said the Duchess: "flamingoes and mustard both bite.
sentences.zh: “说得对，”公爵夫人说，“火烈鸟和芥末都会‘咬’人。

sentences.text: And the moral of that is—'Birds of a feather flock together.'"
sentences.zh: 这里头的寓意就是——‘物以类聚，人以群分。’”

hints.zh: 火烈鸟会咬人，芥末会“呛”人；bite 在这里同时指“咬”和“刺激、呛”。
hints.en: Both bite: a flamingo can bite with its beak, and mustard 'bites' the tongue — bite covers both.

hints.target: Birds of a feather flock together
hints.zh: 谚语：羽毛相同的鸟聚在一起，即“物以类聚，人以群分”。
hints.en: A proverb: birds of the same feathers flock together, that is, similar people keep company.

paragraphs.text: "Only mustard isn't a bird," Alice remarked.

sentences.text: "Only mustard isn't a bird," Alice remarked.
sentences.zh: “可芥末不是鸟啊，”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "Right, as usual," said the Duchess: "what a clear way you have of putting things!"

sentences.text: "Right, as usual," said the Duchess: "what a clear way you have of putting things!"
sentences.zh: “跟平常一样，说得对，”公爵夫人说，“你说话多清楚啊！”

paragraphs.text: "It's a mineral, I think," said Alice.

sentences.text: "It's a mineral, I think," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “我想，它是一种矿物，”爱丽丝说。

introduction.zh: 公爵夫人贴得越来越近，尖尖的小下巴硌着爱丽丝的肩膀，嘴里还在找“寓意”：爱、各管各的事、物以类聚。爱丽丝忍不住纠正了一句，对方却越发夸她聪明。接着话题转到火烈鸟和芥末，这两样都会“咬”人吗？
introduction.en: The Duchess keeps close, resting her sharp little chin on Alice's shoulder and finding a moral in everything. Alice corrects her once and is praised for being so clear. Then the talk turns to flamingos, mustard, and which of them can bite.

quiz.question: Why does the Duchess quote "Birds of a feather flock together"?
options: Because she wants Alice to stop talking.
Because she has just said that flamingoes and mustard both bite.
Because Alice has asked about the croquet game.

feedback.zh: 公爵夫人刚说火烈鸟和芥末都会“咬”人，紧接着就引了这句谚语，意思是同类才相聚。
feedback.en: She has just said that flamingoes and mustard both bite, and then quotes the proverb about birds of a feather.

quiz.question: What does Alice point out about mustard?
options: It is not a bird.
It cannot bite.
It is a kind of flamingo.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝指出芥末不是鸟，随后又说它大概是一种矿物，把公爵夫人的寓意顶了回去。
feedback.en: Alice points out that mustard is not a bird, and then suggests it must be a mineral.

grammar.excerpt: she bore it as well as she could

focus.zh: as well as she could 是同级比较，第二个 as 后面接从句，说明她忍到了自己能忍的程度。
focus.en: As well as she could is an equal comparison: the second as introduces the clause that sets the limit of what she could bear.

paragraphs.text: "Of course it is," said the Duchess, who seemed ready to agree to everything that Alice said; "there's a large mustard-mine near here. And the moral of that is—'The more there is of mine, the less there is of yours.'"

sentences.text: "Of course it is," said the Duchess, who seemed ready to agree to everything that Alice said; "there's a large mustard-mine near here.
sentences.zh: “当然是矿物，”公爵夫人说——她似乎随时准备同意爱丽丝说的每句话，“这附近就有一座大芥末矿。

sentences.text: And the moral of that is—'The more there is of mine, the less there is of yours.'"
sentences.zh: 这里头的寓意就是——‘我的越多，你的就越少。’”

hints.zh: 芥末矿；mine 既指“矿”，也指“我的”，公爵夫人就拿这两个意思玩文字游戏。
hints.en: A mustard-mine: mine means both 'a mine' and 'belonging to me', and the Duchess plays on the two meanings.

paragraphs.text: "Oh, I know!" exclaimed Alice, who had not attended to this last remark, "it's a vegetable. It doesn't look like one, but it is."

sentences.text: "Oh, I know!" exclaimed Alice, who had not attended to this last remark, "it's a vegetable.
sentences.zh: “哦，我知道了！”爱丽丝喊道，她根本没留意刚才那句话，“它是一种蔬菜。

sentences.text: It doesn't look like one, but it is."
sentences.zh: 它看着不像，可实际上就是。”

paragraphs.text: "I quite agree with you," said the Duchess, "and the moral of that is—'Be what you would seem to be '—or, if you'd like it put more simply—'Never imagine yourself not to be otherwise than what it might appear to others that what you were or might have been was not otherwise than what you had been would have appeared to them to be otherwise.'"

sentences.text: "I quite agree with you," said the Duchess, "and the moral of that is—'Be what you would seem to be '—or, if you'd like it put more simply—'Never imagine yourself not to be otherwise than what it might appear to others that what you were or might have been was not otherwise than what you had been would have appeared to them to be otherwise.'"
sentences.zh: “我完全同意你，”公爵夫人说，“这里头的寓意就是——‘做你看起来像的那个样子’——或者，如果你愿意把它说得更简单些——‘永远不要想象你自己不是别人看来你可能的样子；也不要以为，你过去是或可能曾经是的样子，会不同于你过去在别人眼里若是另一副样子时本会呈现的那个样子。’”

paragraphs.text: "I think I should understand that better," Alice said very politely, "if I had it written down: but I can't quite follow it as you say it."

sentences.text: "I think I should understand that better," Alice said very politely, "if I had it written down: but I can't quite follow it as you say it."
sentences.zh: “我想，要是把它写下来，我会更明白些，”爱丽丝非常有礼貌地说，“可你这么说出来，我不太跟得上。”

paragraphs.text: "That's nothing to what I could say if I chose," the Duchess replied, in a pleased tone.

sentences.text: "That's nothing to what I could say if I chose," the Duchess replied, in a pleased tone.
sentences.zh: “这比起我要是愿意就能说的话，算不了什么，”公爵夫人得意地回答。

paragraphs.text: "Pray don't trouble yourself to say it any longer than that," said Alice.

sentences.text: "Pray don't trouble yourself to say it any longer than that," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “请不必费心再多说了，”爱丽丝说。

hints.zh: 请（古旧、客气的说法），相当于 please。
hints.en: Pray: an old-fashioned, polite way of saying please.

paragraphs.text: "Oh, don't talk about trouble!" said the Duchess. "I make you a present of everything I've said as yet."

sentences.text: "Oh, don't talk about trouble!" said the Duchess.
sentences.zh: “哦，别说什么费心！”公爵夫人说。

sentences.text: "I make you a present of everything I've said as yet."
sentences.zh: “我说过的话，全都白送给你。”

hints.zh: 把……当作礼物白送给你；公爵夫人是说自己那些话全送给爱丽丝了。
hints.en: To make somebody a present of something: to give it away as a gift; here, all the words she has spoken.

paragraphs.text: "A cheap sort of present!" thought Alice. "I'm glad they don't give birthday presents like that!" But she did not venture to say it out loud.

sentences.text: "A cheap sort of present!" thought Alice.
sentences.zh: “可真是一份便宜的礼物！”爱丽丝想。

sentences.text: "I'm glad they don't give birthday presents like that!"
sentences.zh: “幸好人家不送这样的生日礼物！”

sentences.text: But she did not venture to say it out loud.
sentences.zh: 不过她没敢大声说出来。

paragraphs.text: "Thinking again?" the Duchess asked, with another dig of her sharp little chin.

sentences.text: "Thinking again?" the Duchess asked, with another dig of her sharp little chin.
sentences.zh: “又在想事情了？”公爵夫人问，尖下巴又顶了一下。

paragraphs.text: "I've a right to think," said Alice sharply, for she was beginning to feel a little worried.

sentences.text: "I've a right to think," said Alice sharply, for she was beginning to feel a little worried.
sentences.zh: “我有权想事情，”爱丽丝尖声说，她开始有点发慌了。

paragraphs.text: "Just about as much right," said the Duchess, "as pigs have to fly: and the m—"

sentences.text: "Just about as much right," said the Duchess, "as pigs have to fly: and the m—"
sentences.zh: “权利嘛，跟猪会飞差不多，”公爵夫人说，“至于那个‘寓’——”

hints.zh: 像猪会飞一样，指根本不可能的事。
hints.en: As pigs have to fly: a way of saying something is impossible.

introduction.zh: 公爵夫人对爱丽丝说的每句话都点头称是，还能立刻配一条“寓意”。她甚至说附近就有一座芥末矿，又讲出一句关于“我的”和“你的”的怪话。爱丽丝越听越糊涂。夫人说，她还能讲得更久——爱丽丝要怎么脱身？
introduction.en: The Duchess agrees with every word Alice says and adds a moral to each. She even claims there is a large mustard mine nearby, and offers a saying about 'mine' and 'yours'. Alice cannot follow any of it. What can she say to stop the flow?

quiz.question: What does the Duchess claim is near them?
options: A vegetable garden.
A second croquet ground.
A large mustard mine.

feedback.zh: 公爵夫人说附近就有一座大芥末矿，还立刻从“矿”这个字里又找出一条寓意。
feedback.en: The Duchess says there is a large mustard mine nearby, and turns even that into another moral.

quiz.question: Why does Alice ask the Duchess not to go on?
options: She wants to go back to the game.
She cannot follow the Duchess's long sayings.
She is afraid the Queen is listening.

feedback.zh: 那句绕来绕去的寓意她听不下去——她说要是写下来也许还能看懂，可听人念就跟不上。
feedback.en: Alice says she might understand the moral if it were written down, but cannot follow it when it is spoken.

grammar.excerpt: The more there is of mine, the less there is of yours

focus.zh: 两个 the + 比较级连用：前一半是条件，后一半跟着变，“越……就越……”。
focus.en: Two the + comparative clauses are paired: the first sets the condition, the second the result.

paragraphs.text: But here, to Alice's great surprise, the Duchess's voice died away, even in the middle of her favourite word 'moral,' and the arm that was linked into hers began to tremble. Alice looked up, and there stood the Queen in front of them, with her arms folded, frowning like a thunderstorm.

sentences.text: But here, to Alice's great surprise, the Duchess's voice died away, even in the middle of her favourite word 'moral,' and the arm that was linked into hers began to tremble.
sentences.zh: 可就在这时，让爱丽丝大为惊讶的是，公爵夫人的声音低了下去，连她最爱说的“寓意”一词都只说了半截，挽着她的那条胳膊也开始发抖。

sentences.text: Alice looked up, and there stood the Queen in front of them, with her arms folded, frowning like a thunderstorm.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝抬头一看，王后正站在她们面前，双臂交叉抱在胸前，眉头皱得像一场雷暴。

paragraphs.text: "A fine day, your Majesty!" the Duchess began in a low, weak voice.

sentences.text: "A fine day, your Majesty!" the Duchess began in a low, weak voice.
sentences.zh: “天气真好，陛下！”公爵夫人用又低又弱的声音开口。

hints.zh: 陛下，对君主的尊称。
hints.en: Your Majesty: the title used when speaking to a king or queen.

paragraphs.text: "Now, I give you fair warning," shouted the Queen, stamping on the ground as she spoke; "either you or your head must be off, and that in about half no time! Take your choice!"

sentences.text: "Now, I give you fair warning," shouted the Queen, stamping on the ground as she spoke; "either you or your head must be off, and that in about half no time!
sentences.zh: “听着，我正正经经警告你，”王后一边跺脚一边喊，“要么你走，要么你的脑袋走，而且就在一眨眼的工夫！

sentences.text: Take your choice!"
sentences.zh: 你挑吧！”

hints.zh: 卡罗尔自造的短语，意思是“一眨眼的工夫”“马上”。
hints.en: Half no time: a phrase Carroll invented, meaning 'in next to no time'.

hints.zh: 必须走开；配 your head 一起说，就是“脑袋得搬家”，是个双关。
hints.en: Must be off: must leave; paired with your head, it also means 'your head must come off'.

paragraphs.text: The Duchess took her choice, and was gone in a moment.

sentences.text: The Duchess took her choice, and was gone in a moment.
sentences.zh: 公爵夫人做出了选择，转眼就不见了。

paragraphs.text: "Let's go on with the game," the Queen said to Alice; and Alice was too much frightened to say a word, but slowly followed her back to the croquet-ground.

sentences.text: "Let's go on with the game," the Queen said to Alice; and Alice was too much frightened to say a word, but slowly followed her back to the croquet-ground.
sentences.zh: “我们接着打球吧，”王后对爱丽丝说；爱丽丝吓得一句话也说不出来，只得慢慢跟着她回到槌球场。

hints.zh: 槌球场，用木槌把球打过铁圈的场地。
hints.en: A croquet-ground: the lawn where croquet is played.

paragraphs.text: The other guests had taken advantage of the Queen's absence, and were resting in the shade: however, the moment they saw her, they hurried back to the game, the Queen merely remarking that a moment's delay would cost them their lives.

sentences.text: The other guests had taken advantage of the Queen's absence, and were resting in the shade: however, the moment they saw her, they hurried back to the game, the Queen merely remarking that a moment's delay would cost them their lives.
sentences.zh: 别的客人趁王后不在，都在阴凉里歇着；可他们一看见她，就赶紧跑回球局。王后只淡淡地说了一句：耽搁片刻就要他们的命。

paragraphs.text: All the time they were playing the Queen never left off quarrelling with the other players, and shouting "Off with his head!" or "Off with her head!" Those whom she sentenced were taken into custody by the soldiers, who of course had to leave off being arches to do this, so that by the end of half an hour or so there were no arches left, and all the players, except the King, the Queen, and Alice, were in custody and under sentence of execution.

sentences.text: All the time they were playing the Queen never left off quarrelling with the other players, and shouting "Off with his head!" or "Off with her head!"
sentences.zh: 打球的时候，王后一直不停地跟别的球手争吵，喊着“砍掉他的脑袋！”或者“砍掉她的脑袋！”

sentences.text: Those whom she sentenced were taken into custody by the soldiers, who of course had to leave off being arches to do this, so that by the end of half an hour or so there were no arches left, and all the players, except the King, the Queen, and Alice, were in custody and under sentence of execution.
sentences.zh: 被她判了刑的人由士兵押起来——士兵们当然得先不当拱门才能干这事——结果大约过了半个钟头，一个拱门也不剩了；除了国王、王后和爱丽丝，所有球手都被押着，判了处决。

hints.zh: 拱门，槌球里要穿过的铁圈；这里士兵被当成拱门用，一被叫走，拱门就少了。
hints.en: Arches: the hoops a croquet ball must pass through; here the soldiers serve as arches.

introduction.zh: 话音未落，公爵夫人的声音忽然低了下去，连“寓意”都只说了一半，挽着爱丽丝的胳膊也抖了起来。爱丽丝抬头，看见王后抱着双臂站在面前，眉头皱得像一场雷雨。王后开口了，她要公爵夫人做一个选择。
introduction.en: In the middle of her favourite word the Duchess's voice fades, and the arm linked in Alice's begins to tremble. Alice looks up: the Queen stands there with folded arms, frowning like a thunderstorm. She has a warning to give and a choice to offer.

quiz.question: What choice does the Queen give the Duchess?
options: To leave, or to lose her head.
To play croquet, or to go home.
To apologise, or to be silent.

feedback.zh: 王后让公爵夫人二选一：要么人走开，要么脑袋走开，而且限她“一眨眼”的工夫。
feedback.en: The Queen says that either the Duchess or her head must be off, and very soon.

quiz.question: What happens to the players the Queen sentences?
options: They are sent to the kitchen.
They have to become arches again.
Soldiers take them into custody.

feedback.zh: 王后判过的人由士兵押走；士兵原本当拱门，一走开，场上的拱门就越来越少。
feedback.en: The soldiers take the sentenced players into custody, so fewer and fewer arches are left on the ground.

grammar.excerpt: was too much frightened to say a word

focus.zh: too…to 结构：too 后的形容词表示程度过了头，to say a word 是她做不到的事。
focus.en: Too … to: the adjective after too is an excess, and the to-clause names what cannot happen.

paragraphs.text: Then the Queen left off, quite out of breath, and said to Alice, "Have you seen the Mock Turtle yet?"

sentences.text: Then the Queen left off, quite out of breath, and said to Alice, "Have you seen the Mock Turtle yet?"
sentences.zh: 后来王后停了下来，喘得上气不接下气，对爱丽丝说：“你见过假海龟了吗？”

hints.zh: 假海龟，因为“假海龟汤”这道菜而被造出来的一只海龟，整章都在讲自己的伤心史。
hints.en: The Mock Turtle, a creature invented from the dish Mock Turtle Soup; he tells his sad history in this chapter.

paragraphs.text: "No," said Alice. "I don't even know what a Mock Turtle is."

sentences.text: "No," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “没有，”爱丽丝说。

sentences.text: "I don't even know what a Mock Turtle is."
sentences.zh: “我连假海龟是什么都不知道。”

paragraphs.text: "It's the thing Mock Turtle Soup is made from," said the Queen.

sentences.text: "It's the thing Mock Turtle Soup is made from," said the Queen.
sentences.zh: “它就是做假海龟汤用的那种东西，”王后说。

hints.zh: 假海龟汤，一种用牛犊肉仿制龟汤的菜；奇境里照这道菜造出了一只“假海龟”。
hints.en: Mock turtle soup: a dish made from veal to imitate green turtle soup; Wonderland turns the dish into a creature.

paragraphs.text: "I never saw one, or heard of one," said Alice.

sentences.text: "I never saw one, or heard of one," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “我从没见过，也没听说过，”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "Come on, then," said the Queen, "and he shall tell you his history."

sentences.text: "Come on, then," said the Queen, "and he shall tell you his history."
sentences.zh: “那就来吧，”王后说，“让他给你讲讲他的经历。”

paragraphs.text: As they walked off together, Alice heard the King say in a low voice, to the company generally, "You are all pardoned." "Come, that's a good thing!" she said to herself, for she had felt quite unhappy at the number of executions the Queen had ordered.

sentences.text: As they walked off together, Alice heard the King say in a low voice, to the company generally, "You are all pardoned."
sentences.zh: 她们一起走开时，爱丽丝听见国王低声对大家说：“你们都被赦免了。”

sentences.text: "Come, that's a good thing!" she said to herself, for she had felt quite unhappy at the number of executions the Queen had ordered.
sentences.zh: “嘿，这倒是件好事！”她自言自语，因为王后判了那么多次处决，她心里一直很不好受。

paragraphs.text: They very soon came upon a Gryphon, lying fast asleep in the sun. (If you don't know what a Gryphon is, look at the picture.) "Up, lazy thing!" said the Queen, "and take this young lady to see the Mock Turtle, and to hear his history. I must go back and see after some executions I have ordered;" and she walked off, leaving Alice alone with the Gryphon. Alice did not quite like the look of the creature, but on the whole she thought it would be quite as safe to stay with it as to go after that savage Queen: so she waited.

sentences.text: They very soon came upon a Gryphon, lying fast asleep in the sun. (If you don't know what a Gryphon is, look at the picture.) "Up, lazy thing!" said the Queen, "and take this young lady to see the Mock Turtle, and to hear his history.
sentences.zh: 她们很快遇见一只狮鹫，正躺在太阳底下睡得正香。（你要是不知道狮鹫长什么样，就看看图吧。）“起来，懒东西！”王后说，“带这位小姐去看假海龟，听他的经历。

sentences.text: I must go back and see after some executions I have ordered;" and she walked off, leaving Alice alone with the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: 我得回去看看我判的那些处决办得怎么样了。”说完她就走了，把爱丽丝一个人留下和狮鹫在一起。

sentences.text: Alice did not quite like the look of the creature, but on the whole she thought it would be quite as safe to stay with it as to go after that savage Queen: so she waited.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝不太喜欢这家伙的样子，不过总的来说，她觉得留在它这儿跟跟着那个凶恶的王后走一样安全：于是她就等着。

hints.zh: 狮鹫，狮身鹰头、长着鹰翼的怪兽，这里是王后的随从。
hints.en: The Gryphon: a monster with a lion's body and an eagle's head and wings, serving the Queen.

paragraphs.text: The Gryphon sat up and rubbed its eyes: then it watched the Queen till she was out of sight: then it chuckled. "What fun!" said the Gryphon, half to itself, half to Alice.

sentences.text: The Gryphon sat up and rubbed its eyes: then it watched the Queen till she was out of sight: then it chuckled.
sentences.zh: 狮鹫坐起来揉揉眼睛：然后看着王后，直到她走出视线：接着它咯咯笑了起来。

sentences.text: "What fun!" said the Gryphon, half to itself, half to Alice.
sentences.zh: “真好玩！”狮鹫说，一半对自己，一半对爱丽丝。

paragraphs.text: "What is the fun?" said Alice.

sentences.text: "What is the fun?" said Alice.
sentences.zh: “有什么好玩的？”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "Why, she," said the Gryphon. "It's all her fancy, that: they never executes nobody, you know. Come on!"

sentences.text: "Why, she," said the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: “嘿，就是她呀，”狮鹫说。

sentences.text: "It's all her fancy, that: they never executes nobody, you know.
sentences.zh: “那全是她自己想出来的：他们谁也不处决，你知道的。

sentences.text: Come on!"
sentences.zh: 走吧！”

hints.zh: 想象、幻想；狮鹫说这一切都是王后自己想出来的。
hints.en: Fancy: imagination; the Gryphon says it is all in the Queen's imagination.

hints.zh: 双重否定，等于“他们谁也不处决”；executes 还用了不合语法的形式，是狮鹫的粗俗口吻。
hints.en: A double negative meaning 'they never execute anybody'; the verb form is also non-standard, in the Gryphon's rough speech.

introduction.zh: 王后带爱丽丝去看假海龟，可爱丽丝连假海龟是什么都不知道。路上她听见国王低声对众人说了一句话，随后她们在一只睡着的狮鹫跟前停下。这只怪兽醒来后只是咯咯笑，说了一句让人摸不着头脑的话。
introduction.en: The Queen leads Alice off to meet the Mock Turtle, though Alice has no idea what one is. On the way she hears the King say something to the crowd. Then they stop beside a Gryphon asleep in the sun, and the creature wakes up laughing.

quiz.question: What does the Queen say a Mock Turtle is?
options: A turtle that has learnt to talk.
The thing Mock Turtle Soup is made from.
A kind of very large fish.

feedback.zh: 王后的答案是：假海龟就是做假海龟汤用的那种东西——等于没有解释。
feedback.en: The Queen's answer is that a Mock Turtle is the thing Mock Turtle Soup is made from, which explains nothing.

quiz.question: What does Alice hear the King say?
options: That everyone is pardoned.
That the game is over.
That the Queen is tired.

feedback.zh: 她们走开时，爱丽丝听见国王低声对众人说“你们都被赦免了”，她这才放下心。
feedback.en: As they walk away, Alice hears the King tell the company in a low voice that they are all pardoned.

grammar.excerpt: I don't even know what a Mock Turtle is

focus.zh: know 后面接 what 引导的小句，用陈述语序：a Mock Turtle 在前，is 在后，不是问句语序。
focus.en: After know, the what-clause keeps statement order: a Mock Turtle comes before is.

paragraphs.text: "Everybody says 'come on!' here," thought Alice, as she went slowly after it: "I never was so ordered about before, in all my life, never!"
