sentences.text: "Everybody says 'come on!' here," thought Alice, as she went slowly after it: "I never was so ordered about before, in all my life, never!"
sentences.zh: “这儿人人都说‘走吧！’”爱丽丝一边想，一边慢吞吞地跟在它后面，“我这辈子还从没被人这么呼来喝去过，从来没有！”

hints.zh: 被人支使来支使去、呼来喝去。
hints.en: Ordered about: told to go here and there by other people.

paragraphs.text: They had not gone far before they saw the Mock Turtle in the distance, sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock, and, as they came nearer, Alice could hear him sighing as if his heart would break. She pitied him deeply. "What is his sorrow?" she asked the Gryphon, and the Gryphon answered, very nearly in the same words as before, "It's all his fancy, that: he hasn't got no sorrow, you know. Come on!"

sentences.text: They had not gone far before they saw the Mock Turtle in the distance, sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock, and, as they came nearer, Alice could hear him sighing as if his heart would break.
sentences.zh: 他们没走多远，就看见远处的假海龟，孤零零、凄凄惨惨地坐在一块突出的岩石上；走近些，爱丽丝能听见他叹气，像是心都要碎了。

sentences.text: She pitied him deeply.
sentences.zh: 她非常同情他。

sentences.text: "What is his sorrow?" she asked the Gryphon, and the Gryphon answered, very nearly in the same words as before, "It's all his fancy, that: he hasn't got no sorrow, you know.
sentences.zh: “他为什么伤心？”她问狮鹫，狮鹫几乎还是用先前那句话回答：“那全是他的幻想：他没有半点伤心事，你知道的。

sentences.text: Come on!"
sentences.zh: 走吧！”

paragraphs.text: So they went up to the Mock Turtle, who looked at them with large eyes full of tears, but said nothing.

sentences.text: So they went up to the Mock Turtle, who looked at them with large eyes full of tears, but said nothing.
sentences.zh: 于是他们走到假海龟跟前，他睁着盈满泪水的大眼睛望着两人，却一句话也不说。

paragraphs.text: "This here young lady," said the Gryphon, "she wants for to know your history, she do."

sentences.text: "This here young lady," said the Gryphon, "she wants for to know your history, she do."
sentences.zh: “这位小姐，”狮鹫说，“她想听听你的经历，她真想听。”

hints.zh: this here 是粗俗、乡下的说法，等于 this；后面 she wants for to know 也不合语法，是狮鹫的口气。
hints.en: This here is a rough, rustic way of saying this; she wants for to know is likewise non-standard, in the Gryphon's voice.

paragraphs.text: "I'll tell it her," said the Mock Turtle in a deep, hollow tone: "sit down both of you, and don't speak a word till I've finished."

sentences.text: "I'll tell it her," said the Mock Turtle in a deep, hollow tone: "sit down both of you, and don't speak a word till I've finished."
sentences.zh: “我会讲给她听，”假海龟用低沉空洞的声音说，“你们俩都坐下，我讲完之前一句话也别说。”

paragraphs.text: So they sat down, and nobody spoke for some minutes. Alice thought to herself, "I don't see how he can ever finish, if he doesn't begin." But she waited patiently.

sentences.text: So they sat down, and nobody spoke for some minutes.
sentences.zh: 于是他们坐下来，好几分钟谁也没说话。

sentences.text: Alice thought to herself, "I don't see how he can ever finish, if he doesn't begin."
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝心里想：“要是他不开始，我看不出他怎么能讲完。”

sentences.text: But she waited patiently.
sentences.zh: 可她还是耐心等着。

paragraphs.text: "Once," said the Mock Turtle at last, with a deep sigh, "I was a real Turtle."

sentences.text: "Once," said the Mock Turtle at last, with a deep sigh, "I was a real Turtle."
sentences.zh: “从前，”假海龟终于深深叹了口气说，“我是一只真正的海龟。”

paragraphs.text: These words were followed by a very long silence, broken only by an occasional exclamation of "Hjckrrh!" from the Gryphon, and the constant heavy sobbing of the Mock Turtle. Alice was very nearly getting up and saying, "Thank you, sir, for your interesting story," but she could not help thinking there must be more to come, so she sat still and said nothing.

sentences.text: These words were followed by a very long silence, broken only by an occasional exclamation of "Hjckrrh!" from the Gryphon, and the constant heavy sobbing of the Mock Turtle.
sentences.zh: 这句话说完，是很长一阵沉默，只有狮鹫偶尔一声“赫克噜！”和假海龟不停的沉重抽泣，才把这沉默打断。

sentences.text: Alice was very nearly getting up and saying, "Thank you, sir, for your interesting story," but she could not help thinking there must be more to come, so she sat still and said nothing.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝几乎要站起来说：“先生，谢谢你讲的有趣故事，”可她忍不住想，后面一定还有，于是坐着不动，什么也没说。

hints.zh: 狮鹫发出的怪叫，无法翻译的拟声词。
hints.en: Hjckrrh!: an untranslatable noise made by the Gryphon.

introduction.zh: 狮鹫领着爱丽丝去找假海龟。远远地，那只海龟孤零零坐在岩石上，叹气叹得像心都要碎了。可一问它为什么伤心，狮鹫的回答还是刚才那句话。等假海龟终于开口，它只说了一句，就久久不出声了。
introduction.en: The Gryphon leads Alice to the Mock Turtle, who sits alone on a rock, sighing as if his heart would break. Asked why he is sad, the Gryphon gives the same answer as before. At last the Mock Turtle speaks one short sentence, then falls silent.

quiz.question: Why does Alice pity the Mock Turtle at first?
options: He has lost all his school books.
The Gryphon keeps shouting at him.
He sits alone on a rock, sighing as if his heart would break.

feedback.zh: 假海龟孤零零坐在岩石上，叹气叹得像心要碎了，爱丽丝因此非常同情它。
feedback.en: The Mock Turtle sits alone on a rock, sighing as if his heart would break, and Alice pities him deeply.

quiz.question: Why doesn't Alice get up and thank the Mock Turtle?
options: She has not heard what he said.
She thinks there must be more of the story to come.
She is afraid of the Gryphon.

feedback.zh: 她几乎要起身道谢，可又觉得故事一定还有下文，于是坐着不动。
feedback.en: She almost gets up to thank him, but thinks there must be more to come, so she stays seated.

grammar.excerpt: Alice could hear him sighing as if his heart would break

focus.zh: hear + 宾语 + 现在分词 sighing，表示听见的是正在进行、还没结束的叹气。
focus.en: Hear + object + present participle sighing: Alice hears the sighing as it goes on, not as a finished action.

paragraphs.text: "When we were little," the Mock Turtle went on at last, more calmly, though still sobbing a little now and then, "we went to school in the sea. The master was an old Turtle—we used to call him Tortoise—"

sentences.text: "When we were little," the Mock Turtle went on at last, more calmly, though still sobbing a little now and then, "we went to school in the sea.
sentences.zh: “我们小的时候，”假海龟终于又往下讲，平静了些，虽然还不时抽泣一下，“我们在海里上学。

sentences.text: The master was an old Turtle—we used to call him Tortoise—"
sentences.zh: 老师是一只老海龟——我们往常叫他陆龟——”

hints.zh: 陆龟；Tortoise 与 taught us（他教我们）读音相近，这是假海龟的谐音玩笑。
hints.en: Tortoise: a land turtle. The word sounds like 'taught us', which is the Mock Turtle's joke.

paragraphs.text: "Why did you call him Tortoise, if he wasn't one?" Alice asked.

sentences.text: "Why did you call him Tortoise, if he wasn't one?"
sentences.zh: “他既然不是陆龟，你们为什么叫他陆龟？”

sentences.text: Alice asked.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝问。

paragraphs.text: "We called him Tortoise, because he taught us," said the Mock Turtle angrily; "really you are very dull!"

sentences.text: "We called him Tortoise, because he taught us," said the Mock Turtle angrily; "really you are very dull!"
sentences.zh: “我们叫他陆龟，因为他教我们，”假海龟气呼呼地说，“你可真够迟钝的！”

paragraphs.text: "You ought to be ashamed of yourself for asking such a simple question," added the Gryphon; and then they both sat silent and looked at poor Alice, who felt ready to sink into the earth. At last the Gryphon said to the Mock Turtle, "Drive on, old fellow! Don't be all day about it!" and he went on in these words:

sentences.text: "You ought to be ashamed of yourself for asking such a simple question," added the Gryphon; and then they both sat silent and looked at poor Alice, who felt ready to sink into the earth.
sentences.zh: “问这么简单的问题，你该为自己害臊，”狮鹫补了一句；然后他们两个都一声不响地坐着，看着可怜的爱丽丝，她恨不得钻进地缝里去。

sentences.text: At last the Gryphon said to the Mock Turtle, "Drive on, old fellow!
sentences.zh: 最后狮鹫对假海龟说：“接着说呀，老伙计！

sentences.text: Don't be all day about it!" and he went on in these words:
sentences.zh: 别磨蹭一整天！”于是他又接着这样说道：

hints.zh: 原意是“赶车往前走”，这里指“接着往下讲”。
hints.en: Drive on: literally 'drive the cart on', here 'go on with your story'.

paragraphs.text: "Yes, we went to school in the sea, though you mayn't believe it—"

sentences.text: "Yes, we went to school in the sea, though you mayn't believe it—"
sentences.zh: “是啊，我们在海里上学，尽管你也许不信——”

paragraphs.text: "I never said I didn't!" interrupted Alice.

sentences.text: "I never said I didn't!" interrupted Alice.
sentences.zh: “我从没说过我不信！”爱丽丝打断他。

paragraphs.text: "You did," said the Mock Turtle.

sentences.text: "You did," said the Mock Turtle.
sentences.zh: “你说过，”假海龟说。

paragraphs.text: "Hold your tongue!" added the Gryphon, before Alice could speak again. The Mock Turtle went on.

sentences.text: "Hold your tongue!" added the Gryphon, before Alice could speak again.
sentences.zh: “住嘴！”爱丽丝还没来得及再开口，狮鹫就补了一句。

sentences.text: The Mock Turtle went on.
sentences.zh: 假海龟继续讲。

paragraphs.text: "We had the best of educations—in fact, we went to school every day—"

sentences.text: "We had the best of educations—in fact, we went to school every day—"
sentences.zh: “我们受的是最好的教育——事实上，我们每天都去上学——”

paragraphs.text: "I've been to a day-school too," said Alice; "you needn't be so proud as all that."

sentences.text: "I've been to a day-school too," said Alice; "you needn't be so proud as all that."
sentences.zh: “我也上过走读学校，”爱丽丝说，“你用不着这么得意。”

hints.zh: 走读学校，学生每天回家，不住校。
hints.en: A day-school: a school where pupils go home every day instead of boarding.

paragraphs.text: "With extras?" asked the Mock Turtle a little anxiously.

sentences.text: "With extras?" asked the Mock Turtle a little anxiously.
sentences.zh: “有额外课程吗？”假海龟有点着急地问。

hints.zh: 额外收费的课程或项目，如音乐、绘画之类。
hints.en: Extras: lessons or subjects charged on top of the ordinary fees.

paragraphs.text: "Yes," said Alice, "we learned French and music."

sentences.text: "Yes," said Alice, "we learned French and music."
sentences.zh: “有，”爱丽丝说，“我们学法语和音乐。”

paragraphs.text: "And washing?" said the Mock Turtle.

sentences.text: "And washing?" said the Mock Turtle.
sentences.zh: “还有洗衣课吗？”假海龟说。

paragraphs.text: "Certainly not!" said Alice indignantly.

sentences.text: "Certainly not!" said Alice indignantly.
sentences.zh: “当然没有！”爱丽丝愤愤地说。

paragraphs.text: "Ah! Then yours wasn't a really good school," said the Mock Turtle in a tone of great relief. "Now at ours they had at the end of the bill, 'French, music, and washing—extra.'"

sentences.text: "Ah!
Then yours wasn't a really good school," said the Mock Turtle in a tone of great relief.
sentences.zh: 那么你上的算不上真正的好学校，”假海龟用大为宽慰的语气说。

sentences.text: "Now at ours they had at the end of the bill, 'French, music, and washing—extra.'"
sentences.zh: “我们学校的账单末尾就写着：‘法语、音乐和洗衣——额外收费。’”

hints.zh: 学校账单末尾的额外收费项目；海底的学校把“游泳”也算成一门“洗衣”课。
hints.en: The list of extras at the end of the school bill; in a sea school, swimming counts as 'washing'.

hints.zh: 账单；这里指学校的收费单，不是人名“比尔”。
hints.en: Bill here means the school's bill for fees, not the name Bill.

paragraphs.text: "You couldn't have wanted it much," said Alice: "living at the bottom of the sea."

sentences.text: "You couldn't have wanted it much," said Alice: "living at the bottom of the sea."
sentences.zh: “你大概也不会太想要它，”爱丽丝说，“你们住在海底呀。”

introduction.zh: 假海龟讲起小时候在海里的学校：老师是一只老海龟，他们却管他叫“陆龟”。爱丽丝问了一句为什么，两个家伙都认定她太笨。接着他们说起课程和学费账单，越说越得意。海底的学校究竟教些什么？
introduction.en: The Mock Turtle describes his school at the bottom of the sea, where the master was an old Turtle they called Tortoise. Alice asks why, and both creatures decide she is very dull. Then they begin to boast about their lessons and their school bills.

quiz.question: Why did they call the old Turtle "Tortoise"?
options: Because he taught them.
Because he was very slow.
Because he lived on land.

feedback.zh: 假海龟说他们叫他 Tortoise，是因为他教他们（taught us）——这是拿谐音当理由，爱丽丝却当真了。
feedback.en: The Mock Turtle says they called him Tortoise because he taught them; it is a pun on 'taught us', not a real reason.

quiz.question: What did the Mock Turtle say was at the end of their school bill?
options: "Ten hours of lessons a day."
"No extras at all."
"French, music, and washing—extra."

feedback.zh: 他说他们学校账单末尾写着“法语、音乐和洗衣——额外收费”，还把“洗衣”当成一门正经课程。
feedback.en: He says their bill ended with 'French, music, and washing—extra', treating washing as a real subject.

grammar.excerpt: You ought to be ashamed of yourself

focus.zh: ought to 是“应该”，比 should 更带责备意味；狮鹫在说爱丽丝该为自己害臊。
focus.en: Ought to means 'should', with a stronger note of blame: the Gryphon says Alice ought to feel ashamed.

paragraphs.text: "I couldn't afford to learn it," said the Mock Turtle with a sigh. "I only took the regular course."

sentences.text: "I couldn't afford to learn it," said the Mock Turtle with a sigh.
sentences.zh: “我学不起，”假海龟叹了口气说。

sentences.text: "I only took the regular course."
sentences.zh: “我只上了常规课程。”

paragraphs.text: "What was that?" inquired Alice.

sentences.text: "What was that?" inquired Alice.
sentences.zh: “那是什么？”爱丽丝问。

paragraphs.text: "Reeling and Writhing, of course, to begin with," the Mock Turtle replied: "and then the different branches of Arithmetic—Ambition, Distraction, Uglification, and Derision."

sentences.text: "Reeling and Writhing, of course, to begin with," the Mock Turtle replied: "and then the different branches of Arithmetic—Ambition, Distraction, Uglification, and Derision."
sentences.zh: “当然，先学‘打转’和‘扭动’，”假海龟回答，“然后是算术的各个分支——‘野心’、‘分心’、‘丑化’和‘嘲笑’。”

hints.zh: 谐音 reading and writing（读和写）；假海龟把学校的科目都说成了谐音笑话。
hints.en: A pun on 'reading and writing': the Mock Turtle turns every school subject into a pun.

hints.zh: 四则运算的谐音：addition（加）、subtraction（减）、multiplication（乘）、division（除）。
hints.en: Puns on the four operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.

paragraphs.text: "I never heard of 'Uglification,'" Alice ventured to say. "What is it?"

sentences.text: "I never heard of 'Uglification,'" Alice ventured to say.
sentences.zh: “我从没听说过‘丑化’这门课，”爱丽丝壮着胆说。

sentences.text: "What is it?"
sentences.zh: “那是什么？”

paragraphs.text: The Gryphon lifted up both its paws in surprise. "Never heard of uglifying!" it exclaimed. "You know what to beautify is, I suppose?"

sentences.text: The Gryphon lifted up both its paws in surprise.
sentences.zh: 狮鹫惊讶地举起两只前爪。

sentences.text: "Never heard of uglifying!" it exclaimed.
sentences.zh: “没听说过‘丑化’！”它叫道。

sentences.text: "You know what to beautify is, I suppose?"
sentences.zh: “你总该知道‘美化’是什么意思吧？”

paragraphs.text: "Yes," said Alice, doubtfully: "it means—to—make—anything—prettier."

sentences.text: "Yes," said Alice, doubtfully: "it means—to—make—anything—prettier."
sentences.zh: “知道，”爱丽丝迟疑地说，“意思是——把——什么东西——弄得——更好看。”

paragraphs.text: "Well then," the Gryphon went on, "if you don't know what to uglify is, you are a simpleton."

sentences.text: "Well then," the Gryphon went on, "if you don't know what to uglify is, you are a simpleton."
sentences.zh: “那么，”狮鹫说，“你要是不知道‘丑化’是什么意思，你就是个傻瓜。”

paragraphs.text: Alice did not feel encouraged to ask any more questions about it, so she turned to the Mock Turtle, and said, "What else had you to learn?"

sentences.text: Alice did not feel encouraged to ask any more questions about it, so she turned to the Mock Turtle, and said, "What else had you to learn?"
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝觉得不便再问这个了，就转向假海龟，说：“你们还要学什么？”

paragraphs.text: "Well, there was Mystery," the Mock Turtle replied, counting off the subjects on his flappers,—"Mystery, ancient and modern, with Seaography: then Drawling—the Drawling-master was an old conger-eel, that used to come once a week: he taught us Drawling, Stretching, and Fainting in Coils."

sentences.text: "Well, there was Mystery," the Mock Turtle replied, counting off the subjects on his flappers,—"Mystery, ancient and modern, with Seaography: then Drawling—the Drawling-master was an old conger-eel, that used to come once a week: he taught us Drawling, Stretching, and Fainting in Coils."
sentences.zh: “嗯，还有‘秘史’，”假海龟回答，一边用鳍数着科目，“古代和现代的‘秘史’，再加上‘海洋地理’：然后是‘拖长腔’——教拖长腔的老师是一条老海鳗，每星期来一次：他教我们拖长腔、伸展，还有盘成一团地昏倒。”

hints.target: Mystery, ancient and modern, with Seaography
hints.zh: 谐音 history（历史）和 geography（地理）；“古代和现代”是历史的说法。
hints.en: Puns on 'history' and 'geography'; 'ancient and modern' is how history is usually described.

hints.target: Drawling, Stretching, and Fainting in Coils
hints.zh: 谐音 drawing（素描）、sketching（写生）、painting in oils（油画）；字面却是“拖长腔、伸展、盘成一团地昏倒”。
hints.en: Puns on 'drawing', 'sketching' and 'painting in oils', though the words say 'drawling, stretching and fainting'.

paragraphs.text: "What was that like?" said Alice.

sentences.text: "What was that like?" said Alice.
sentences.zh: “那是什么样的？”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "Well, I can't show it you, myself," the Mock Turtle said: "I'm too stiff. And the Gryphon never learnt it."

sentences.text: "Well, I can't show it you, myself," the Mock Turtle said: "I'm too stiff.
sentences.zh: “嗯，我自己没法做给你看，”假海龟说，“我太僵硬了。

sentences.text: And the Gryphon never learnt it."
sentences.zh: 再说狮鹫从没学过。”

paragraphs.text: "Hadn't time," said the Gryphon: "I went to the Classical master, though. He was an old crab, he was."

sentences.text: "Hadn't time," said the Gryphon: "I went to the Classical master, though.
sentences.zh: “没时间，”狮鹫说，“不过我去上过古典文学老师的课。

sentences.text: He was an old crab, he was."
sentences.zh: 他是一只老螃蟹，真的。”

paragraphs.text: "I never went to him," the Mock Turtle said with a sigh: "he taught Laughing and Grief, they used to say."

sentences.text: "I never went to him," the Mock Turtle said with a sigh: "he taught Laughing and Grief, they used to say."
sentences.zh: “我从没上过他的课，”假海龟叹着气说，“他们常说，他教‘笑’和‘悲’。”

hints.zh: 谐音 Latin and Greek（拉丁文和希腊文），正是古典文学老师教的科目。
hints.en: A pun on 'Latin and Greek', the subjects a classical master would teach.

paragraphs.text: "So he did, so he did," said the Gryphon, sighing in his turn, and both creatures hid their faces in their paws.

sentences.text: "So he did, so he did," said the Gryphon, sighing in his turn, and both creatures hid their faces in their paws.
sentences.zh: “他是教这些，他是教这些，”狮鹫说着，也叹了口气，两个家伙都把脸埋进了爪子。

introduction.zh: 假海龟报出一串奇怪的课名：旋转、扭动，还有算术的各个分支。爱丽丝只问了一句“丑化”是什么，狮鹫就举起两只前爪，说她是个傻瓜。接着又是“拖长腔”“盘成一团地昏倒”——这些课到底怎么上？
introduction.en: The Mock Turtle lists his subjects: Reeling and Writhing, then the branches of Arithmetic. Alice asks what Uglification is, and the Gryphon lifts both paws and calls her a simpleton. More strange lessons follow, taught by an old conger-eel and an old crab.

quiz.question: Why does the Gryphon call Alice a simpleton?
options: She has never been to school.
She does not know what "uglify" means.
She cannot swim.

feedback.zh: 狮鹫先问她知不知道 beautify（美化），她答上来了；可她说不出 uglify，于是被叫作傻瓜。
feedback.en: Alice can explain 'beautify' but not 'uglify', so the Gryphon calls her a simpleton.

quiz.question: Which subjects did the Drawling-master teach?
options: Drawling, Stretching, and Fainting in Coils.
Laughing and Grief.
Reeling and Writhing.

feedback.zh: 假海龟说，教“拖长腔”的老师是一条老海鳗，教的是拖长腔、伸展和盘成一团地昏倒。
feedback.en: The Mock Turtle says the old conger-eel taught Drawling, Stretching, and Fainting in Coils.

grammar.excerpt: if you don't know what to uglify is, you are a simpleton

focus.zh: if 从句用现在时 don't know，主句也用现在时 you are：真实条件，条件一成立结论就成立。
focus.en: Both clauses take the present: don't know in the if-clause, you are in the main clause — a real condition.

paragraphs.text: "And how many hours a day did you do lessons?" said Alice, in a hurry to change the subject.

sentences.text: "And how many hours a day did you do lessons?" said Alice, in a hurry to change the subject.
sentences.zh: “你们一天上几个小时的课？”爱丽丝说，急着换个话题。

hints.target: in a hurry to change the subject
hints.zh: 急着换个话题，不想再谈刚才那件事。
hints.en: In a hurry to change the subject: eager to talk about something else.

paragraphs.text: "Ten hours the first day," said the Mock Turtle: "nine the next, and so on."

sentences.text: "Ten hours the first day," said the Mock Turtle: "nine the next, and so on."
sentences.zh: “第一天十小时，”假海龟说，“第二天九小时，依此类推。”

paragraphs.text: "What a curious plan!" exclaimed Alice.

sentences.text: "What a curious plan!" exclaimed Alice.
sentences.zh: “多古怪的安排！”爱丽丝叫道。

paragraphs.text: "That's the reason they're called lessons," the Gryphon remarked: "because they lessen from day to day."

sentences.text: "That's the reason they're called lessons," the Gryphon remarked: "because they lessen from day to day."
sentences.zh: “这就是为什么管它们叫‘课’，”狮鹫说，“因为它们一天比一天少。”

hints.zh: 减少；与 lessons（课）读音相近，狮鹫就拿这个谐音解释“课”为什么叫 lesson。
hints.en: Lessen: to become less. It sounds like 'lessons', which is the Gryphon's joke.

paragraphs.text: This was quite a new idea to Alice, and she thought it over a little before she made her next remark. "Then the eleventh day must have been a holiday?"

sentences.text: This was quite a new idea to Alice, and she thought it over a little before she made her next remark.
sentences.zh: 这对爱丽丝来说是个全新的想法，她想了一会儿才说下一句话。

sentences.text: "Then the eleventh day must have been a holiday?"
sentences.zh: “那么第十一天一定放假了？”

paragraphs.text: "Of course it was," said the Mock Turtle.

sentences.text: "Of course it was," said the Mock Turtle.
sentences.zh: “当然放假，”假海龟说。

paragraphs.text: "And how did you manage on the twelfth?" Alice went on eagerly.

sentences.text: "And how did you manage on the twelfth?"
sentences.zh: “那第十二天你们怎么办呢？”

sentences.text: Alice went on eagerly.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝急切地追问。

paragraphs.text: "That's enough about lessons," the Gryphon interrupted in a very decided tone: "tell her something about the games now."

sentences.text: "That's enough about lessons," the Gryphon interrupted in a very decided tone: "tell her something about the games now."
sentences.zh: “课的事说得够多了，”狮鹫用非常决断的口气打断，“现在给她讲讲游戏的事吧。”

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝赶紧把话题转到功课上，问他们一天上几个小时的课。假海龟答得干脆：第一天十小时，第二天九小时。这个安排让爱丽丝觉得古怪，狮鹫却给出一个听起来挺有道理的解释。那么第十一天呢？
introduction.en: Alice hurries to change the subject and asks how many hours of lessons they had each day. Ten the first day, nine the next, says the Mock Turtle. Alice finds the plan curious, and the Gryphon offers an explanation that almost sounds reasonable.

quiz.question: How many hours of lessons did they have on the second day?
options: Ten.
Eleven.
Nine.

feedback.zh: 假海龟说第一天十小时，第二天九小时，以后每天再少一小时。
feedback.en: The Mock Turtle says ten hours the first day and nine the next, one hour less each day.

quiz.question: What reason does the Gryphon give for the name "lessons"?
options: They are always extras.
They lessen from day to day.
They are taught in the sea.

feedback.zh: 狮鹫说，正因为一天比一天少（lessen），这些课才叫 lessons——又是拿谐音当解释。
feedback.en: The Gryphon says they are called lessons because they lessen from day to day, another pun.

grammar.excerpt: What a curious plan!

focus.zh: What + a + 形容词 + 名词，主语和 be 全省了；完整说法是 What a curious plan it is!
focus.en: What + a + adjective + noun, with subject and verb left out: the full form would be 'What a curious plan it is!'

title.en: How to Dance Under the Sea

paragraphs.text: The Mock Turtle sighed deeply, and drew the back of one flapper across his eyes. He looked at Alice and tried to speak, but for a minute or two sobs choked his voice. "Same as if he had a bone in his throat," said the Gryphon, and it set to work shaking him and punching him in the back. At last the Mock Turtle recovered his voice, and, with tears running down his cheeks, he went on again:—

sentences.text: The Mock Turtle sighed deeply, and drew the back of one flapper across his eyes.
sentences.zh: 假海龟深深叹了口气，抬起一只鳍肢，用鳍背抹了抹眼睛。

sentences.text: He looked at Alice and tried to speak, but for a minute or two sobs choked his voice.
sentences.zh: 他望着爱丽丝，想开口说话，可有一两分钟，抽泣堵住了他的嗓子。

sentences.text: "Same as if he had a bone in his throat," said the Gryphon, and it set to work shaking him and punching him in the back.
sentences.zh: “就像他喉咙里卡了根骨头，”狮鹫说，接着就动手摇他、捶他的背。

sentences.text: At last the Mock Turtle recovered his voice, and, with tears running down his cheeks, he went on again:—
sentences.zh: 假海龟终于缓过声来，眼泪顺着脸颊往下淌，又接着说了下去：——

hints.zh: 爱丽丝，本书主角，追着白兔掉进兔子洞的小姑娘。
hints.en: Alice, the girl who followed the White Rabbit down the hole and is the heroine of the book.

hints.zh: 假海龟，海里的一只海龟，为失去的童年伤心，说话常带着哭腔。
hints.en: The Mock Turtle, a sea turtle who mourns his lost childhood and often speaks through sobs.

hints.zh: 狮鹫，狮身鹰翼的怪兽，说话直率，常替假海龟把话说完。
hints.en: The Gryphon, a creature with a lion's body and eagle's wings, blunt and fond of finishing the Mock Turtle's sentences.

hints.zh: 海龟的鳍状肢；这里指他抬起鳍来，用鳍背抹眼泪。
hints.en: A flapper is a turtle's flipper; here he wipes his eyes with the back of one.

paragraphs.text: "You may not have lived much under the sea—" ("I haven't," said Alice)—"and perhaps you were never even introduced to a lobster—" (Alice began to say "I once tasted—" but checked herself hastily, and said, "No, never")—"so you can have no idea what a delightful thing a Lobster-Quadrille is!"

sentences.text: "You may not have lived much under the sea—" ("I haven't," said Alice)—"and perhaps you were never even introduced to a lobster—" (Alice began to say "I once tasted—" but checked herself hastily, and said, "No, never")—"so you can have no idea what a delightful thing a Lobster-Quadrille is!"
sentences.zh: “你大概没怎么在海底住过——”（“我没住过，”爱丽丝说）——“说不定还从来没人给你引见过龙虾——”（爱丽丝刚要说“我尝过一次——”，又急忙收住，改口说“没有，从来没有”）——“所以你想不出龙虾四对舞是件多快活的事！”

hints.zh: 龙虾四对舞，假海龟讲的那种海底舞蹈，跳舞的人要拿龙虾当舞伴。
hints.en: The Lobster Quadrille, the sea dance the Mock Turtle describes, danced with lobsters as partners.

paragraphs.text: "No, indeed," said Alice. "What sort of a dance is it?"

sentences.text: "No, indeed," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “是没有，真的。”爱丽丝说。

sentences.text: "What sort of a dance is it?"
sentences.zh: “那是一种什么样的舞？”

paragraphs.text: "Why," said the Gryphon, "you first form into a line along the sea-shore—"

sentences.text: "Why," said the Gryphon, "you first form into a line along the sea-shore—"
sentences.zh: “这个嘛，”狮鹫说，“你先沿着海岸排成一行——”

paragraphs.text: "Two lines!" cried the Mock Turtle. "Seals, turtles, salmon, and so on: then, when you've cleared all the jelly-fish out of the way—"

sentences.text: "Two lines!" cried the Mock Turtle.
sentences.zh: “两行！”假海龟喊道。

sentences.text: "Seals, turtles, salmon, and so on: then, when you've cleared all the jelly-fish out of the way—"
sentences.zh: “海豹、海龟、鲑鱼，等等：然后，等你们把水母全都清到一边去——”

paragraphs.text: "That generally takes some time," interrupted the Gryphon.

sentences.text: "That generally takes some time," interrupted the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: “那一般得花不少时间。”狮鹫插嘴说。

paragraphs.text: "—you advance twice—"

sentences.text: "—you advance twice—"
sentences.zh: “——你向前进两步——”

paragraphs.text: "Each with a lobster as a partner!" cried the Gryphon.

sentences.text: "Each with a lobster as a partner!" cried the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: “每人带一只龙虾当舞伴！”狮鹫喊道。

paragraphs.text: "Of course," the Mock Turtle said: "advance twice, set to partners—"

sentences.text: "Of course," the Mock Turtle said: "advance twice, set to partners—"
sentences.zh: “当然，”假海龟说，“向前进两步，和舞伴对舞——”

hints.zh: 对舞中的一步：和舞伴面对面站好，相对而舞。
hints.en: A country-dance step: to face your partner and dance towards each other.

paragraphs.text: "—change lobsters, and retire in the same order," continued the Gryphon.

sentences.text: "—change lobsters, and retire in the same order," continued the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: “——交换龙虾，再按原来的次序退回来。”狮鹫接着说。

paragraphs.text: "Then, you know," the Mock Turtle went on, "you throw the—"

sentences.text: "Then, you know," the Mock Turtle went on, "you throw the—"
sentences.zh: “然后，你知道，”假海龟继续说，“你把那——”

paragraphs.text: "The lobsters!" shouted the Gryphon, with a bound into the air.

sentences.text: "The lobsters!" shouted the Gryphon, with a bound into the air.
sentences.zh: “把龙虾！”狮鹫大喊一声，往空中一跳。

paragraphs.text: "—as far out to sea as you can—"

sentences.text: "—as far out to sea as you can—"
sentences.zh: “——往海里扔得越远越好——”

paragraphs.text: "Swim after them!" screamed the Gryphon.

sentences.text: "Swim after them!" screamed the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: “再游过去追它们！”狮鹫尖叫道。

paragraphs.text: "Turn a somersault in the sea!" cried the Mock Turtle, capering wildly about.

sentences.text: "Turn a somersault in the sea!" cried the Mock Turtle, capering wildly about.
sentences.zh: “在海里翻个跟头！”假海龟喊道，发疯似的蹦来蹦去。

paragraphs.text: "Change lobsters again!" yelled the Gryphon at the top of its voice.

sentences.text: "Change lobsters again!" yelled the Gryphon at the top of its voice.
sentences.zh: “再换一回龙虾！”狮鹫扯着嗓子大叫。

introduction.zh: 假海龟哭得说不出话，狮鹫只好又摇又捶他的背。等他终于开口，讲的却是一种海边的舞：要排成两行，还得带上龙虾当舞伴。为什么非要龙虾不可？
introduction.en: The Mock Turtle is sobbing so hard that the Gryphon has to shake him and punch his back. When he can speak at last, he describes a dance on the sea-shore: two lines, and a lobster for every dancer. Why a lobster, of all things?

quiz.question: What does the Gryphon do to help the Mock Turtle?
options: It carries him down to the shore.
It gives him a drink of water.
It shakes him and punches him in the back.

feedback.zh: 假海龟抽泣得说不出话，狮鹫说他像是喉咙里卡了骨头，就动手摇他、捶他的背。
feedback.en: The Mock Turtle cannot speak for sobbing, so the Gryphon shakes him and punches his back.

quiz.question: What does every dancer need in the Lobster Quadrille?
options: A line of seals to dance behind.
A lobster as a partner.
A shell to carry in one hand.

feedback.zh: 狮鹫喊出舞步的要点：每人要带一只龙虾当舞伴。
feedback.en: The Gryphon cries out that each dancer has a lobster as a partner.

grammar.excerpt: You may not have lived much under the sea

focus.zh: may not have lived 是情态动词 + have + 过去分词，用来推测过去的经历：也许你并没有在海底住过。
focus.en: May not have lived is a modal with have and a past participle, guessing about a past experience: perhaps you never lived under the sea.

paragraphs.text: "Back to land again, and—that's all the first figure," said the Mock Turtle, suddenly dropping his voice; and the two creatures, who had been jumping about like mad things all this time, sat down again very sadly and quietly, and looked at Alice.

sentences.text: "Back to land again, and—that's all the first figure," said the Mock Turtle, suddenly dropping his voice; and the two creatures, who had been jumping about like mad things all this time, sat down again very sadly and quietly, and looked at Alice.
sentences.zh: “再回到岸上，然后——第一段就是这样，”假海龟说着，忽然压低了声音；这两个家伙先前一直像疯子一样蹦来蹦去，这时又很伤心、很安静地坐了下来，看着爱丽丝。

hints.zh: figure 这里指一套舞步、一段舞（第一段），不是“数字”或“人物”。
hints.en: A figure here is one part or set of steps in a dance, not a number or a person.

paragraphs.text: "It must be a very pretty dance," said Alice timidly.

sentences.text: "It must be a very pretty dance," said Alice timidly.
sentences.zh: “那一定是一支很好看的舞。”爱丽丝怯生生地说。

paragraphs.text: "Would you like to see a little of it?" said the Mock Turtle.

sentences.text: "Would you like to see a little of it?" said the Mock Turtle.
sentences.zh: “你想不想看一点点？”假海龟说。

paragraphs.text: "Very much indeed," said Alice.

sentences.text: "Very much indeed," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “非常想。”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "Come, let's try the first figure!" said the Mock Turtle to the Gryphon. "We can do it without lobsters, you know. Which shall sing?"

sentences.text: "Come, let's try the first figure!" said the Mock Turtle to the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: “来吧，咱们试试第一段！”假海龟对狮鹫说。

sentences.text: "We can do it without lobsters, you know.
sentences.zh: “没有龙虾，咱们也能跳，你知道。

sentences.text: Which shall sing?"
sentences.zh: 谁来唱？”

paragraphs.text: "Oh, you sing," said the Gryphon. "I've forgotten the words."

sentences.text: "Oh, you sing," said the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: “哦，你唱。”狮鹫说。

sentences.text: "I've forgotten the words."
sentences.zh: “我忘了词了。”

paragraphs.text: So they began solemnly dancing round and round Alice, every now and then treading on her toes when they passed too close, and waving their fore-paws to mark the time, while the Mock Turtle sang this, very slowly and sadly:—

sentences.text: So they began solemnly dancing round and round Alice, every now and then treading on her toes when they passed too close, and waving their fore-paws to mark the time, while the Mock Turtle sang this, very slowly and sadly:—
sentences.zh: 于是他们郑重其事地围着爱丽丝一圈一圈地跳，经过时靠得太近就踩到她的脚趾，还挥着前爪打拍子；假海龟则非常缓慢、非常伤心地唱了起来：——

paragraphs.text: "Will you walk a little faster?" said a whiting to a snail, "There's a porpoise close behind us, and he's treading on my tail. See how eagerly the lobsters and the turtles all advance! They are waiting on the shingle—will you come and join the dance? Will you, won't you, will you, won't you, will you join the dance? Will you, won't you, will you, won't you, won't you join the dance?

sentences.text: "Will you walk a little faster?" said a whiting to a snail, "There's a porpoise close behind us, and he's treading on my tail.
sentences.zh: “你走快一点好不好？”一条牙鳕对蜗牛说，“咱们身后就有一只海豚，他正踩着我的尾巴呢。

sentences.text: See how eagerly the lobsters and the turtles all advance!
sentences.zh: 你看那些龙虾和乌龟，全都往前赶得多起劲！

sentences.text: They are waiting on the shingle—will you come and join the dance?
sentences.zh: 它们在卵石滩上等着——你来不来一起跳舞？

sentences.text: Will you, won't you, will you, won't you, will you join the dance?
sentences.zh: 你来不来，来不来，你来不来，来不来，你来跳舞吗？

sentences.text: Will you, won't you, will you, won't you, won't you join the dance?
sentences.zh: 你来不来，来不来，你来不来，来不来，你就不来跳舞吗？

hints.zh: 牙鳕，一种海鱼；歌里正是它在劝蜗牛去跳舞。
hints.en: A whiting, a small sea fish; in the song it is the whiting who urges the snail to dance.

hints.zh: 海豚（鼠海豚），歌里紧跟在它们身后的那一只。
hints.en: A porpoise, a sea animal like a small dolphin; in the song one is close behind them.

hints.zh: shingle 这里指海边铺满小石子的卵石滩，不是屋顶上的木瓦。
hints.en: Shingle here means a beach covered with small stones, not the tiles on a roof.

introduction.zh: 两只海里的动物说，没有龙虾也能跳第一段，就在爱丽丝身边跳起来。它们转着圈，时不时踩到她的脚趾，假海龟还唱起一支很慢、很伤心的歌：一条牙鳕在劝蜗牛跳舞。
introduction.en: The two sea creatures say they can try the first figure without lobsters, and they dance around Alice instead. They tread on her toes as they pass, while the Mock Turtle sings a slow, sad song about a whiting who asks a snail to join the dance.

quiz.question: What happens to Alice while the two creatures dance around her?
options: They tread on her toes when they pass close.
They push her into the sea.
They ask her to sing the chorus with them.

feedback.zh: 它们绕着爱丽丝一圈圈地跳，靠得太近时就踩到她的脚趾，还挥着前爪打拍子。
feedback.en: They dance round Alice and tread on her toes whenever they pass too close.

quiz.question: Who are the two animals talking in the song the Mock Turtle sings?
options: A porpoise and a seal.
A lobster and a turtle.
A whiting and a snail.

feedback.zh: 歌一开口就是一条牙鳕在对蜗牛说话，催它走快一点。
feedback.en: The song opens with a whiting speaking to a snail and urging it to walk faster.

grammar.excerpt: who had been jumping about like mad things

focus.zh: had been jumping 是过去完成进行时：在他们坐下来之前，已经这样蹦了好一阵。
focus.en: Had been jumping is past perfect continuous: the jumping had gone on for some time before they sat down.

paragraphs.text: "You can really have no notion how delightful it will be When they take us up and throw us, with the lobsters, out to sea!" But the snail replied, "Too far, too far!" and gave a look askance— Said he thanked the whiting kindly, but he would not join the dance. Would not, could not, would not, could not, would not join the dance. Would not, could not, would not, could not, could not join the dance.

sentences.text: "You can really have no notion how delightful it will be When they take us up and throw us, with the lobsters, out to sea!"
sentences.zh: “你真想不到那会有多快活：等他们把我们抬起来，跟龙虾一起扔到海里去！”

sentences.text: But the snail replied, "Too far, too far!" and gave a look askance— Said he thanked the whiting kindly, but he would not join the dance.
sentences.zh: 可蜗牛回答说：“太远了，太远了！”还斜斜地瞥了一眼——他说他很感谢牙鳕的好意，可他不想去跳舞。

sentences.text: Would not, could not, would not, could not, would not join the dance.
sentences.zh: 不去，不能去，不去，不能去，不去跳舞。

sentences.text: Would not, could not, would not, could not, could not join the dance.
sentences.zh: 不去，不能去，不去，不能去，不能去跳舞。

hints.zh: 斜着眼睛看，带着怀疑、不赞成的意思。
hints.en: To look askance is to glance sideways with doubt or disapproval.

paragraphs.text: "What matters it how far we go?" his scaly friend replied, "There is another shore, you know, upon the other side. The further off from England the nearer is to France— Then turn not pale, beloved snail, but come and join the dance. Will you, won't you, will you, won't you, will you join the dance? Will you, won't you, will you, won't you, won't you join the dance?"

sentences.text: "What matters it how far we go?" his scaly friend replied, "There is another shore, you know, upon the other side.
sentences.zh: “走远一点又有什么关系？”他那长鳞的朋友回答说，“你知道，另一边还有一片海岸。

sentences.text: The further off from England the nearer is to France— Then turn not pale, beloved snail, but come and join the dance.
sentences.zh: 离英格兰越远，就离法国越近——那么别脸色发白，亲爱的蜗牛，来一起跳舞吧。

sentences.text: Will you, won't you, will you, won't you, will you join the dance?
sentences.zh: 你来不来，来不来，你来不来，你来跳舞吗？

sentences.text: Will you, won't you, will you, won't you, won't you join the dance?"
sentences.zh: 你来不来，来不来，你来不来，你就不来跳舞吗？”

paragraphs.text: "Thank you, it's a very interesting dance to watch," said Alice, feeling very glad that it was over at last: "and I do so like that curious song about the whiting!"

sentences.text: "Thank you, it's a very interesting dance to watch," said Alice, feeling very glad that it was over at last: "and I do so like that curious song about the whiting!"
sentences.zh: “谢谢你，这支舞看着很有意思。”爱丽丝说，心里很高兴它总算跳完了，“我真的很喜欢那支关于牙鳕的怪歌！”

paragraphs.text: "Oh, as to the whiting," said the Mock Turtle, "they—you've seen them, of course?"

sentences.text: "Oh, as to the whiting," said the Mock Turtle, "they—you've seen them, of course?"
sentences.zh: “哦，说到牙鳕，”假海龟说，“它们——你当然见过它们吧？”

paragraphs.text: "Yes," said Alice, "I've often seen them at dinn—" she checked herself hastily.

sentences.text: "Yes," said Alice, "I've often seen them at dinn—" she checked herself hastily.
sentences.zh: “见过，”爱丽丝说，“我常常见它们摆在餐——”她急忙收住了嘴。

paragraphs.text: "I don't know where Dinn may be," said the Mock Turtle, "but if you've seen them so often, of course you know what they're like."

sentences.text: "I don't know where Dinn may be," said the Mock Turtle, "but if you've seen them so often, of course you know what they're like."
sentences.zh: “我不知道‘餐’在什么地方，”假海龟说，“可你要是常常见到它们，当然知道它们长什么样。”

hints.zh: 爱丽丝本要说 at dinner（在餐桌上），刚说半个词就停住；假海龟却把“Dinn”当成一个地名。
hints.en: Alice was about to say 'at dinner' and stopped halfway; the Mock Turtle takes 'Dinn' for the name of a place.

paragraphs.text: "I believe so," Alice replied thoughtfully. "They have their tails in their mouths;—and they're all over crumbs."

sentences.text: "I believe so," Alice replied thoughtfully.
sentences.zh: “我想是的。”爱丽丝若有所思地回答。

sentences.text: "They have their tails in their mouths;—and they're all over crumbs."
sentences.zh: “它们的尾巴衔在嘴里——而且浑身都是面包屑。”

introduction.zh: 歌里的蜗牛怎么也不肯往前走，爱丽丝很高兴这支舞总算跳完了。她说自己很喜欢那支关于牙鳕的歌，假海龟便问她见没见过牙鳕。她刚说出“在餐——”，就急忙住口。她差点说出什么？
introduction.en: The snail refuses to go further, and Alice is glad when the dance ends. She says she likes the song about the whiting, so the Mock Turtle asks if she has seen one. She starts to answer 'at dinn—' and stops. What was she about to say?

quiz.question: Why does the snail refuse to join the dance?
options: He thinks the sea is too far away.
He cannot swim.
He is afraid of the whiting.

feedback.zh: 蜗牛只回答“太远了，太远了”，说谢谢牙鳕的好意，可他不肯去。
feedback.en: The snail answers 'Too far, too far!' and politely declines the whiting's invitation.

quiz.question: What is Alice about to say when she checks herself?
options: That she has never seen a whiting.
That she once danced with a whiting.
That she has often seen whiting at dinner.

feedback.zh: 她说自己常常见到牙鳕“摆在餐——”，显然要说的是餐桌上，所以急忙改了口。
feedback.en: She says she has often seen whiting 'at dinn—', clearly meaning at dinner, and stops herself.

grammar.excerpt: The further off from England the nearer is to France

focus.zh: The further… the nearer… 是“越……就越……”；两个 the 后面都跟比较级，诗里语序有些颠倒。
focus.en: The further ... the nearer ... is the 'the more, the more' pattern: each the is followed by a comparative, with the word order turned round for the verse.

title.en: Why the Tail Is in the Mouth

paragraphs.text: "You're wrong about the crumbs," said the Mock Turtle: "crumbs would all wash off in the sea. But they have their tails in their mouths; and the reason is—" here the Mock Turtle yawned and shut his eyes.—"Tell her about the reason and all that," he said to the Gryphon.

sentences.text: "You're wrong about the crumbs," said the Mock Turtle: "crumbs would all wash off in the sea.
sentences.zh: “面包屑的事你说错了，”假海龟说，“面包屑在海里全会冲掉的。

sentences.text: But they have their tails in their mouths; and the reason is—" here the Mock Turtle yawned and shut his eyes.—"Tell her about the reason and all that," he said to the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: 可它们的尾巴确实衔在嘴里；原因是——”说到这里，假海龟打了个哈欠，闭上了眼睛。——“你把原因什么的讲给她听吧。”他对狮鹫说。

paragraphs.text: "The reason is," said the Gryphon, "that they would go with the lobsters to the dance. So they got thrown out to sea. So they had to fall a long way. So they got their tails fast in their mouths. So they couldn't get them out again. That's all."

sentences.text: "The reason is," said the Gryphon, "that they would go with the lobsters to the dance.
sentences.zh: “原因是，”狮鹫说，“它们要跟龙虾一起去跳舞。

sentences.text: So they got thrown out to sea.
sentences.zh: 于是它们被扔到了海里。

sentences.text: So they had to fall a long way.
sentences.zh: 于是它们得往下落好长一段。

sentences.text: So they got their tails fast in their mouths.
sentences.zh: 于是它们的尾巴就牢牢卡在嘴里了。

sentences.text: So they couldn't get them out again.
sentences.zh: 于是它们再也拔不出来了。

sentences.text: That's all."
sentences.zh: 就是这么回事。”

hints.zh: fast 这里不是“快”，而是“牢牢地、紧紧地”。
hints.en: Fast here does not mean quickly; it means firmly or tightly.

paragraphs.text: "Thank you," said Alice, "it's very interesting. I never knew so much about a whiting before."

sentences.text: "Thank you," said Alice, "it's very interesting.
sentences.zh: “谢谢你，”爱丽丝说，“真有意思。

sentences.text: I never knew so much about a whiting before."
sentences.zh: 我以前从没听说过这么多关于牙鳕的事。”

paragraphs.text: "I can tell you more than that, if you like,' said the Gryphon. "Do you know why it's called a whiting?"

sentences.text: "I can tell you more than that, if you like,' said the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: “你要是愿意，我还能多讲些。”狮鹫说。

sentences.text: "Do you know why it's called a whiting?"
sentences.zh: “你知道它为什么叫牙鳕吗？”

hints.zh: 这里的 whiting 是双关：既是鱼名“牙鳕”，也指把鞋刷白的白垩粉。
hints.en: Whiting is a pun here: it is both the fish and the white chalk powder used to whiten shoes.

paragraphs.text: "I never thought about it," said Alice. "Why?"

sentences.text: "I never thought about it," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “我从没想过这个。”爱丽丝说。

sentences.text: "Why?"
sentences.zh: “为什么？”

paragraphs.text: "It does the boots and shoes," the Gryphon replied very solemnly.

sentences.text: "It does the boots and shoes," the Gryphon replied very solemnly.
sentences.zh: “它负责刷靴子和鞋。”狮鹫非常严肃地回答。

paragraphs.text: Alice was thoroughly puzzled. "Does the boots and shoes!" she repeated in a wondering tone.

sentences.text: Alice was thoroughly puzzled.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝完全糊涂了。

sentences.text: "Does the boots and shoes!" she repeated in a wondering tone.
sentences.zh: “它刷靴子和鞋！”她用惊讶的口气重复了一遍。

paragraphs.text: "Why, what are your shoes done with?" said the Gryphon. "I mean, what makes them so shiny?"

sentences.text: "Why, what are your shoes done with?" said the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: “怎么，你的鞋是用什么刷的？”狮鹫说。

sentences.text: "I mean, what makes them so shiny?"
sentences.zh: “我是说，是什么让它们那么亮？”

paragraphs.text: Alice looked down at them, and considered a little before she gave her answer. "They're done with blacking, I believe."

sentences.text: Alice looked down at them, and considered a little before she gave her answer.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝低头看了看自己的鞋，想了一会儿才回答。

sentences.text: "They're done with blacking, I believe."
sentences.zh: “我想是用黑鞋油刷的吧。”

hints.zh: 黑鞋油，擦黑皮鞋用的那种。
hints.en: Blacking: the black polish used on leather boots and shoes.

paragraphs.text: "Boots and shoes under the sea," the Gryphon went on in a deep voice, "are done with whiting. Now you know."

sentences.text: "Boots and shoes under the sea," the Gryphon went on in a deep voice, "are done with whiting.
sentences.zh: “海底的靴子和鞋，”狮鹫用低沉的声音接着说，“是用牙鳕刷的。

sentences.text: Now you know."
sentences.zh: 现在你明白了。”

paragraphs.text: "And what are they made of?" Alice asked in a tone of great curiosity.

sentences.text: "And what are they made of?"
sentences.zh: “那它们是用什么做的？”

sentences.text: Alice asked in a tone of great curiosity.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝非常好奇地问。

paragraphs.text: "Soles and eels, of course," the Gryphon replied rather impatiently: "any shrimp could have told you that."

sentences.text: "Soles and eels, of course," the Gryphon replied rather impatiently: "any shrimp could have told you that."
sentences.zh: “当然是鞋底和鳗鱼，”狮鹫相当不耐烦地回答，“随便哪只虾都能告诉你。”

hints.zh: 双关：sole 既是“鞋底”也是一种鱼（鳎），eels（鳗鱼）又和 heels（鞋跟）同音。
hints.en: A pun: soles are the bottoms of shoes and also a kind of fish, and eels sounds like heels.

introduction.zh: 假海龟说面包屑在海里早冲掉了，狮鹫便一口气讲出牙鳕尾巴衔在嘴里的“原因”。接着他问爱丽丝，知不知道这种鱼为什么叫“牙鳕”。他的答案跟靴子和鞋有关——这两样怎么会扯到一起？
introduction.en: The Mock Turtle says crumbs would wash off in the sea, and the Gryphon explains those tails. He asks Alice why the fish is called a whiting, and the answer has to do with boots and shoes. What can shoes have to do with a fish?

quiz.question: What does the Gryphon say boots and shoes under the sea are cleaned with?
options: Sea water.
Blacking.
Whiting.

feedback.zh: 狮鹫说海底的靴子和鞋是用 whiting 刷的——这个词既是“牙鳕”，也指刷白的白垩粉。
feedback.en: The Gryphon says they are done with whiting, the word for both the fish and the white chalk used to clean shoes.

quiz.question: According to the Gryphon, what happened to the whiting after they were thrown into the sea?
options: They swam back to land.
Their tails stuck fast in their mouths.
They were caught by the lobsters.

feedback.zh: 狮鹫说它们落了好长一段，尾巴就牢牢卡进嘴里，再也拔不出来。
feedback.en: The Gryphon says they fell a long way, their tails stuck fast in their mouths and never came out.

grammar.excerpt: they would go with the lobsters to the dance

focus.zh: would go 里的 would 表示意愿，不是过去将来：它们当初存心要跟龙虾去跳舞。
focus.en: Would go here shows willingness, not future-in-the-past: the whiting were set on going to the dance with the lobsters.

paragraphs.text: "If I'd been the whiting," said Alice, whose thoughts were still running on the song, "I'd have said to the porpoise, 'Keep back, please: we don't want you with us!'"

sentences.text: "If I'd been the whiting," said Alice, whose thoughts were still running on the song, "I'd have said to the porpoise, 'Keep back, please: we don't want you with us!'"
sentences.zh: “要是我是那条牙鳕，”爱丽丝说，她的心思还在这支歌上，“我就会对海豚说：‘请退后一点：我们不想让你跟着我们！’”

paragraphs.text: "They were obliged to have him with them," the Mock Turtle said: "no wise fish would go anywhere without a porpoise."

sentences.text: "They were obliged to have him with them," the Mock Turtle said: "no wise fish would go anywhere without a porpoise."
sentences.zh: “它们不得不带上他，”假海龟说，“聪明的鱼出门，没有不带海豚的。”

hints.zh: be obliged to 意思是“不得不、只好”。
hints.en: To be obliged to do something means to have no choice but to do it.

paragraphs.text: "Wouldn't it really?" said Alice in a tone of great surprise.

sentences.text: "Wouldn't it really?" said Alice in a tone of great surprise.
sentences.zh: “真的非带不可吗？”爱丽丝非常惊讶地问。

paragraphs.text: "Of course not", said the Mock Turtle: "why, if a fish came to me, and told me he was going a journey, I should say, 'With what porpoise?'"

sentences.text: "Of course not", said the Mock Turtle: "why, if a fish came to me, and told me he was going a journey, I should say, 'With what porpoise?'"
sentences.zh: “当然不是，”假海龟说，“你想，要是有条鱼来找我，跟我说他要去旅行，我就会问：‘带着什么海豚去呢？’”

hints.zh: 假海龟把 porpoise（海豚）当成 purpose（目的）来用，故意这样问；下一句爱丽丝替他改正。
hints.en: The Mock Turtle uses porpoise as if it were purpose; Alice corrects the word in her next line.

paragraphs.text: "Don't you mean 'purpose?'" said Alice.

sentences.text: "Don't you mean 'purpose?'" said Alice.
sentences.zh: “你的意思是‘目的’吧？”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "I mean what I say," the Mock Turtle replied in an offended tone. And the Gryphon added, "Come, let's hear some of your adventures."

sentences.text: "I mean what I say," the Mock Turtle replied in an offended tone.
sentences.zh: “我说的是什么，就是什么。”假海龟不高兴地回答。

sentences.text: And the Gryphon added, "Come, let's hear some of your adventures."
sentences.zh: 狮鹫又补了一句：“来吧，讲讲你的一些奇遇。”

paragraphs.text: "I could tell you my adventures—beginning from this morning," said Alice a little timidly: "but it's no use going back to yesterday, because I was a different person then."

sentences.text: "I could tell you my adventures—beginning from this morning," said Alice a little timidly: "but it's no use going back to yesterday, because I was a different person then."
sentences.zh: “我可以讲讲我的奇遇——从今天早上讲起，”爱丽丝有点胆怯地说，“可从昨天讲起就没用了，因为那时候我是另一个人。”

paragraphs.text: "Explain all that," said the Mock Turtle.

sentences.text: "Explain all that," said the Mock Turtle.
sentences.zh: “你把这一切解释一下。”假海龟说。

paragraphs.text: "No, no! the adventures first," said the Gryphon in an impatient tone: "explanations take such a dreadful time."

sentences.text: "No, no! the adventures first," said the Gryphon in an impatient tone: "explanations take such a dreadful time."
sentences.zh: “不，不！先讲奇遇，”狮鹫不耐烦地说，“解释起来太费时间了。”

paragraphs.text: So Alice began telling them her adventures from the time when she first saw the White Rabbit: she was a little nervous about it just at first, the two creatures got so close to her, one on each side, and opened their eyes and mouths so very wide, but she gained courage as she went on. Her listeners were perfectly quiet till she got to the part about her repeating "You are old, Father William," to the Caterpillar, and the words all coming different, and then the Mock Turtle drew a long breath, and said, "That's very curious."

sentences.text: So Alice began telling them her adventures from the time when she first saw the White Rabbit: she was a little nervous about it just at first, the two creatures got so close to her, one on each side, and opened their eyes and mouths so very wide, but she gained courage as she went on.
sentences.zh: 于是爱丽丝从她第一次看见白兔的时候讲起，讲起她的种种奇遇：一开始她有点紧张，因为这两个家伙挨得那么近，一边一个，眼睛和嘴都张得大大的；不过她讲着讲着就壮起了胆子。

sentences.text: Her listeners were perfectly quiet till she got to the part about her repeating "You are old, Father William," to the Caterpillar, and the words all coming different, and then the Mock Turtle drew a long breath, and said, "That's very curious."
sentences.zh: 听她讲的人一直安安静静，直到她讲到她给毛毛虫背《你老了，威廉爸爸》，词儿全变了样；这时假海龟深深吸了口气，说：“那可真是奇怪。”

hints.zh: 白兔，揣着怀表、把爱丽丝引进奇境的那只兔子。
hints.en: The White Rabbit, the waistcoat-and-watch rabbit who first led Alice into Wonderland.

hints.zh: 毛毛虫，抽水烟、让爱丽丝背《你老了，威廉爸爸》的那条虫子。
hints.en: The Caterpillar, the hookah-smoking insect Alice recited 'You are old, Father William' to.

hints.zh: 《你老了，威廉爸爸》，书中一首戏仿的老诗，爱丽丝背给毛毛虫听过。
hints.en: 'You are old, Father William', a parody poem that Alice recites to the Caterpillar.

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝想，要是她是那条牙鳕，就会请海豚让开。假海龟却说，聪明的鱼出门总得带上一条海豚，还把“海豚”和“目的”混作一谈。话题转到她的奇遇，她却说没法从昨天讲起——那时她是另一个人。
introduction.en: Alice thinks what she would have said to the porpoise. The Mock Turtle insists that no wise fish travels without one, and mixes up porpoise with purpose. Then talk turns to her adventures, and she says she cannot begin from yesterday, when she was a different person.

quiz.question: What is the Mock Turtle doing with the word 'porpoise'?
options: He really wants to know which porpoise it is.
He is asking what the fish will eat on the journey.
He is making a joke on the word 'purpose'.

feedback.zh: 他把 porpoise（海豚）当成 purpose（目的）来用，故意问鱼带着什么“海豚”，爱丽丝只好提醒他说的是“目的”。
feedback.en: He treats porpoise as if it meant purpose, so Alice has to suggest that he means 'purpose'.

quiz.question: Why does Alice say she cannot begin her story from yesterday?
options: Yesterday was too dull to describe.
She cannot remember yesterday.
She was a different person then.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝说从昨天讲起没用，因为那时候她是另一个人。
feedback.en: Alice says it is no use going back to yesterday, because she was a different person then.

grammar.excerpt: If I'd been the whiting

focus.zh: If I'd been 是 if + had + 过去分词，假设与过去事实相反——她并不是牙鳕；主句用 I'd have said。
focus.en: If I'd been is if with had and a past participle, imagining the opposite of the past; the main clause takes would have said.

paragraphs.text: "It's all about as curious as it can be," said the Gryphon.

sentences.text: "It's all about as curious as it can be," said the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: “真是怪得不能再怪了。”狮鹫说。

paragraphs.text: "It all came different!" the Mock Turtle repeated thoughtfully. "I should like to hear her try and repeat something now. Tell her to begin." He looked at the Gryphon as if he thought it had some kind of authority over Alice.

sentences.text: "It all came different!" the Mock Turtle repeated thoughtfully.
sentences.zh: “全变了样！”假海龟若有所思地重复道。

sentences.text: "I should like to hear her try and repeat something now.
sentences.zh: “我现在倒想听她试着背点什么。

sentences.text: Tell her to begin."
sentences.zh: 叫她开始吧。”

sentences.text: He looked at the Gryphon as if he thought it had some kind of authority over Alice.
sentences.zh: 他看了看狮鹫，好像觉得狮鹫对爱丽丝有某种管束的权力。

paragraphs.text: "Stand up and repeat ''Tis the voice of the sluggard,'" said the Gryphon.

sentences.text: "Stand up and repeat ''Tis the voice of the sluggard,'" said the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: “站起来，背《懒汉之声》。”狮鹫说。

hints.zh: 懒汉、懒人；《懒汉之声》是爱丽丝要背的那首诗的题目。
hints.en: A sluggard is a lazy person; 'Tis the voice of the sluggard' is the poem Alice has to recite.

paragraphs.text: "How the creatures order one about, and make one repeat lessons!" thought Alice; "I might just as well be at school at once." However, she got up, and began to repeat it, but her head was so full of the Lobster Quadrille, that she hardly knew what she was saying, and the words came very queer indeed:—

sentences.text: "How the creatures order one about, and make one repeat lessons!" thought Alice; "I might just as well be at school at once."
sentences.zh: “这些家伙多会支使人，还叫人背课文！”爱丽丝心想，“我还不如马上回学校去。”

sentences.text: However, she got up, and began to repeat it, but her head was so full of the Lobster Quadrille, that she hardly knew what she was saying, and the words came very queer indeed:—
sentences.zh: 可她还是站了起来，开口背；只是她脑子里装满了龙虾四对舞，几乎不知道自己念的是什么，出来的词儿确实古怪得很：——

hints.zh: 支使人、对人呼来喝去。
hints.en: To order someone about is to keep telling them what to do.

paragraphs.text: "'Tis the voice of the lobster; I heard him declare, 'You have baked me too brown, I must sugar my hair.' As a duck with its eyelids, so he with his nose Trims his belt and his buttons, and turns out his toes."

sentences.text: "'Tis the voice of the lobster; I heard him declare, 'You have baked me too brown, I must sugar my hair.' As a duck with its eyelids, so he with his nose Trims his belt and his buttons, and turns out his toes."
sentences.zh: “‘这是龙虾的声音；我听见他宣告：‘你把我烤得太焦了，我得给头发加点糖。’就像鸭子用它的眼皮，他用鼻子理好腰带和纽扣，还把脚趾朝外撇。”

paragraphs.text: "That's different from what I used to say when I was a child," said the Gryphon.

sentences.text: "That's different from what I used to say when I was a child," said the Gryphon.
sentences.zh: “这跟我小时候念的不一样。”狮鹫说。

paragraphs.text: "Well, I never heard it before," said the Mock Turtle; "but it sounds uncommon nonsense."

sentences.text: "Well, I never heard it before," said the Mock Turtle; "but it sounds uncommon nonsense."
sentences.zh: “嗯，我以前从没听过，”假海龟说，“不过听起来是少有的胡说八道。”

hints.zh: uncommon 这里不是“不常见”，而是加强语气：“非同一般的、十足的”胡说八道。
hints.en: Uncommon here strengthens the noun: quite extraordinary nonsense, not merely unusual.

paragraphs.text: Alice said nothing: she had sat down again with her face in her hands, wondering if anything would ever happen in a natural way again.

sentences.text: Alice said nothing: she had sat down again with her face in her hands, wondering if anything would ever happen in a natural way again.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝什么也没说：她又坐了下来，双手捂着脸，心里想着，还会不会有哪件事按常理发生。

paragraphs.text: "I should like to have it explained," said the Mock Turtle.

sentences.text: "I should like to have it explained," said the Mock Turtle.
sentences.zh: “我倒希望有人解释一下。”假海龟说。

paragraphs.text: "She can't explain it," said the Gryphon hastily. "Go on with the next verse."

sentences.text: "She can't explain it," said the Gryphon hastily.
sentences.zh: “她解释不了。”狮鹫急忙说。

sentences.text: "Go on with the next verse."
sentences.zh: “接着背下一节。”

paragraphs.text: "But about his toes?" the Mock Turtle persisted. "How could he turn them out with his nose, you know?"

sentences.text: "But about his toes?" the Mock Turtle persisted.
sentences.zh: “可他的脚趾是怎么回事？”假海龟不肯放过。

sentences.text: "How could he turn them out with his nose, you know?"
sentences.zh: “你想，他怎么能用鼻子把脚趾朝外撇呢？”

introduction.zh: 两只动物让爱丽丝站起来，背一首她从小就会的诗。可她脑子里全是龙虾四对舞，一开口，词儿就变了样：龙虾抱怨自己被烤得太焦，还得给头发加糖。这样的诗，听众会怎么说？
introduction.en: The two creatures make Alice stand up and repeat a poem she has known since childhood. Her head is full of the Lobster Quadrille, so the words come out wrong: a lobster complains of being baked too brown and must sugar his hair. What will her listeners say?

quiz.question: Why do the words of the poem come out wrong?
options: She has never learned the poem.
Her head is full of the Lobster Quadrille.
The Gryphon tells her the wrong words.

feedback.zh: 她站起来背诗，可脑子里装满了龙虾四对舞，几乎不知道自己念的是什么。
feedback.en: She gets up to recite, but her head is so full of the Lobster Quadrille that she hardly knows what she is saying.

quiz.question: What does the Mock Turtle think of the poem?
options: It sounds like uncommon nonsense.
It is exactly what he used to say.
It is the best poem he has ever heard.

feedback.zh: 假海龟说自己从没听过这首诗，只觉得它是少有的胡说八道。
feedback.en: The Mock Turtle says he has never heard it before and that it sounds uncommon nonsense.

grammar.excerpt: I might just as well be at school at once

focus.zh: might just as well 意思是“倒不如、干脆……也一样”，爱丽丝觉得被支使背课文，跟在学校没两样。
focus.en: Might just as well means there is no real difference: being ordered to recite makes Alice feel she may as well be at school.

paragraphs.text: "It's the first position in dancing," Alice said; but she was dreadfully puzzled by the whole thing, and longed to change the subject.

introduction.en: Alice tries to explain the first position in dancing, but the Mock Turtle complains that she will not explain as she goes. The Gryphon lets her stop and offers a choice: another figure of the dance, or a song. She answers so eagerly that the Gryphon seems hurt.

quiz.question: What choice does the Gryphon offer Alice?

To go home or to stay with them.
Another figure of the dance or a song.

quiz.question: Why does the Gryphon sound rather offended?

Alice is far more eager for the Mock Turtle's song than for the dance.
Alice refuses to explain the poem.

introduction.en: The soup song is not over when the Gryphon calls for the chorus again. Then a shout comes from the distance, and the Gryphon seizes Alice's hand and runs, without waiting for the end. As she runs, Alice asks what trial it is.

quiz.question: What interrupts the song?
options: The Queen calling for Alice.
The Mock Turtle beginning to cry.
A cry that the trial is beginning.

feedback.zh: 假海龟刚要重唱，远处就传来一声喊：“审判开始了！”
feedback.en: The Mock Turtle is about to repeat the chorus when a cry of 'The trial's beginning!' comes from the distance.

quiz.question: What does the Gryphon do when he hears the cry?
options: He explains what the trial is about.
He waits for the last chorus.
He takes Alice's hand and hurries away.

focus.en: Had just begun is past perfect: the second singing had started only a moment before the shout came.

paragraphs.text: The King and Queen of Hearts were seated on their throne when they arrived, with a great crowd assembled about them—all sorts of little birds and beasts, as well as the whole pack of cards: the Knave was standing before them, in chains, with a soldier on each side to guard him; and near the King was the White Rabbit, with a trumpet in one hand, and a scroll of parchment in the other. In the very middle of the court was a table, with a large dish of tarts upon it: they looked so good, that it made Alice quite hungry to look at them—"I wish they'd get the trial done," she thought, "and hand round the refreshments!" But there seemed to be no chance of this, so she began looking at everything about her, to pass away the time.

sentences.text: The King and Queen of Hearts were seated on their throne when they arrived, with a great crowd assembled about them—all sorts of little birds and beasts, as well as the whole pack of cards: the Knave was standing before them, in chains, with a soldier on each side to guard him; and near the King was the White Rabbit, with a trumpet in one hand, and a scroll of parchment in the other.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝和狮鹫到时，红心国王和王后已经坐在宝座上了，四周聚着一大群人——各式各样的小鸟和野兽，还有整整一副纸牌：红心骑士站在他们面前，身上戴着镣铐，两边各有一名士兵看守；国王身边站着白兔，一手拿号角，一手拿一卷羊皮纸。

sentences.text: In the very middle of the court was a table, with a large dish of tarts upon it: they looked so good, that it made Alice quite hungry to look at them—"I wish they'd get the trial done," she thought, "and hand round the refreshments!"

sentences.zh: 可是看样子根本没这个可能，她只好东张西望，打发时间。

hints.en: The King and Queen of Hearts, who preside over the court.

hints.en: The White Rabbit, the pocket-watch rabbit, now standing beside the King.

hints.zh: 馅饼，一种果馅小圆饼；也是这场审判的焦点。
hints.en: Tarts, small fruit pies — the very things this trial is about.

paragraphs.text: Alice had never been in a court of justice before, but she had read about them in books, and she was quite pleased to find that she knew the name of nearly everything there. "That's the judge," she said to herself, "because of his great wig."

sentences.text: Alice had never been in a court of justice before, but she had read about them in books, and she was quite pleased to find that she knew the name of nearly everything there.

sentences.text: "That's the judge," she said to herself, "because of his great wig."

hints.en: The judge's great wig, the curled white wig worn in court.

sentences.text: The judge, by the way, was the King; and as he wore his crown over the wig, (look at the frontispiece if you want to see how he did it,) he did not look at all comfortable, and it was certainly not becoming.

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝跟着狮鹫走进一间大法庭：红心国王和王后高坐在宝座上，红心骑士戴着镣铐站在中间，四周挤满了鸟兽和纸牌。屋子正中摆着一大盘香喷喷的馅饼，她看着看着就饿了。这场审判到底要审出什么结果？
introduction.en: Alice and the Gryphon enter a great court, where the King and Queen of Hearts sit on their thrones and the Knave stands in chains. A dish of tarts in the middle of the room makes Alice hungry, and the court seems in no hurry to hand them round.

quiz.question: What does Alice wish the court would do?
options: Call the Queen to give evidence
Send the Knave away in chains
Finish the trial and hand round the refreshments

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝盯着那盘馅饼，心想“但愿他们快点审完，好把点心分给大家”，可见她最惦记的是吃。
feedback.en: Looking at the tarts, Alice thinks, "I wish they'd get the trial done and hand round the refreshments."

quiz.question: How does Alice recognise the judge?
options: By the scroll in his hand
By the great wig he is wearing
By the crown on his head

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝自言自语说“那是法官，因为他戴着那顶大假发”；王冠戴在假发外面，是她后来才注意到的。
feedback.en: Alice tells herself, "That's the judge, because of his great wig." The crown over the wig comes later.

focus.en: Had never been is past perfect: before she entered, she had never been in a court of justice.

paragraphs.text: "And that's the jury-box," thought Alice, "and those twelve creatures," (she was obliged to say "creatures," you see, because some of them were animals, and some were birds,) "I suppose they are the jurors." She said this last word two or three times over to herself, being rather proud of it: for she thought, and rightly too, that very few little girls of her age knew the meaning of it at all. However, "jurymen" would have done just as well.

sentences.text: "And that's the jury-box," thought Alice, "and those twelve creatures," (she was obliged to say "creatures," you see, because some of them were animals, and some were birds,) "I suppose they are the jurors."

sentences.text: She said this last word two or three times over to herself, being rather proud of it: for she thought, and rightly too, that very few little girls of her age knew the meaning of it at all.

paragraphs.text: Alice could see, as well as if she were looking over their shoulders, that all the jurors were writing down "stupid things!" on their slates, and she could even make out that one of them didn't know how to spell "stupid," and that he had to ask his neighbour to tell him. "A nice muddle their slates'll be in before the trial's over!" thought Alice.

sentences.text: Alice could see, as well as if she were looking over their shoulders, that all the jurors were writing down "stupid things!" on their slates, and she could even make out that one of them didn't know how to spell "stupid," and that he had to ask his neighbour to tell him.

sentences.text: "A nice muddle their slates'll be in before the trial's over!" thought Alice.
sentences.zh: “审判结束前，他们的石板准会乱成一团！”爱丽丝想。

introduction.zh: 十二只小动物和鸟坐在陪审席上，埋头在石板上写个不停。爱丽丝很得意自己知道“陪审员”这个词，却想不通：审判还没开始，他们有什么可记的？狮鹫凑过来，小声说出了原因。
introduction.en: Twelve small creatures sit in the jury-box, writing busily on their slates. Alice is proud that she knows the word "jurors", but she cannot think what they have to write down before the trial begins. The Gryphon leans over to explain.

quiz.question: Why are the jurors writing on their slates?
options: To put down their own names
To record what the witnesses say
To draw pictures of the court

feedback.zh: 狮鹫解释说，他们是在写自己的名字，怕审判结束前把名字忘了。
feedback.en: The Gryphon explains that they are writing down their names for fear they should forget them.

quiz.question: Why does Alice stop her angry outburst?
options: The Gryphon tells her to be quiet
She forgets what she was going to say
The White Rabbit calls for silence and the King looks round

feedback.zh: 白兔喊“法庭肃静！”，国王又戴上眼镜四处张望，爱丽丝只好把话咽了回去。
feedback.en: The White Rabbit cries "Silence in the court!" and the King looks anxiously round, so Alice stops herself.

grammar.excerpt: as well as if she were looking over their shoulders

focus.zh: as if 后用 were looking 表示假设：仿佛正从他们肩头看过去，其实并没有。
focus.en: After as if, were looking marks an imagined situation: she is not really looking over their shoulders.

paragraphs.text: One of the jurors had a pencil that squeaked. This, of course, Alice could not stand, and she went round the court and got behind him, and very soon found an opportunity of taking it away. She did it so quickly that the poor little juror (it was Bill, the Lizard) could not make out at all what had become of it; so, after hunting all about for it, he was obliged to write with one finger for the rest of the day; and this was of very little use, as it left no mark on the slate.

sentences.text: One of the jurors had a pencil that squeaked.
sentences.zh: 有一名陪审员有一支铅笔，写起来吱吱作响。

sentences.text: This, of course, Alice could not stand, and she went round the court and got behind him, and very soon found an opportunity of taking it away.
sentences.zh: 这声音爱丽丝当然受不了，她绕过法庭，走到他背后，很快就找到机会把铅笔拿走了。

sentences.text: She did it so quickly that the poor little juror (it was Bill, the Lizard) could not make out at all what had become of it; so, after hunting all about for it, he was obliged to write with one finger for the rest of the day; and this was of very little use, as it left no mark on the slate.
sentences.zh: 她动作太快，那可怜的小陪审员（就是那只壁虎比尔）根本弄不清铅笔到哪儿去了；他四处找了一阵，只好用一根手指写下去，写了一天也没什么用，因为石板上一点痕迹都没留下。

hints.zh: 比尔，那只壁虎，十二名陪审员之一。
hints.en: Bill the Lizard, one of the twelve jurors.

paragraphs.text: "Herald, read the accusation!" said the King.

sentences.text: "Herald, read the accusation!" said the King.
sentences.zh: “传令官，宣读控词！”国王说。

hints.zh: 传令官，法庭上负责宣读的人。
hints.en: The herald, the officer who reads things out in court.

hints.zh: 控词，对被告的正式指控。
hints.en: The accusation, the formal charge against the prisoner.

paragraphs.text: On this the White Rabbit blew three blasts on the trumpet, and then unrolled the parchment scroll, and read as follows:—

sentences.text: On this the White Rabbit blew three blasts on the trumpet, and then unrolled the parchment scroll, and read as follows:—
sentences.zh: 白兔听了，吹了三声号角，然后展开那卷羊皮纸，念道：——

paragraphs.text: "The Queen of Hearts, she made some tarts, All on a summer day: The Knave of Hearts, he stole those tarts, And took them, quite away!"

sentences.text: "The Queen of Hearts, she made some tarts, All on a summer day: The Knave of Hearts, he stole those tarts, And took them, quite away!"
sentences.zh: “红心王后做馅饼，／全在一个夏日里：／红心骑士偷馅饼，／一股脑儿全拿走！”

hints.zh: 红心骑士，控词里被点名的那个人。
hints.en: The Knave of Hearts, the man named in the charge.

paragraphs.text: "Consider your verdict," the King said to the jury.

sentences.text: "Consider your verdict," the King said to the jury.
sentences.zh: “考虑你们的裁决吧。”国王对陪审团说。

hints.zh: 裁决，陪审团对案件的正式结论。
hints.en: The verdict, the jury's formal decision on the case.

paragraphs.text: "Not yet, not yet!" the Rabbit hastily interrupted. "There's a great deal to come before that!"

sentences.text: "Not yet, not yet!" the Rabbit hastily interrupted.
sentences.zh: “还不行，还不行！”白兔急忙插嘴。

sentences.text: "There's a great deal to come before that!"
sentences.zh: “在那之前还有很多事要做呢！”

paragraphs.text: "Call the first witness," said the King; and the White Rabbit blew three blasts on the trumpet, and called out, "First witness!"

sentences.text: "Call the first witness," said the King; and the White Rabbit blew three blasts on the trumpet, and called out, "First witness!"
sentences.zh: “传第一个证人！”国王说；白兔又吹了三声号角，喊道：“第一个证人！”

paragraphs.text: The first witness was the Hatter. He came in with a teacup in one hand and a piece of bread-and-butter in the other. "I beg pardon, your Majesty," he began, "for bringing these in: but I hadn't quite finished my tea when I was sent for."

sentences.text: The first witness was the Hatter.
sentences.zh: 第一个证人是帽匠。

sentences.text: He came in with a teacup in one hand and a piece of bread-and-butter in the other.
sentences.zh: 他一手端着茶杯，一手拿着黄油面包走了进来。

sentences.text: "I beg pardon, your Majesty," he began, "for bringing these in: but I hadn't quite finished my tea when I was sent for."
sentences.zh: “请陛下恕罪，”他开口道，“恕我把这些东西带进来：可我被叫来的时候，茶还没喝完呢。”

hints.zh: 帽匠，也就是疯帽匠，茶会上的主人之一，这会儿成了证人。
hints.en: The Hatter, one of the tea-party hosts, now a witness.

paragraphs.text: "You ought to have finished," said the King. "When did you begin?"

sentences.text: "You ought to have finished," said the King.
sentences.zh: “你本该早就喝完的。”国王说。

sentences.text: "When did you begin?"
sentences.zh: “你是什么时候开始喝的？”

introduction.zh: 白兔宣读控词：红心骑士被控偷了馅饼。国王听完就想让陪审团立刻定案，白兔连忙拦住他，说还早得很。第一位证人被传上堂，他一手端着茶杯，一手拿着黄油面包。
introduction.en: The White Rabbit reads out the charge: the Knave of Hearts is accused of stealing tarts. The King wants a verdict at once, but the Rabbit stops him. Then the first witness is called, and he walks in holding a teacup and a piece of bread-and-butter.

quiz.question: What is the Knave of Hearts accused of?
options: Blowing the herald's trumpet
Stealing the Queen's tarts
Stealing the King's crown

feedback.zh: 白兔宣读的控词是一首押韵的小诗，说红心骑士偷了红心王后做的馅饼。
feedback.en: The charge, read out in rhyme, says the Knave of Hearts stole the tarts the Queen made.

quiz.question: Why does the White Rabbit interrupt the King?
options: Because a great deal must happen before a verdict
Because the jury has not arrived
Because the Hatter is still drinking tea

feedback.zh: 国王刚让陪审团考虑裁决，白兔就急忙说“还不行”，因为在那之前还有很多事要做。
feedback.en: The King asks for a verdict, but the Rabbit says a great deal must come before that.

grammar.excerpt: You ought to have finished

focus.zh: ought to have finished 是情态动词 + 完成式，指本该早就喝完，实际却没喝完。
focus.en: Ought to have finished is a modal with a perfect infinitive: he should have finished, but did not.

paragraphs.text: The Hatter looked at the March Hare, who had followed him into the court, arm-in-arm with the Dormouse. "Fourteenth of March, I think it was," he said.

sentences.text: The Hatter looked at the March Hare, who had followed him into the court, arm-in-arm with the Dormouse.
sentences.zh: 帽匠看了看三月兔——他跟着帽匠进了法庭，还和睡鼠挽着胳膊。

sentences.text: "Fourteenth of March, I think it was," he said.
sentences.zh: “我想是三月十四日吧。”他说。

hints.zh: 三月兔，茶会上的主人之一，跟着帽匠进了法庭。
hints.en: The March Hare, one of the tea-party hosts, who follows the Hatter into court.

hints.zh: 睡鼠，茶会上总打瞌睡的伙伴，和三月兔挽着胳膊。
hints.en: The Dormouse, the sleepy guest from the tea party, arm-in-arm with the March Hare.

paragraphs.text: "Fifteenth," said the March Hare.

sentences.text: "Fifteenth," said the March Hare.
sentences.zh: “十五日。”三月兔说。

paragraphs.text: "Sixteenth," added the Dormouse.

sentences.text: "Sixteenth," added the Dormouse.
sentences.zh: “十六日。”睡鼠补了一句。

paragraphs.text: "Write that down," the King said to the jury, and the jury eagerly wrote down all three dates on their slates, and then added them up, and reduced the answer to shillings and pence.

sentences.text: "Write that down," the King said to the jury, and the jury eagerly wrote down all three dates on their slates, and then added them up, and reduced the answer to shillings and pence.
sentences.zh: “记下来。”国王对陪审团说。陪审员们赶紧把三个日期都写在石板上，然后把它们加起来，再把得数换算成先令和便士。

hints.zh: 先令和便士，英国旧币制；把日期加起来再换算成钱，正是审判荒唐的地方。
hints.en: Shillings and pence, old British money; turning a sum of dates into money is part of the joke.

paragraphs.text: "Take off your hat," the King said to the Hatter.

sentences.text: "Take off your hat," the King said to the Hatter.
sentences.zh: “把你的帽子摘下来。”国王对帽匠说。

paragraphs.text: "It isn't mine," said the Hatter.

sentences.text: "It isn't mine," said the Hatter.
sentences.zh: “这帽子不是我的。”帽匠说。

paragraphs.text: "Stolen!" the King exclaimed, turning to the jury, who instantly made a memorandum of the fact.

sentences.text: "Stolen!" the King exclaimed, turning to the jury, who instantly made a memorandum of the fact.
sentences.zh: “偷来的！”国王大声说，转向陪审团，陪审员们立刻把这件事记了下来。

paragraphs.text: "I keep them to sell," the Hatter added as an explanation: "I've none of my own. I'm a hatter."

sentences.text: "I keep them to sell," the Hatter added as an explanation: "I've none of my own.
sentences.zh: “我留着这些帽子是要卖的，”帽匠解释说，“我自己一顶也没有。

sentences.text: I'm a hatter."
sentences.zh: 我是个帽匠。”

paragraphs.text: Here the Queen put on her spectacles, and began staring hard at the Hatter, who turned pale and fidgeted.

sentences.text: Here the Queen put on her spectacles, and began staring hard at the Hatter, who turned pale and fidgeted.
sentences.zh: 这时王后戴上眼镜，死死盯着帽匠；帽匠脸都白了，坐立不安。

paragraphs.text: "Give your evidence," said the King; "and don't be nervous, or I'll have you executed on the spot."

sentences.text: "Give your evidence," said the King; "and don't be nervous, or I'll have you executed on the spot."
sentences.zh: “说你的证词，”国王说，“别紧张，不然我当场把你处死。”

hints.zh: 当场、立刻。
hints.en: On the spot: at once, right there.

paragraphs.text: This did not seem to encourage the witness at all: he kept shifting from one foot to the other, looking uneasily at the Queen, and in his confusion he bit a large piece out of his teacup instead of the bread-and-butter.

sentences.text: This did not seem to encourage the witness at all: he kept shifting from one foot to the other, looking uneasily at the Queen, and in his confusion he bit a large piece out of his teacup instead of the bread-and-butter.
sentences.zh: 这话似乎一点也没让证人安心：他不停地换脚站着，不安地瞟着王后，慌乱之中竟在茶杯上咬了一大口，而不是去咬黄油面包。

paragraphs.text: Just at this moment Alice felt a very curious sensation, which puzzled her a good deal until she made out what it was: she was beginning to grow larger again, and she thought at first she would get up and leave the court; but on second thoughts she decided to remain where she was as long as there was room for her.

sentences.text: Just at this moment Alice felt a very curious sensation, which puzzled her a good deal until she made out what it was: she was beginning to grow larger again, and she thought at first she would get up and leave the court; but on second thoughts she decided to remain where she was as long as there was room for her.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，爱丽丝有一种很奇怪的感觉，她好一会儿都没弄明白是怎么回事：她又在开始变大了。起初她想站起来离开法庭，但转念一想，只要还坐得下，她就决定待在原地。

paragraphs.text: "I wish you wouldn't squeeze so," said the Dormouse, who was sitting next to her. "I can hardly breathe."

sentences.text: "I wish you wouldn't squeeze so," said the Dormouse, who was sitting next to her.
sentences.zh: “我希望你别挤得这么厉害。”坐在她旁边的睡鼠说。

sentences.text: "I can hardly breathe."
sentences.zh: “我几乎喘不过气了。”

introduction.zh: 国王问帽匠是什么时候开始喝茶的，三月兔和睡鼠却各报了一个不同的日子。陪审团郑重地把三个日期加起来，还把得数换算成先令和便士。接着，国王注意到了帽匠头上的帽子。
introduction.en: Asked when he began his tea, the Hatter gives a date, and the March Hare and the Dormouse each give another. The jury solemnly adds the three dates together and turns the sum into shillings and pence. Then the King turns his attention to the Hatter's hat.

quiz.question: What do the jurors do with the three dates?
options: They read them out to the Queen
They write them on the parchment scroll
They add them up and turn the answer into shillings and pence

feedback.zh: 陪审员们把三个日期都记下来，加起来，还把得数换算成先令和便士——这正显出审判的荒唐。
feedback.en: The jurors write down all three dates, add them up, and reduce the answer to shillings and pence.

quiz.question: What does Alice decide when she feels herself growing?
options: To ask the King to wait
To stay where she is as long as there is room
To leave the court at once

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝先是想起身离开，转念又想：只要还坐得下，就待在原地不动。
feedback.en: At first she thinks of leaving, but on second thoughts she stays as long as there is room for her.

grammar.excerpt: the March Hare, who had followed him into the court

focus.zh: 逗号后的 who had followed... 是非限制性定语从句，只是补充说明三月兔，不是在限定哪一个。
focus.en: The comma before who marks a non-defining relative clause: it adds a fact about the March Hare rather than identifying him.

paragraphs.text: "I can't help it," said Alice very meekly: "I'm growing."

sentences.text: "I can't help it," said Alice very meekly: "I'm growing."
sentences.zh: “我也没办法，”爱丽丝很温顺地说，“我在长个儿。”

paragraphs.text: "You've no right to grow here," said the Dormouse.

sentences.text: "You've no right to grow here," said the Dormouse.
sentences.zh: “你在这儿长个儿可没道理。”睡鼠说。

paragraphs.text: "Don't talk nonsense," said Alice more boldly: "you know you're growing too."

sentences.text: "Don't talk nonsense," said Alice more boldly: "you know you're growing too."
sentences.zh: “别说傻话，”爱丽丝更大胆了些，“你自己也在长呀。”

paragraphs.text: "Yes, but I grow at a reasonable pace," said the Dormouse: "not in that ridiculous fashion." And he got up very sulkily and crossed over to the other side of the court.

sentences.text: "Yes, but I grow at a reasonable pace," said the Dormouse: "not in that ridiculous fashion."
sentences.zh: “没错，可我长起来是有分寸的，”睡鼠说，“不像你那样，荒唐得要命。”

sentences.text: And he got up very sulkily and crossed over to the other side of the court.
sentences.zh: 他气鼓鼓地站起来，走到法庭的另一边去了。

hints.zh: 以合理的速度，不快不慢。
hints.en: At a reasonable pace: at a sensible speed.

paragraphs.text: All this time the Queen had never left off staring at the Hatter, and, just as the Dormouse crossed the court, she said to one of the officers of the court, "Bring me the list of the singers in the last concert!" on which the wretched Hatter trembled so, that he shook both his shoes off.

sentences.text: All this time the Queen had never left off staring at the Hatter, and, just as the Dormouse crossed the court, she said to one of the officers of the court, "Bring me the list of the singers in the last concert!" on which the wretched Hatter trembled so, that he shook both his shoes off.
sentences.zh: 这期间，王后一直没停止盯着帽匠；就在睡鼠穿过法庭的时候，她对一名法庭官员说：“把上次音乐会的歌手名单给我拿来！”那可怜的帽匠听了浑身发抖，把两只鞋都抖掉了。

hints.zh: 上次音乐会的歌手名单；王后突然要这个，把帽匠吓坏了。
hints.en: The list of the singers in the last concert, which the Queen suddenly demands.

paragraphs.text: "Give your evidence," the King repeated angrily, "or I'll have you executed, whether you're nervous or not."

sentences.text: "Give your evidence," the King repeated angrily, "or I'll have you executed, whether you're nervous or not."
