sentences.zh: “说你的证词，”国王生气地重复道，“不然我就把你处死，管你紧不紧张。”

hints.zh: 证词，证人在法庭上说的话。
hints.en: Evidence: what a witness says in court.

paragraphs.text: "I'm a poor man, your Majesty," the Hatter began in a trembling voice, "and I hadn't begun my tea—not above a week or so—and what with the bread-and-butter getting so thin—and the twinkling of the tea——"

sentences.text: "I'm a poor man, your Majesty," the Hatter began in a trembling voice, "and I hadn't begun my tea—not above a week or so—and what with the bread-and-butter getting so thin—and the twinkling of the tea——"
sentences.zh: “我是个穷人，陛下，”帽匠用发抖的声音开口，“我还没开始喝我的茶——不过一星期左右以前——再说黄油面包越来越薄——还有那茶的闪闪烁烁——”

hints.zh: 闪烁、忽明忽暗；帽匠用它形容茶，国王却听成了字母。
hints.en: Twinkling: a flickering light; the Hatter uses it of tea, and the King hears a letter instead.

paragraphs.text: "The twinkling of what?" said the King.

sentences.text: "The twinkling of what?" said the King.
sentences.zh: “什么的闪闪烁烁？”国王问。

paragraphs.text: "It began with the tea," the Hatter replied.

sentences.text: "It began with the tea," the Hatter replied.
sentences.zh: “是从茶开始的。”帽匠回答。

paragraphs.text: "Of course twinkling begins with a T!" said the King sharply. "Do you take me for a dunce? Go on!"

sentences.text: "Of course twinkling begins with a T!" said the King sharply.
sentences.zh: “闪烁当然是从字母 T 开头！”国王尖刻地说。

sentences.text: "Do you take me for a dunce?
sentences.zh: “你当我是个笨蛋吗？

sentences.text: Go on!"
sentences.zh: 接着说！”

paragraphs.text: "I'm a poor man," the Hatter went on, "and most things twinkled after that—only the March Hare said——"

sentences.text: "I'm a poor man," the Hatter went on, "and most things twinkled after that—only the March Hare said——"
sentences.zh: “我是个穷人，”帽匠继续说，“从那以后，大多数东西都闪闪烁烁——只有三月兔说——”

paragraphs.text: "I didn't!" the March Hare interrupted in a great hurry.

sentences.text: "I didn't!" the March Hare interrupted in a great hurry.
sentences.zh: “我没有！”三月兔急忙打断他。

paragraphs.text: "You did!" said the Hatter.

sentences.text: "You did!" said the Hatter.
sentences.zh: “你有！”帽匠说。

paragraphs.text: "I deny it!" said the March Hare.

sentences.text: "I deny it!" said the March Hare.
sentences.zh: “我否认！”三月兔说。

paragraphs.text: "He denies it," said the King: "leave out that part."

sentences.text: "He denies it," said the King: "leave out that part."
sentences.zh: “他否认了，”国王说，“把那一段删掉。”

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝说自己忍不住在长高，睡鼠气呼呼地挪到了法庭另一边。王后一直盯着帽匠，还叫人去取上次音乐会的歌手名单，帽匠吓得把两只鞋都抖掉了。国王催他作证，他却说起一杯会“闪烁”的茶。
introduction.en: Alice says she cannot help growing, and the Dormouse moves away in a huff. The Queen keeps staring at the Hatter and calls for a list of singers, which frightens him badly. When the King demands his evidence, the Hatter begins to talk about tea that twinkles.

quiz.question: What does the Dormouse do after arguing with Alice?
options: He crosses to the other side of the court
He falls asleep on the spot
He calls for the Queen's officers

feedback.zh: 睡鼠说自己长个儿“有分寸”，然后气鼓鼓地起身，走到法庭另一边去了。
feedback.en: After saying he grows at a reasonable pace, the Dormouse gets up sulkily and crosses the court.

quiz.question: What does the King think "twinkling" means?
options: That it is a kind of singing
That it has something to do with teacups
That it must begin with the letter T

feedback.zh: 帽匠说“茶的闪烁”，国王却听成了拼写问题，说“闪烁当然从字母 T 开始”，还问帽匠是不是把他当笨蛋。
feedback.en: The King takes "twinkling" as a spelling matter: "Of course twinkling begins with a T!"

grammar.excerpt: the wretched Hatter trembled so, that he shook both his shoes off

focus.zh: trembled so, that... 是 so + 副词 + that 从句，说明抖到什么程度：连鞋都抖掉了。
focus.en: Trembled so, that... is so + adverb + that-clause, showing the result: he shook off both his shoes.

title.en: A Cheer in a Canvas Bag

paragraphs.text: "Well, at any rate, the Dormouse said—" the Hatter went on, looking anxiously round to see if he would deny it too: but the Dormouse denied nothing, being fast asleep.

sentences.text: "Well, at any rate, the Dormouse said—" the Hatter went on, looking anxiously round to see if he would deny it too: but the Dormouse denied nothing, being fast asleep.
sentences.zh: “好吧，不管怎么说，睡鼠说过——”帽匠接着说，一边不安地四下张望，看睡鼠会不会也否认；可睡鼠什么也没否认，他睡得正香。

paragraphs.text: "After that," continued the Hatter, "I cut some more bread-and-butter——"

sentences.text: "After that," continued the Hatter, "I cut some more bread-and-butter——"
sentences.zh: “那以后，”帽匠接着说，“我又切了些黄油面包——”

paragraphs.text: "But what did the Dormouse say?" one of the jury asked.

sentences.text: "But what did the Dormouse say?" one of the jury asked.
sentences.zh: “可睡鼠到底说了什么？”陪审团里有人问。

paragraphs.text: "That I can't remember," said the Hatter.

sentences.text: "That I can't remember," said the Hatter.
sentences.zh: “这我可记不得了。”帽匠说。

paragraphs.text: "You must remember," remarked the King, "or I'll have you executed."

sentences.text: "You must remember," remarked the King, "or I'll have you executed."
sentences.zh: “你必须记得，”国王说，“不然我就把你处死。”

paragraphs.text: The miserable Hatter dropped his teacup and bread-and-butter, and went down on one knee. "I'm a poor man, your Majesty," he began.

sentences.text: The miserable Hatter dropped his teacup and bread-and-butter, and went down on one knee.
sentences.zh: 可怜的帽匠丢下茶杯和黄油面包，单膝跪了下来。

sentences.text: "I'm a poor man, your Majesty," he began.
sentences.zh: “我是个穷人，陛下。”他开口道。

paragraphs.text: "You're a very poor speaker," said the King.

sentences.text: "You're a very poor speaker," said the King.
sentences.zh: “你是个穷人，口才也真够差的。”国王说。

paragraphs.text: Here one of the guinea-pigs cheered, and was immediately suppressed by the officers of the court. (As that is rather a hard word, I will just explain to you how it was done. They had a large canvas bag, which tied up at the mouth with strings: into this they slipped the guinea-pig, head first, and then sat upon it.)

sentences.text: Here one of the guinea-pigs cheered, and was immediately suppressed by the officers of the court. (As that is rather a hard word, I will just explain to you how it was done.
sentences.zh: 这时，一只豚鼠喝起彩来，立刻被法庭官员“镇压”了。（这个词有点难，我就说说他们是怎么做的。

sentences.text: They had a large canvas bag, which tied up at the mouth with strings: into this they slipped the guinea-pig, head first, and then sat upon it.)
sentences.zh: 他们有一个大帆布袋，袋口用绳子扎紧：他们把豚鼠头朝下塞进去，然后一屁股坐在上面。）

hints.zh: 镇压、制止；这里指把喝彩的豚鼠塞进袋子。
hints.en: Suppressed: put down or stopped; here, the guinea-pig is bundled into a bag.

hints.zh: 帆布袋，用厚帆布做的袋子。
hints.en: A canvas bag, a strong bag made of canvas.

paragraphs.text: "I'm glad I've seen that done," thought Alice. "I've so often read in the newspapers, at the end of trials, 'There was some attempt at applause, which was immediately suppressed by the officers of the court,' and I never understood what it meant till now."

sentences.text: "I'm glad I've seen that done," thought Alice.
sentences.zh: “很高兴我亲眼见过这回事。”爱丽丝想。

sentences.text: "I've so often read in the newspapers, at the end of trials, 'There was some attempt at applause, which was immediately suppressed by the officers of the court,' and I never understood what it meant till now."
sentences.zh: “我常在报纸上读到，审判结束时写着：‘有人试图鼓掌，但立刻被法庭官员制止了。’直到现在我才明白那是什么意思。”

paragraphs.text: "If that's all you know about it, you may stand down," continued the King.

sentences.text: "If that's all you know about it, you may stand down," continued the King.
sentences.zh: “如果你知道的就这些，你可以退下了。”国王接着说。

hints.zh: 退下（证人席）；帽匠却听成“往下站”。
hints.en: Stand down: leave the witness-box; the Hatter takes it literally.

paragraphs.text: "I can't go no lower," said the Hatter: "I'm on the floor, as it is."

sentences.text: "I can't go no lower," said the Hatter: "I'm on the floor, as it is."
sentences.zh: “我没法再往下低了，”帽匠说，“我已经在地上跪着了。”

hints.zh: 本来就、已经。
hints.en: As it is: already, as things stand.

paragraphs.text: "Then you may sit down," the King replied.

sentences.text: "Then you may sit down," the King replied.
sentences.zh: “那你就坐下吧。”国王回答。

paragraphs.text: Here the other guinea-pig cheered, and was suppressed.

sentences.text: Here the other guinea-pig cheered, and was suppressed.
sentences.zh: 这时，另一只豚鼠也喝起彩来，同样被镇压了。

paragraphs.text: "Come, that finishes the guinea-pigs!" thought Alice. "Now we shall get on better."

sentences.text: "Come, that finishes the guinea-pigs!" thought Alice.
sentences.zh: “好啦，豚鼠总算都解决完了！”爱丽丝想。

sentences.text: "Now we shall get on better."
sentences.zh: “这下我们该顺利些了。”

introduction.zh: 帽匠怎么也想不起睡鼠说过什么，国王又拿处死来吓他。一只豚鼠喝起彩来，立刻被官员们“镇压”——做法让人哭笑不得。爱丽丝忽然明白，报纸上常写的那句话究竟指什么。
introduction.en: The Hatter cannot remember what the Dormouse said, and the King threatens him again. A guinea-pig cheers and is at once "suppressed", in a way Alice finds hard to believe. At last she understands a phrase she has often read in newspaper reports.

quiz.question: How is the cheering guinea-pig suppressed?
options: It is made to stand down from the witness-box
It is put head first into a canvas bag and sat upon
It is carried out by two soldiers

feedback.zh: 官员们拿来一个大帆布袋，把豚鼠头朝下塞进去，然后坐在袋子上。
feedback.en: The officers slip the guinea-pig head first into a canvas bag tied with strings, then sit upon it.

quiz.question: Why does the Hatter say he cannot go any lower?
options: Because he is already on the floor
Because his shoes have come off
Because the King has forbidden it

feedback.zh: 国王让他退下，帽匠却把 stand down 听成“往下站”，说自己已经跪在地上，没法再低了。
feedback.en: The Hatter takes "stand down" literally: he is already on the floor, so he cannot go any lower.

grammar.excerpt: I've seen that done

focus.zh: seen that done 是感官动词 + 宾语 + 过去分词：that 指那件事，done 表示它被人做过。
focus.en: Seen that done is see + object + past participle: that is the thing, and done says it was carried out.

paragraphs.text: "I'd rather finish my tea," said the Hatter, with an anxious look at the Queen, who was reading the list of singers.

sentences.text: "I'd rather finish my tea," said the Hatter, with an anxious look at the Queen, who was reading the list of singers.
sentences.zh: “我宁愿先把茶喝完。”帽匠说，不安地看了王后一眼，她正在看歌手名单。

paragraphs.text: "You may go," said the King, and the Hatter hurriedly left the court, without even waiting to put his shoes on.

sentences.text: "You may go," said the King, and the Hatter hurriedly left the court, without even waiting to put his shoes on.
sentences.zh: “你可以走了。”国王说。帽匠急忙离开法庭，连鞋都来不及穿。

paragraphs.text: "——and just take his head off outside," the Queen added to one of the officers; but the Hatter was out of sight before the officer could get to the door.

sentences.text: "——and just take his head off outside," the Queen added to one of the officers; but the Hatter was out of sight before the officer could get to the door.
sentences.zh: “——顺便在外面把他的头取下来。”王后对一名官员补了一句；可那名官员还没走到门口，帽匠已经不见了踪影。

paragraphs.text: "Call the next witness!" said the King.

sentences.text: "Call the next witness!" said the King.
sentences.zh: “传下一个证人！”国王说。

paragraphs.text: The next witness was the Duchess's cook. She carried the pepper-box in her hand, and Alice guessed who it was, even before she got into the court, by the way the people near the door began sneezing all at once.

sentences.text: The next witness was the Duchess's cook.
sentences.zh: 下一个证人是公爵夫人的厨娘。

sentences.text: She carried the pepper-box in her hand, and Alice guessed who it was, even before she got into the court, by the way the people near the door began sneezing all at once.
sentences.zh: 她手里端着胡椒罐；还没等她走进法庭，爱丽丝就凭门口那些人突然一齐打起喷嚏猜出了她是谁。

hints.zh: 公爵夫人，厨娘的东家。
hints.en: The Duchess, the cook's mistress.

hints.zh: 胡椒罐，一打开就让人打喷嚏。
hints.en: A pepper-box: open it and everyone starts sneezing.

paragraphs.text: "Give your evidence," said the King.

sentences.text: "Give your evidence," said the King.
sentences.zh: “说你的证词。”国王说。

paragraphs.text: "Shan't," said the cook.

sentences.text: "Shan't," said the cook.
sentences.zh: “才不呢。”厨娘说。

hints.zh: shan't 是 shall not 的缩写，这里表示“我才不呢”。
hints.en: Shan't is short for shall not: here it means "I won't".

paragraphs.text: The King looked anxiously at the White Rabbit, who said in a low voice. "Your Majesty must cross-examine this witness."

sentences.text: The King looked anxiously at the White Rabbit, who said in a low voice.
sentences.zh: 国王不安地望向白兔，白兔压低了声音。

sentences.text: "Your Majesty must cross-examine this witness."
sentences.zh: “陛下必须盘问这个证人。”

hints.zh: 盘问，向证人追问细节。
hints.en: Cross-examine: to question a witness closely.

paragraphs.text: "Well, if I must, I must," the King said with a melancholy air, and, after folding his arms and frowning at the cook till his eyes were nearly out of sight, he said in a deep voice, "What are tarts made of?"

sentences.text: "Well, if I must, I must," the King said with a melancholy air, and, after folding his arms and frowning at the cook till his eyes were nearly out of sight, he said in a deep voice, "What are tarts made of?"
sentences.zh: “好吧，既然非问不可，那就问吧。”国王神情忧郁地说。他抱起双臂，皱着眉盯着厨娘，盯得眼睛都快看不见了，然后用低沉的声音说：“馅饼是用什么做的？”

paragraphs.text: "Pepper, mostly," said the cook.

sentences.text: "Pepper, mostly," said the cook.
sentences.zh: “主要是胡椒。”厨娘说。

paragraphs.text: "Treacle," said a sleepy voice behind her.

sentences.text: "Treacle," said a sleepy voice behind her.
sentences.zh: “糖浆。”她身后传来一个睡意朦胧的声音。

hints.zh: 糖浆，英国常见的一种深色甜浆。
hints.en: Treacle: a thick dark syrup.

paragraphs.text: "Collar that Dormouse!" the Queen shrieked out. "Behead that Dormouse! Turn that Dormouse out of court! Suppress him! Pinch him! Off with his whiskers!"

sentences.text: "Collar that Dormouse!" the Queen shrieked out.
sentences.zh: “抓住那只睡鼠！”王后尖叫道。

sentences.text: "Behead that Dormouse!
sentences.zh: “砍掉那只睡鼠的脑袋！

sentences.text: Turn that Dormouse out of court!
sentences.zh: 把那只睡鼠赶出法庭！

sentences.text: Suppress him!
sentences.zh: 镇压他！

sentences.text: Pinch him!
sentences.zh: 掐他！

sentences.text: Off with his whiskers!"
sentences.zh: 剃掉他的胡子！”

hints.zh: collar 在这里是“抓住”，不是“衣领”。
hints.en: Collar here means "seize", not a shirt collar.

paragraphs.text: For some minutes the whole court was in confusion, getting the Dormouse turned out, and, by the time they had settled down again, the cook had disappeared.

sentences.text: For some minutes the whole court was in confusion, getting the Dormouse turned out, and, by the time they had settled down again, the cook had disappeared.
sentences.zh: 法庭乱了好几分钟，忙着把睡鼠赶出去；等大家重新安顿下来，厨娘已经不见了。

introduction.zh: 帽匠只想回去把那杯茶喝完。王后翻着歌手名单，似乎另有打算。下一位证人是公爵夫人的厨娘，她端着胡椒罐上堂，门口的人立刻喷嚏连天。国王要问她的，只是馅饼里放了什么。
introduction.en: The Hatter would rather finish his tea, while the Queen reads her list of singers and seems to have other plans. The next witness is the Duchess's cook, whose pepper-box sets everyone near the door sneezing. The King has only one question for her: what are tarts made of?

quiz.question: How does Alice guess who the next witness is before seeing her?
options: The King announces the cook's name
She sees a pepper-box through the door
People near the door begin sneezing all at once

feedback.zh: 厨娘还没进法庭，门口的人就一齐打起喷嚏，爱丽丝因此猜到了她是谁。
feedback.en: Before the cook enters, everyone near the door starts sneezing, and Alice guesses who it is.

quiz.question: Why does the King agree to question the cook himself?
options: Because the cook asks him a question
Because the White Rabbit says he must cross-examine her
Because the Queen orders him to do it

feedback.zh: 厨娘只说“才不呢”，国王不知所措，白兔低声提醒他必须盘问这个证人，他只好照办。
feedback.en: The cook refuses to speak, and the White Rabbit tells the King that he must cross-examine this witness.

grammar.excerpt: I'd rather finish my tea

focus.zh: I'd rather 是 would rather + 动词原形，表示“宁愿”，后面不接 to。
focus.en: I'd rather is would rather + bare infinitive: it means he would prefer to finish his tea.

title.en: The Next Name on the List

paragraphs.text: "Never mind!" said the King, with an air of great relief. "Call the next witness." And, he added in an under-tone to the Queen, "Really, my dear, you must cross-examine the next witness. It quite makes my forehead ache!"

sentences.text: "Never mind!" said the King, with an air of great relief.
sentences.zh: “没关系！”国王说，显得大大松了口气。

sentences.text: "Call the next witness."
sentences.zh: “传下一个证人。”

sentences.text: And, he added in an under-tone to the Queen, "Really, my dear, you must cross-examine the next witness.
sentences.zh: 接着，他压低声音对王后补了一句：“真的，亲爱的，下一个证人得由你来盘问。

sentences.text: It quite makes my forehead ache!"
sentences.zh: 这问得我脑门都疼了！”

hints.zh: 压低声音、小声地。
hints.en: In an under-tone: in a quiet voice.

paragraphs.text: Alice watched the White Rabbit as he fumbled over the list, feeling very curious to see what the next witness would be like, "—for they haven't got much evidence yet," she said to herself. Imagine her surprise, when the White Rabbit read out, at the top of his shrill little voice, the name "Alice!"

sentences.text: Alice watched the White Rabbit as he fumbled over the list, feeling very curious to see what the next witness would be like, "—for they haven't got much evidence yet," she said to herself.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝看着白兔在名单上翻找，很想知道下一个证人会是什么样子，“——毕竟他们还没问出多少证词呢，”她自言自语。

sentences.text: Imagine her surprise, when the White Rabbit read out, at the top of his shrill little voice, the name "Alice!"
sentences.zh: 想想看，当白兔用又尖又细的嗓子高声念出“爱丽丝！”这个名字时，她有多惊讶。

hints.zh: 手忙脚乱地翻找。
hints.en: Fumbled over: handled awkwardly while searching.

introduction.zh: 厨娘不见了，国王反倒松了口气，还悄悄请王后亲自盘问下一位证人，说这差事让他脑门发疼。爱丽丝盯着白兔在名单上翻找，很想知道下一个上场的会是谁——到现在，他们还没问出多少证词。
introduction.en: With the cook gone, the King feels relieved and asks the Queen to question the next witness herself, saying it makes his forehead ache. Alice watches the White Rabbit fumble over the list, eager to see who will come next.

quiz.question: Why does the King want the Queen to question the next witness?
options: Because it makes his forehead ache
Because he has to leave the court
Because the Rabbit is too busy

feedback.zh: 国王悄悄对王后说，盘问证人“问得我脑门都疼了”，所以下一个证人得由她来问。
feedback.en: The King whispers to the Queen that cross-examining quite makes his forehead ache.

quiz.question: What is Alice curious about?
options: Whether the cook will come back
What the tarts are made of
What the next witness will be like

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝看着白兔在名单上翻找，很想知道下一个证人会是什么样子。
feedback.en: Alice watches the Rabbit fumble over the list, curious to see what the next witness will be like.

grammar.excerpt: Alice watched the White Rabbit as he fumbled over the list

focus.zh: as 引导时间状语从句，表示“当……的时候”，与主句 watched 同时发生。
focus.en: As introduces a time clause: the Rabbit's fumbling and Alice's watching happen at the same moment.

paragraphs.text: "Here!" cried Alice, quite forgetting in the flurry of the moment how large she had grown in the last few minutes, and she jumped up in such a hurry that she tipped over the jury-box with the edge of her skirt, upsetting all the jurymen on to the heads of the crowd below, and there they lay sprawling about, reminding her very much of a globe of gold-fish she had accidentally upset the week before.

sentences.text: "Here!" cried Alice, quite forgetting in the flurry of the moment how large she had grown in the last few minutes, and she jumped up in such a hurry that she tipped over the jury-box with the edge of her skirt, upsetting all the jurymen on to the heads of the crowd below, and there they lay sprawling about, reminding her very much of a globe of gold-fish she had accidentally upset the week before.
sentences.zh: “到！”爱丽丝喊道，一时慌乱，完全忘了自己在刚才那几分钟里已经长得多大；她匆匆跳起来，裙边把陪审团席撞翻了，陪审员们全摔到下面人群的头上，摊手摊脚地躺了一地，让她想起上星期自己不小心打翻的那缸金鱼。

hints.zh: 爱丽丝，本书主角，在奇境里经历这一切的小姑娘。
hints.en: Alice, the girl who has lived through all these strange things in Wonderland.

hints.zh: 陪审团席，法庭上陪审员坐的一排座位，围着矮栏。
hints.en: The jury-box, the railed seats where the jury sit in a court.

hints.zh: 金鱼缸，旧时那种圆球形的玻璃缸。
hints.en: A globe of gold-fish, an old round glass fish-bowl.

paragraphs.text: "Oh, I beg your pardon!" she exclaimed in a tone of great dismay, and began picking them up again as quickly as she could, for the accident of the gold-fish kept running in her head, and she had a vague sort of idea that they must be collected at once and put back into the jury-box, or they would die.

sentences.text: "Oh, I beg your pardon!" she exclaimed in a tone of great dismay, and began picking them up again as quickly as she could, for the accident of the gold-fish kept running in her head, and she had a vague sort of idea that they must be collected at once and put back into the jury-box, or they would die.
sentences.zh: “哦，我求您原谅！”她非常沮丧地叫了一声，又赶紧把陪审员们捡起来，因为金鱼缸的事老在她脑子里转，她隐约觉得必须马上把它们收齐，放回陪审席，否则它们会死的。

paragraphs.text: "The trial cannot proceed," said the King in a very grave voice, "until all the jurymen are back in their proper places—all," he repeated with great emphasis, looking hard at Alice as he said so.

sentences.text: "The trial cannot proceed," said the King in a very grave voice, "until all the jurymen are back in their proper places—all," he repeated with great emphasis, looking hard at Alice as he said so.
sentences.zh: “审判不能继续，”国王用非常严肃的声音说，“除非所有陪审员都回到各自的位置上——所有，”他加重语气重复了一遍，说这话时紧紧盯着爱丽丝。

paragraphs.text: Alice looked at the jury-box, and saw that, in her haste, she had put the Lizard in head downwards, and the poor little thing was waving its tail about in a melancholy way, being quite unable to move. She soon got it out again, and put it right; "not that it signifies much," she said to herself; "I should think it would be quite as much use in the trial one way up as the other."

sentences.text: Alice looked at the jury-box, and saw that, in her haste, she had put the Lizard in head downwards, and the poor little thing was waving its tail about in a melancholy way, being quite unable to move.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝看了看陪审团席，发现自己在匆忙中把壁虎头朝下放了进去，这可怜的小东西正愁苦地摆着尾巴，一动也动不了。

sentences.text: She soon got it out again, and put it right; "not that it signifies much," she said to herself; "I should think it would be quite as much use in the trial one way up as the other."
sentences.zh: 她很快又把它取出来，摆正了；“不过这也没什么要紧，”她自言自语，“我倒觉得，审案的时候它正着放还是倒着放，用处都差不多。”

hints.zh: 壁虎，陪审员之一，就是先前被白兔派下烟囱的那只。
hints.en: The Lizard, one of the jurymen: the one the White Rabbit once sent down the chimney.

hints.zh: 在这里是“要紧、有影响”，不是“表示”。
hints.en: Here 'signify' means 'matter', not 'mean'.

introduction.zh: 听见喊自己的名字，爱丽丝忘了自己已经长得又高又大，猛地站起来答“到”。裙边一带，陪审团席就被掀翻了。这下该怎么收场？
introduction.en: The King calls for the witness. Alice jumps up to answer, but she has forgotten how big she has grown, and the edge of her skirt catches the jury-box. Down go the jurymen, and the trial stops. Can she put things right?

quiz.question: Why does the jury-box tip over?
options: Alice stands up too quickly to answer her name.
The King knocks it over as he enters the court.
The jurymen jump out to get a better look at Alice.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝听见喊自己的名字，忘了自己已经变得很大，急忙起身，裙边带翻了陪审团席。
feedback.en: Alice forgets how large she has grown and jumps up in a hurry, so the edge of her skirt tips the jury-box over.

quiz.question: What does Alice do with the Lizard?
options: She throws it out of the court.
She writes its name on a slate.
She puts it back in the box the wrong way up, then turns it right.

feedback.zh: 她匆忙间把壁虎头朝下塞进了陪审席，随后又把它取出来摆正。
feedback.en: In her haste she has put the Lizard in head downwards, and she soon takes it out and sets it right.

grammar.excerpt: quite forgetting in the flurry of the moment how large she had grown in the last few minutes

focus.zh: how large she had grown 是疑问词引导的从句，用陈述语序（she had grown），不是 had she grown。
focus.en: How large she had grown is an embedded question: the wh-word is followed by statement order, not by had she grown.

paragraphs.text: As soon as the jury had a little recovered from the shock of being upset, and their slates and pencils had been found and handed back to them, they set to work very diligently to write out a history of the accident, all except the Lizard, who seemed too much overcome to do anything but sit with its mouth open, gazing up into the roof of the court.

sentences.text: As soon as the jury had a little recovered from the shock of being upset, and their slates and pencils had been found and handed back to them, they set to work very diligently to write out a history of the accident, all except the Lizard, who seemed too much overcome to do anything but sit with its mouth open, gazing up into the roof of the court.
sentences.zh: 陪审员们从被掀翻的惊吓中稍稍缓过神来，石板和铅笔也找回来交到他们手上，他们便十分勤快地动手，把这场事故的经过写下来；只有壁虎例外，它似乎吓得太过，除了张着嘴坐在那里、呆呆望着法庭的屋顶，什么也做不了。

hints.zh: 石板，陪审员用来随手记话的写字板。
hints.en: Slates, small writing boards the jurymen use for their notes.

hints.zh: history 在这里指“经过、来龙去脉”，不是“历史”。
hints.en: 'A history of the accident' means an account of what happened, not the subject of history.

paragraphs.text: "What do you know about this business?" the King said to Alice.

sentences.text: "What do you know about this business?" the King said to Alice.
sentences.zh: “你对这件事知道些什么？”国王问爱丽丝。

paragraphs.text: "Nothing," said Alice.

sentences.text: "Nothing," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “什么也不知道。”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "Nothing whatever?" persisted the King.

sentences.text: "Nothing whatever?" persisted the King.
sentences.zh: “一点也不知道？”国王追问道。

paragraphs.text: "Nothing whatever," said Alice.

sentences.text: "Nothing whatever," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “一点也不知道。”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "That's very important," the King said, turning to the jury. They were just beginning to write this down on their slates, when the White Rabbit interrupted: "Unimportant, your Majesty means, of course," he said in a very respectful tone, but frowning and making faces at him as he spoke.

sentences.text: "That's very important," the King said, turning to the jury.
sentences.zh: “这非常重要。”国王说着，转向陪审团。

sentences.text: They were just beginning to write this down on their slates, when the White Rabbit interrupted: "Unimportant, your Majesty means, of course," he said in a very respectful tone, but frowning and making faces at him as he spoke.
sentences.zh: 他们刚要把这句话记到石板上，白兔就插了进来：“陛下当然是想说，无关紧要，”他语气十分恭敬，可说话时却皱着眉头冲国王做鬼脸。

hints.zh: 白兔，揣着怀表的那只兔子，如今在法庭上当传令官。
hints.en: The White Rabbit, the rabbit with the pocket watch, now acting as the court's messenger.

hints.zh: 陛下，当面对国王或王后说话时的尊称。
hints.en: Your Majesty, the respectful way to address a king or queen.

paragraphs.text: "Unimportant, of course, I meant," the King hastily said, and went on to himself in an undertone, "important—unimportant—unimportant—important———" as if he were trying which word sounded best.

sentences.text: "Unimportant, of course, I meant," the King hastily said, and went on to himself in an undertone, "important—unimportant—unimportant—important———" as if he were trying which word sounded best.
sentences.zh: “无关紧要，对，我是这个意思，”国王连忙说，又低声自言自语下去，“重要——无关紧要——无关紧要——重要———”，像是在掂量哪个词听起来更好。

paragraphs.text: Some of the jury wrote it down "important," and some "unimportant." Alice could see this, as she was near enough to look over their slates; "but it doesn't matter a bit," she thought to herself.

sentences.text: Some of the jury wrote it down "important," and some "unimportant."
sentences.zh: 有的陪审员记下“重要”，有的记下“无关紧要”。

sentences.text: Alice could see this, as she was near enough to look over their slates; "but it doesn't matter a bit," she thought to herself.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝看得见这些，因为她离得近，能从他们肩头看到石板；“不过这根本没关系，”她心里想。

paragraphs.text: At this moment the King, who had been for some time busily writing in his note-book, called out "Silence!" and read out from his book, "Rule Forty-two. All persons more than a mile high to leave the court."

sentences.text: At this moment the King, who had been for some time busily writing in his note-book, called out "Silence!" and read out from his book, "Rule Forty-two.
sentences.zh: 这时，国王已经在笔记本上忙着写了一阵子，他喊道：“肃静！”又从本子上念道：“第四十二条规则。

sentences.text: All persons more than a mile high to leave the court."
sentences.zh: 身高超过一英里者，一律离开法庭。”

hints.zh: 第四十二条规则，国王临时翻出来的条文，编号本身就带着荒唐。
hints.en: Rule Forty-two, a rule the King produces from his book; the number itself sounds absurd.

paragraphs.text: Everybody looked at Alice.

sentences.text: Everybody looked at Alice.
sentences.zh: 大家都看着爱丽丝。

paragraphs.text: "I'm not a mile high," said Alice.

sentences.text: "I'm not a mile high," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “我不到一英里高。”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "You are," said the King.

sentences.text: "You are," said the King.
sentences.zh: “你就是。”国王说。

paragraphs.text: "Nearly two miles high," added the Queen.

sentences.text: "Nearly two miles high," added the Queen.
sentences.zh: “快有两英里高了。”王后补了一句。

hints.zh: 红心王后，法庭上坐在国王身边，最爱喊“砍头”。
hints.en: The Queen of Hearts, who sits beside the King and loves shouting for heads to be cut off.

introduction.zh: 国王问爱丽丝知道些什么，她答什么也不知道，国王却说这“很重要”。白兔一边恭敬地纠正他，一边冲他做鬼脸。接着国王翻开笔记本，念出一条谁也没听过的规则——这条规则对谁不利？
introduction.en: Alice tells the King she knows nothing at all. He calls that very important, and the White Rabbit hurriedly says it is not. Then the King reads out a rule from his note-book. Who is it meant for?

quiz.question: What does the King call Alice's answer, and how does the White Rabbit correct him?
options: Wrong; the Rabbit says her answer is right.
Important; the Rabbit says he means unimportant.
Unimportant; the Rabbit says he means important.

feedback.zh: 国王说“很重要”，白兔一边恭敬地说“陛下是说无关紧要”，一边冲他做鬼脸。
feedback.en: The King says it is very important, and the Rabbit respectfully corrects him to 'unimportant' while pulling faces at him.

quiz.question: What is Rule Forty-two?
options: Everyone more than a mile high must leave the court.
Nobody may speak without the King's permission.
The jury must write down every word that is said.

feedback.zh: 国王从笔记本里念出第四十二条：身高超过一英里的人必须离开法庭，于是众人都看向爱丽丝。
feedback.en: The King reads Rule Forty-two from his book: anyone more than a mile high must leave the court, and everybody looks at Alice.

grammar.excerpt: They were just beginning to write this down on their slates, when the White Rabbit interrupted

focus.zh: were beginning 是过去进行时：记笔记的动作正在进行，白兔的插话把它打断了。
focus.en: Were beginning is past continuous: the writing was in progress when the Rabbit cut in.

paragraphs.text: "Well, I shan't go, at any rate," said Alice; "besides, that's not a regular rule: you invented it just now."

sentences.text: "Well, I shan't go, at any rate," said Alice; "besides, that's not a regular rule: you invented it just now."
sentences.zh: “反正我不走，”爱丽丝说，“再说，这也不算正经规则：是你刚刚编出来的。”

paragraphs.text: "It's the oldest rule in the book," said the King.

sentences.text: "It's the oldest rule in the book," said the King.
sentences.zh: “这是本法典里最古老的一条规则。”国王说。

paragraphs.text: "Then it ought to be Number One," said Alice. The King turned pale, and shut his notebook hastily.

sentences.text: "Then it ought to be Number One," said Alice.
sentences.zh: “那它就该是第一号。”爱丽丝说。

sentences.text: The King turned pale, and shut his notebook hastily.
sentences.zh: 国王脸色发白，急忙合上了笔记本。

paragraphs.text: "Consider your verdict," he said to the jury, in a low trembling voice.

sentences.text: "Consider your verdict," he said to the jury, in a low trembling voice.
sentences.zh: “考虑你们的裁决吧。”他用低沉发颤的声音对陪审团说。

paragraphs.text: "There's more evidence to come yet, please your Majesty," said the White Rabbit, jumping up in a great hurry; "this paper has just been picked up."

sentences.text: "There's more evidence to come yet, please your Majesty," said the White Rabbit, jumping up in a great hurry; "this paper has just been picked up."
sentences.zh: “陛下，还有证据没呈上来呢，”白兔说着，急匆匆跳起来，“这张纸是刚捡到的。”

paragraphs.text: "What's in it?" said the Queen.

sentences.text: "What's in it?" said the Queen.
sentences.zh: “上面写了什么？”王后问。

paragraphs.text: "I haven't opened it yet," said the White Rabbit, "but it seems to be a letter, written by the prisoner to—to somebody."

sentences.text: "I haven't opened it yet," said the White Rabbit, "but it seems to be a letter, written by the prisoner to—to somebody."
sentences.zh: “我还没打开呢，”白兔说，“不过看样子是封信，是犯人写给——写给什么人的。”

hints.zh: 被告，这里指被控偷馅饼的红心骑士。
hints.en: 'The prisoner' here is the Knave of Hearts, accused of stealing the tarts.

paragraphs.text: "It must have been that," said the King, "unless it was written to nobody, which isn't usual, you know."

sentences.text: "It must have been that," said the King, "unless it was written to nobody, which isn't usual, you know."
sentences.zh: “那一定就是这封了，”国王说，“除非它是写给‘没有人’的，可那又不合常理，你知道。”

paragraphs.text: "Who is it directed to?" said one of the jurymen.

sentences.text: "Who is it directed to?" said one of the jurymen.
sentences.zh: “它是寄给谁的？”一个陪审员问。

hints.zh: direct a letter 指在信上写收信人的姓名地址，所以问的是“寄给谁”。
hints.en: To direct a letter is to write the name and address on it, so the question is who it is addressed to.

paragraphs.text: "It isn't directed at all," said the White Rabbit; "in fact, there's nothing written on the outside." He unfolded the paper as he spoke, and added, "It isn't a letter after all: it's a set of verses."

sentences.text: "It isn't directed at all," said the White Rabbit; "in fact, there's nothing written on the outside."
sentences.zh: “根本没写收信人，”白兔说，“说实话，外面什么字也没有。”

sentences.text: He unfolded the paper as he spoke, and added, "It isn't a letter after all: it's a set of verses."
sentences.zh: 他一边说一边把纸展开，又补了一句：“这根本不是信：是一首诗。”

hints.zh: verses 指诗行、诗节，这里就是“一首诗”。
hints.en: 'Verses' means lines of poetry: here, simply a poem.

paragraphs.text: "Are they in the prisoner's handwriting?" asked another of the jurymen.

sentences.text: "Are they in the prisoner's handwriting?" asked another of the jurymen.
sentences.zh: “是犯人的笔迹吗？”另一个陪审员问。

paragraphs.text: "No, they're not," said the White Rabbit, "and that's the queerest thing about it." (The jury all looked puzzled.)

sentences.text: "No, they're not," said the White Rabbit, "and that's the queerest thing about it." (The jury all looked puzzled.)
sentences.zh: “不，不是，”白兔说，“古怪就古怪在这里。”（陪审团都面露困惑。）

paragraphs.text: "He must have imitated somebody else's hand," said the King. (The jury all brightened up again.)

sentences.text: "He must have imitated somebody else's hand," said the King. (The jury all brightened up again.)
sentences.zh: “那他一定是模仿了别人的笔迹。”国王说。（陪审团又都高兴起来。）

hints.zh: hand 在这里指“笔迹、字迹”，不是“手”。
hints.en: 'Hand' here means handwriting, not the body part.

paragraphs.text: "Please your Majesty," said the Knave, "I didn't write it, and they can't prove I did: there's no name signed at the end."

sentences.text: "Please your Majesty," said the Knave, "I didn't write it, and they can't prove I did: there's no name signed at the end."
sentences.zh: “陛下，”红心骑士说，“我没有写它，他们也证明不了是我写的：末尾没有签名。”

hints.zh: 红心骑士，被控偷馅饼的被告，全书最后受审的人。
hints.en: The Knave of Hearts, the prisoner on trial for stealing the tarts.

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝不肯离庭，国王便想让陪审团直接裁决。白兔跳起来说还有证据：一张刚捡到的纸。可纸上没有收信人，没有签名，也不是一封信。它到底是什么？
introduction.en: Alice refuses to leave the court, so the King wants the jury to decide at once. The White Rabbit jumps up with a paper that has just been picked up. It has no address, no name signed, and it is not even a letter. What can it be?

quiz.question: What does the White Rabbit say about the paper?
options: It has no address and no signature, and is really a set of verses.
It is the Knave's confession, signed at the end.
It is a letter from the prisoner to the Queen.

feedback.zh: 白兔说纸的外面什么也没写，展开一看不是信，而是一首诗。
feedback.en: The Rabbit says nothing is written on the outside, and the paper turns out to be a set of verses, not a letter.

quiz.question: How does the jury react when they hear the verses are not in the prisoner's handwriting?
options: They ask for the paper to be read aloud again.
They look puzzled at first, then brighten up when the King explains it.
They laugh and clap their hands.

feedback.zh: 陪审团先是一脸困惑，国王说“他准是模仿了别人的笔迹”，他们又都高兴起来。
feedback.en: The jury look puzzled, then cheer up when the King suggests the Knave imitated somebody else's hand.

grammar.excerpt: unless it was written to nobody

focus.zh: unless 引导条件从句（到 nobody 结束），相当于 if not：除非这信是写给“没有人”的。
focus.en: Unless introduces the condition (it ends at 'nobody') and means if not: the letter would have to be written to nobody.

paragraphs.text: "If you didn't sign it," said the King, "that only makes the matter worse. You must have meant some mischief, or else you'd have signed your name like an honest man."

sentences.text: "If you didn't sign it," said the King, "that only makes the matter worse.
sentences.zh: “如果你没签名，”国王说，“那只会让事情更糟。

sentences.text: You must have meant some mischief, or else you'd have signed your name like an honest man."
sentences.zh: 你一定是存了什么坏心，不然你就会像老实人那样签上自己的名字。”

hints.zh: 坏心思、惹祸的念头，不是普通的玩笑。
hints.en: 'Mischief' here means a harmful intention, not a harmless prank.

paragraphs.text: There was a general clapping of hands at this: it was the first really clever thing the King had said that day.

sentences.text: There was a general clapping of hands at this: it was the first really clever thing the King had said that day.
sentences.zh: 这话引来一片掌声：这是国王那天说出的第一句真正聪明的话。

paragraphs.text: "That proves his guilt," said the Queen.

sentences.text: "That proves his guilt," said the Queen.
sentences.zh: “这证明他有罪。”王后说。

paragraphs.text: "It proves nothing of the sort!" said Alice. "Why, you don't even know what they're about!"

sentences.text: "It proves nothing of the sort!" said Alice.
sentences.zh: “根本证明不了什么！”爱丽丝说。

sentences.text: "Why, you don't even know what they're about!"
sentences.zh: “哎呀，你们连诗里讲的是什么都不知道！”

hints.zh: 固定说法，意思是“完全不是那么回事”“一点也证明不了”。
hints.en: 'Nothing of the sort' is a fixed phrase meaning 'not at all' or 'nothing like that'.

paragraphs.text: "Read them," said the King.

sentences.text: "Read them," said the King.
sentences.zh: “念出来。”国王说。

paragraphs.text: The White Rabbit put on his spectacles. "Where shall I begin, please your Majesty?" he asked.

sentences.text: The White Rabbit put on his spectacles.
sentences.zh: 白兔戴上眼镜。

sentences.text: "Where shall I begin, please your Majesty?" he asked.
sentences.zh: “陛下，我该从哪里念起？”他问。

hints.zh: 眼镜，旧时说法，相当于 glasses。
hints.en: Spectacles: an older word for glasses.

paragraphs.text: "Begin at the beginning," the King said, gravely, "and go on till you come to the end: then stop."

sentences.text: "Begin at the beginning," the King said, gravely, "and go on till you come to the end: then stop."
sentences.zh: “从头开始，”国王庄重地说，“一直念到结尾：然后停下。”

paragraphs.text: These were the verses the White Rabbit read:—

sentences.text: These were the verses the White Rabbit read:—
sentences.zh: 白兔念的就是这样一首诗：——

paragraphs.text: "They told me you had been to her, And mentioned me to him: She gave me a good character, But said I could not swim.

sentences.text: "They told me you had been to her, And mentioned me to him: She gave me a good character, But said I could not swim.
sentences.zh: “他们告诉我你去过她那儿，还向他提起过我：她替我说了句好话，却又说我不会游泳。

hints.zh: character 在这里指“品行、名声”，give somebody a good character 就是替他说好话。
hints.en: 'Character' here means reputation: to give somebody a good character is to speak well of them.

paragraphs.text: He sent them word I had not gone (We know it to be true): If she should push the matter on, What would become of you?

sentences.text: He sent them word I had not gone (We know it to be true): If she should push the matter on, What would become of you?
sentences.zh: 他捎信给他们，说我没有走（我们知道这是真的）：要是她非要把事情闹下去，你会怎么样呢？

paragraphs.text: I gave her one, they gave him two, You gave us three or more; They all returned from him to you, Though they were mine before.

sentences.text: I gave her one, they gave him two, You gave us three or more; They all returned from him to you, Though they were mine before.
sentences.zh: 我给了她一个，他们给了他两个，你给了我们三个还多；他们全从他那儿回到了你那儿，虽然它们本来是我的。

paragraphs.text: If I or she should chance to be Involved in this affair, He trusts to you to set them free, Exactly as we were.

sentences.text: If I or she should chance to be Involved in this affair, He trusts to you to set them free, Exactly as we were.
sentences.zh: 如果我或者她碰巧卷进了这桩事，他指望你去把他们放出来，就像我们从前那样。

hints.zh: chance 这里作动词，意思是“碰巧”；should chance to be 就是“万一碰巧卷入”。
hints.en: 'Chance' is a verb here, meaning 'happen to': should chance to be = happened to be.

paragraphs.text: My notion was that you had been (Before she had this fit) An obstacle that came between Him, and ourselves, and it.

sentences.text: My notion was that you had been (Before she had this fit) An obstacle that came between Him, and ourselves, and it.
sentences.zh: 我的想法是，你一直（在她发这阵脾气之前）是横在他、我们自己，还有它之间的一个障碍。

paragraphs.text: Don't let him know she liked them best. For this must ever be A secret, kept from all the rest, Between yourself and me."

sentences.text: Don't let him know she liked them best.
sentences.zh: 别让他知道她最喜欢它们。

sentences.text: For this must ever be A secret, kept from all the rest, Between yourself and me."
sentences.zh: 因为这件事必须永远是个秘密，对别的人全瞒着，只在你我之间。”

introduction.zh: 国王认定不签名就说明心里有鬼，王后立刻说这已经证明有罪。爱丽丝忍不住反驳：你们连这些诗句讲什么都还不知道。白兔戴上眼镜，准备从头念起。
introduction.en: The King decides that not signing a letter shows bad intent, and the Queen says guilt is already proved. Alice points out that nobody yet knows what the verses are about. The White Rabbit puts on his spectacles to read them.

quiz.question: Why does the King say that not signing the letter makes things worse?
options: Because an unsigned letter shows the writer meant mischief.
Because the law requires two signatures on every letter.
Because the Knave cannot write his own name.

feedback.zh: 国王说，不签名说明写信人存心不良，否则就会像老实人那样署上名字。
feedback.en: The King argues that not signing shows bad intent; an honest man would have signed his name.

quiz.question: How does Alice answer the Queen's claim that the verses prove guilt?
options: She says they prove nothing, since nobody knows what the verses are about.
She asks the White Rabbit to stop reading.
She agrees that the verses are clear proof.

feedback.zh: 王后说“这证明他有罪”，爱丽丝立刻反驳，说大家连诗里讲什么都还不知道。
feedback.en: The Queen says the verses prove guilt, and Alice replies that nobody even knows what they are about.

grammar.excerpt: If I or she should chance to be Involved in this affair

focus.zh: if + should 表示“万一”：should chance to be 把可能性说得很轻，像在设想未必发生的情形。
focus.en: If + should makes the condition sound unlikely: 'should chance to be' means 'happened to be'.

paragraphs.text: "That's the most important piece of evidence we've heard yet," said the King, rubbing his hands; "so now let the jury———"

sentences.text: "That's the most important piece of evidence we've heard yet," said the King, rubbing his hands; "so now let the jury———"
sentences.zh: “这是我们听过的最要紧的一份证据，”国王搓着手说，“那么现在让陪审团———”

hints.zh: 搓手，常表示得意、满意，这里写出国王自以为得计。
hints.en: Rubbing his hands shows pleasure or satisfaction: the King thinks he has done well.

paragraphs.text: "If any one of them can explain it," said Alice, (she had grown so large in the last few minutes that she wasn't a bit afraid of interrupting him,) "I'll give him sixpence. I don't believe there's an atom of meaning in it."

sentences.text: "If any one of them can explain it," said Alice, (she had grown so large in the last few minutes that she wasn't a bit afraid of interrupting him,) "I'll give him sixpence.
sentences.zh: “他们当中要是有谁解释得出来，”爱丽丝说（她在刚才几分钟里长得那么大，一点也不怕打断他了），“我就给他六便士。

sentences.text: I don't believe there's an atom of meaning in it."
sentences.zh: 我不相信这里头有一点意思。”

hints.zh: 六便士，当时英国的小额硬币，这里当玩笑的赏钱。
hints.en: Sixpence, a small British coin of the time, offered here as a joke reward.

paragraphs.text: The jury all wrote down on their slates, "She doesn't believe there's an atom of meaning in it," but none of them attempted to explain the paper.

sentences.text: The jury all wrote down on their slates, "She doesn't believe there's an atom of meaning in it," but none of them attempted to explain the paper.
sentences.zh: 陪审团都在石板上写下：“她不相信这里头有一点意思。”可他们谁也没打算解释那张纸。

paragraphs.text: "If there's no meaning in it," said the King, "that saves a world of trouble, you know, as we needn't try to find any. And yet I don't know," he went on, spreading out the verses on his knee, and looking at them with one eye; "I seem to see some meaning in them, after all. '—said I could not swim—' you can't swim, can you?" he added, turning to the Knave.

sentences.text: "If there's no meaning in it," said the King, "that saves a world of trouble, you know, as we needn't try to find any.
sentences.zh: “要是里面没有意思，”国王说，“那倒省了一大堆麻烦，你知道，我们就不用费劲去找意思了。

sentences.text: And yet I don't know," he went on, spreading out the verses on his knee, and looking at them with one eye; "I seem to see some meaning in them, after all. '—said I could not swim—' you can't swim, can you?" he added, turning to the Knave.
sentences.zh: 可我又说不准，”他接着说，把诗摊在膝上，眯起一只眼睛看，“说到底，我好像还是看出点意思来。‘——说我不会游泳——’你不会游泳，对吧？”他转向红心骑士补了一句。

hints.zh: a world of 是夸张说法，等于“一大堆、极大的”。
hints.en: 'A world of trouble' means a great deal of trouble.

paragraphs.text: The Knave shook his head sadly. "Do I look like it?" he said. (Which he certainly did not, being made entirely of cardboard.)

sentences.text: The Knave shook his head sadly.
sentences.zh: 红心骑士难过地摇了摇头。

sentences.text: "Do I look like it?" he said. (Which he certainly did not, being made entirely of cardboard.)
sentences.zh: “我像会游泳的样子吗？”他说。（他当然一点也不像，因为他整个身子都是硬纸板做的。）

hints.zh: 硬纸板；点明红心骑士不过是纸牌上画出来的人。
hints.en: Cardboard: a reminder that the Knave is only a figure printed on a playing card.

paragraphs.text: "All right, so far," said the King, and he went on muttering over the verses to himself: "'We know it to be true—' that's the jury, of course— 'I gave her one, they gave him two—' why, that must be what he did with the tarts, you know—"

sentences.text: "All right, so far," said the King, and he went on muttering over the verses to himself: "'We know it to be true—' that's the jury, of course— 'I gave her one, they gave him two—' why, that must be what he did with the tarts, you know—"
sentences.zh: “好，到这儿都还说得通，”国王说，又自顾自地念叨起那些诗来，“‘我们知道这是真的——’这当然是陪审团——‘我给了她一个，他们给了他两个——’哎呀，那他准是用那些馅饼干了这事，你知道——”

hints.zh: 果馅饼，全书的关键物证：红心骑士被控偷的就是王后的馅饼。
hints.en: Tarts, the stolen pies at the heart of the case: the Knave is accused of taking the Queen's tarts.

paragraphs.text: "But it goes on 'they all returned from him to you,'" said Alice.

sentences.text: "But it goes on 'they all returned from him to you,'" said Alice.
sentences.zh: “可下面接着说‘他们全从他那儿回到了你那儿’。”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "Why, there they are!" said the King triumphantly, pointing to the tarts on the table. "Nothing can be clearer than that. Then again—'before she had this fit—' you never had fits, my dear, I think?" he said to the Queen. "Never!" said the Queen furiously, throwing an inkstand at the Lizard as she spoke. (The unfortunate little Bill had left off writing on his slate with one finger as he found it made no mark; but he now hastily began again, using the ink, that was trickling down his face, as long as it lasted.) "Then the words don't fit you," said the King, looking round the court with a smile. There was a dead silence.

sentences.text: "Why, there they are!" said the King triumphantly, pointing to the tarts on the table.
sentences.zh: “咦，它们不就在那儿吗！”国王得意洋洋地说，指着桌上的馅饼。

sentences.text: "Nothing can be clearer than that.
sentences.zh: “再清楚不过了。

sentences.text: Then again—'before she had this fit—' you never had fits, my dear, I think?" he said to the Queen.
sentences.zh: 再说——‘在她发作之前——’我想你从没发过脾气吧，亲爱的？”他对王后说。

sentences.text: "Never!" said the Queen furiously, throwing an inkstand at the Lizard as she spoke. (The unfortunate little Bill had left off writing on his slate with one finger as he found it made no mark; but he now hastily began again, using the ink, that was trickling down his face, as long as it lasted.) "Then the words don't fit you," said the King, looking round the court with a smile.
sentences.zh: “从来没有！”王后怒气冲冲地说，一边说一边把墨水瓶朝壁虎扔去。（不幸的小比尔本来已经不用手指在石板上写字了，因为他发现那样写不出痕迹；可这时他又急忙写起来，用脸上淌下来的墨水，能写多久就写多久。）“那么这些话就跟你不相干了，”国王说着，环顾法庭，微微一笑。

sentences.text: There was a dead silence.
sentences.zh: 全场一片死寂。

hints.zh: 比尔，那只壁虎，陪审团书记员。
hints.en: Bill, the Lizard, clerk of the jury.

introduction.zh: 国王搓着手说这是最要紧的证据，爱丽丝却愿意出六便士，赌没人能说清这些诗句的意思。国王把诗摊在膝上，眯起一只眼睛，忽然觉得看出了什么。他盯上了“不会游泳”那一句——被告会游泳吗？
introduction.en: The King rubs his hands and calls the verses the best evidence yet. Alice offers sixpence to anyone who can explain them. Then the King spreads the paper on his knee and thinks he sees a meaning. He turns to the Knave: can he swim?

quiz.question: What does Alice offer to anyone who can explain the verses?
options: Her place in the court.
Sixpence.
A cup of tea.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝说谁能解释这首诗，她就给谁六便士，因为她认定诗里一点意思也没有。
feedback.en: Alice offers sixpence to anyone who can explain the paper, because she believes it has no meaning at all.

quiz.question: What 'meaning' does the King find in the verses?
options: That the Knave cannot swim.
That the jury stole the tarts.
That the Queen wrote the letter herself.

feedback.zh: 国王念到“说我不会游泳”，便转头问被告是不是不会游泳；被告只能摇头。
feedback.en: The King reads out 'said I could not swim' and asks the Knave whether he can swim; the Knave can only shake his head.

grammar.excerpt: being made entirely of cardboard

focus.zh: being made 是 being + 过去分词，主语仍是 he；放在逗号后补出原因——他全身是硬纸板做的。
focus.en: Being made is being + past participle, with he as its subject; after the comma it gives the reason: he is made of cardboard.

paragraphs.text: "It's a pun!" the King added in an angry tone, and everybody laughed. "Let the jury consider their verdict," the King said, for about the twentieth time that day.

sentences.text: "It's a pun!" the King added in an angry tone, and everybody laughed.
sentences.zh: “这是双关！”国王气呼呼地补了一句，大家都笑了。

sentences.text: "Let the jury consider their verdict," the King said, for about the twentieth time that day.
sentences.zh: “让陪审团考虑他们的裁决吧。”国王说，这话他那天大概已经说了二十遍。

hints.zh: 双关语，一个词同时带两层意思；国王拿它当万能的解释。
hints.en: A pun, a word playing on two meanings; the King uses it as a catch-all explanation.

paragraphs.text: "No, no!" said the Queen. "Sentence first—verdict afterwards."

sentences.text: "No, no!" said the Queen.
sentences.zh: “不，不！”王后说。

sentences.text: "Sentence first—verdict afterwards."
sentences.zh: “先判刑——再裁决。”

hints.zh: sentence 在这里是“判决、刑罚”，不是“句子”；王后要把判刑挪到裁决前面。
hints.en: 'Sentence' here means the punishment, not a line of grammar: the Queen wants the punishment before the verdict.

paragraphs.text: "Stuff and nonsense!" said Alice loudly. "The idea of having the sentence first!"

sentences.text: "Stuff and nonsense!" said Alice loudly.
sentences.zh: “胡说八道！”爱丽丝大声说。

sentences.text: "The idea of having the sentence first!"
sentences.zh: “先判刑，这算什么主意！”

paragraphs.text: "Hold your tongue!" said the Queen, turning purple.

sentences.text: "Hold your tongue!" said the Queen, turning purple.
sentences.zh: “闭嘴！”王后说着，脸都气紫了。

hints.zh: 固定说法，意思是“闭嘴、不许再说”。
hints.en: 'Hold your tongue' is a fixed phrase meaning 'stop talking'.

paragraphs.text: "I won't!" said Alice.

sentences.text: "I won't!" said Alice.
sentences.zh: “我就不！”爱丽丝说。

paragraphs.text: "Off with her head!" the Queen shouted at the top of her voice. Nobody moved.

sentences.text: "Off with her head!" the Queen shouted at the top of her voice.
sentences.zh: “砍掉她的头！”王后扯着嗓子尖声叫道。

sentences.text: Nobody moved.
sentences.zh: 没有人动。

hints.zh: 王后的口头禅，“把她的头砍下来”。
hints.en: The Queen's favourite order: 'Cut off her head.'

paragraphs.text: "Who cares for you?" said Alice, (she had grown to her full size by this time.) "You're nothing but a pack of cards!"

sentences.text: "Who cares for you?" said Alice, (she had grown to her full size by this time.) "You're nothing but a pack of cards!"
sentences.zh: “谁怕你？”爱丽丝说（这时她已经长到了原来的大小），“你不过是一副纸牌！”

hints.zh: 一副纸牌；这句话点破了整个庭审的真相。
hints.en: 'A pack of cards', the words that give the whole trial away.

paragraphs.text: At this the whole pack rose up into the air, and came flying down upon her; she gave a little scream, half of fright and half of anger, and tried to beat them off, and found herself lying on the bank, with her head in the lap of her sister, who was gently brushing away some dead leaves that had fluttered down from the trees upon her face.

sentences.text: At this the whole pack rose up into the air, and came flying down upon her; she gave a little scream, half of fright and half of anger, and tried to beat them off, and found herself lying on the bank, with her head in the lap of her sister, who was gently brushing away some dead leaves that had fluttered down from the trees upon her face.
sentences.zh: 话音一落，整副纸牌腾空而起，朝她飞扑下来；她轻轻惊叫了一声，一半是吓的，一半是气的，伸手想把它们打退，却发现自己躺在河岸上，头枕在姐姐的膝上，姐姐正轻轻拂去从树上飘落到她脸上的几片枯叶。

paragraphs.text: "Wake up, Alice dear!" said her sister; "why, what a long sleep you've had!"

sentences.text: "Wake up, Alice dear!" said her sister; "why, what a long sleep you've had!"
sentences.zh: “醒醒，亲爱的爱丽丝！”姐姐说，“哎呀，你这一觉睡得可真长！”

paragraphs.text: "Oh, I've had such a curious dream!" said Alice, and she told her sister, as well as she could remember them, all these strange Adventures of hers that you have just been reading about; and when she had finished, her sister kissed her, and said, "It was a curious dream, dear, certainly: but now run in to your tea; it's getting late." So Alice got up and ran off, thinking while she ran, as well she might, what a wonderful dream it had been.

sentences.text: "Oh, I've had such a curious dream!" said Alice, and she told her sister, as well as she could remember them, all these strange Adventures of hers that you have just been reading about; and when she had finished, her sister kissed her, and said, "It was a curious dream, dear, certainly: but now run in to your tea; it's getting late."
sentences.zh: “哦，我做了个好奇怪的梦！”爱丽丝说，然后尽其所能，把她那些奇遇——也就是你刚刚读到的这些怪事——全讲给姐姐听；讲完之后，姐姐亲了亲她，说：“这梦确实奇怪，亲爱的：不过现在快进去喝茶吧，时候不早了。”

sentences.text: So Alice got up and ran off, thinking while she ran, as well she might, what a wonderful dream it had been.
sentences.zh: 于是爱丽丝起身跑开了，一边跑一边想——她也确实该这么想——这梦是多么奇妙啊。

introduction.zh: 王后等不及裁决，要先判刑再说。爱丽丝大声说这全是胡闹，王后气得脸都紫了，尖声喊出那句口头禅。可这一次，竟没有一个人动。她的话真能兑现吗？
introduction.en: The Queen will not wait for a verdict: she wants the sentence first. Alice calls the whole thing nonsense, and the Queen turns purple and screams her favourite order. This time, nobody moves. What will happen to Alice?

quiz.question: What does the Queen demand before the verdict?
options: That Alice leave the court at once.
That the jury write everything down.
That the sentence come first.

feedback.zh: 王后喊“先判刑——再裁决”，把审案的顺序整个颠倒了。
feedback.en: The Queen shouts 'Sentence first—verdict afterwards,' turning the proper order upside down.

quiz.question: What happens after Alice calls them a pack of cards?
options: The jury-box is carried out of the court.
The whole pack rises into the air and flies at her.
The King orders her to be silent.

feedback.zh: 她话音一落，整副纸牌腾空而起，朝她扑下来；她尖叫着醒来，发现自己躺在河岸上。
feedback.en: At once the whole pack rises into the air and flies down at her; she screams and finds herself on the bank.

grammar.excerpt: some dead leaves that had fluttered down from the trees upon her face

focus.zh: that 引导限制性定语从句，修饰 dead leaves，从句到 face 结束：从树上飘落到她脸上的枯叶。
focus.en: That introduces a defining relative clause on dead leaves; it runs to 'face' and tells us which leaves they were.

paragraphs.text: But her sister sat still just as she left her, leaning her head on her hand, watching the setting sun, and thinking of little Alice and all her wonderful Adventures, till she too began dreaming after a fashion, and this was her dream:—

sentences.text: But her sister sat still just as she left her, leaning her head on her hand, watching the setting sun, and thinking of little Alice and all her wonderful Adventures, till she too began dreaming after a fashion, and this was her dream:—
sentences.zh: 可姐姐在她走后仍旧坐在原处，一手托着头，望着落日，想着小爱丽丝和她那些奇妙的奇遇，直到她自己也勉强算做起梦来，她的梦是这样的：——

hints.zh: 固定说法，意思是“勉强算得上、以某种方式”。
hints.en: 'After a fashion' means 'in a way' or 'not very well'.

paragraphs.text: First, she dreamed of little Alice herself, and once again the tiny hands were clasped upon her knee, and the bright eager eyes were looking up into hers—she could hear the very tones of her voice, and see that queer little toss of her head to keep back the wandering hair that would always get into her eyes—and still as she listened, or seemed to listen, the whole place around her became alive with the strange creatures of her little sister's dream.

sentences.text: First, she dreamed of little Alice herself, and once again the tiny hands were clasped upon her knee, and the bright eager eyes were looking up into hers—she could hear the very tones of her voice, and see that queer little toss of her head to keep back the wandering hair that would always get into her eyes—and still as she listened, or seemed to listen, the whole place around her became alive with the strange creatures of her little sister's dream.
sentences.zh: 她先梦见了小爱丽丝本人，那双小手又交叠在她的膝上，那双明亮热切的眼睛又抬起来望着她——她听得见妹妹说话的腔调，看得见她为了把总爱跑到眼睛前面的乱发甩回去，那样古怪地把头一扬——她听着，或者像是听着，周围整个地方都活了起来，满是妹妹梦里的那些奇怪生灵。

paragraphs.text: The long grass rustled at her feet as the White Rabbit hurried by—the frightened Mouse splashed his way through the neighbouring pool—she could hear the rattle of the teacups as the March Hare and his friends shared their never-ending meal, and the shrill voice of the Queen ordering off her unfortunate guests to execution—once more the pig-baby was sneezing on the Duchess' knee, while plates and dishes crashed around it—once more the shriek of the Gryphon, the squeaking of the Lizard's slate-pencil, and the choking of the suppressed guinea-pigs, filled the air, mixed up with the distant sob of the miserable Mock Turtle.

sentences.text: The long grass rustled at her feet as the White Rabbit hurried by—the frightened Mouse splashed his way through the neighbouring pool—she could hear the rattle of the teacups as the March Hare and his friends shared their never-ending meal, and the shrill voice of the Queen ordering off her unfortunate guests to execution—once more the pig-baby was sneezing on the Duchess' knee, while plates and dishes crashed around it—once more the shriek of the Gryphon, the squeaking of the Lizard's slate-pencil, and the choking of the suppressed guinea-pigs, filled the air, mixed up with the distant sob of the miserable Mock Turtle.
sentences.zh: 长长的草在她脚边沙沙作响，白兔匆匆走过——受惊的老鼠哗啦哗啦地蹚过旁边的水塘——她听得见茶具的叮当声，那是三月兔和他的朋友们在吃那顿没完没了的茶点，还有王后尖声下令，把她那些倒霉的客人送去砍头——那猪娃娃又在公爵夫人膝上打喷嚏，盘子碟子在它周围摔得粉碎——又一次，狮鹫的尖叫、壁虎在石板上写字的吱吱声，还有那些被硬压下去的豚鼠的憋气声，一齐弥漫在空气里，混着可怜的假海龟远远的抽泣。

hints.zh: 老鼠，眼泪池里那只，被爱丽丝吓得直打哆嗦。
hints.en: The Mouse, the one from the pool of tears, frightened by Alice.

hints.zh: 三月兔，茶会的主人之一，那顿茶点永远吃不完。
hints.en: The March Hare, one of the tea-party hosts, whose meal never ends.

hints.zh: 公爵夫人，胡椒厨房里那位，怀里抱着个打喷嚏的猪娃娃。
hints.en: The Duchess, from the pepper kitchen, with the sneezing baby on her knee.

hints.zh: 狮鹫，带爱丽丝去见假海龟的那只半狮半鹰的怪物。
hints.en: The Gryphon, the lion-and-eagle creature who took Alice to the Mock Turtle.

hints.zh: 假海龟，讲自己伤心史的那只，总在远处抽泣。
hints.en: The Mock Turtle, who told his sad story and sobs in the distance.

introduction.zh: 爱丽丝跑回茶点去了，姐姐却仍坐在河边，望着落日，想着妹妹讲的那些奇遇。想着想着，她自己也开始做梦——梦里，奇境的声音一个接一个回来了。
introduction.en: Alice runs off to her tea, but her sister stays by the river, watching the sunset and thinking of the child's adventures. Slowly she begins to dream too, and the sounds of Wonderland come back one by one.

quiz.question: What is the sister doing as she begins to dream?
options: Sitting by the river, watching the sunset and thinking of Alice.
Walking home with Alice.
Reading the verses aloud from a paper.

feedback.zh: 爱丽丝走后，姐姐仍坐在原处，一手托着头，望着落日，想着妹妹的奇遇。
feedback.en: After Alice runs off, her sister stays where she is, leaning on her hand, watching the sunset and thinking of the child.

quiz.question: Which sounds of Wonderland come back in her dream?
options: The singing of birds and the ringing of church bells.
The King's voice reading Rule Forty-two.
The rustle of grass, the splash of the Mouse and the rattle of teacups.

feedback.zh: 梦里白兔匆匆走过，老鼠蹚水，茶具叮当，还有王后尖声下令——奇境的声音全回来了。
feedback.en: In the dream the White Rabbit hurries by, the Mouse splashes, teacups rattle and the Queen's shrill voice orders executions.

grammar.excerpt: as the March Hare and his friends shared their never-ending meal

focus.zh: as 引导时间从句，意思是“当……的时候”：茶具的响声与他们的茶点同时进行。
focus.en: As introduces a time clause: the rattle of the cups goes on while the March Hare and his friends eat.

paragraphs.text: So she sat on, with closed eyes, and half believed herself in Wonderland, though she knew she had but to open them again and all would change to dull reality—the grass would be only rustling in the wind, and the pool rippling to the waving of the reeds—the rattling teacups would change to tinkling sheep-bells, and the Queen's shrill cries to the voice of the shepherd boy—and the sneeze of the baby, the shriek of the Gryphon, and all the other queer noises, would change (she knew) to the confused clamour of the busy farm-yard—while the lowing of the cattle in the distance would take the place of the Mock Turtle's heavy sobs.

sentences.text: So she sat on, with closed eyes, and half believed herself in Wonderland, though she knew she had but to open them again and all would change to dull reality—the grass would be only rustling in the wind, and the pool rippling to the waving of the reeds—the rattling teacups would change to tinkling sheep-bells, and the Queen's shrill cries to the voice of the shepherd boy—and the sneeze of the baby, the shriek of the Gryphon, and all the other queer noises, would change (she knew) to the confused clamour of the busy farm-yard—while the lowing of the cattle in the distance would take the place of the Mock Turtle's heavy sobs.
sentences.zh: 于是她闭着眼睛坐在那里，半信自己就在奇境里，尽管她知道只要再睁开眼，一切就会变回沉闷的现实——草只是在风里沙沙响，水塘只是随着芦苇的摆动泛起波纹——叮当的茶具会变成叮铃的羊铃，王后的尖叫声会变成牧童的声音——娃娃的喷嚏、狮鹫的尖叫，以及其他所有古怪的声响，都会（她知道的）变成忙碌农院里乱哄哄的喧闹——而远处牛的哞叫声，会取代假海龟沉重的抽泣。

hints.zh: 牛的低沉的哞叫声，来自动词 low。
hints.en: Lowing: the deep sound a cow makes, from the verb 'low'.

hints.zh: 沉闷的现实，与奇境的热闹相对。
hints.en: 'Dull reality': the ordinary world, as opposed to the excitement of Wonderland.

paragraphs.text: Lastly, she pictured to herself how this same little sister of hers would, in the after-time, be herself a grown woman; and how she would keep, through all her riper years, the simple and loving heart of her childhood: and how she would gather about her other little children, and make their eyes bright and eager with many a strange tale, perhaps even with the dream of Wonderland of long-ago: and how she would feel with all their simple sorrows, and find a pleasure in all their simple joys, remembering her own child-life, and the happy summer days.

sentences.text: Lastly, she pictured to herself how this same little sister of hers would, in the after-time, be herself a grown woman; and how she would keep, through all her riper years, the simple and loving heart of her childhood: and how she would gather about her other little children, and make their eyes bright and eager with many a strange tale, perhaps even with the dream of Wonderland of long-ago: and how she would feel with all their simple sorrows, and find a pleasure in all their simple joys, remembering her own child-life, and the happy summer days.
sentences.zh: 最后，她想象着这个妹妹日后怎样长成一个妇人；怎样在成熟的岁月里始终保留童年那颗单纯而充满爱的心；怎样把自己的孩子聚到身边，用许多奇妙的故事，也许还用很久以前那个奇境的梦，让他们的眼睛变得明亮而热切；怎样体会他们所有单纯的忧愁，又从他们所有单纯的欢乐里得到乐趣，一边想起自己的童年，想起那些快乐的夏日。

hints.zh: 往后的岁月、日后，不是“之后的某个时间点”。
hints.en: 'The after-time' means the years to come.

hints.zh: 成熟的年岁，指成年以后的日子。
hints.en: 'Riper years' means her more mature adult years.

hints.zh: many a + 单数名词，意思等于 many，但语气更文雅。
hints.en: 'Many a strange tale' means many strange tales; the pattern is a literary way of saying many.

introduction.zh: 姐姐闭着眼，半信自己就在奇境里。她知道只要睁开眼，风声、羊铃和农场的喧闹就会回来。可她还想再想一件事：许多年后，那个小女孩会变成什么样的人？
introduction.en: With her eyes closed, the sister half believes she is in Wonderland. She knows that opening them would bring back the wind, the sheep-bells and the farm-yard. But one more picture keeps her sitting there: what will the little girl be like when she grows up?

quiz.question: What does the sister know would happen if she opened her eyes?
options: The White Rabbit would disappear for ever.
The strange noises would turn into ordinary farm sounds.
Alice would wake up and tell her more adventures.

feedback.zh: 她知道一睁眼，奇境的声音就会变回风声、羊铃和农场的喧闹。
feedback.en: She knows that opening her eyes would turn the queer noises back into wind, sheep-bells and the clamour of the farm-yard.

quiz.question: What last picture does she keep in her mind?
options: Alice as a grown woman, telling Wonderland to her own children.
Alice running back to the house for tea.
The Queen calling off the trial.

feedback.zh: 她想象妹妹长大成人，仍保留童年的心，会把奇境的故事讲给自己的孩子听。
feedback.en: She pictures Alice grown up, keeping her childhood heart and passing the dream of Wonderland on to her own children.

grammar.excerpt: make their eyes bright and eager with many a strange tale

focus.zh: make their eyes bright and eager：make + 宾语 + 形容词，说她讲的故事让孩子眼里发亮、心里急切。
focus.en: Make + object + adjective: 'make their eyes bright and eager' tells us what her stories do to the children.
